title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄕試錄序
萬曆壬午秋八月廣西當復
大比士前御史李東敎選相
繼疏
請代
上命御史馬呈圖馳往監臨之至
則謹布禮官科條令西士力
===
正文體以歸大雅諸不急務
姑未遑專意掄文旣戒旣毖
乃提調以左參政彭富右參
政胡維新監試以按察使陳
應春右參政兼僉事葉朝陽
其執經品藻則以敬修曁敎
諭賈宗正爲考試官敎諭梁
punctuated:
廣西鄕試錄序

萬曆壬午秋八月，廣西當復大比士。前御史李東、敎選相繼疏請代，上命御史馬呈圖馳往監臨之。至則謹布禮官科條，令西士力正文體以歸大雅。諸不急務，姑未遑，專意掄文，旣戒旣毖。乃提調以左參政彭富、右參政胡維新，監試以按察使陳應春、右參政兼僉事葉朝陽。其執經品藻，則以敬修曁敎諭賈宗正爲考試官，敎諭梁
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli reign (1582), Guangxi was due once again to hold the triennial examination of scholars. After the former Censors Li Dong 李東 and Jiao Xuan 敎選 successively submitted memorials requesting to be replaced, the Emperor ordered Censor Ma Chengtu 馬呈圖 to travel by post to serve as Supervising Official over the proceedings. Upon his arrival, he carefully promulgated the regulations of the Ministry of Rites, instructing the scholars of Guangxi to strive to rectify their literary style so as to return to classical elegance. Setting aside various non-urgent affairs for the time being, he devoted his full attention to the selection of essays, maintaining both vigilance and caution. Thereupon, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Fu 彭富 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Weixin 胡維新 were appointed as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yingchun 陳應春 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Ye Chaoyang 葉朝陽 were appointed as Monitoring Officials. As for upholding the classics and evaluating the candidates' compositions, I, Jingxiu 敬修, together with Confucian School Instructor Jia Zongzheng 賈宗正, were appointed to serve as Examiners, and Confucian School Instructors Liang …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
懋勳王希堯訓導郭藎臣丁
繼宗張沛陳茂鵞爲同考試
官餘百執事亦各愼遴部署
以待乃合饗誓眾就棘闈以
提學僉事袁昌祚所選士一
千五百有奇嚴扃鑰而試之
三擇其儁五十有五人籍
===
奏之敬修嘗聞三代之盛南不
過衡山而粤西當衡嶽西南
數百餘里未列禹貢職方氏
然南交分宅紀在帝典而八
桂扶疎由秦漢迄今世以名
郡孰謂山海經盡繆悠語也
第其時山川尚縕祕神奇卽
punctuated:
懋勳、王希堯，訓導郭藎臣、丁繼宗、張沛、陳茂鵞爲同考試官。餘百執事，亦各愼遴部署以待。乃合饗誓眾，就棘闈，以提學僉事袁昌祚所選士一千五百有奇，嚴扃鑰而試之三，擇其儁五十有五人，籍奏之。

敬修嘗聞：三代之盛，南不過衡山，而粤西當衡嶽西南數百餘里，未列《禹貢》、《職方氏》。然南交分宅，紀在《帝典》，而八桂扶疎，由秦、漢迄今，世以名郡，孰謂《山海經》盡繆悠語也？第其時山川尚縕祕神奇，卽
translation_en:
… Maoxun 梁懋勳 and Wang Xiyao 王希堯, and Assistant Instructors Guo Jinchen 郭藎臣, Ding Jizong 丁繼宗, Zhang Pei 張沛, and Chen Mao'e 陳茂鵞 as Associate Examiners. All the remaining myriad functionaries were also carefully selected and deployed to stand in readiness. Thereupon, a joint banquet was held to administer the oath to the assembled officials, and they entered the thorny examination compound. Taking the more than one thousand five hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Changzuo 袁昌祚, they strictly locked the gates and tested them across three sessions, choosing fifty-five outstanding men among them and registering their names to be memorialized to the throne.

I, Jingxiu, have heard that at the height of the Three Dynasties, their southern reach did not extend beyond Mount Heng, and since western Guangdong and Guangxi (Yuexi 粤西) lie several hundred li southwest of the Southern Marchmount Heng, they were not listed in the Tribute of Yu (Yugong 禹貢) or the職方氏 Direction of Regions (Zhifang shi 職方氏). Yet the assigned residence in Nanjiao 南交 is recorded in the Canon of the Emperor (Didian 帝典), and the luxuriant "Eight Cinnamon Trees" (Bagui 八桂, i.e., Guangxi) have, from the Qin and Han dynasties down to the present day, been renowned through the ages as famous commanderies—who then could say that the Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai jing 山海經) consists entirely of absurd and groundless words? It is only that in those early times the mountains and rivers still held their wondrous mysteries locked within, and even if…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有雄特右武尠文學故後世
靡得稱云玆敬修幸以校役
遡洮源出靈渠其堯山漓水
環車幙後先奇秀刺目彼靈
氣在天地蜿蜒南下若大軍
鼓行將趨溟海始飲馬蓐食
而三江若帶諸山皆屹然壁
===
立若重關東扼之此其積乆
磅礴以待
文明
鴻化厚發於賢儁有顯融也頃歲
十寨平捷告
郊
廟岑溪大峒亦相率蛾伏願繕城
punctuated: 有雄特，右武尠文學，故後世靡得稱云。玆敬修幸以校役，遡洮源，出靈渠，其堯山、漓水環車幙後先，奇秀刺目。彼靈氣在天地，蜿蜒南下，若大軍鼓行將趨溟海，始飲馬蓐食，而三江若帶，諸山皆屹然壁立，若重關東扼之。此其積乆磅礴，以待文明鴻化，厚發於賢儁，有顯融也。頃歲十寨平，捷告郊廟，岑溪大峒亦相率蛾伏，願繕城
translation_en: …there were heroic and outstanding figures, they valued martial prowess and were sparse in literary learning; thus later generations had nothing to praise of them. Now I, Jingxiu, have been fortunate to travel on this duty of examining: going upstream to the source of the Tao River and emerging from the Ling Canal, Mount Yao and the Li River encircled my carriage curtains before and behind, their marvelous beauty striking the eye. That numinous vitality in heaven and earth winds its way southward, like a great army marching to the beat of drums, about to hasten toward the vast sea, just watering its horses and eating on its bedding-mats; while the Three Rivers are like a girdle, and the various mountains all stand precipitously like walls, as though double passes were holding them back in the east. This is its long-accumulated, vast energy awaiting the grand transformation of civilizing enlightenment, to burst forth richly in worthy talents with illustrious distinction. In recent years, the Ten Stockades were pacified and the victory was announced at the Suburban Altar and the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Great Grottoes of Cenxi also one after another submitted like ants, wishing to repair cities…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
授田如昭江俱齒編氓守亭
障者歲鮮橫草之警川無駭
艫陸無剽槖皆喁喁仰
聖德苞覆萬里諸士益得以從事
鉛槧而希大雅之矩日彬彬
焉卽銓第其所爲文類能明
習世務而不詭於道義其咀
===
華斂鄂視
制式罔失尺矱而英思勁氣坌發
滃溢直與此中奇秀爭雄長
於穎素間莫可禁圉非夫
聖化之型範靈氣之鼓龠也有是
哉顧惟士起三代所敷對率
簡質無長語而考論其所表
punctuated: 授田，如昭江俱齒編氓。守亭障者歲鮮橫草之警，川無駭艫，陸無剽槖，皆喁喁仰聖德苞覆萬里。諸士益得以從事鉛槧，而希大雅之矩，日彬彬焉。卽銓第其所爲文，類能明習世務，而不詭於道義；其咀華斂鄂，視制式罔失尺矱；而英思勁氣，坌發滃溢，直與此中奇秀爭雄長於穎素間，莫可禁圉。非夫聖化之型範，靈氣之鼓龠也，有是哉？顧惟士起三代，所敷對率簡質無長語，而考論其所表
translation_en: … and receive land, so that just as along the Zhao River (Zhaojiang 昭江), all are enrolled among the registered commoners. Those who guard the border posts and forts rarely see an alarm across the grasses all year; on the rivers there are no startled boats, and on land there are no plundered travel-sacks. All look up in eager admiration to the Sacred Virtue that envelopes and shelters ten thousand li. The scholars have thus been all the more able to devote themselves to writing tablets and brushes, aspiring to the standards of high elegance, growing daily more refined and accomplished. Now, in evaluating and ranking the essays they have composed, they generally show a clear grasp of worldly affairs without deviating from moral principle; as they savor the blossoms and gather the calyxes of literature, they observe the prescribed imperial format without losing a foot or an inch of its measure; and their brilliant thoughts and vigorous spirit burst forth and brim over, directly vying for supremacy with the wondrous beauty of this region's landscapes upon the brush-tip and white silk, impossible to hold back or contain. Were it not for the molding influence of Sacred Transformation and the bellows-breath of the land's numinous ether, could it be like this? Yet when we reflect on the scholars who arose in the Three Dynasties, the responses they set forth were generally simple and unadorned, without superfluous words; and when one examines and evaluates what they…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
樹輒與言相畫一以其心榮
利不入而一意於亮天工明
主德故稱為不二心之臣盛
莫加焉今諸士言則旣儷儷
侈矣假令以厝諸用能一一
必成信者乎夫論疆土則化
軼三代而謂無一庶幾於三
===
代之士者恥也言詞視三代
益閎以肆而行實不相副者
虛也語曰玉產於山工得琢
焉而眞璞不完士脩於家主
得用焉而純白不存信若言
也毋寧
國家熙化靡所恃賴將五嶠三
punctuated: 樹，輒與言相畫一。以其心榮利不入，而一意於亮天工、明主德，故稱為「不二心之臣」，盛莫加焉。今諸士言則旣儷儷侈矣，假令以厝諸用，能一一必成信者乎？夫論疆土則化軼三代，而謂無一庶幾於三代之士者，恥也；言詞視三代益閎以肆，而行實不相副者，虛也。語曰：「玉產於山，工得琢焉，而眞璞不完；士脩於家，主得用焉，而純白不存。」信若言也，毋寧國家熙化靡所恃賴，將五嶠、三
translation_en: …achievements, they always matched their words as if drawn to a single line. Because thoughts of glory and profit did not enter their minds, and they were wholly devoted to assisting the work of Heaven and making bright the virtue of their sovereign, they were praised as "ministers of undivided heart"—a flourishing state that could not be surpassed. Now, what the scholars have said in their essays is already finely paired and lavish; yet suppose they are placed into practical service—will they be able to make every single word prove trustworthy in accomplishment? Indeed, if in speaking of our territory its civilizing transformation surpasses that of the Three Dynasties, yet one were to say there is not a single scholar who approaches those of the Three Dynasties, that would be a shame; and if their diction and phrasing are even more grand and uninhibited compared to those of the Three Dynasties, yet their actual conduct does not match, that is mere emptiness. As the saying goes: "Jade is produced in the mountains, and when the artisan gets to carve it, its true uncarved simplicity is no longer intact; a scholar cultivates himself at home, and when the ruler gets to employ him, his pure whiteness no longer remains." If it were truly as this saying has it, then not only would the flourishing transformation of the dynasty have nothing to rely upon, but would not even the Five Ridges and the Three…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
江得無謂其生也實徼靈于
彼今不惠之光寵而重泄越
之慚負若何今有指嘉畝以
語人曰是歲萬鍾其藨蔉不
力登困不如數則世必以譙
語者為謾諸士今萬鍾價矣
行奉
===
大對服中外事以自試於藨蔉
一切聲利棼華方日朋起而
戰其中扃稍不制而甘之必
且言行相背馳若兩人然業
何辭而謝斯世之不譙吾謾
也尚務守一於其心如農夫
之有畔歲服勤以為常罔以
punctuated: 江，得無謂其生也，實徼靈于彼，今不惠之光寵，而重泄越之慚，負若何？今有指嘉畝以語人曰：「是歲萬鍾。」其藨蔉不力，登困不如數，則世必以譙語者為謾。諸士今萬鍾價矣，行奉大對，服中外事，以自試於藨蔉。一切聲利棼華，方日朋起而戰其中扃，稍不制而甘之，必且言行相背馳，若兩人然。業何辭而謝斯世之不譙吾謾也？尚務守一於其心，如農夫之有畔，歲服勤以為常，罔以
translation_en: … the Three Rivers would surely say that when these men were born, they truly drew their spiritual vitality from those peaks and waters; yet now, instead of bestowing glorious honor upon them, they add the shame of squandering and disgracing that heritage—how great a betrayal would that be? Suppose someone today points to a fine plot of land and tells others, "This will yield ten thousand zhong of grain a year." If the weeding and hilling are not done with effort, and the grain stored in the granaries falls short of that amount, then the world will surely reproach the speaker for making an empty boast. You gentlemen today are valued at ten thousand zhong! Soon you will present your Great Responses at the Palace Examination and take up service in the capital and the provinces, testing yourselves in the work of weeding and hilling. All manner of fame, profit, and dazzling luxury will daily rise up together to wage war within your hearts. If you fail even slightly to restrain yourselves and instead indulge in them, your words and deeds will inevitably run counter to each other as though you were two different people. With what words could we then excuse ourselves when this world reproaches us for making an empty boast? You must strive to hold fast to single-mindedness in your hearts, just as a farmer keeps to his field boundaries, taking yearly toil as the constant norm, and never allowing…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
靡麗渝貞繁膴改素諸所展
錯各求自効其長而要諸衷
皆務斷斷明
主德勿後斯樹駿垂鴻榮鏡史籍
敬修且竦意以拜諸士之貺
是舉也前總督兩廣兵部右
侍郎兼右僉都御史今晉南
===
京都察院右都御史劉堯誨
威略茂宣弘裨文教今總督
兩廣兵部尚書兼左副都御
史陳瑞規恢謨烈賁及章縫
巡撫廣西兵部右侍郎兼右
僉都御史郭應聘德威乂孚
文武丕式若前總兵署都督
punctuated:
靡麗渝貞、繁膴改素。諸所展錯，各求自効其長，而要諸衷，皆務斷斷明主德，勿後。斯樹駿垂鴻，榮鏡史籍，敬修且竦意以拜諸士之貺。

是舉也，前總督兩廣兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史、今晉南京都察院右都御史劉堯誨，威略茂宣，弘裨文教；今總督兩廣兵部尚書兼左副都御史陳瑞，規恢謨烈，賁及章縫；巡撫廣西兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史郭應聘，德威乂孚，文武丕式。若前總兵署都督
translation_en:
…extravagance alter their integrity, or sumptuous abundance change their simplicity. In all that they put into practice and undertake, let each seek to contribute his strengths, yet in the essentials of their hearts, let all strive with single-minded devotion to make manifest the virtue of the Sovereign, never falling behind. Thus will they establish great achievements and hand down grand legacies, shining gloriously in the historical records, and I, Jingxiu, shall respectfully and eagerly bow to receive the gift of these gentlemen's accomplishments.

In this undertaking, the former Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief of the Nanjing Censorate, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, abundantly displayed his majestic strategy and greatly aided civil education; the current Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Minister of War and concurrently Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Chen Rui 陳瑞, broadened the grand plans and achievements, extending adornment to the Confucian scholars; the Grand Coordinator of Guangxi, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, Guo Yingping 郭應聘, inspired trust and order through both virtue and majesty, serving as a great model in both civil and military affairs. As for the former Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同知王尚文崇儒奮武參議
彭應時李淶副使徐儒皆以
綜理宣猷副總兵李應祥參
將白玉金丹周勳署都指揮
僉事戴應麟鍾維岳蔡春及
皆以扞掫祗事其入
賀則右布政使今轉左胡定副
===
使秦寵其遷秩及檄調則右
布政吳善參政項思教參議
陳尚伊副使劉世賞吳哲而
刑部員外郎孫從龍行人司
行人孫愈賢則皆以使
命弭節玆土光重人文者也法得
竝書
punctuated: 同知王尚文崇儒奮武；參議彭應時、李淶，副使徐儒，皆以綜理宣猷；副總兵李應祥，參將白玉、金丹、周勳，署都指揮僉事戴應麟、鍾維岳、蔡春及，皆以扞掫祗事；其入賀，則右布政使今轉左胡定、副使秦寵；其遷秩及檄調，則右布政吳善，參政項思教，參議陳尚伊，副使劉世賞、吳哲；而刑部員外郎孫從龍、行人司行人孫愈賢，則皆以使命弭節玆土，光重人文者也。法得竝書。
translation_en: … Vice Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Shangwen 王尚文 revered Confucian scholarship while displaying martial vigor; Assistant Administration Commissioners Peng Yingshi 彭應時 and Li Lai 李淶, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Ru 徐儒, all manifested grand plans through their comprehensive administration; Vice Regional Commander Li Yingxiang 李應祥, Assistant Regional Commanders Bai Yu 白玉, Jin Dan 金丹, and Zhou Xun 周勳, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Dai Yinglin 戴應麟, Zhong Weiyue 鍾維岳, and Cai Chunji 蔡春及, all reverently fulfilled their duties in defense and patrol; as for those who entered the capital to offer congratulations, there were Right Administration Commissioner Hu Ding 胡定, now transferred to Left Administration Commissioner, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qin Chong 秦寵; as for those who were promoted or transferred by official dispatch, there were Right Administration Commissioner Wu Shan 吳善, Left or Right Administration Vice Commissioner Xiang Sijiao 項思教, Assistant Administration Commissioner Chen Shangyi 陳尚伊, and Surveillance Vice Commissioners Liu Shishang 劉世賞 and Wu Zhe 吳哲; whereas Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice Sun Conglong 孫從龍 and Messenger in the Messenger Office Sun Yuxian 孫愈賢 both halted their envoys' carriages in this land on imperial missions, lending luster and weight to our literary culture. By regulation, it is proper that they all be recorded together.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
江西贛州府興國縣儒學敎
諭汪敬修謹序
punctuated: 江西贛州府興國縣儒學敎諭汪敬修謹序。
translation_en: Respectfully prefaced by Wang Jingxiu 汪敬修, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xingguo County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史馬呈圖〔道甫四川內江縣人辛酉貢士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政彭富〔中禮雲南大理衛籍合肥縣人壬戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政胡維新〔文化浙江餘姚縣人己未進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使陳應春〔汝和福建長樂縣人壬戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政兼按察司僉事葉朝陽〔見心浙江秀水縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官

Guangxi Provincial Examination of the Tenth Year of the Wanli Reign (1582)

Supervising Official
Ma Chengtu 馬呈圖 (courtesy name Daofu 道甫), Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor of Guangxi. He is a native of Neijiang County, Sichuan, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinyou year (1561).

Proctors
Peng Fu 彭富 (courtesy name Zhongli 中禮), Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. Registered in the Dali Guard in Yunnan and originally from Hefei County, he is a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562).
Hu Weixin 胡維新 (courtesy name Wenhua 文化), Right Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission. He is a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiwei year (1559).

Monitors
Chen Yingchun 陳應春 (courtesy name Ruhe 汝和), Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. He is a native of Changle County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562).
Ye Chaoyang 葉朝陽 (courtesy name Jianxin 見心), Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. He is a native of Xiushui County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year (1565).

Examiners
Wang Jingxiu 汪敬修 (courtesy name Daoqing 道卿), Instructor in the Confucian School of Xingguo County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. He is a native of Wuyuan County, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), and a tribute student (gongshi) of the gengwu year (1570).
Jia Zongzheng 賈宗正 (courtesy name Chengfu 誠甫), Instructor in the Confucian School of Le'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. He is a native of Dongyang County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the gengwu year (1570).

Associate Examiners
Liang Maoxun 梁懋勳 (courtesy name Rujian 孺建), Instructor in the Confucian School of Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. He is a native of Panyu County, Guangdong, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the jiazi year (1564).
Wang Xiyao 王希堯 (courtesy name Weizhong 惟中), Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhushan County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang. Registered in the Yunnan Central Guard and originally from Dangtu County, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), he is a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year (1579).
Guo Jinchen 郭藎臣 (courtesy name Xiaozhong 孝仲), Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. He is a native of Chengdu County, Sichuan, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the bingzi year (1576).
Ding Jizong 丁繼宗 (courtesy name Weixiao 惟孝), Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Xiangxiang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. He is a native of Yuanzhou, Huguang, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the dingmao year (1567).
Zhang Pei 張沛 (courtesy name Defu 德夫), Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili). He is a native of Ouning County, Fujian, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the gengwu year (1570).

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰辭達而已矣
脩道之謂教道也者不可須臾離也
舜何人也予何人也有爲者亦若是
易
聖人養賢以及萬民
九二之孚有喜也
言行君子之所以動天地也可不慎乎
===
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
有能奮庸熙帝之載使宅百揆亮采惠疇
非天私我有商惟天佑于一德非商求于
下民惟民歸于一德德惟一動罔不吉
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
子曰：「辭達而已矣。」
脩道之謂教。道也者，不可須臾離也。
舜何人也？予何人也？有爲者亦若是。

易
聖人養賢以及萬民。
九二之孚，有喜也。
言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎！
昔者聖人之作《易》也，將以順性命之理。是以立天之道，曰陰與陽；立地之道，曰柔與剛；立人之道，曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故《易》六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故《易》六位而成章。

書
有能奮庸，熙帝之載，使宅百揆，亮采惠疇？
非天私我有商，惟天佑于一德；非商求于下民，惟民歸于一德。德惟一，動罔不吉。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books
The Master said, "In language, it is simply required that it convey the meaning." (Analects 15.41)
Cultivating the Way is called instruction. As for the Way, one may not depart from it for even an instant. (Doctrine of the Mean 1)
What kind of man was Shun? What kind of man am I? Anyone who exerts himself will also become like this. (Mencius 3A.1)

Classic of Changes (Yi)
The sage nourishes the worthy and thereby reaches the myriad people. (Hexagram 27, Yi, Commentary on the Decision)
The sincerity of the Nine in the Second Place brings joy. (Hexagram 58, Dui, Commentary on the Images)
Words and deeds are that whereby the noble man moves Heaven and Earth. Must one not be cautious with them? (Appended Remarks, Part I, Ch. 8)
In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes, they intended thereby to conform to the principles of human nature and destiny. Therefore they established the Way of Heaven, calling it yin and yang; they established the Way of Earth, calling it the soft and the hard; and they established the Way of Man, calling it benevolence and righteousness. They combined the Three Powers and doubled them; therefore in the Changes six lines form a hexagram. They divided the yin and the yang and alternately employed the soft and the hard; therefore in the Changes the six positions form a pattern. (Discussion of the Trigrams, Ch. 2)

Classic of Documents (Shu)
"Is there anyone who can vigorously display his merits and make bright the Emperor's undertakings, whom I might place as General Regulator to aid in affairs and accord with the categories?" ("Canon of Shun")
It is not that Heaven shows partiality toward our house of Shang; it is only that Heaven aids pure virtue. It is not that Shang sought out the people below; it is only that the people turn toward pure virtue. Where virtue is pure and single, in no movement will it fail to be auspicious. ("Both Possessed Pure Virtue")

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歲月日時無易百穀用成
惟公克成厥終
詩
我稼旣同上入執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索
綯亟其乘屋其始播百穀二之日鑿冰
冲冲三之日納于凌陰四之日其蚤獻
羔祭韭
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天
受祿于天保右命之自天申之干祿百福
===
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
成王不敢康夙夜基命宥密
春秋
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年
次于陘 楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵俱
僖公四年
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒成公九年秋楚公
子壬夫帥師侵宋襄公元年
五月公及諸侯盟于皐鼬定公四年
punctuated:
歲、月、日、時無易，百穀用成。
惟公克成厥終。
《詩》：
我稼旣同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。
受祿于天，保右命之，自天申之。干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。
《春秋》：
夏，單伯會伐宋。莊公十有四年。
次于陘；楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。俱僖公四年。
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒，成公九年；秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋，襄公元年。
五月，公及諸侯盟于皐鼬。定公四年。
translation_en:
"When the year, the month, the day, and the season have no irregularities, the hundred grains thereby mature." (Book of Documents, "Hongfan")
"Only the Duke can bring the end to completion." (Book of Documents, "Luogao")

Book of Odes (Shijing):
"When our harvests are gathered in, we go up and enter to undertake the work on the houses. In the day go gather thatch-rushes; in the night twist ropes. Make haste to get up on the roofs; soon we shall begin to sow the hundred grains. In the days of the second month, they hew out the ice with ringing blows; in the days of the third month, they convey it into the ice-house. In the days of the fourth month, very early in the morning, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with scallions." ("Qiyue")
"The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the heavens." ("Heming")
"He receives blessings from Heaven; It protects, helps, and appoints him, renewing them from Heaven. Seeking blessings and a hundred felicities, his sons and grandsons are a thousand and a hundred million. Solemn and august, fit to be ruler, fit to be king." ("Jiale")
"Cheng Wang did not dare to take his ease; day and night he laid the foundations of the mandate in deep and quiet wisdom." ("Hao Tian You Cheng Ming")

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禮記
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
天子使其大夫爲三監監於方伯之國
大章章之也
儒有内稱不辟親外舉不辟怨程功積事
推賢而進達之不望其報君得其志苟
利國家不求富貴其舉賢援能有如此
者
第貳場
===
論
平天下之要道
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢賜天下田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬宋以文彦博富弼同平章事誥〔至和二年〕
擬吏部尚書兼翰林院學士李賢等
進
大明一統志表〔天順五年〕

第貳場

「平天下之要道」

詔、誥、表〔内科一道〕

translation_en:

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
判語〔五條〕
講讀律令
市司評物價
私越冒度關津
聞有恩赦而故犯
有司官吏不住公廨
第參場
策五道
問書陳典學詩咏緝熙卽紀傳所稱唐虞
===
三代之隆亦各有師授故君人者未有
不懋學而能以明聖自表見者也後世
學術廢闕主德鮮茂間有喜近儒紳游
神縹素則前史以爲豔談若召講石渠
稱制臨決講論經理夜分不寐精選文
學之士更日直宿引入與論前言往行
自巳至申然後釋卷寫尚書無逸篇于
屛玆其章章較著也其於古帝王所謂
學者同乎抑或華實異也
punctuated:
判語〔五條〕：
講讀律令。
市司評物價。
私越冒度關津。
聞有恩赦而故犯。
有司官吏不住公廨。

第參場
策五道

問：《書》陳典學，《詩》咏緝熙，卽紀傳所稱唐、虞、三代之隆，亦各有師授。故君人者，未有不懋學而能以明聖自表見者也。後世學術廢闕，主德鮮茂。間有喜近儒紳、游神縹素，則前史以爲豔談：若召講石渠，稱制臨決；講論經理，夜分不寐；精選文學之士，更日直宿；引入與論前言往行，自巳至申然後釋卷；寫《尚書·無逸篇》于屛，玆其章章較著也。其於古帝王所謂學者同乎？抑或華實異也？
translation_en:
Legal Judgments [Five Topics]:
Expounding and Reading the Statutes and Ordinances.
Evaluation of Prices by Market Officials.
Illicitly Bypassing or Fraudulently Passing Through Passes and Fords.
Deliberately Committing an Offense Upon Hearing of an Imperial Amnesty.
Administrative Officials and Functionaries Not Residing in Public Quarters.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents (Shu) sets forth constant devotion to learning, and the Book of Odes (Shi) sings of continuous bright diligence; even at the height of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties as recounted in the annals and biographies, rulers each had their own teachers and instruction. Therefore, among those who rule over men, there has never been one who did not exert himself in learning and yet was able to manifest himself in enlightened sageliness. In later ages, learning and scholarship fell into neglect, and the virtue of sovereigns rarely flourished. Occasionally there were those who delighted in drawing close to Confucian gentry and letting their minds roam among books and scrolls, which earlier histories treated as admirable tales: such as summoning scholars to lecture in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) and personally pronouncing imperial decisions thereon; lecturing on and discussing the principles of the Classics without sleeping past midnight; carefully selecting men of letters to take turns on night duty; ushering them in to discuss the words and deeds of antiquity, laying down the scrolls only after the hours from si [9–11 a.m.] to shen [3–5 p.m.] had passed; or inscribing the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) chapter of the Book of Documents upon a screen—these are the most strikingly evident examples. Are they the same as what the ancient emperors and kings called learning, or do they differ in outward splendor versus inner substance? …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上神聖天縱
鋭意進脩
卽位以來非隆冬盛夏不輟
講筵卽
端居
禁中亦日
親典籍無它嗜好雖高成不足侔矣顧帝王之
學非專事博雅爲名必有本始嘗觀我
太祖
===
成祖與儒臣論經術治理每推原於心體
世宗稡學甚盛而
敬一之箴學士大夫至今誦之玆非卓然與
唐虞三代同源合契者哉玆欲繩
祖武而纂
聖傳惟
聖天子已有定術顧揚厲
休美而因獻其矻矻之思以少佐
聖學之萬一則諸士烏得以不敏謝也其著于
punctuated: 皇上神聖天縱，鋭意進脩，卽位以來，非隆冬盛夏不輟講筵，卽端居禁中，亦日親典籍，無它嗜好，雖高、成不足侔矣。顧帝王之學，非專事博雅爲名，必有本始。嘗觀我太祖、成祖與儒臣論經術治理，每推原於心體；世宗稡學甚盛，而《敬一之箴》，學士大夫至今誦之，玆非卓然與唐、虞、三代同源合契者哉？玆欲繩祖武而纂聖傳，惟聖天子已有定術；顧揚厲休美，而因獻其矻矻之思，以少佐聖學之萬一，則諸士烏得以不敏謝也？其著于
translation_en: His Majesty is divinely sage and endowed by Heaven, keenly intent upon advancing his self-cultivation. Since ascending the throne, except in the dead of winter and the height of summer, he has not suspended the Classics Mat colloquia. Even when dwelling in formal repose within the Forbidden Palace, he daily familiarizes himself with the canonical texts and records, having no other pastimes; even Gaozong of Yin and King Cheng of Zhou are insufficient to match him. Yet the learning of emperors and kings is not merely a matter of pursuing broad erudition for the sake of reputation; it must have a fundamental root and origin. Consider how Our Taizu and Chengzu, in discussing classical statecraft and the principles of governance with their Confucian ministers, always traced them back to the substance of the mind; and how Shizong’s pure learning was exceedingly flourishing, such that his Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi zhi zhen) is recited by scholar-officials to this day. Are these not toweringly of the same source and in exact accord with Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? Now, in wishing to follow in the footsteps of the Imperial Ancestors and carry on the sage transmission, our Sage Son of Heaven already possesses an established method. Yet to extol this splendid excellence, and thereby offer up your diligent thoughts so as to assist, even in one part in ten thousand, the Sage Learning—how could you gentlemen decline on the grounds of lack of acuity? Set it forth…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
篇
問帝王保命凝圖於天人之際兢兢焉稽
古孰踰堯舜二典所載可鏡已三代而
後時亦有詔災異求直言與蠲租賑粟
者以文以實可指乎我
太祖順天應人再造寰宇考其求言之
詔或以五星並見或以七曜紊度而蠲賑之
令無歲不下何
敕天閔人之切也亦可揚厲之幷遡其本歟今
===
皇上
德茂中外
道洽華夷至盛也邇象緯失次至廑
下諭脩省都畿彌月不雨疫癘爲眚則又
躬自齋禱卽靈雨三應且不謂祥貺也更
命司農發帑賑卹惠藥以濟所疾苦覈民間積
逋盡蠲之春噓和洽咸用汔康此其
敬天勤民之心何如于
祖宗有相符否夫
punctuated:
篇。

問：帝王保命凝圖，於天人之際兢兢焉。稽古孰踰堯、舜？《二典》所載可鏡已。三代而後，時亦有詔災異、求直言，與蠲租賑粟者，以文、以實，可指乎？我太祖順天應人，再造寰宇。考其求言之詔，或以五星並見，或以七曜紊度；而蠲賑之令，無歲不下。何敕天閔人之切也！亦可揚厲之，幷遡其本歟？今皇上德茂中外，道洽華夷，至盛也。邇象緯失次，至廑下諭脩省；都畿彌月不雨，疫癘爲眚，則又躬自齋禱。卽靈雨三應，且不謂祥貺也，更命司農發帑賑卹，惠藥以濟所疾苦，覈民間積逋盡蠲之。春噓和洽，咸用汔康。此其敬天勤民之心何如？于祖宗有相符否？夫
translation_en:
…in your essays.

Question: In preserving the Mandate and consolidating their rule, emperors and kings have been cautiously reverent regarding the relationship between Heaven and humankind. When examining antiquity, who surpasses Yao and Shun? What is recorded in the Two Canons (Er dian) can serve as a mirror. After the Three Dynasties, there were also times when edicts were issued on account of natural disasters and anomalies to seek candid remonstrance, as well as to remit taxes and distribute grain in relief; can you point out which of these were done merely as a formality and which in true substance? Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), acting in accordance with Heaven and responding to the people, remade the realm. If we examine his edicts seeking counsel, some were prompted by the simultaneous appearance of the five planets, and others by the seven luminaries falling out of their regular courses; meanwhile, orders for tax remission and famine relief were handed down every single year. How earnest he was in heeding Heaven's admonitions and commiserating with the people! Can you also extol these deeds and trace them back to their fundamental root? Today, His Majesty's virtue flourishes both at court and in the provinces, and his Way permeates both Chinese and non-Chinese peoples—it is the pinnacle of prosperity. Recently, when the celestial bodies lost their regular order, he was so concerned as to issue an edict calling for self-cultivation and reflection; when the capital region went a full month without rain and epidemic disease brought calamity, he personally fasted and prayed. Even when auspicious rains responded three times, he still did not regard them as felicitous blessings; instead, he further ordered the Minister of Revenue (sinong) to disburse treasury funds for relief, bestowed medicine to succor those suffering from illness, and investigated the accumulated tax arrears among the people in order to remit them in full. Like the warm breath of spring bringing harmony, all were thereby brought to peace and recovery. What is the nature of this mind that reveres Heaven and labors diligently for the people? Does it tally with that of the Imperial Ancestors or not? Now,…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天心仁愛因象致儆今旣消弭之顧
當宁尤切切不置卽非
堯舜之心與諸士生斯世幸親見之豈無所攄
究以寬
宸懷萬分一執事者將轉以
聞
問太史公有言學者載籍極博猶考信於
六藝則周孔代降士之立言者第取諸
六藝足矣而何其說之多岐也漢初止
===
敘六家其後稍別爲九流而諸子肇編
則自周文有感於捕獸逐麋之對而師
事鬻子始也嗣是老莊競鶩而鬼谷鶡
冠子華野老靑史尉繚皆以子名紛紛
莫可究詰云漢成帝始令劉子政校讎
殺靑所紀凡百八十餘家視前滋侈矣
迨梁通事舍人復加品隲之爲說似核
然首稱諸子爲入道見志之書而大賢
若子輿氏亦臚列其內何比方失倫也
punctuated:
天心仁愛，因象致儆。今旣消弭之，顧當宁尤切切不置，卽非堯、舜之心與？諸士生斯世，幸親見之，豈無所攄究，以寬宸懷萬分一？執事者將轉以聞。

問：太史公有言：「學者載籍極博，猶考信於六藝。」則周、孔代降，士之立言者第取諸六藝足矣，而何其說之多岐也？漢初止敘六家，其後稍別爲九流；而諸子肇編，則自周文有感於捕獸逐麋之對而師事鬻子始也。嗣是老、莊競鶩，而鬼谷、鶡冠、子華、野老、靑史、尉繚皆以「子」名，紛紛莫可究詰云。漢成帝始令劉子政校讎殺靑，所紀凡百八十餘家，視前滋侈矣。迨梁通事舍人復加品隲之，爲說似核；然首稱諸子爲「入道見志之書」，而大賢若子輿氏亦臚列其內，何比方失倫也？
translation_en:
… Heaven's heart is benevolent and loving, using celestial phenomena to issue warnings. Even now that these calamities have been dispelled, the Emperor on the throne remains deeply and unceasingly concerned—is this not the very heart of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜? Living in this age and having the good fortune to witness this personally, how could you scholars have nothing to set forth from your inquiries so as to ease the imperial concern by even one part in ten thousand? The officiating examiners will transmit your words to the throne.

Question: The Grand Historian (Taishigong 太史公, Sima Qian 司馬遷) said: "Though written records for scholars are exceedingly vast, one must still verify their trustworthiness against the Six Arts (Liuyi 六藝)." Thus, as the ages descended from the Duke of Zhou 周公 and Confucius 孔子, for scholars who sought to establish their words, drawing solely upon the Six Arts should have sufficed; why then did their doctrines diverge into so many branches? At the beginning of the Han dynasty, only the Six Schools (liujia 六家) were recounted, which were later further distinguished into the Nine Streams (jiuliu 九流). Yet the earliest compilation of the Masters (zhuzi 諸子) began when King Wen of Zhou 周文王, moved by the reply concerning catching beasts and chasing elk, served Master Yu (Yuzi 鬻子) as his teacher. Thereafter, Laozi 老子 and Zhuangzi 莊子 vied in galloping forth, while Guiguzi 鬼谷子, Heguanzi 鶡冠子, Zihuazi 子華子, Yelao 野老, Qingshizi 青史子, and Weiliaozi 尉繚子 all took the title of "Master" (zi 子), proliferating in such confusion that they could scarcely be fully investigated. Emperor Cheng of Han 漢成帝 first ordered Liu Zizheng 劉子政 (Liu Xiang 劉向) to collate the texts on cured bamboo slips, recording in all more than one hundred and eighty schools—far more extravagant than before. Coming down to the Liang dynasty, the Drafter in the Palace Domestic Service (tongshi sheren 通事舍人, Liu Xie 劉勰) further evaluated and ranked them. His account seems precise; yet at the outset he praised the Masters as "books that enter into the Way and reveal personal aspirations," while even a great worthy such as Master Ziyu 子輿氏 (Mencius 孟子) was listed among them. Why was his comparison so out of order? …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
顧其說其人可詳述歟厥後齊丘文中
鹿門玄眞代有著述較前數子其說孰
為得也頃者士習浮誕為文或祖述老
莊靡曼不根之談數
下功令禁止至其覽華而食實棄邪而採正
不為彼說所誘奪則在其人自決擇何
如爾玆欲舉諸子而別以九流舉九流
而本諸六家要其歸務不詭於六藝其
究安在幸詳言之非第以徵博雅也
===
問古者司勳詔功祭于大烝為典凡六其
有道與德者使敎焉沒則以為樂祖而
祭于瞽宗次亦祠于社示不忘云玆名
宦鄕賢之所為祀也
明興立二祠于學宮歲二丁釋奠畢有司帥博
士弟子謁祠意義甚盛姑無暇遠引卽
以粵西舊牒所紀載者而尚論其世則
宦蹟自史祿而下百數十人其中則有
歌賈父來晚者有稱府君恩廣大者有
punctuated:
顧其說其人可詳述歟？厥後齊丘、文中、鹿門、玄眞代有著述，較前數子，其說孰為得也？頃者士習浮誕，為文或祖述老、莊靡曼不根之談，數下功令禁止。至其覽華而食實，棄邪而採正，不為彼說所誘奪，則在其人自決擇何如爾。玆欲舉諸子而別以九流，舉九流而本諸六家，要其歸務不詭於六藝，其究安在？幸詳言之，非第以徵博雅也。

問：古者司勳詔功，祭于大烝，為典凡六；其有道與德者使敎焉，沒則以為樂祖而祭于瞽宗，次亦祠于社，示不忘云。玆名宦、鄕賢之所為祀也。明興，立二祠于學宮，歲二丁釋奠畢，有司帥博士弟子謁祠，意義甚盛。姑無暇遠引，卽以粵西舊牒所紀載者而尚論其世，則宦蹟自史祿而下百數十人，其中則有歌「賈父來晚」者，有稱「府君恩廣大」者，有
translation_en:
Yet can that doctrine and that man be recounted in detail? Thereafter, in successive eras there were writings by Master Qiqiu (齊丘子), Master Wenzhong (文中子), Master Lumen (鹿門子), and Master Xuanzhen (玄眞子); compared with the several masters mentioned before, which of their doctrines hit the mark? Lately the habits of scholars have grown superficial and extravagant; in composing essays, some model themselves on the ornate and baseless talk of Laozi and Zhuangzi, so that imperial regulations have repeatedly been handed down to prohibit it. As for beholding the blossoms while feeding on the fruit, casting aside the heterodox while adopting the orthodox, and not being seduced or carried away by those doctrines—that depends entirely on how a person makes his own choices. Now, if one wishes to take up the Various Masters and classify them into the Nine Streams, and take up the Nine Streams and trace them back to the Six Schools, ensuring that their ultimate aim does not deviate from the Six Arts, wherein lies the key? Please set this forth in detail, not merely to display broad learning and elegance.

Question: In antiquity, the Director of Merits (司勳) proclaimed meritorious achievements to be sacrificed to at the great winter sacrifice (大烝), for which there were six categories in the canons; those who possessed the Way and virtue were employed to teach, and when they died they were honored as Patriarchs of Music and sacrificed to in the Blind Musicians' Hall (瞽宗), or, next to that, enshrined at the local altar of the soil, so as to show that they were not forgotten. Such is the origin of the sacrifices to Eminent Officials (名宦) and Local Worthies (鄉賢). With the rise of the Ming, the two shrines were established within the Confucian school compounds; each year, after the shidian (釋奠) sacrifice on the two ding days is concluded, the authorities lead the erudites and students to pay homage at the shrines—an institution of most exalted significance. Leaving aside distant examples for the moment, if we simply take what is recorded in the old registers of Guangxi (粵西) and evaluate those figures in the context of their times, the officials of notable achievement from Shi Lu (史祿) downward number well over a hundred. Among them was one of whom the people sang, "Father Jia came late," one whose "Grace of the Prefectural Governor" was praised as vast and great, one who…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
便宜活萬夫者有恩信被異域者此其
彪然較著也獻民自陳元而下亦百數
人則有士依避難者有再試及第而高
遯者有抵營諭賊使順歸者有去邕州
而人思之如一日者亦其彪然較著也
可具述歟頃者積漸滋濫
天子
令禮臣覆言官疏
下郡國釐正之至斤斤矣顧典籍廢缺靡所
===
考鏡故有列祀者未必皆名賢而名且
賢者會不得以希俎豆之餘芬與庶民
無異甚非所以重盛典章往而勸來也
茲欲精覈而慎擇之務令祀必當其實
毋徇世俗為低昂其道何繇願悉心言
之以觀嚮往
問聖人養天下在田賦為貢為助為徹其
法在正經界心至均也三代下田不皆
在官故有限有均有永業為塞兼并計
punctuated:
便宜活萬夫者，有恩信被異域者，此其彪然較著也。獻民自陳元而下亦百數人，則有士依避難者，有再試及第而高遯者，有抵營諭賊使順歸者，有去邕州而人思之如一日者，亦其彪然較著也。可具述歟？頃者積漸滋濫，天子令禮臣覆言官疏，下郡國釐正之，至斤斤矣。顧典籍廢缺，靡所考鏡，故有列祀者未必皆名賢，而名且賢者會不得以希俎豆之餘芬，與庶民無異，甚非所以重盛典、章往而勸來也。茲欲精覈而慎擇之，務令祀必當其實，毋徇世俗為低昂，其道何繇？願悉心言之，以觀嚮往。

問：聖人養天下在田賦，為貢、為助、為徹，其法在正經界，心至均也。三代下，田不皆在官，故有限、有均、有永業，為塞兼并計
translation_en:
… acted on his own authority as expedient to save the lives of ten thousand men, and one whose kindness and good faith extended to foreign lands—these are the ones who are brilliantly conspicuous. Of model local worthies, from Chen Yuan 陳元 on down there are also a hundred or so: among them were one upon whom scholars relied to take refuge from turmoil, one who twice passed the examinations at the top tier and yet loftily withdrew into seclusion, one who went straight to the rebels' camp to admonish them and make them submit in allegiance, and one who left Yongzhou 邕州 and whom the people longed for as if it had been but a single day—these too are the ones who are brilliantly conspicuous. Can you recount them in full? Recently, over time, the selections have become increasingly indiscriminate. The Son of Heaven ordered the officials of the Ministry of Rites to review the memorials of the speaking officials and send instructions down to the commanderies and principalities to rectify the matter, showing the utmost discernment. Yet because records and books have fallen into ruin and are incomplete, there is nothing by which to examine and verify the past. Consequently, some of those enrolled for sacrifice are not necessarily all eminent or worthy, while some who were truly eminent and worthy happen to have no hope of sharing even the lingering fragrance of the sacrificial vessels, being no different from the common people. This is very far from the way to honor a grand institution, illuminate the past, and encourage the future. Now, if we wish to investigate thoroughly and select carefully, ensuring that the sacrifices always match reality and do not follow vulgar opinion in raising or lowering people's standing, by what way can this be achieved? I hope you will speak of this with all your heart, so that we may observe your aspirations.

Question: The sages nourished the world through land and taxes, instituting the tribute (gong 貢), aid (zhu 助), and tithing (che 徹) systems; their method lay in rectifying the land boundaries, and their intention was the utmost equality. After the Three Dynasties, land did not all belong to the state; therefore there were the land-limitation (xian 限), equal-field (jun 均), and perpetual-holding (yongye 永業) systems, designed as measures to block land engrossment…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
耳其于古法得失何如承平日久詭灑
吞噬賦且混淆矣百姓苦之幸
天子神聖
下所司清丈天下莫不願觀化成緩須臾視
息也寧獨粤以西姑即粤以西清丈言
之古今墾業若干盈虧無定數能試屈
指否
憲式示所部則官履畝胥里執度罔不詳覈
敝源則平額復夙夜祗竣玆役矣第魚
===
鱗叢造舞弄抽移究詰爲難郡若縣長
吏少不慎偵之不無貽憂異日者否况
俠豪大家佃僕異種相藉避征稅久之
恐成厲階破壞良法以累蔀屋氓不淺
計坊之當何以重之人有遺力故地有
遺利將何以督成之地有可耕人無可
耕將何以招徠之猺獞非吾族類將何
以馴伏使回心疾耕以同齊民世酋負
固隱蓄將何以處置俾盡獻圖版以增
punctuated: 耳。其于古法得失何如？承平日久，詭灑吞噬，賦且混淆矣，百姓苦之。幸天子神聖，下所司清丈，天下莫不願觀化成，緩須臾視息也，寧獨粤以西？姑即粤以西清丈言之：古今墾業若干，盈虧無定數，能試屈指否？憲式示所部，則官履畝，胥里執度，罔不詳覈；敝源則平，額復，夙夜祗竣玆役矣。第魚鱗叢造，舞弄抽移，究詰爲難。郡若縣長吏少不慎偵之，不無貽憂異日者否？况俠豪大家、佃僕異種，相藉避征稅；久之，恐成厲階，破壞良法，以累蔀屋氓不淺。計坊之當何以重之？人有遺力，故地有遺利，將何以督成之？地有可耕，人無可耕，將何以招徠之？猺獞非吾族類，將何以馴伏，使回心疾耕，以同齊民？世酋負固隱蓄，將何以處置，俾盡獻圖版，以增
translation_en: … How do their merits and defects compare with the ancient methods? After a long period of peace, through fraudulent registration, tax-shifting, and predatory annexation, the land tax has become thoroughly confused, and the common people suffer from it. Fortunately, the Son of Heaven, in his divine sagacity, has ordered the competent authorities to conduct a cadastral resurvey. None in the realm does not wish to witness the completion of this transformation, lingering a moment longer to draw breath and see it—and how could this be true of Guangxi alone? Let us speak for now specifically of the cadastral survey in Guangxi: how much land has been brought under cultivation from ancient times to the present, with its increases and decreases having no fixed figure—can you try to reckon it on your fingers? Once the statutory models were proclaimed to the jurisdictions, officials paced the fields in person while clerks and village headmen held the measuring rods; nothing went unexamined in detail. The sources of abuse were leveled out, the quotas were restored, and working reverently day and night, they have brought this task to completion. Yet when the fish-scale registers are compiled in dense multitude, fraudulent manipulation, extraction, and shifting of entries are hard to investigate and expose. If the chief magistrates of prefectures and counties are even slightly careless in inspecting them, will this not leave behind troubles for a future day? Moreover, local bullies and powerful families, along with tenant-servants and non-Han peoples, rely on one another to evade tax levies; over time, it is to be feared this will become a source of disaster, ruining a sound law and imposing no small burden upon the humble folk in their thatched huts. In planning how to guard against [坊, for 防] this, how should we give it due weight? Where people have spare labor and the land consequently has untapped benefit, how shall we supervise and bring it to fruition? Where there is arable land but no people to till it, how shall we attract settlers to it? The Yao and Zhuang peoples are not of our kind; how shall we tame and pacify them so that they turn their hearts to diligent farming and become like the registered commoners? And where hereditary chieftains rely on their strongholds to conceal land and harbor populations, how shall we deal with them so that they submit all their maps and registers to increase…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國額夫必使土無曠民無游卽寸尺盡入貢
賦斯毋負於
聖人均天下之心也諸生首四民受廛或有慨
于中如漢文學論鹽鐵者其籌之
punctuated: 國額？夫必使土無曠、民無游，卽寸尺盡入貢賦，斯毋負於聖人均天下之心也。諸生首四民受廛，或有慨于中，如漢文學論鹽鐵者，其籌之。
translation_en: …the state's tax quota? Indeed, only when we ensure that no land is left uncultivated and no people are left idle, so that every inch and foot of land is brought into tribute and taxation, will we not fail the Sage's intention of bringing equitable distribution to all under Heaven. You students stand at the head of the four classes of people and occupy dwellings in the realm; perhaps some among you feel a deep concern in your hearts, like the Literary Scholars of the Han dynasty who debated salt and iron—pray devise your plans for this.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰辭達而已矣
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批以精邃之識發爲易簡之
詞務去陳言還歸大雅非子誰可語達者宜冠多士
考試官敎諭賈批理致雋永
考試官敎諭汪批辭意精雅
聖人示脩辭者不以文勝焉蓋辭之所脩意之
===
所寓也意達而辭斯善矣奚取於文之勝哉夫
子之意若曰自世之不能忘言而以言者尚其
辭勢也君子所不廢也然是辭也豈簡要之莫
崇而以其浮者示天下抑典則之不貴而以其
華者炫天下哉吾知未有辭先有意而意所以
主乎其辭既有音斯有辭而辭不過宣乎其意
立訓者意將以明道也能闡揚其蘊使可明徵
止耳此而繁華務焉無乃晦道乎非所以明吉
人之辭寡也陳謨者意將以經世也能敷布其
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「子曰：『辭達而已矣。』」
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批：以精邃之識，發爲易簡之詞，務去陳言，還歸大雅。非子誰可語達者？宜冠多士。
考試官敎諭賈批：理致雋永。
考試官敎諭汪批：辭意精雅。

聖人示脩辭者，不以文勝焉。蓋辭之所脩，意之所寓也。意達而辭斯善矣，奚取於文之勝哉？夫子之意若曰：自世之不能忘言，而以言者尚其辭，勢也，君子所不廢也。然是辭也，豈簡要之莫崇，而以其浮者示天下？抑典則之不貴，而以其華者炫天下哉？吾知未有辭先有意，而意所以主乎其辭；既有音斯有辭，而辭不過宣乎其意。立訓者，意將以明道也，能闡揚其蘊，使可明徵止耳。此而繁華務焉，無乃晦道乎？非所以明吉人之辭寡也。陳謨者，意將以經世也，能敷布其
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"The Master said: 'In words, it is simply enough that they convey the meaning.'" (Analects 15.41)
Tan Rushi 譚汝試
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭: From a refined and profound insight, he brings forth easy and simple expressions, striving to cast off trite phrases and return to great elegance. If not with you, with whom could one speak of conveying meaning? He deserves to crown the multitude of scholars.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia 賈: Its reasoning and flavor are rich and enduring.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang 汪: Both the words and the meaning are refined and elegant.

The Sage instructed those who cultivate their words not to let literary ornament prevail. For that by which words are cultivated is where the meaning resides. Once the meaning is conveyed, the words are thereby good; what need is there for literary ornament to prevail? The Master's meaning is as if to say: Ever since the world could no longer do without speech, those who speak have valued their words—this is the natural tendency of things, and something the gentleman does not abolish. Yet as for these words, how could one fail to revere conciseness and essentials, and instead display superficiality to the world? Or how could one fail to prize canonical standards, and instead dazzle the world with floridness? I know that before there are words, there is first meaning, and meaning is what governs the words; once there is meaning [reading 音 as 意][?], there are then words, and words do no more than declare that meaning. Those who establish teachings intend thereby to illuminate the Way; if they can expound its deeper significance so that it can be clearly verified, they stop there. If beyond this they pursue luxuriant ornament, would that not obscure the Way? That is not the way to illustrate how the auspicious man uses few words. Those who set forth counsels intend thereby to order the world; if they can set out their…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旨使足承聽止耳此而藻飾加焉無乃誇世乎
非所以昭君子之論篤也蓋心聲吐露其自然
而然也既有得於易簡之理而意趣流通有不
文而文者又安取乎枝葉之盛近而遠約而盡
吾以為世之脩辭者不當如是耶吁斯言也夫
亦感時之文勝而挽之質也然非聖人意也四
時行百物生方欲與天相忘於言而又何辭之
為辭之勝聖人之憂也憂之而身示之觀其所
刪述筆削而聖人之辭可知矣獨奈何風之愈
===
下其說滋長而夫子之憂滋甚也
脩道之謂教道也者不可須臾離也
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批體格渾成語意融徹講不
可離處尤親切有味非邃養者不能
考試官教諭賈批理貫詞暢
考試官教諭汪批善發題旨
中庸論道脩于教而切于人也夫道於人固甚
切也聖人之教脩此耳而入教者可離道哉且
punctuated:
旨，使足承聽止耳。此而藻飾加焉，無乃誇世乎？非所以昭君子之論篤也。蓋心聲吐露，其自然而然也。既有得於易簡之理，而意趣流通，有不文而文者，又安取乎枝葉之盛？近而遠，約而盡，吾以為世之脩辭者，不當如是耶？吁！斯言也，夫亦感時之文勝，而挽之質也。然非聖人意也。四時行，百物生，方欲與天相忘於言，而又何辭之為？辭之勝，聖人之憂也。憂之而身示之，觀其所刪述筆削，而聖人之辭可知矣。獨奈何風之愈下，其說滋長，而夫子之憂滋甚也！

脩道之謂教，道也者，不可須臾離也。
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批：體格渾成，語意融徹。講不可離處，尤親切有味，非邃養者不能。
考試官教諭賈批：理貫詞暢。
考試官教諭汪批：善發題旨。

中庸論道脩于教而切于人也。夫道於人固甚切也，聖人之教，脩此耳，而入教者可離道哉？且
translation_en:
… purport, making it sufficient to be heeded and nothing more. If beyond this one adds ornate embellishments, is it not boasting to the world? This is not the way to manifest the earnestness of a gentleman's discourse. Indeed, the utterance of the voice of the mind is something that happens naturally of itself. Once one has grasped the principle of ease and simplicity, and one's meaning and intent flow smoothly, there is a literary quality without deliberate adornment—what need is there for an abundance of branches and leaves? Near yet reaching far, concise yet exhaustive—do I not think that those in the world who cultivate their words ought to be like this? Alas! These words were spoken because he was moved by the triumph of floridness over substance in his time and sought to draw it back to plainness. Yet even this was not the sage's ultimate wish. The four seasons proceed, the hundred things are generated; he wished rather to join Heaven in forgetting words altogether—so what need would there be for rhetoric at all? The triumph of rhetoric was the sage's sorrow. Sorrowing over it, he demonstrated the way in his own person: look at what he edited, transmitted, wrote, and excised, and the sage's use of words can be known. Yet how could it be helped that as customs declined ever further, such theories grew ever more rampant, and the Master's sorrow grew ever deeper!

"Cultivating the Way is called instruction. As for the Way, it may not be left for an instant."
By Tao Mingli 陶明禮.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Ding comments: The structure is seamlessly integrated, and the phrasing and meaning are thoroughly lucid. His discussion of how the Way cannot be left is especially intimate and rich in flavor; none without deep cultivation could achieve this.
Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: The reasoning is coherent and the diction fluent.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Adept at bringing out the import of the topic.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) discusses how the Way is cultivated through instruction and is intimately relevant to human beings. Now, the Way is indeed most intimate to human beings. The instruction of the sages merely cultivates this; how then could those who enter into instruction depart from the Way? Moreover, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夫性命合而聖人之道易明也其爲敎亦易行
也第人不知敎之所由名則以爲道之不甚切
耳孰知聖人之設敎非離道者也卽所爲道而
脩之聖人之脩道非强世者也因所固有而裁
之稟氣異矣而命則同惟本其命于天者一品
節焉皇極所以建也賦質殊矣而性則一惟緣
其率於性者一裁成焉物軌所以彰也斯則聖
人之敎不離乎道也而是道也獨可離乎人哉
吾知此理此身其相須焉甚切而一動一靜卽
===
頃刻不可違道寓於物其紛然散殊者皆道也
吾不能離物乃離道乎卽離之須臾不可也道
行於時其沛然流行者皆道也吾不能離時乃
離道乎卽離之須臾不可也故由其不可離者
而脩之聖人之所爲敎也從其不可離者而入
之君子所以體聖人之敎也而天人性命將一
以貫之矣嗟乎道無古今聖愚一也彼聖人所
以參贊位育而成敎焉者豈其運用有殊絕哉
亦吾性道中故物耳君子誠密其功于須臾則
punctuated: 夫性命合，而聖人之道易明也，其爲敎亦易行也。第人不知敎之所由名，則以爲道之不甚切耳。孰知聖人之設敎，非離道者也，卽所爲道而脩之；聖人之脩道，非强世者也，因所固有而裁之。稟氣異矣，而命則同，惟本其命于天者一品節焉，皇極所以建也；賦質殊矣，而性則一，惟緣其率於性者一裁成焉，物軌所以彰也。斯則聖人之敎，不離乎道也，而是道也，獨可離乎人哉？吾知此理此身，其相須焉甚切，而一動一靜，卽頃刻不可違。道寓於物，其紛然散殊者，皆道也，吾不能離物，乃離道乎？卽離之須臾，不可也。道行於時，其沛然流行者，皆道也，吾不能離時，乃離道乎？卽離之須臾，不可也。故由其不可離者而脩之，聖人之所爲敎也；從其不可離者而入之，君子所以體聖人之敎也，而天人性命，將一以貫之矣。嗟乎！道無古今，聖愚一也。彼聖人所以參贊位育而成敎焉者，豈其運用有殊絕哉？亦吾性道中故物耳。君子誠密其功于須臾，則
translation_en:
…when human nature and the Heavenly endowment are united, the Way of the sage is easy to understand, and his instruction is likewise easy to practice. Yet when people do not understand the reason why instruction is so named, they suppose that the Way is not very relevant to them. Who realizes that when the sage establishes instruction, he does not depart from the Way, but simply regulates that which constitutes the Way; and when the sage regulates the Way, he does not force anything upon the world, but simply tailors what is already inherent in it?

Endowments of vital force differ, yet the Heavenly mandate is the same; only by taking what is mandated by Heaven as the basis and giving it uniform grade and measure is the Supreme Standard established. Physical constitutions vary, yet human nature is one; only by following what is led by human nature and giving it uniform regulation and completion are the norms of things made manifest. Thus the instruction of the sage does not depart from the Way; and can this Way alone be separated from man?

I know that this principle and this person depend upon each other most intimately, and in every movement and every moment of stillness, it cannot be violated even for an instant. The Way resides in things, and all their manifold, scattered particularities are the Way; since I cannot separate myself from things, how could I separate myself from the Way? Even to leave it for an instant is impossible. The Way operates through time, and all its abundant, flowing currents are the Way; since I cannot separate myself from time, how could I separate myself from the Way? Even to leave it for an instant is impossible. Therefore, to regulate it on the basis of what cannot be left is what constitutes the sage's instruction; to enter into it by following what cannot be left is how the noble man embodies the sage's instruction, and Heaven and man, human nature and the Heavenly mandate, will thereby be bound together by a single thread.

Alas! The Way knows no ancient or modern; for sage and fool it is one. As for that whereby the sage assists in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth, brings about order and flourishing, and so completes his instruction—how could its operation be something extraordinarily remote? It is nothing more than what originally belongs to our own nature and the Way. If the noble man truly makes his effort dense and unceasing in every passing instant, then…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盡性至命而德業將上下同流何聖人之不若
也故曰下學極功卽上達能事
舜何人也予何人也有爲者亦若是
劉祖堯
同考試官訓導張批認理精切而復力洗時套
字字皆有根據是亦見道之言
同考試官教諭王批命意渾融措詞剴切蓋有
希顏之志者錄之
考試官教諭賈批精鍊非苟作者
===
考試官教諭汪批整潔可誦
觀大賢希聖之言而道一足徵矣甚矣聖人無
異於人也有爲舜而舜不可爲哉此顏子見道
之言也而孟子引以告滕文公若曰古今聖賢
一道也舜以是受之堯顏淵以是希乎舜者也
其言不云乎舜作千載之上今之稱舜必曰聖
人也其去予也遠矣予生千載之後人之謂予
必曰鄉人也其去舜也遠矣然自予觀之舜卽
至德人耳舜何人也回雖不敏亦人耳予何人
punctuated:
盡性至命，而德業將上下同流，何聖人之不若也？故曰：下學極功，卽上達能事。

舜何人也？予何人也？有爲者亦若是。
劉祖堯
同考試官訓導張批：認理精切，而復力洗時套，字字皆有根據，是亦見道之言。
同考試官教諭王批：命意渾融，措詞剴切，蓋有希顏之志者。錄之。
考試官教諭賈批：精鍊，非苟作者。
考試官教諭汪批：整潔可誦。

觀大賢希聖之言，而道一足徵矣。甚矣，聖人無異於人也！有爲舜而舜不可爲哉？此顏子見道之言也，而孟子引以告滕文公，若曰：古今聖賢，一道也；舜以是受之堯，顏淵以是希乎舜者也。其言不云乎：「舜作千載之上，今之稱舜，必曰『聖人也，其去予也遠矣』。予生千載之後，人之謂予，必曰『鄉人也，其去舜也遠矣』。然自予觀之，舜卽至德，人耳，舜何人也？回雖不敏，亦人耳，予何人
translation_en:
… exhaust his nature and reach the decree of Heaven, and his virtue and achievements will flow in harmony with Heaven above and Earth below; how would he be anything less than a sage? Therefore it is said: the ultimate effort of learning here below is itself the capable work of penetrating upward.

"What kind of man was Shun? What kind of man am I? Anyone who makes the effort can also be like this."
By Liu Zuyao 劉祖堯.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Zhang comments: His grasp of principle is precise and incisive, and he vigorously washes away contemporary clichés. Every word is well-grounded; these too are words that manifest an understanding of the Way.
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: The conception of ideas is harmonious and integrated, and the phrasing is incisive and to the point. He is surely one who aspires to emulate Yan Yuan. Record it.
Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: Refined and polished; not the work of a careless writer.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Neat and worthy of recitation.

When we examine the words of a great worthy aspiring to sagehood, the oneness of the Way is amply attested. Indeed, how true it is that a sage is no different from other men! If one strives to be a Shun, how could one not become a Shun? These were the words of Master Yan (Yan Hui 顏回) upon perceiving the Way, and Mencius quoted them in speaking to Duke Wen of Teng, as if to say: Sages and worthies, ancient and modern, share a single Way. Through this, Shun received it from Yao, and through this, Yan Yuan aspired to emulate Shun. Did his words not say: "Shun arose a thousand years ago; those who speak of Shun today must say, 'He was a sage; he is far removed from me indeed!' I was born a thousand years later; those who speak of me must say, 'He is an ordinary villager; he is far removed from Shun indeed!' Yet as I see it, even though Shun was of supreme virtue, he was simply a man—what kind of man was Shun? Though I, Hui, am not clever, I too am simply a man—what kind of man am I? …"

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也惟限以聖凡之見故視為二人而不知有必
為之心則實無難事倫物之明察非舜其獨知
也予以知者致知之及其知之一也舜何為
其不可為也仁義之安行非舜其殊行也予以
其行者果行之及其成功一也予何為其不舜
若也蓋惟精惟一之妙舜固以其無為者而繼
堯之統而此心此理之同予將以其有為者而
與舜同歸噫此顏子之所以希舜者也知舜之
可為而遡之堯其道一也道一而性善之旨愈
===
明矣世子疑吾言乎抑天有恒性厥賦惟均而
秉懿在民其好德一也惟是異端紛紛而世之
無志者不足以有為性道始為天下裂嗟夫為
舜則舜希顏而顏微孟氏之開示吾志固在也
而况性善之訓昭如也
易
聖人養賢以及萬民
劉祖堯
同考試官訓導張 批 養賢及民是聖人之善用
punctuated:
也？惟限以聖凡之見，故視為二人，而不知有必為之心，則實無難事。倫物之明察，非舜其獨知也；予以知者致知之，及其知之，一也。舜何為其不可為也？仁義之安行，非舜其殊行也；予以其行者果行之，及其成功，一也。予何為其不舜若也？蓋惟精惟一之妙，舜固以其無為者而繼堯之統；而此心此理之同，予將以其有為者而與舜同歸。噫！此顏子之所以希舜者也。知舜之可為，而遡之堯，其道一也。道一，而性善之旨愈明矣。世子疑吾言乎？抑天有恒性，厥賦惟均，而秉懿在民，其好德一也。惟是異端紛紛，而世之無志者不足以有為，性道始為天下裂。嗟夫！為舜則舜，希顏而顏。微孟氏之開示，吾志固在也，而况性善之訓昭如也。

易

「聖人養賢以及萬民。」

劉祖堯

同考試官訓導張批：養賢及民，是聖人之善用
translation_en:
… [What sort of person am I]? Only when one is limited by the view that separates the sage from the ordinary person does one regard the two as fundamentally different people, not realizing that if one possesses a mind determined to act, there is truly nothing difficult about it. Clear perception of human relationships and affairs is not something Shun alone knew; if I extend my knowledge through that which can be known, once I come to know it, it is one and the same. Why should Shun be impossible to become? Practicing benevolence and righteousness with ease is not a mode of conduct unique to Shun; if I resolutely carry out that which he practiced, once the achievement is complete, it is one and the same. Why should I not be like Shun? Indeed, in the subtlety of being refined and single-minded, Shun surely succeeded to the line of Yao through effortless non-action; yet because this mind and this principle are the same, through purposeful action I shall arrive at the same destination as Shun. Ah! This is how Master Yan aspired to become like Shun. Knowing that one can become like Shun, and tracing this back to Yao, the Way is one. Since the Way is one, the meaning of the goodness of human nature becomes all the clearer. Does the Heir Apparent doubt my words?

Moreover, Heaven bestows a constant nature, distributing it evenly, and the people hold fast to this admirable virtue, being one in their love of moral excellence. It is only because heterodox teachings have arisen in confusion, and those in the world who lack aspiration are unequal to purposeful action, that human nature and the Way have come to be torn apart across the realm. Alas! If one acts to become Shun, one becomes Shun; if one aspires to become Yan, one becomes Yan. Even without the revelations of Mencius, my aspiration would surely still be there—how much more so when the teaching that human nature is good shines so brightly!

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The sage nourishes the worthy and thereby reaches the myriad people."

By Liu Zuyao 劉祖堯.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang comments: Nourishing the worthy so as to reach the people is how the sage makes good use of…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其養處此作意旨瑩明發揮雅暢佳士
同考試官教諭王批剀琱追雅不厭咀嚼是易
義之最佳者
考試官教諭賈批文氣疏爽繳結尤有餘味
考試官教諭汪批詞簡而意足錄之
聖人養先于賢而所及者廣矣甚矣聖人善用
其養也因賢以及萬民其及不亦廣乎夫子傳
頤彖而極言之也意謂頤道之大非特天地之
于萬物也而聖人之于萬民亦有然者蓋聖人
===
欲舉萬民而養之者其心也不能盡萬民而自
養之者其勢也故愛不徧物而鼎養致隆必先
於仁賢之賚斯心有所寄而膏澤下究自弘乎
博施之恩吾為天下得人而推厚祿與賢者共
之由是容保無疆而民作康不必家賜人給而
賢者之施惠於民也皆吾惠也吾不以天下自
養而隆大烹以養乎賢者由是教思無窮而民
作乂不必家喻戶曉而賢者之導民於善也皆
吾善也是其始也為萬民而養賢君主其要臣
punctuated:
其養處。此作意旨瑩明，發揮雅暢，佳士。
同考試官教諭王批：剀琱追雅，不厭咀嚼，是《易》義之最佳者。
考試官教諭賈批：文氣疏爽，繳結尤有餘味。
考試官教諭汪批：詞簡而意足，錄之。

聖人養先于賢，而所及者廣矣。甚矣，聖人善用其養也！因賢以及萬民，其及不亦廣乎？夫子傳《頤·彖》而極言之也。意謂頤道之大，非特天地之于萬物也，而聖人之于萬民亦有然者。蓋聖人欲舉萬民而養之者，其心也；不能盡萬民而自養之者，其勢也。故愛不徧物，而鼎養致隆，必先於仁賢之賚；斯心有所寄，而膏澤下究，自弘乎博施之恩。吾為天下得人，而推厚祿與賢者共之；由是容保無疆，而民作康，不必家賜人給，而賢者之施惠於民也，皆吾惠也。吾不以天下自養，而隆大烹以養乎賢者；由是教思無窮，而民作乂，不必家喻戶曉，而賢者之導民於善也，皆吾善也。是其始也，為萬民而養賢，君主其要，臣
translation_en:
… his nourishment. In this piece, the meaning and purport are crystal clear, and the elaboration is refined and fluent. A fine scholar.
Associate Examiner Instructor Wang comments: Incisively crafted and pursuing elegance, one never tires of savoring it; it is the finest of the essays on the Book of Changes (Yijing).
Examiner Instructor Jia comments: The literary vitality is open and brisk, and the conclusion has a particularly lingering flavor.
Examiner Instructor Wang comments: The words are concise yet the meaning is complete; record it.

The sage places nourishment of the worthy first, and what it extends to is vast indeed! Truly, how well the sage employs his nourishment! Through the worthy, he reaches the myriad people—is not its reach vast indeed? The Master, in his Commentary on the Judgment (Tuanzhuan) of the "Nourishment" (Yi) hexagram, spoke of this to the utmost. His meaning is that the greatness of the Way of Nourishment lies not only in Heaven and Earth's relation to the myriad things, for the sage's relation to the myriad people is also like this. Indeed, to wish to take up all the myriad people and nourish them is the sage's heart; yet to be unable to exhaustively nourish all the myriad people in person is the reality of his situation. Therefore, his love does not directly cover every single thing, and in bestowing the highest sacrificial-cauldron nourishment, he must first direct his gifts to the benevolent and worthy; thus his heart has something to entrust itself to, and as rich blessings reach down to the bottom, the grace of broad bestowal naturally expands. "I obtain men for the sake of all under Heaven, and extend generous emoluments to share with the worthy; through this, tolerance and protection are boundless and the people are made peaceful—there is no need to bestow gifts on every family and supply every person, for the kindnesses that the worthy bestow upon the people are all my kindnesses. I do not use all under Heaven to nourish myself, but exalt the grand feast to nourish the worthy; through this, educational thought is inexhaustible and the people are made well-governed—there is no need to instruct every family and inform every household, for the goodness toward which the worthy guide the people is all my goodness." Thus, at the beginning, he nourishes the worthy for the sake of the myriad people: the ruler presides over the essentials, while the ministers …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
職其詳天下服聖人之智其旣也以賢人養萬
民臣效其勞君享其逸天下稱聖人之仁然則
聖人之盡民信與天地之盡物而同功矣順道
之大曷以加此抑論養賢固足以及民養民亦
足以致賢堯養舜矣而成敷治之功由上以達
下也文王養二老矣而獲鷹揚之佐由下以應
上也後世此禮闕而豐于自養或賢者未養所
養非賢宜仁民之政弗行也噫願道其可以弗
講哉
===
言行君子之所以動天地也可不愼乎
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批天人感通之理說得透徹
而格正詞瑩深於易者
同考試官教諭王批體裁整潔詞意渾融後段
發當愼意尤見警策讀之令人惕然
考試官教諭賈批詞旨融徹
考試官教諭汪批典雅明盡
大傳極言君子之言行通於造化而不可忽也
punctuated:
職其詳，天下服聖人之智；其旣也，以賢人養萬民，臣效其勞，君享其逸，天下稱聖人之仁。然則聖人之盡民，信與天地之盡物而同功矣！順道之大，曷以加此？抑論養賢固足以及民，養民亦足以致賢。堯養舜矣，而成敷治之功，由上以達下也；文王養二老矣，而獲鷹揚之佐，由下以應上也。後世此禮闕，而豐于自養，或賢者未養，所養非賢，宜仁民之政弗行也。噫！願道其可以弗講哉？

言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不愼乎？
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批：天人感通之理，說得透徹，而格正詞瑩，深於《易》者。
同考試官教諭王批：體裁整潔，詞意渾融，後段發當愼意，尤見警策，讀之令人惕然。
考試官教諭賈批：詞旨融徹。
考試官教諭汪批：典雅明盡。

《大傳》極言君子之言行通於造化，而不可忽也。
translation_en:
… attend to the details, and all under Heaven submit to the sage’s wisdom. In the end, he uses worthy men to nourish the myriad people: the ministers exert their labor while the ruler enjoys his ease, and all under Heaven praise the sage’s benevolence. Thus, the sage’s fulfillment of the people’s needs truly achieves the same merit as Heaven and Earth’s fulfillment of the myriad things! How could the greatness of the Way of Nourishment (Yi) be surpassed by anything? Moreover, while nourishing the worthy is certainly sufficient to reach the people, nourishing the people is also sufficient to attract the worthy. Yao nourished Shun and thereby accomplished the merit of spreading governance, reaching from above to below; King Wen nourished the two elders [Boyi and Taigong] and thereby obtained hawk-like, soaring assistants, responding from below to above. In later ages this ritual was neglected, and rulers were lavish in nourishing themselves; either the worthy were not nourished, or those nourished were not worthy, so it is no wonder that benevolent governance toward the people was not practiced. Alas! How could the Way of Nourishment [reading 頤 for 願?] not be studied?

"Words and deeds are that whereby the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. May one not be cautious?" [Book of Changes, "Appended Remarks," Part I]
By Xu Changzhao 徐昌兆.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Zhang comments: The principle of mutual resonance between Heaven and humanity is explained thoroughly, while the structure is upright and the diction lustrous—one who is profound in the Book of Changes.
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: The form is neat and clean, and the wording and meaning are harmoniously blended. The latter section, in bringing out the meaning of the need for caution, is especially incisive and alerting; reading it makes one feel a sense of awe.
Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: The diction and purport are harmoniously penetrating.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Classically elegant, clear, and exhaustive.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) speaks to the utmost of how the gentleman’s words and deeds communicate with the creative forces of nature, and therefore must not be neglected.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夫天地至大也而言行足以動之如之何其可
忽哉此夫子釋中孚爻義也意以為言行之在
人固甚微而其所感通則甚大樞機之發豈特
為榮辱之主已哉蓋無形無聲者天地也而其
應未甞不係於人心有言有為者君子也而其
感未始不通乎造化言行而善即居室之間天
地之和氣應焉蓋順吾心之理固所以順天地
之心而休徵之至惟善有以動之也言行而不
善即居室之間天地之戾氣應焉蓋逆吾心之
===
理固所以逆天地之心而咎徵之至惟不善有
以動之也夫一身之榮辱匪輕也而通極于造
化尤匪輕也千里之應違可畏也而感通于天
地尤可畏也言方出乎其身而休咎之徵隨之
此其所關之大雖擬之後言尤恐不足以當天
地之心也而可以弗慎乎行方發乎其邇而順
逆之氣因之此其所係之重雖議之後動尤恐
不足以召天地之和也而敢以弗慎乎吁觀是
人當擬議於中孚之爻矣雖然君子戒慎之心
punctuated: 夫天地至大也，而言行足以動之，如之何其可忽哉？此夫子釋《中孚》爻義也，意以為：言行之在人固甚微，而其所感通則甚大，樞機之發，豈特為榮辱之主已哉？蓋無形無聲者，天地也，而其應未甞不係於人心；有言有為者，君子也，而其感未始不通乎造化。言行而善，即居室之間，天地之和氣應焉，蓋順吾心之理，固所以順天地之心，而休徵之至，惟善有以動之也；言行而不善，即居室之間，天地之戾氣應焉，蓋逆吾心之理，固所以逆天地之心，而咎徵之至，惟不善有以動之也。夫一身之榮辱匪輕也，而通極于造化尤匪輕也；千里之應違可畏也，而感通于天地尤可畏也。言方出乎其身，而休咎之徵隨之，此其所關之大，雖擬之後言，尤恐不足以當天地之心也，而可以弗慎乎？行方發乎其邇，而順逆之氣因之，此其所係之重，雖議之後動，尤恐不足以召天地之和也，而敢以弗慎乎？吁！觀是，人當擬議於《中孚》之爻矣。雖然，君子戒慎之心，
translation_en: Now, Heaven and Earth are supremely vast, yet one's words and deeds are sufficient to move them—how then could they be neglected? This is the Master explaining the meaning of the line in the Zhongfu (Inner Trust) hexagram. The thought is that while words and deeds in a person are certainly very subtle, what they move and penetrate is immense; when the trigger and pivot are released, how could they merely be the master of honor and disgrace alone? For that which is without form and without sound is Heaven and Earth, yet their response never fails to be tied to the human mind; he who speaks and acts is the noble man, and the stimulus he provides never fails to communicate with the creative forces of nature. If one's words and deeds are good, then right within one's dwelling chamber the harmonious ether of Heaven and Earth responds to them; for to accord with the principle of one's own mind is inherently how one accords with the mind of Heaven and Earth, and the arrival of auspicious signs is moved solely by goodness. If one's words and deeds are not good, then right within one's dwelling chamber the perverse ether of Heaven and Earth responds to them; for to go against the principle of one's own mind is inherently how one goes against the mind of Heaven and Earth, and the arrival of inauspicious signs is moved solely by what is not good. Now, the honor or disgrace of one's own person is no light matter, yet communicating all the way to the creative forces of nature is even less a light matter; agreement or opposition from a thousand li away is to be feared, yet moving and communicating with Heaven and Earth is even more to be feared. No sooner do words issue from one's person than auspicious or inauspicious signs follow them; so great is what hinges on this that even if one deliberates before speaking, one still fears it may be insufficient to match the mind of Heaven and Earth—so how could one fail to be cautious? No sooner do deeds issue from what is near at hand than harmonious or adverse ethers arise from them; so weighty is what is tied to this that even if one discusses before acting, one still fears it may be insufficient to summon the harmony of Heaven and Earth—so how could one dare to be incautious? Alas! Seeing this, a person ought to deliberate and discuss upon the line of the Zhongfu hexagram. Even so, the noble man's mind of apprehensive caution…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以獲底績之休二公之所爲于此有全能矣事
若相反而且道實相成東郊之治不得公而有終
耶此固公之所必克者也予小子何幸得仰其
成哉嗟夫頑民蕞爾何至煩師保更治歷三紀
而猶廑成終之慮豈過計歟夷攷其時賢聖繼
作君臣同德以苞覆含生其廣大眞如天地非
所謂必世後仁者哉姒籙之長信非偶矣彼以
小康自足者視此何如
詩
===
受祿于天保右命之自天申之干祿百福
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
楊允京
同考試官教諭梁 批 體莊詞整而過繳處尤雋
永有味忠愛之忱藹然宜錄以式
考試官教諭賈 批 詞旨典雅不著一閒語
考試官教諭汪 批 醇潔可錄
天之眷君有常而徵于後嗣之多賢焉夫天心
仁愛惟君也以有常之眷而得子孫之多賢君
punctuated:
以獲底績之休，二公之所爲，于此有全能矣。事若相反，而且道實相成，東郊之治，不得公而有終耶？此固公之所必克者也，予小子何幸得仰其成哉！嗟夫！頑民蕞爾，何至煩師保更治，歷三紀而猶廑成終之慮，豈過計歟？夷攷其時，賢聖繼作，君臣同德，以苞覆含生，其廣大眞如天地，非所謂「必世後仁」者哉？姒籙之長，信非偶矣，彼以小康自足者，視此何如？

詩

「受祿于天，保右命之，自天申之。干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。」
楊允京
同考試官教諭梁批：體莊詞整，而過繳處尤雋永有味，忠愛之忱藹然，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭賈批：詞旨典雅，不著一閒語。
考試官教諭汪批：醇潔可錄。

天之眷君有常，而徵于後嗣之多賢焉。夫天心仁愛，惟君也；以有常之眷，而得子孫之多賢，君
translation_en:
… so as to attain the blessing of bringing the work to fruition; what the two Dukes accomplished would herein achieve complete perfection. Their methods seemed opposite, yet their Way was actually complementary; will the governance of the eastern outskirts not find its completion through you, Duke? This is assuredly what the Duke is certain to accomplish, and how fortunate am I, the Little Child, to look up to its fulfillment! Alas! Those recalcitrant people were but a tiny remnant—why should they have required the Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian to govern them in turn, and after three decades still evoke anxiety over bringing the work to a final close? Was this excessive calculation? Yet when we calmly examine that era, worthies and sages arose in succession, and ruler and ministers were of one virtue in embracing and sheltering all living beings. Their vastness truly resembled heaven and earth—was this not what is meant by "after a generation, benevolence will prevail"? The longevity of the Zhou mandate [note: written 姒籙 "Xia mandate" in error for 姬籙] was truly no accident. How do those who are content with mere Lesser Tranquility compare to this?

Book of Odes (Shijing)

"He receives blessings from Heaven; It protects, aids, and mandates him, and from Heaven renews them. In seeking emolument he receives a hundred blessings; his sons and grandsons are a hundred million. Reverent and august, fit to be sovereign, fit to be king."

By Yang Yunjing 楊允京.

Associate Examiner and Director of Studies Liang 梁 comments: The structure is dignified and the diction neat, while the transitions and conclusions are especially meaningful and rich in flavor. A spirit of loyal affection shines forth amiably; it is fitting to record this as a model.
Examiner and Director of Studies Jia 賈 comments: The diction and purport are classic and elegant, without a single superfluous word.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang 汪 comments: Pure and lucid; worthy of being recorded.

Heaven's favor toward the sovereign is constant, and is attested by the abundance of worthies among his descendants. Indeed, Heaven's heart of benevolent love rests solely upon the sovereign; through this constant favor, to obtain many worthies among his sons and grandsons—the sovereign …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲周家太平之盛而必推本于君德之茂知言
哉
成王不敢康夙夜基命宥密
項雲
同考試官教諭梁批發揮題意明徹而詞更雅
潔讀之洋洋然其太龢之音與
考試官教諭賈批詞葩而正善學詩者
考試官教諭汪批理明詞瑩
詩人頌賢王之保命惟勤以進德而已夫命基
===
于德也賢王存心之勤而積德之宥密也有由
哉頌成王者謂夫創業固難守成不易我周之
命受於二后矣成王繼之何如彼天命至重惟
德足以基之君德難成惟勤足以積之也故成
王也志切勵精而不安于成命之集心存無逸
而每勤於脩德之圖上宇之版章天所命也二
后勤勞以遺之我敢安居以撫乎兢兢然自夜
而夙而積德以凝承之者無怠朝焉人心之攸
同天所命也二后憂勤以莅之我敢荒寧以肆
punctuated:
爲周家太平之盛，而必推本于君德之茂，知言哉！

成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。
項雲
同考試官教諭梁批：發揮題意明徹，而詞更雅潔。讀之洋洋然，其太龢之音與！
考試官教諭賈批：詞葩而正，善學《詩》者。
考試官教諭汪批：理明詞瑩。

詩人頌賢王之保命，惟勤以進德而已。夫命基于德也，賢王存心之勤，而積德之宥密也，有由哉！頌成王者，謂夫創業固難，守成不易。我周之命，受於二后矣，成王繼之何如？彼天命至重，惟德足以基之；君德難成，惟勤足以積之也。故成王也，志切勵精，而不安于成命之集；心存無逸，而每勤於脩德之圖。上宇之版章，天所命也，二后勤勞以遺之，我敢安居以撫乎？兢兢然自夜而夙，而積德以凝承之者，無怠朝焉；人心之攸同，天所命也，二后憂勤以莅之，我敢荒寧以肆…
translation_en:
…taking this as the flourishing peace of the House of Zhou, while necessarily tracing its root to the abundance of the ruler's virtue—how well he understands words!

"King Cheng did not dare to rest in comfort; morning and night he laid the foundation of the Mandate in deep and quiet virtue." [Book of Odes, Zhou song, "Hao Tian you cheng ming"]
Xiang Yun 

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Liang: It brings out the meaning of the theme with clarity and penetration, and its diction is even more elegant and pure. Reading it, how expansive and grand—is it not the sound of Great Harmony!
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia: The diction is ornate yet upright; one who is skilled in studying the Odes (Shi).
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: The principle is clear and the diction is lustrous.

The poet praises the worthy king's preservation of the Mandate Simply through diligence in advancing his virtue. Now, the Mandate has its foundation in virtue; that the worthy king was diligent in preserving his mind, so that the accumulation of his virtue was deep and quiet—there was indeed a reason for it! The one who praised King Cheng meant to say: founding a dynastic enterprise is certainly difficult, and maintaining an established achievement is not easy. The Mandate of our Zhou was received by the Two Sovereigns [Kings Wen and Wu]; how did King Cheng succeed to it? That Mandate of Heaven is supremely weighty, and only virtue is sufficient to lay its foundation; the ruler's virtue is difficult to bring to completion, and only diligence is sufficient to accumulate it. Therefore, as for King Cheng, his ambition was earnest in rousing his spirit, and he did not rest complacent in the settling of the established Mandate; his mind abided in "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wu yi), and he was ever diligent in plans for cultivating virtue. The vast territory of the upper realm is what Heaven mandated; the Two Sovereigns labored diligently to bequeath it—dare I dwell in ease while soothing it? Cautiously and warily, from night until morning, accumulating virtue so as to consolidate and uphold it, there was no negligent morning. The solidarity of human hearts is what Heaven mandated; the Two Sovereigns presided over them with anxious diligence—dare I indulge in idle tranquility and…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乎凜凜然自夙而夜而積德以憑藉之者無怠
夕焉德有以宥爲貴者茲愈操存則愈光大日
見其宏以深而溥將之命此其容受之有基矣
德有以密爲貴者茲愈涵養則愈精微日見其
靜以密而於穆之命此其凝聚之有基矣惟成
王匪康之心方切乎泮渙之慮而要成王積德
之素則已造于宥密之純夫是以能保成命而
與二后竝稱也嘗考訪落敬之諸篇成王力學
者至矣而無逸之書七月之咏周召啓迪不啻
===
詳焉德躋宥密豈自致哉後之守成者將若何
亦曰脩德要矣親賢急焉
春秋
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳 批 發平詞意甚明而語復莊
重可式
考試官教諭賈 批 簡勁無一浮語
考試官教諭汪 批 意精詞妥
punctuated:
乎？凜凜然自夙而夜，而積德以憑藉之者，無怠夕焉。德有以宥爲貴者，茲愈操存則愈光大，日見其宏以深，而溥將之命，此其容受之有基矣；德有以密爲貴者，茲愈涵養則愈精微，日見其靜以密，而於穆之命，此其凝聚之有基矣。惟成王匪康之心，方切乎泮渙之慮，而要成王積德之素，則已造于宥密之純，夫是以能保成命而與二后竝稱也。嘗考《訪落》、《敬之》諸篇，成王力學者至矣；而《無逸》之書、《七月》之咏，周、召啓迪不啻詳焉。德躋宥密，豈自致哉？後之守成者將若何？亦曰脩德要矣，親賢急焉。

《春秋》
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳批：發平詞意甚明，而語復莊重，可式。
考試官教諭賈批：簡勁，無一浮語。
考試官教諭汪批：意精詞妥。
translation_en:
… over them? With trembling awe from morning until night, he accumulated virtue on which to rely, without a single evening of laxity. In virtue, there is that which takes breadth as precious; here, the more he preserved and held fast to it, the more glorious and great it became, daily seen to be vast and deep, so that for the廣泛 and great Mandate, here was the foundation for receiving and containing it. In virtue, there is that which takes profundity as precious; here, the more he nurtured it, the more refined and subtle it became, daily seen to be tranquil and profound, so that for the august and solemn Mandate, here was the foundation for condensing and consolidating it. While King Cheng’s mind, never indulging in ease, was just then keenly anxious about dispersion and laxity, in sum his constant accumulation of virtue had already reached the pure perfection of breadth and profundity. That is why he was able to preserve the settled Mandate and be praised alongside the Two Sovereigns. If we examine such odes as "Fang luo" (Taking Counsel at the Beginning) and "Jing zhi" (Be Reverent), King Cheng’s strenuous devotion to learning was utmost indeed; yet in the document "Wu yi" (Against Luxurious Ease) and the song "Qi yue" (The Seventh Month), the instruction and guidance of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao were nothing less than thorough. How could his virtue have ascended to breadth and profundity all by itself? What then should later rulers who maintain an established order do? It is simply this: cultivating virtue is essential, and staying close to the worthy is urgent.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In summer, the Earl of Shan joined in invading Song." (Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang)
Peng Ziguang
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen: It brings out the meaning of the plain wording very clearly, and the language is moreover grave and dignified; it can serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia: Concise and vigorous, without a single superficial word.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: The ideas are refined and the diction is apt.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
經於內臣從霸之兵而平詞以紀之焉此單伯
之會師以臨宋其兵爲有名矣所以免於貶乎
且單伯曷爲會伐宋也偕陳曹以從齊討宋之
貳也則宜從再序之例矣而經平詞紀之者何
蓋兵之動也惟揆諸義揆諸義而弗協則主者
與從者皆比也揆諸義而協則主者與從者皆
正也玆三國之伐果若東門求寵乎哉迺單伯
之行非子羽請兵者類矣比杏有會宋寔奸之
魯爲人望正所需于協謀討貳者何可以弗會
===
耶睢陽有伐齊實倡之魯爲鄰壤正所亟于同
心翼霸者又何嫌於會耶內遣上卿悉敝賦以
共濟非從齊也從攘夷之義也外聯陳曹見眾
志之僉同非比桓也比尊王之霸也天下未有
議桓之伐宋者其可議單伯之會伐乎故春秋
直書單伯會伐若曰宋無惡於伐則無惡於會
矣故平詞以紀之如此不然胡不與再序四國
者同書哉知此而翼戴尊攘之義明矣嗟夫此
聖人不得已之意也是時列國上卿尚知請命
punctuated:
經於內臣從霸之兵，而平詞以紀之焉。此單伯之會師以臨宋，其兵爲有名矣，所以免於貶乎！

且單伯曷爲會伐宋也？偕陳、曹以從齊，討宋之貳也，則宜從再序之例矣，而經平詞紀之者，何？蓋兵之動也，惟揆諸義。揆諸義而弗協，則主者與從者皆比也；揆諸義而協，則主者與從者皆正也。玆三國之伐，果若東門求寵乎哉？迺單伯之行，非子羽請兵者類矣。比杏有會，宋寔奸之；魯爲人望，正所需于協謀討貳者，何可以弗會耶？睢陽有伐，齊實倡之；魯爲鄰壤，正所亟于同心翼霸者，又何嫌於會耶？內遣上卿，悉敝賦以共濟，非從齊也，從攘夷之義也；外聯陳、曹，見眾志之僉同，非比桓也，比尊王之霸也。天下未有議桓之伐宋者，其可議單伯之會伐乎？故《春秋》直書「單伯會伐」，若曰：宋無惡於伐，則無惡於會矣。故平詞以紀之如此。不然，胡不與再序四國者同書哉？知此，而翼戴尊攘之義明矣。

嗟夫！此聖人不得已之意也。是時列國上卿尚知請命
translation_en:
When the Classic records an expedition in which an inner minister [of Lu] follows the troops of a hegemon, it does so with neutral wording. Thus, when Earl Shan (Shan Bo 單伯) joined the army to march against Song, the campaign had a legitimate cause—and is this not why he was spared censure?

Moreover, why did Earl Shan join in attacking Song? He went along with Chen and Cao to follow Qi in punishing Song's duplicity. By rights, this should have followed the precedent of listing the states a second time; why, then, did the Classic record it with neutral wording? For when troops are mobilized, one must measure the action solely against righteousness. If measured against righteousness it does not accord, then both the initiator and the followers are engaged in partisan collusion; if measured against righteousness it does accord, then both the initiator and the followers are acting uprightly. Was this punitive expedition by the three states truly like the campaign at the Eastern Gate (Dongmen 東門) [of郑 Zheng] aimed at currying favor? Accordingly, Earl Shan's mission was not of the same sort as Ziyu's (子羽, i.e.,公子翬 Gongzi Hui) requesting troops. Recently, there had been the covenant at Beixing (北杏), which Song in fact violated. As Lu was a state that others looked up to, it was precisely needed to join in counsels to punish the duplicitous—how could it not join the meeting? Now there was the attack on Suiyang (睢陽, capital of Song), which Qi in fact initiated. As Lu was a neighboring territory, it was urgently required to be of one mind in assisting the hegemon—what suspicion could there be in joining? Within, sending a senior minister with all our humble levies to aid the common cause was not merely following Qi, but following the righteous duty of repelling the barbarians; without, allying with Chen and Cao to show the unanimity of all wills was not partisan collusion with Duke Huan (Huan 桓), but aligning with a hegemon who revered the King. Since no one in the realm criticized Duke Huan's attack on Song, how could anyone criticize Earl Shan's joining the attack? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) straightforwardly writes, "Earl Shan joined in attacking," as if to say: since there was nothing objectionable in attacking Song, there was nothing objectionable in joining the expedition. Thus it recorded it in neutral wording like this. Otherwise, why would it not have been written in the same manner as the entry that lists the four states a second time? Understand this, and the righteous principles of assisting and upholding [the hegemon] to revere [the King] and repel [the barbarians] become clear.

Alas! This was the sage's reluctant intention. At that time, the senior ministers of the various states still knew to request investiture…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
于周自單伯女叔而後命卿無幾矣則五伯興
而侯度之日恣也噫不有齊桓則周室陵夷夷
狄强橫九鼎之問寧待定王時哉此聖人猶有
取於從覇之單伯也
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒〔成公九年〕秋楚公
子壬夫帥師侵宋〔襄公元年〕
蔣守浩
同考試官訓導陳批〔鄭無可救發揮詳悉而於〕
〔中敘事灑灑然令人喜讀〕
===
考試官敎諭賈批〔格調嚴整〕
考試官敎諭汪批〔旨明詞警〕
春秋兩削外救責貳國之昧義也夫從楚非義
也而鄭一溺於利一溺於惠亦奚取於楚之救
哉宜春秋削之也蓋嘗觀華夷之際矣象否泰
則外四夷者甚嚴審從違則入幽谷者必禁故
春秋於鄭之從楚每致謹焉彼嬰齊之伐莒非
以銅鞮故乎俘其君而戮其使於時蓋未有拯
伯蠲之難者而子重至焉宜簡書之急在是舉
punctuated:
于周。自單伯、女叔而後，命卿無幾矣，則五伯興而侯度之日恣也。噫！不有齊桓，則周室陵夷，夷狄强橫，九鼎之問，寧待定王時哉？此聖人猶有取於從覇之單伯也。

楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒〔成公九年〕。秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋〔襄公元年〕。
蔣守浩
同考試官訓導陳批：〔鄭無可救，發揮詳悉，而於〕〔中敘事灑灑然，令人喜讀。〕
考試官敎諭賈批：〔格調嚴整。〕
考試官敎諭汪批：〔旨明詞警。〕

《春秋》兩削外救，責貳國之昧義也。夫從楚非義也，而鄭一溺於利，一溺於惠，亦奚取於楚之救哉？宜《春秋》削之也。蓋嘗觀華夷之際矣：象否泰則外四夷者甚嚴，審從違則入幽谷者必禁。故《春秋》於鄭之從楚，每致謹焉。彼嬰齊之伐莒，非以銅鞮故乎？俘其君而戮其使，於時蓋未有拯伯蠲之難者，而子重至焉，宜簡書之急在是舉
translation_en:
… from Zhou. After Shan Bo 單伯 and Nü Shu 女叔, there were few ministers commissioned by the king; this was because as the Five Hegemons arose, the feudal lords grew daily more unbridled in violating their proper bounds. Alas! Had there been no Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓, the house of Zhou would have fallen into decline and the barbarian tribes grown powerful and rampant; would the inquiry after the weight of the Nine Tripods have waited until the time of King Ding 定王? This is why the Sage still found something to approve in Shan Bo’s following the hegemon.

"Gongzi Yingqi 嬰齊 of Chu led an army and attacked Ju" 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng 成公〕; "In autumn, Gongzi Renfu 壬夫 of Chu led an army and raided Song" 〔First year of Duke Xiang 襄公〕.
Jiang Shouhao 蔣守浩
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Chen 陳 comments: 〔That Zheng 鄭 did not deserve to be rescued is expounded in full detail, and within it the narration of events flows briskly, making it a delight to read.〕
Examiner, Instructor Jia 賈 comments: 〔The structure and style are rigorous and well-ordered.〕
Examiner, Instructor Wang 汪 comments: 〔The purport is clear and the diction incisive.〕
