When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) twice excised mention of foreign rescue, it was to censure a vacillating state for being blind to righteousness. Now, following Chu is unrighteous; yet Zheng 鄭 once drowned itself in profit and once drowned itself in favor—what was there to approve in Chu’s rescuing it? Rightly did the Annals excise it! I have observed the boundary between Chinese and barbarian: in figuring the hexagrams Obstruction (Pi 否) and Peace (Tai 泰), keeping the four barbarian tribes on the outside is most strict; in judging whom to follow and whom to shun, entering the "dark valley" must be forbidden. Therefore, with regard to Zheng’s following Chu, the Annals always exercised the utmost caution. As for that attack on Ju by Yingqi, was it not on account of Tongdi 銅鞮? Its ruler had been taken captive and its envoy put to death; at that time there was as yet no one to relieve the crisis of Bo Juan 伯蠲, when Zizhong 子重 arrived—surely the urgency of the bamboo dispatches lay in this campaign…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣君子曰彼于鄧之戍何爲也蔑德忘親而寵
賂是彰則貪不足言而坊潰甚矣授鉞欒書而
問焉正伯義所得討者鄭當討而救之亦焉用
是渠丘之暴哉此子重之救所爲不經見也故
止書伐莒以鄭之迫於欒書義無可救者也壬
夫之侵宋非以洧上故乎入其郛而敗其兵于
時蓋未有援瓠丘之置者而子辛至焉宜纓冠
之往在是舉矣君子曰彼彭城之納何爲也披
地崇奸而叛人是登則悖不足言而坊潰又甚
===
矣推轂韓厥而問焉正伯義所當討者鄭當討
而救之亦烏用是呂留之師哉此子辛之救所
爲不經見也故止書侵宋以鄭之討於韓厥義
無可救者也雖然鄭之從楚非矣浹辰而三都
克何晉之未聞屏蔽也若後虎牢之城終不免
爲脅持計耳何惑乎鄭之反覆依違也故君子
觀楚之進而未嘗不慨盟戲蕭魚之晚
禮記
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
punctuated:
矣。君子曰：「彼于鄧之戍，何爲也？蔑德忘親而寵賂是彰，則貪不足言，而坊潰甚矣。授鉞欒書而問焉，正伯義所得討者。鄭當討而救之，亦焉用是渠丘之暴哉？」此子重之救所爲不經見也，故止書「伐莒」，以鄭之迫於欒書，義無可救者也。壬夫之侵宋，非以洧上故乎？入其郛而敗其兵，于時蓋未有援瓠丘之置者，而子辛至焉，宜纓冠之往在是舉矣。君子曰：「彼彭城之納，何爲也？披地崇奸而叛人是登，則悖不足言，而坊潰又甚矣。推轂韓厥而問焉，正伯義所當討者。鄭當討而救之，亦烏用是呂留之師哉？」此子辛之救所爲不經見也，故止書「侵宋」，以鄭之討於韓厥，義無可救者也。雖然，鄭之從楚非矣；浹辰而三都克，何晉之未聞屏蔽也？若後虎牢之城，終不免爲脅持計耳，何惑乎鄭之反覆依違也？故君子觀楚之進，而未嘗不慨盟戲、蕭魚之晚。
禮記
凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。
translation_en:
…undertaking. Yet the gentleman says: "What was the purpose of that garrisoning at Deng? By scorning virtue, forgetting kinship, and openly indulging in favoritism and bribery, their greed is beneath mention, and the collapse of moral bounds was extreme. Bestowing the battle-axe upon Luan Shu to call them to account was precisely what the duty of a霸 (hegemon) rightfully permitted him to punish. Since Zheng deserved punishment, to rescue it instead—what use was that violence at Quqiu?" This is why the rescue by Zizhong is not recorded in the Classic; therefore it merely records "attacked Ju," because in Zheng's being pressed by Luan Shu, there was in righteousness nothing that merited rescue.

As for Renfu's invasion of Song, was it not because of the campaign on the Wei River? When its outer walls were breached and its troops defeated, at that time no one had yet come to relieve the siege [?] at Huqiu, and then Zixin arrived; it would seem that rushing to aid with cap strings untied lay in this undertaking. Yet the gentleman says: "What was the purpose of that installing of fugitives at Pengcheng? By carving up territory, exalting the wicked, and elevating rebels, their perversity is beneath mention, and the collapse of moral bounds was even more extreme. Pushing the wheel-hubs to commission Han Jue to call them to account was precisely what the duty of a hegemon ought to punish. Since Zheng deserved punishment, to rescue it instead—what use was that expedition against Lü and Liu?" This is why the rescue by Zixin is not recorded in the Classic; therefore it merely records "invaded Song," because in Zheng's being punished by Han Jue, there was in righteousness nothing that merited rescue.

Even so, while Zheng's following Chu was wrong, when three cities fell within twelve days, why was Jin not heard to act as a protective screen? As for the subsequent fortifying of Hulao, in the end it could not avoid being merely a scheme of coercion; what wonder is it that Zheng repeatedly vacillated and wavered? Therefore, when the gentleman observes the advance of Chu, he never fails to lament how late the covenants at Xi and Xiaoyu came.

Record of Rites (Liji)

Whenever one serves as an envoy for his ruler, once he has received the command, the ruler's words do not stay overnight at his home.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批以簡奧之詞挑剔題旨而
講不宿家處尤能發爲使分義卽他日承皇華之遣
不當如是耶佳士佳士
考試官敎諭賈批古雅不浮
考試官敎諭汪批句健意足
臣使於君以奉命爲急焉蓋臣者行君之命而
達之天下者也有其受之莫敢緩矣而奚以家
爲哉且夫鼓舞天下人君所以制命奉揚休命
===
人臣所以爲忠故凡爲君使者豈可以君命而
宿於家哉吾知君使臣以禮而選擇以行也必
寄以文命之重臣視君如天而肅將其命者當
忘乎家室之私朝而受命朝行之矣承言王所
而邁往不俟於崇朝蓋曰今日之事君之事也
以家之顧而稽君之事可乎夕而受命夕行之
矣拜命自公而啓行不遑於夙夜蓋曰吾之有
身君之身也不有其身乃有其家可乎念綸音
之載道則馳驅之靡寧豈不懷歸也畏此簡書
punctuated:
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批：以簡奧之詞，挑剔題旨，而講「不宿家」處，尤能發「爲使」分義。卽他日承皇華之遣，不當如是耶？佳士！佳士！
考試官敎諭賈批：古雅不浮。
考試官敎諭汪批：句健意足。

臣使於君，以奉命爲急焉。蓋臣者，行君之命而達之天下者也。有其受之，莫敢緩矣，而奚以家爲哉？且夫鼓舞天下，人君所以制命；奉揚休命，人臣所以爲忠。故凡爲君使者，豈可以君命而宿於家哉？吾知君使臣以禮，而選擇以行也，必寄以文命之重；臣視君如天，而肅將其命者，當忘乎家室之私。朝而受命，朝行之矣，承言王所，而邁往不俟於崇朝，蓋曰：今日之事，君之事也，以家之顧而稽君之事，可乎？夕而受命，夕行之矣，拜命自公，而啓行不遑於夙夜，蓋曰：吾之有身，君之身也，不有其身，乃有其家，可乎？念綸音之載道，則馳驅之靡寧。豈不懷歸也？畏此簡書，
translation_en:
Tao Mingli 陶明禮
Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Ding 丁: With concise and profound words, he draws out and analyzes the essence of the topic, and in explaining the point of "not letting it stay overnight at home," he is especially able to bring out the proper duty of "serving as an envoy." If one day in the future he receives an imperial commission as envoy, should he not act just like this? A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Jia 賈: Classically elegant and free of superficiality.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wang 汪: Vigorous sentences and ample meaning.

When a minister is sent as an envoy by his ruler, he takes the execution of the command as his urgent priority. For a minister is one who carries out the ruler's command and conveys it throughout the realm. Once he has received it, he dares not delay—so what concern should he have for his family? Moreover, to inspire and rouse the realm is why the ruler issues commands; to uphold and proclaim the illustrious command is how the minister shows loyalty. Therefore, among all who serve as envoys for their ruler, how could anyone let the ruler's command stay overnight at home? I know that the ruler employs his ministers according to ritual propriety, and in selecting them to go forth, he必ず entrusts them with the weight of his civilizing mandate; the minister regards his ruler as Heaven, and in reverently carrying out his command, he ought to forget the private concerns of household and family. If he receives the command in the morning, he sets out in the morning; receiving the words at the royal court, he proceeds without waiting for the morning to pass, as if to say: "Today's affair is the ruler's affair; is it permissible to delay the ruler's affair out of regard for one's family?" If he receives the command in the evening, he sets out in the evening; bowing to receive the command from the court, he departs without leisure for rest day or night, as if to say: "This body that I have is the ruler's body; when I do not even treat my own body as my own, is it permissible to treat my family as my own?" Mindful that the royal words are carried along the road, he gallops onward without peace. Is it that he does not long to return home? He stands in awe of the royal commission inscribed on these bamboo slips…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下而會之心本也以吾心而通乎天下機也
不求其本則將率吾之意而强人必從不持其
機則雖有意於人之從而其勢亦從窒也然則
天下之不治未必皆斯人之過或者吾亦有過
焉爾君子之道則不然卽吾之所欲而推之而
不病其爲私因人之所欲而應之而不嫌其爲
徇吾固不待施之政教而其心將日下焉者必
不吾違天下亦不待吾政教之加而其心將曰
上焉者必不吾拂始也能通天下之志而終也
===
聯屬天下以成其身此致治之所以爲盛也而
其要豈外于絜矩哉曷觀之天地乎天地之于
萬物未嘗有心而能使萬物各得其所靈者爲
人蠢者爲鳥獸跂息蠕動者爲昆虫皆以類取
足于天地之化而無不均焉故曰天地無心而
成化至于栽培傾覆之際若其有必然者而亦
非有所厚薄其間是故春榮而秋瘁晝動而夜
息雖物亦不自知其所以然而於天地又奚憾
焉使其道有所偏則物不得其平而天地之化
punctuated: 天下而會之心，本也；以吾心而通乎天下，機也。不求其本，則將率吾之意而强人必從；不持其機，則雖有意於人之從，而其勢亦從窒也。然則天下之不治，未必皆斯人之過，或者吾亦有過焉爾。君子之道則不然，卽吾之所欲而推之，而不病其爲私；因人之所欲而應之，而不嫌其爲徇。吾固不待施之政教，而其心將日：「下焉者必不吾違。」天下亦不待吾政教之加，而其心將曰：「上焉者必不吾拂。」始也能通天下之志，而終也聯屬天下以成其身，此致治之所以爲盛也，而其要豈外于絜矩哉！曷觀之天地乎？天地之于萬物，未嘗有心，而能使萬物各得其所。靈者爲人，蠢者爲鳥獸，跂息蠕動者爲昆虫，皆以類取足于天地之化，而無不均焉。故曰：「天地無心而成化。」至于栽培傾覆之際，若其有必然者，而亦非有所厚薄其間。是故春榮而秋瘁，晝動而夜息，雖物亦不自知其所以然，而於天地又奚憾焉！使其道有所偏，則物不得其平，而天地之化
translation_en: … the world and bringing it together in the mind is the root; using my own mind to communicate with the world is the pivotal mechanism. If one does not seek the root, one will follow one's own arbitrary will and force others to obey; if one does not grasp the mechanism, then even if one wishes for others to follow, the circumstances will inevitably become obstructed. Thus, when the world is not well-governed, it is not necessarily all the fault of the people; perhaps I, too, have faults therein. The Way of the noble man is not like this. He extends what he himself desires without worrying that it is selfish; he responds according to what others desire without suspecting that it is pandering. Even before I apply governance and instruction, my mind will say [?]: "Those below will surely not defy me." And even before the world experiences the application of my governance and instruction, its mind will say: "Those above will surely not oppose our wishes." In the beginning, one is able to communicate the aspirations of the world, and in the end, one binds the world together to complete one's own person. This is why the attainment of order is so flourishing—and how could its essence lie outside the principle of the measuring square (xieju)! Why not observe heaven and earth? In their relation to the myriad things, heaven and earth never have a deliberate mind, yet they enable the myriad things to each find their proper place. The intelligent become humans, the dull-witted become birds and beasts, and those that crawl, breathe, and wriggle become insects and reptiles; all, according to their kind, draw sufficiency from the transformations of heaven and earth, and none are treated unequally. Therefore it is said: "Heaven and earth have no deliberate mind, yet they accomplish transformation." When it comes to planting and nurturing or overthrowing and destroying, although it seems there is an inevitability to it, there is no partiality of favor or disfavor therein. For this reason, things flourish in spring and wither in autumn, move by day and rest by night; even the things themselves do not know why it is so, and what resentment could they harbor toward heaven and earth! If their Way were partial, then things would not obtain their balance, and the transformations of heaven and earth…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
或幾乎塞矣故曰以直養萬物夫聖人之道猶
天地也聖人之于萬民猶其于萬物也然天地
無心以成之而聖人有心以應之宜若異于天
地焉者而不知聖人之心上與天地一下與天
下一雖聖人不得以私心與之而天下囿于聖
人之道亦若天之覆地之載而取足于聖人之
仁是其有心之化未必非無心者以致之也君
子知治天下之道其本在我而其機又不必求
諸天下故反而觀之吾心焉思吾所喜天下必
===
有欣然以同樂者思吾所憎天下必有拂然以
同惡者思吾所憂天下必有惻然以同戚者思
吾所懼天下必有凜然以同畏者夫吾凡以求
治者為天下也非為我也故其視吾之心惟天
下而其視天下皆吾之心其忍恝然而已哉蓋
天下之所欲不能自遂必賴吾以濟之而其所
惡亦不能自去又必賴吾以祛之然則天下之
望我也甚殷而我之慰天下也亦甚切蓋嘗盡
吾之孝矣而不忍民之頑囂未變也蓋嘗致吾
punctuated: 或幾乎塞矣。故曰：「以直養萬物。」夫聖人之道，猶天地也；聖人之于萬民，猶其于萬物也。然天地無心以成之，而聖人有心以應之，宜若異于天地焉者；而不知聖人之心，上與天地一，下與天下一，雖聖人不得以私心與之，而天下囿于聖人之道，亦若天之覆、地之載，而取足于聖人之仁。是其有心之化，未必非無心者以致之也。君子知治天下之道，其本在我，而其機又不必求諸天下，故反而觀之吾心焉。思吾所喜，天下必有欣然以同樂者；思吾所憎，天下必有拂然以同惡者；思吾所憂，天下必有惻然以同戚者；思吾所懼，天下必有凜然以同畏者。夫吾凡以求治者，為天下也，非為我也。故其視吾之心惟天下，而其視天下皆吾之心，其忍恝然而已哉？蓋天下之所欲不能自遂，必賴吾以濟之；而其所惡亦不能自去，又必賴吾以祛之。然則天下之望我也甚殷，而我之慰天下也亦甚切。蓋嘗盡吾之孝矣，而不忍民之頑囂未變也；蓋嘗致吾
translation_en: …would nearly be obstructed! Therefore it is said: "Nourishing the myriad things with uprightness." Now, the Way of the sage is like Heaven and Earth; the sage's relation to the myriad people is like their relation to the myriad things. Yet Heaven and Earth bring them to completion without deliberate mind, whereas the sage responds to them with a deliberate mind. It might seem as though he differs from Heaven and Earth; yet one does not realize that the mind of the sage is one with Heaven and Earth above, and one with the world below. Even the sage cannot interpose a selfish mind into it, and the world, encompassed within the Way of the sage, is also as if overspread by Heaven and supported by Earth, drawing sufficiency from the sage's benevolence. Thus his transformation through a deliberate mind is not necessarily not brought about by that which has no deliberate mind. The gentleman knows that in the Way of governing the world, the root lies within oneself, and its vital mechanism need not be sought in the world; therefore he turns back and observes it in his own mind. Reflecting on what I rejoice in, in the world there must be those who gladly share the same joy; reflecting on what I loathe, in the world there must be those who indignantly share the same dislike; reflecting on what I worry about, in the world there must be those who sorrowfully share the same grief; reflecting on what I fear, in the world there must be those who tremblingly share the same dread. Now, in all my seeking of good governance, it is for the sake of the world, not for my own sake. Therefore, he regards his own mind as solely the world, and regards the whole world as his own mind—how could he bear to remain indifferent and nothing more? For what the world desires it cannot fulfill by itself, and must rely on me to accomplish it; and what it dislikes it likewise cannot remove by itself, and again must rely on me to dispel it. This being so, the world's hope in me is most earnest, and my comforting of the world is likewise most urgent. Indeed, I may have exhausted my filial piety, yet cannot bear that the people's obstinacy and insincerity remain untransformed; I may have carried to the utmost my…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之弟矣而不忍民之交相為瘉也蓋嘗廣吾之
慈矣而不忍民之顛連無告也不惟是也為天
下進賢則與天下同舉之為天下退不肖則與
天下同棄之為天下生財則不敢斂天下之怨
為天下用財則不敢後天下之費凡利在天下
者興之必力而不敢私一身之圖凡害在天下
者除之必速而不敢貽一身之患玆絜矩之道
所由立也今夫工師之為矩也寸寸度之至于
尋丈不繆然後合衆材成大用均齊方正而無
===
偏枉之失也此法廢即公輸無所用其巧離婁
無所用其明夫治器亦有然者何獨至于治天
下疑之君子之為矩也其亦有由矣始之以致
格其準繩之稽乎繼之以誠正其程度之立乎
約之以脩身其範圍之定乎吾之心不出是理
之外而天下之心不出吾心之外同人于野吾
得此道于易焉遵道遵路吾得此道于書焉徧
為爾德吾得此道于詩焉順事恕施吾得此道
于春秋焉以天下為一家以中國為一人吾得
punctuated: 之弟矣，而不忍民之交相為瘉也；蓋嘗廣吾之慈矣，而不忍民之顛連無告也。不惟是也，為天下進賢，則與天下同舉之；為天下退不肖，則與天下同棄之；為天下生財，則不敢斂天下之怨；為天下用財，則不敢後天下之費。凡利在天下者，興之必力，而不敢私一身之圖；凡害在天下者，除之必速，而不敢貽一身之患。玆絜矩之道所由立也。今夫工師之為矩也，寸寸度之，至于尋丈不繆，然後合衆材、成大用，均齊方正而無偏枉之失也。此法廢，即公輸無所用其巧，離婁無所用其明。夫治器亦有然者，何獨至于治天下疑之？君子之為矩也，其亦有由矣。始之以致格，其準繩之稽乎？繼之以誠正，其程度之立乎？約之以脩身，其範圍之定乎？吾之心不出是理之外，而天下之心不出吾心之外。「同人于野」，吾得此道于《易》焉；「遵道遵路」，吾得此道于《書》焉；「徧為爾德」，吾得此道于《詩》焉；「順事恕施」，吾得此道于《春秋》焉；「以天下為一家，以中國為一人」，吾得
translation_en:
…my fraternal respect, yet I cannot bear that the people still mutually harm one another; I have broadened my parental compassion, yet I cannot bear that the people remain in distress with no one to turn to. Nor is it only this: in advancing the worthy for the sake of the empire, I promote them together with the empire; in dismissing the unworthy for the sake of the empire, I cast them aside together with the empire; in producing wealth for the empire, I dare not amass the resentment of the empire; in expending wealth for the empire, I dare not put the needs of the empire last. Whenever something is beneficial to the empire, I unfailingly exert myself to promote it, daring not harbor selfish designs for my own person; whenever something is harmful to the empire, I unfailingly hasten to remove it, daring not leave behind troubles for my own person [?]. This is whereby the Way of the measuring square (xieju) is established.

Now, when a master carpenter makes use of a carpenter's square, he measures inch by inch until at lengths of eight or ten feet there is no error; only then does he join the various timbers to complete a great work, uniform and square without the flaw of being skewed or crooked. If this method is abandoned, even Gongshu Ban would have no way to use his skill, and Li Lou would have no way to use his keen sight. If fashioning vessels is like this, why should one doubt it when it comes to governing the empire?

When the gentleman acts as a measuring square, this too has its source. Beginning with the extension of knowledge and the investigation of things—is this not the verification of the plumb line? Continuing with making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind—is this not the establishment of the standard of measure? Summarizing it in the cultivation of the person—is this not the fixing of the mold and bounds? My mind does not go beyond this principle, and the mind of the empire does not go beyond my mind. "Fellowship with men in the open country"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Changes (Yi); "following the Way and following the road"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Documents (Shu); "universally practicing your virtue"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Odes (Shi); "acting in accordance with circumstances and applying reciprocity"—I have obtained this Way from the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); "regarding the empire as one family and the Central States as one person"—I have obtained…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
此道于禮焉必如夫子之所謂巳所不欲勿施
于人必如孟子之所謂行有不得反求諸巳視
家知國視國知天下若是而曰天下不平未之
有也不然四海遠矣或以壅滯而不能平兆民
廣矣或以怨懣而弗可平萬機煩矣或以叢脞
而弗暇平天下之治果何由而成之嘗考益之
戒舜曰罔違道以干百姓之譽罔咈百姓以從
巳之欲然後知絜矩之道盡是矣巳之所欲咈
百姓以從之固不可至于順斯民之情以求其
===
譽則亦以欲從人耳而聖王固不屑爲之也何
也天下之民至愚而神者也惟其神也必有機
以鼓舞之惟其愚也必有本以禁道之若一徇
其情而違道有所不計則吾之所施巳不得其
平而何以平天下爲哉故雖政教以督率之而
不爲多事刑罰以董治之而不爲寡恩征伐以
勦刈之而不爲過暴要皆去其所以不平者就
其所以平者故絜矩之道操之若約而施之寔
博爲之似易而推之寔難行之若近而垂之愈
punctuated: 此道于《禮》焉。必如夫子之所謂「巳所不欲，勿施于人」，必如孟子之所謂「行有不得，反求諸巳」，視家知國，視國知天下，若是而曰天下不平，未之有也。不然，四海遠矣，或以壅滯而不能平；兆民廣矣，或以怨懣而弗可平；萬機煩矣，或以叢脞而弗暇平；天下之治，果何由而成之？嘗考益之戒舜曰：「罔違道以干百姓之譽，罔咈百姓以從巳之欲。」然後知絜矩之道盡是矣。巳之所欲，咈百姓以從之，固不可；至于順斯民之情以求其譽，則亦以欲從人耳，而聖王固不屑爲之也。何也？天下之民，至愚而神者也。惟其神也，必有機以鼓舞之；惟其愚也，必有本以禁道之。若一徇其情，而違道有所不計，則吾之所施巳不得其平，而何以平天下爲哉？故雖政教以督率之，而不爲多事；刑罰以董治之，而不爲寡恩；征伐以勦刈之，而不爲過暴。要皆去其所以不平者，就其所以平者。故絜矩之道，操之若約而施之寔博，爲之似易而推之寔難，行之若近而垂之愈
translation_en: … this Way from the Record of Rites (Li). It must be like what the Master called, "What you do not desire for yourself, do not impose on others," and must be like what Mencius called, "Whenever one's actions fail to achieve their end, turn inward and examine oneself." By observing the family, one knows the state; by observing the state, one knows the realm under Heaven. That one should act like this and yet say that the realm under Heaven is not brought to peace—there has never been such a thing. Otherwise, the Four Seas are distant, and perhaps because of blockage and stagnation they cannot be brought to peace; the millions of people are vast, and perhaps because of resentment and discontent they cannot be brought to peace; the myriad affairs of state are繁瑣 (numerous and vexing), and perhaps because of petty details there is no leisure to bring them to peace—by what means, then, could the ordering of the realm under Heaven truly be accomplished? I have examined Yi's admonition to Shun, which says: "Do not violate the Way to seek the praise of the hundred surnames; do not oppose the hundred surnames to follow your own desires." Only after this does one know that the Way of the measuring square is exhausted in this. As for what one desires for oneself, to oppose the hundred surnames in order to follow it is certainly impermissible; yet as for indulging the feelings of these people in order to seek their praise, that too is merely following others out of selfish desire, and the sage kings certainly disdained to do so. Why is this? The people of the realm are supremely foolish and yet spirit-like. Because they are spirit-like, there must be a vital mechanism to inspire and rouse them; because they are foolish, there must be a fundamental standard to restrain and guide them. If one wholly yields to their feelings without regard for violating the Way, then what one dispenses has already lost its fairness and balance—and how then could one bring peace and balance to the realm under Heaven? Therefore, even though one supervises and leads them with governance and instruction, it is not considered meddlesome; even though one corrects and regulates them with punishments and penalties, it is not considered lacking in grace; even though one suppresses and cuts them down with punitive expeditions, it is not considered excessively violent. In sum, all of this is to remove that by which things are unbalanced and to advance that by which they are balanced. Therefore, the Way of the measuring square seems concise when held in the hand, yet is truly broad when applied; it seems easy when practiced, yet is truly difficult when extended; it seems near when carried out, yet when handed down it is ever more …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭汪批瞻典則是足以華
國矣錄之
天順五年某月某日具官臣賢等奉
命編緝
大明一統志成謹用繕寫裝潢呈
進者伏以受
天明命萬年仰
日月之照臨纘
祖鴻圖一統昭
===
乾坤之覆載
創貽有自
紹述彌光臣賢等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首粤惟古
昔帝王肇建無窮之緒必資紀録永垂可
久之規畫野制昉軒轅步極筭精豎亥爰
稽謨典參攷職方封山濬川咨十二官而
命牧揆教奮衛别五百里而建侯郊鄏之
鼎始新卜年卜世洛師之墨初食宜民宜
人辨區域於司徒執度相衆乎居邑藏簡
punctuated:
考試官、教諭汪批：「贍典則是，足以華國矣。錄之。」

天順五年某月某日，具官臣賢等奉命編緝《大明一統志》成，謹用繕寫裝潢呈進者。伏以：受天明命，萬年仰日月之照臨；纘祖鴻圖，一統昭乾坤之覆載。創貽有自，紹述彌光。臣賢等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。粤惟古昔帝王，肇建無窮之緒，必資紀録，永垂可久之規。畫野制昉軒轅，步極筭精豎亥。爰稽謨典，參攷職方：封山濬川，咨十二官而命牧；揆教奮衛，别五百里而建侯。郊鄏之鼎始新，卜年卜世；洛師之墨初食，宜民宜人。辨區域於司徒，執度相衆乎居邑；藏簡
translation_en:
Comment by the Examiner, Instructor Wang: "Rich in classical allusions and proper in rule—it is sufficient to bring luster to the state. Recorded."

On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of the Tianshun era (1461), Your Servant Li Xian and others, holding official titles as listed, having received the Imperial command to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi) and brought it to completion, respectfully have it copied, mounted, and presented to the Throne.

We humbly reflect: Having received Heaven's bright mandate, for ten thousand years the realm looks up to the illumination of the sun and moon; continuing the Ancestors' grand design, the unified empire makes manifest the canopy of Heaven and the support of Earth. The founding and bequeathing had their origin; the succession and transmission shine ever brighter. Your Servant Xian and others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground.

We observe that when the emperors and kings of antiquity first established their boundless enterprises, they invariably relied upon records and registers to hand down enduring standards forever. The system of dividing the fields originated with Xuanyuan (the Yellow Emperor), and the calculation of pacing the poles was perfected by Shuhai. Examining the counsels and canons, and cross-referencing the Direction of the Domain (Zhifang): in raising altars on mountains and dredging rivers, Shun consulted the Twelve Pastors and appointed regional governors; in measuring instruction and rousing defense, Yu distinguished the five-hundred-li zones and established feudal lords. When the tripods at Jia鄏 were newly settled, the years and generations were divined; when the ink on the tortoise shell at Luoshi was first consumed by fire, it was fitting for the commoners and fitting for the men of worth. The Minister of Education (Situ) distinguished the regions, holding the surveyor's cord to inspect the multitudes in their settlements; the External Scribe (Waishi) stored the bamboo slips…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
編於外史保障兼重乎塞垣山海不經宇
寰徒記迨金玉靡昭王度而埏垓空侈帝
紘鹿逐龍興府籍先收於勝算狐鳴虎踞
霸功誰紀乎偏安混一無由函三奚望欽
惟
聖祖肇造
洪基
握彖契元首三才而開物除凶刷恥渾六合
以為家率土共惟
===
帝臣蒸民會歸
皇極尚
廑貽燕爰集儒髦言輯輶軒將欲載艱難之
業志餘弓鼎竟未成渾灝之書事豈偶然
時如有待恭惟
皇帝陛下
德隆協帝
福斂惟皇
正位
punctuated: 編於外史，保障兼重乎塞垣。《山海》不經，宇寰徒記。迨金玉靡昭王度，而埏垓空侈帝紘。鹿逐龍興，府籍先收於勝算；狐鳴虎踞，霸功誰紀乎偏安？混一無由，函三奚望？欽惟聖祖，肇造洪基，握彖契元，首三才而開物；除凶刷恥，渾六合以為家。率土共惟帝臣，蒸民會歸皇極。尚廑貽燕，爰集儒髦。言輯輶軒，將欲載艱難之業；志餘弓鼎，竟未成渾灝之書。事豈偶然，時如有待。恭惟皇帝陛下，德隆協帝，福斂惟皇，正位
translation_en: … bamboo slips and records in the charge of the External Scribe (waishi), while bulwarks of defense simultaneously emphasized the frontier walls. The Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai jing) is uncanonical, and accounts of the world merely record it in vain. Coming down to the time when gold and jade no longer manifested kingly measure, the eight directions and nine regions vainly boasted of the imperial cordon. As the deer was pursued and the dragon arose, the registers of the storehouses were first gathered in a victorious strategy; where foxes cried out and tigers crouched, who would chronicle hegemonic achievements in a state of partial sovereignty? With no way to achieve grand unification, how could one hope to encompass the triad of Heaven, Earth, and Man? We reverently reflect that the Sacred Ancestor founded the great enterprise: grasping the hexagram judgments and tallying with the Primal, he stood at the head of the Three Powers and inaugurated all things; eliminating the wicked and wiping away disgrace, he merged the Six Directions into a single family. All within the bounds of the land together became servants of the Emperor, and the multitudes of the people converged upon the August Ultimate. Still solicitous of bequeathing a peaceful legacy to his descendants, he thereupon assembled the eminent Confucians. What was gathered by the light carriages of his envoys was intended to record an enterprise achieved through hardship; yet his ambition lingered by the bow and cauldron of his passing, and in the end the vast and boundless book was left uncompleted. How could this matter have been mere coincidence? The time was as if awaiting completion. We respectfully reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, whose lofty virtue harmonizes with the Lord on High and who gathers blessings as the August Sovereign, has taken Your rightful place…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
紫樞受球而綴下國
穆容
黼宁輯瑞而覲羣工
中天化日重暉
慶合堯封而再覩異域青雲簇彩
聖占周曆以彌昌蓋觀乎天文人文已見
化成之治而思夫丕承丕顯可忘
啟佑之功爰率
祖之攸行乃自
===
天而申
命取材藝苑分館蓬山競效編摩期奏全功于
菲劣誰能筆削仰承
獨斷於淵深類以羣分例因義起經史之網羅
盡矣流略之證引昭然系首
大明尊歸一統昭回
玉版鑠懿金鋪翼翼
京師儷
天樞而表則巍巍方岳絡地軸而作屏由二十
punctuated: 紫樞，受球而綴下國；穆容黼宁，輯瑞而覲羣工。中天化日重暉，慶合堯封而再覩；異域青雲簇彩，聖占周曆以彌昌。蓋觀乎天文人文，已見化成之治；而思夫丕承丕顯，可忘啟佑之功？爰率祖之攸行，乃自天而申命。取材藝苑，分館蓬山。競效編摩，期奏全功于菲劣；誰能筆削，仰承獨斷於淵深。類以羣分，例因義起。經史之網羅盡矣，流略之證引昭然。系首大明，尊歸一統；昭回玉版，鑠懿金鋪。翼翼京師，儷天樞而表則；巍巍方岳，絡地軸而作屏。由二十
translation_en: … the Purple Pivot, receiving the jade regalia and binding together the subordinate states; with solemn countenance before the embroidered screen, gathering the auspicious jade tablets and giving audience to all the officials. In mid-heaven the transforming sun shines anew, a blessing matching the realm of Yao and witnessed once again; in distant lands the azure clouds cluster in splendor, a sacred omen that the calendar of Zhou shall flourish ever more. Indeed, observing the patterns of heaven and the patterns of humanity, one already sees a governance of complete transformation; yet in reflecting upon the great inheritance and great manifestation, how could one forget the merit of our predecessors' enlightening guidance? Thereupon, following the path walked by the Ancestors, a renewed mandate was issued from Heaven. Talents were selected from the garden of letters, and bureaus were apportioned on Mount Peng [the Hanlin Academy]. Vying to devote themselves to compiling and polishing, we hoped to achieve complete success despite our meager abilities; yet who among us could wield the brush to add or delete, looking up instead to receive Your Majesty's sole decision from the profound depths of wisdom? Categories were divided according to kind, and editorial principles arose from righteous meaning. The net cast over the Classics and Histories is exhaustive, and the citations from the various schools and epitomes are crystal clear. Heading the genealogy with the Great Ming, supreme honor returns to the Grand Unity; the jade tablets shine with revolving brilliance, and the golden knockers gleam with resplendent virtue. Reverent and majestic is the Capital, matching the Celestial Pivot to stand as a model; lofty and towering are the regional mountains, girdling the earthly axis to serve as a protective screen. From the twenty-…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
八宿之分垣察氛祲于經緯從千八百國
之列土稽沿革于封疆采謠問俗而媺惡
互陳胙土藉茅而親賢竝建志學校志書
院志戎衞具文武之弛張紀公署紀壇廟
紀關梁儼幽明之森列山川詳流峙之勝
用示壯觀方產存華實之毛豈珍異品徵
文獻於鄉賢名宦而流寓幷收卓矣風猷
如在摭遺跡於寺觀墓陵而僊釋附紀逖
哉玄覽何窮褒列女以嗣徽音王化首二
===
南之意別裔夷不亂華夏聖人嚴四塞之
防文省而意則該實符而名不爽使寸天
尺地一舉目而可知即往古來今如指掌
而易見傳疑傳信此豈一家之言有要有
倫可為萬世之典尤詳禹貢無論周官臣
等才謝三長慙左狐之上乘業窮五技拜
班馬於下風窺測海天僅同蠡管閱歷寒
暑甫竣槧鉛緬懷二酉之藏竊比九州之
戒傳誤敢辭訛豕反約或免汗牛幸萃全
punctuated: 八宿之分垣，察氛祲于經緯；從千八百國之列土，稽沿革于封疆。采謠問俗，而媺惡互陳；胙土藉茅，而親賢竝建。志學校、志書院、志戎衞，具文武之弛張；紀公署、紀壇廟、紀關梁，儼幽明之森列。山川詳流峙之勝，用示壯觀；方產存華實之毛，豈珍異品。徵文獻於鄉賢、名宦，而流寓幷收，卓矣風猷如在；摭遺跡於寺觀、墓陵，而僊釋附紀，逖哉玄覽何窮。褒列女以嗣徽音，王化首《二南》之意；別裔夷不亂華夏，聖人嚴四塞之防。文省而意則該，實符而名不爽。使寸天尺地，一舉目而可知；即往古來今，如指掌而易見。傳疑傳信，此豈一家之言？有要有倫，可為萬世之典。尤詳《禹貢》，無論《周官》。臣等才謝三長，慙左狐之上乘；業窮五技，拜班馬於下風。窺測海天，僅同蠡管；閱歷寒暑，甫竣槧鉛。緬懷二酉之藏，竊比九州之戒。傳誤敢辭訛豕？反約或免汗牛。幸萃全
translation_en: …the divided enclosures of the twenty-eight lunar mansions, one observes auspicious and ominous portents along the warp and woof of the heavens; following the arrayed territories of the eighteen hundred states, one investigates the historical changes of their borders. Collecting folk ballads and inquiring into local customs, both the admirable and the base are mutually set forth; granting lands and wrapping the earth in white cogon grass, both imperial kinsmen and worthy men are enfeoffed together. Recording schools, recording academies, and recording military guards, it encompasses the relaxation and tension of civil and military governance; chronicling government offices, chronicling altars and temples, and chronicling passes and bridges, it displays the majestic array of the unseen and visible realms. Under mountains and rivers, the scenic beauty of flowing waters and towering peaks is detailed so as to manifest their grand spectacle; under local products, the vegetation bearing blossoms and fruits is preserved—how could it prize exotic rarities? Seeking documentary and oral evidence among local worthies and eminent officials, while also including sojourners—lofty indeed, their moral influence seems still present! Gathering historical traces among Buddhist monasteries, Daoist temples, tombs, and mausoleums, while appending accounts of immortals and Buddhists—far-reaching indeed, how inexhaustible is this profound survey! Praising exemplary women to carry on virtuous reputations embodies the intent of royal transformation beginning with the Two Nan [odes of the Book of Songs]; distinguishing frontier tribes so that they do not throw China into disorder upholds the sages' strict defense of the four borders. The wording is concise yet the meaning is comprehensive; the reality corresponds and the names do not err. It makes every inch of heaven and foot of earth knowable at a single glance, and allows the past and present to be as easily seen as pointing to one's palm. Transmitting both what is doubtful and what is certain, how could this be the words of a single school? Possessing both essentials and order, it can serve as a canon for ten thousand generations. It is even more detailed than the Tribute of Yu (Yugong), to say nothing of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). Your servants lack the three merits of the historian and feel ashamed before the supreme mastery of Zuo Qiuming and Dong Hu; our craft is exhausted like the five skills of the flying squirrel, and we bow downwind in deference to Ban Gu and Sima Qian. Peering at and measuring the sea and sky, our efforts are merely like using a calabash ladle or a narrow tube; passing through cold and heat, we have only just completed our work with writing tablets and lead powder. Fondly recalling the book collections of the Two You mountains, we privately compare this work to the admonitions of the Nine Provinces. In transmitting errors, how dare we absolve ourselves of the mistake of writing "pig" for "hai" (訛豕)? Yet by returning to conciseness, we may perhaps avoid works so bulky as to make a draft ox sweat. Fortunately having gathered the complete…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批我
祖宗心法同符帝王而
皇上心法同符
祖宗
聖學淵源度越千古矣是作能窺測其精微揚厲其盛美而要歸於純
亦不已尤見忠懇宜錄以式
考試官敎諭賈批揄揚我
皇上緝熈
===
聖學旣極詳悉而末所敷陳尤知靖獻之義是涵濡
聖化而有得者
考試官敎諭汪批規頌得體具見學識
論聖學者豈以萬乗之尊躬博士之業足
稱述哉其研精省驗欲以資化理故日求
諸聞且見者以廣其聰明其操存檢約欲
以敦化原故日求諸不聞且見者以養其
純一二者交致于心亹亹而不息故德業
長裕而名號休美也非
punctuated:
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批：我祖宗心法同符帝王，而皇上心法同符祖宗，聖學淵源，度越千古矣。是作能窺測其精微，揚厲其盛美，而要歸於純亦不已，尤見忠懇，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭賈批：揄揚我皇上緝熈聖學，旣極詳悉，而末所敷陳，尤知靖獻之義，是涵濡聖化而有得者。
考試官敎諭汪批：規頌得體，具見學識。
論聖學者，豈以萬乗之尊，躬博士之業，足稱述哉？其研精省驗，欲以資化理，故日求諸聞且見者，以廣其聰明；其操存檢約，欲以敦化原，故日求諸不聞且見者，以養其純一。二者交致于心，亹亹而不息，故德業長裕，而名號休美也。非
translation_en:
Tan Rushi 譚汝試.

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Guo 郭, comments: The transmission of the mind (xinfa) of our Imperial Ancestors tallies with that of the ancient Emperors and Kings, and His Majesty's transmission of the mind tallies with that of the Imperial Ancestors; the profound origins of his sagely learning surpass a thousand ages! This composition is able to fathom its subtle depths, extol its magnificent beauty, and ultimately bring it back to "purity that never ceases" (chun yi bu yi), which especially reveals loyal sincerity. It is fitting to record it as a model.

Examiner, Instructor Jia 賈, comments: In extolling His Majesty's bright and continuous sagely learning, it is already extremely detailed and thorough, and what is set forth at the end especially grasps the principle of reverently offering counsel (jingxian). He is one who has been steeped in sagely transformation and gained insight from it.

Examiner, Instructor Wang 汪, comments: Both admonition and praise are fittingly measured, fully demonstrating his learning and insight.

When discussing sagely learning, how could it merely be that the sovereign of ten thousand chariots personally engaging in the pursuits of an erudite is sufficient to warrant praise and recounting? His refining of essence and self-examination are intended to aid in transformative governance; therefore, he daily seeks within what is heard and seen in order to broaden his acute hearing and clear sight. His preservation of the mind and self-restraint are intended to thicken the source of transformation; therefore, he daily seeks within what is neither heard nor seen in order to nourish his pure oneness. When both are mutually brought to bear upon the mind, tirelessly and without cease, moral virtue and grand enterprise grow ever more abundant, and his reputation and title become splendid and fine. Unless one is…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
大聖人其孰能與此者乎請對揚之今夫烝庶
之家稍能操奇贏必聚詩書延師儒不惜
伏臘費課其子力學上則望其邁迹褎倫
顯融於當世次亦望其辨物數計資糈謹
守先世之籍毋墜况人主之尊纂有鴻業
為宗社天人之所繫命非第奇贏任也故
典學緝煕之說自高成二君而始見於詩
書顧所從來乆遠矣考諸韓詩外傳謂黃
帝學于大墳顓頊學于祿圖堯學于務成
===
子附舜學于尹壽禹學于西王國湯學于
貸乎相文王學于錫疇子斯武王學于太
公雖於六籍靡所考見而帝王之務學玆
亦足以徵焉晚近世而斯道闕矣其稍能
近儒紳親縹素考虙於今古之林則前史
往往豔談之故石渠臨決肇於宣帝夜分
講論見於光武文學直宿引與論議著於
貞觀自巳至申然後釋卷稱於興國屏書
無逸紀於明道非不誠好學也而終不能
punctuated: 大聖人，其孰能與此者乎？請對揚之。今夫烝庶之家，稍能操奇贏，必聚《詩》、《書》，延師儒，不惜伏臘費，課其子力學。上則望其邁迹褎倫，顯融於當世；次亦望其辨物數、計資糈，謹守先世之籍毋墜。况人主之尊，纂有鴻業，為宗社、天人之所繫命，非第奇贏任也！故典學、緝煕之說，自高、成二君而始見於《詩》、《書》，顧所從來乆遠矣。考諸《韓詩外傳》，謂黃帝學于大墳，顓頊學于祿圖，堯學于務成子附，舜學于尹壽，禹學于西王國，湯學于貸乎相，文王學于錫疇子斯，武王學于太公。雖於六籍靡所考見，而帝王之務學，玆亦足以徵焉。晚近世而斯道闕矣。其稍能近儒紳、親縹素、考虙於今古之林，則前史往往豔談之。故石渠臨決，肇於宣帝；夜分講論，見於光武；文學直宿，引與論議，著於貞觀；自巳至申然後釋卷，稱於興國；屏書《無逸》，紀於明道。非不誠好學也，而終不能
translation_en:
…a great sage, who could take part in this? Allow me to respond and extol it.

Now, among the families of the common people, those who are even slightly able to manage a surplus of wealth will certainly gather the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, invite teachers and Confucian scholars, and, sparing no expense for the summer and winter festivals, urge their sons to study diligently. At best, they hope their sons will surpass the footsteps of others and rise above their peers, achieving prominence and distinction in their own time; at the very least, they hope they will be able to distinguish goods and numbers, calculate resources and provisions, and carefully guard the patrimony of their ancestors without letting it fall into ruin. How much more so for the exalted ruler of men, who inherits the great enterprise upon which the fate of the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, Heaven, and humanity depends—a responsibility that is by no means merely the management of a financial surplus!

Therefore, although the doctrines of "devoting oneself to learning" (dianxue) and "continuing the bright virtue" (jixi) first appeared in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents with the two monarchs Gaozong of Shang and King Cheng of Zhou, their origins in fact go back a very long way. Examining the Outer Commentary to the Book of Odes by Master Han (Hanshi waizhuan), it states that the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) studied under Dafen, Zhuanxu studied under Lutu, Yao studied under Wucheng Zifu, Shun studied under Yin Shou, Yu studied under Xiwang Guo, Tang studied under Dai Zixiang [transcribed as 貸乎相], King Wen studied under Xichou Zisi, and King Wu studied under Taigong. Although these accounts cannot be verified in the Six Classics, they are nonetheless sufficient to attest to the fact that emperors and kings devoted themselves to learning.

In more recent ages, however, this Way has fallen into neglect. Whenever a ruler was even slightly able to draw close to Confucian scholars and officials, acquaint himself with books and scrolls, and investigate and deliberate [?] in the forest of past and present, previous histories would often speak of it with admiration. Thus, presiding over the final decisions on the classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) began with Emperor Xuan of Han; lecturing and discussing until midnight was seen under Guangwu of Han; having literary scholars keep night duty and summoning them for discussions was famed in the Zhenguan era (under Taizong of Tang); reading from the si hour (9–11 a.m.) to the shen hour (3–5 p.m.) before putting down the scroll was praised in the Taiping Xingguo era (under Taizong of Song); and writing out the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) chapter on a folding screen was recorded in the Mingdao era (under Renzong of Song). It is not that they were not genuinely fond of learning, yet in the end they could not…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與聖人聯鑣而共軌者其所繇異術也彼
唐虞三代經綸探討原非二途其學已實
而不華而危微祗敬之念其握之爲本始
者尤足以綱百爲而統羣籍故能神聖獨
詣卓然稱邁迹覔倫之主彪炳往牒若漢
唐宋數君其能然乎而亦不失爲堇堇守
先籍者則學之功也洪惟
皇上
睿德天授
===
聖功日新
卽位以來非隆冬盛夏不輟
講筵
端居
禁中亦日
親典籍無他嗜好嘗于
文華殿
御書學二帝三王治天下大經大法又甞
御書謹天戒任賢能親賢臣遠嬖佞明賞罰謹
punctuated: 與聖人聯鑣而共軌者，其所繇異術也。彼唐、虞、三代，經綸探討，原非二途，其學已實而不華；而危微祗敬之念，其握之爲本始者，尤足以綱百爲而統羣籍。故能神聖獨詣，卓然稱邁迹覔倫之主，彪炳往牒。若漢、唐、宋數君，其能然乎？而亦不失爲堇堇守先籍者，則學之功也。洪惟皇上，睿德天授，聖功日新。卽位以來，非隆冬盛夏，不輟講筵；端居禁中，亦日親典籍，無他嗜好。嘗于文華殿御書「學二帝三王治天下大經大法」；又甞御書「謹天戒、任賢能、親賢臣、遠嬖佞、明賞罰、謹
translation_en:
… ride side by side and share the same track with the sages is that the path they followed was a different art. In the times of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, statecraft and scholarly inquiry were originally not two separate paths, and their learning was already substantial rather than华麗 (superficial/ornate); moreover, their mindfulness of what is precarious and what is subtle, together with their reverent caution—which they grasped as the fundamental beginning—was especially sufficient to serve as the guiding cord for all actions and to unify all books. Thus they were able to reach a divine and sagely attainment all their own, standing out eminenty as rulers who surpassed prior footsteps and were beyond compare [? 覔倫, for 絕倫], shining brilliantly in past records. Could those several rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song be capable of such as this? Yet that they still did not fail to be rulers who at least preserved the ancestral records was the achievement of learning.

Humbly reflecting upon Your Majesty: Your sagely virtue is bestowed by Heaven, and Your sacred achievement is daily renewed. Since ascending the throne, except in the depth of winter and the height of summer, You have not suspended the Classics Mat lectures; dwelling in rectitude within the Forbidden Palace, You also daily acquaint Yourself with the canonical books and have no other indulgences. Once, in the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua dian), You wrote in Your imperial hand: "Study the great invariable principles and great laws by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings governed the world"; and on another occasion You wrote in Your imperial hand: "Heed the warnings of Heaven, employ the worthy and capable, draw close to worthy ministers, keep far from favorites and flatterers, make clear rewards and punishments, be cautious in…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
出入慎起居節飲食收放心存敬畏納忠言
撙節用凡十二事蓋瞽御之所未箴工師之
所未誦而我
皇上方且兢兢然常凝常運於淵閎沕穆之原
而研精省驗於鑒觀獻納之所翕受殆舉
二帝三王而羹牆見也故邇來邊堠息燧
海波鮮揚河淮安流遼左屢捷大小臣工
皆楛法守職中外樂業玆非
懋學之符鏡哉乃執事復求所以佐萬分一
===
者愚以為今所急第法
祖宗巳爾夫人主之銳意有為語以帝王則怡
然滿志語以先世家法必且謂其習見而
易焉然馳神遠慕未易以驟至而見成功
則內惑而趨不固此武帝神宗之所以鮮
完美也故不若學
祖宗效何者以
祖宗所得雖二帝三王不能加也甞觀我
太祖之
punctuated: 出入、慎起居、節飲食、收放心、存敬畏、納忠言、撙節用，凡十二事。蓋瞽御之所未箴，工師之所未誦，而我皇上方且兢兢然常凝常運於淵閎沕穆之原，而研精省驗於鑒觀獻納之所翕受，殆舉二帝三王而羹牆見也。故邇來邊堠息燧，海波鮮揚，河淮安流，遼左屢捷，大小臣工皆楛法守職，中外樂業，玆非懋學之符鏡哉？乃執事復求所以佐萬分一者，愚以為今所急第法祖宗巳爾。夫人主之銳意有為，語以帝王，則怡然滿志；語以先世家法，必且謂其習見而易焉。然馳神遠慕，未易以驟至而見成功，則內惑而趨不固，此武帝、神宗之所以鮮完美也。故不若學祖宗效。何者？以祖宗所得，雖二帝三王不能加也。甞觀我太祖之
translation_en:
… one's goings out and comings in, being cautious in daily life, moderating food and drink, recovering the straying mind, preserving reverence and awe, accepting loyal counsel, and economizing on expenditures"—altogether twelve matters. Indeed, these are what blind musicians and attendants had not yet offered as admonitions, and what master artisans had not yet recited, yet Our Majesty is even now cautiously and constantly concentrating and exercising his mind at the deep, vast, and profound source, while refining and examining what is gathered through observation and presented counsel, almost bringing the Two Emperors and Three Kings into view as if seeing them in his soup and on his walls. Thus, in recent times, the frontier watchtowers have extinguished their beacon fires, the ocean waves are seldom stirred up, the Yellow and Huai rivers flow peacefully, Liaodong has won repeated victories, great and small officials alike strictly [?] abide by the laws and fulfill their duties, and both the court and the provinces enjoy their livelihoods—is this not the tally and mirror of His diligent study?

Now you, sir, further seek a way to assist by even one part in ten thousand; in my humble opinion, what is urgent today is simply to model ourselves upon the Imperial Ancestors and nothing more. When a ruler is eagerly intent on accomplishing great things, if one speaks to him of the ancient Emperors and Kings, he is pleased and fully satisfied; if one speaks to him of the family laws of prior generations, he will surely consider them familiar and take them lightly. Yet when the spirit gallops after distant objects of admiration, it is not easy to reach them all at once and see success; then inwardly one becomes perplexed and one's direction is not firm. This is why Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Shenzong of Song seldom achieved perfection. Therefore, nothing is as effective as studying the Imperial Ancestors. Why is this? Because what the Imperial Ancestors attained could not be surpassed even by the Two Emperors and Three Kings. I have observed that Our Grand Progenitor's …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖學淵源未易殫述而舉其大略則若
諭李善長以心爲身之主帥若一事不合理則
百事皆廢所以常自點檢
諭宋濂以人心虛靈乗氣機出入操而存之爲
難玆非危微之後再揭奧眇者乎
成祖之
諭楊士奇也曰帝王之學貴切己實用一切浮
泛無益之語勿進至其
諭解縉則謂毎退朝默坐未嘗不思管束此心
===
爲切要思爲人君但于宮室車馬服食玩好
無所增加則天下自然無事皇皇乎
聖學之大律也迨于
世宗殖學甚盛毎
清問策士
裁决章疏皆啓口成章公卿大夫曾不能賛
一詞而其所爲
敬一箴者有曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗純又舉
聖學之要領而標禁之至矣盡矣則今所當仰
punctuated: 聖學淵源，未易殫述。而舉其大略，則若諭李善長以「心爲身之主帥，若一事不合理，則百事皆廢，所以常自點檢」；諭宋濂以「人心虛靈，乗氣機出入，操而存之爲難」。玆非「危微」之後，再揭奧眇者乎？成祖之諭楊士奇也，曰：「帝王之學，貴切己實用，一切浮泛無益之語勿進。」至其諭解縉，則謂：「毎退朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要；思爲人君，但于宮室、車馬、服食、玩好無所增加，則天下自然無事。」皇皇乎，聖學之大律也！迨于世宗，殖學甚盛，毎清問、策士、裁决章疏，皆啓口成章，公卿大夫曾不能賛一詞。而其所爲《敬一箴》者，有曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。」又舉聖學之要領而標禁之，至矣，盡矣！則今所當仰
translation_en:
… the origins and depth of his sagely learning cannot easily be recounted in full. Yet to cite its general outline: there is, for instance, his instruction to Li Shanchang 李善長 that "the mind is the commander-in-chief of the body; if a single matter does not accord with principle, then a hundred matters are all ruined, which is why I constantly examine myself"; and his instruction to Song Lian 宋濂 that "the human mind is empty and numinous, going out and coming in as it rides the mechanisms of vital force, so that grasping and preserving it is difficult." After the teaching on the "precarious and subtle," does this not once again reveal the profound mysteries?

When Emperor Chengzu 成祖 instructed Yang Shiqi 楊士奇, he said: "The learning of emperors and kings values what is personally relevant and of practical use; do not present any superficial, vague, or unprofitable words." And in his instruction to Xie Jin 解縉, he stated: "Whenever I retire from court and sit in silence, I never fail to reflect that restraining this mind is of the utmost urgency; I reflect that in being a ruler of men, if only one makes no additions to palaces, carriages and horses, clothing and food, or curiosities and pastimes, the realm will naturally be free of trouble." How grand indeed—the great standard of sagely learning!

When it came down to Emperor Shizong 世宗, his cultivation of learning was exceedingly flourishing. Whenever he posed pure inquiries, presented policy questions to scholars, or rendered decisions on memorials, his words formed finished compositions as soon as he opened his mouth, such that the dukes, ministers, and grandees could not add a single word in assistance. And in the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi zhen 敬一箴) that he composed, it is said: "Without reverence there is no concentration; without oneness there is no purity." Thus he too raised up the essential import of sagely learning and set it forth as an admonitory standard [? 標禁]—reaching the utmost perfection and completeness! Then what we ought today to look up to and …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
求
祖宗心法者夫寧有他矩哉故特達卓偉之質
不以自有恐易驕也日升川至之年不以
自恃恐易惰也窮富極貴鉅麗之觀不以
自御慮易侈也其威足以震懾庶官而辨
足以籠挫萬物不敢自用慮易壅也其餘
力足富記誦而麗詞章不敢自逞慮騖於
外也綽約靡曼便嬖使令日環給而伺進
不以易吾聖賢神僊黄白與遊畋喜功之
===
說不以易吾經術慮易誘也
深宮燕閒猶之乎聆炯誨納顯諍屬屬乎其
弗敢弛也夙夜寧寂猶之乎奉駿奔事對
越勉勉乎其弗敢間也日取諸前言往行
以涵泳於吾心叅酌於世務而本其所為
心則又兢兢業業舉經術世務而一以貫
之毋勤始而怠終毋炫名而遺實是隨所
聞見與所不聞見皆若乾道之常運純亦
不已焉斯
punctuated: 求祖宗心法者，夫寧有他矩哉？故特達卓偉之質，不以自有，恐易驕也；日升川至之年，不以自恃，恐易惰也；窮富極貴鉅麗之觀，不以自御，慮易侈也。其威足以震懾庶官，而辨足以籠挫萬物，不敢自用，慮易壅也；其餘力足富記誦而麗詞章，不敢自逞，慮騖於外也；綽約靡曼、便嬖使令日環給而伺進，不以易吾聖賢，神僊、黄白與遊畋、喜功之說，不以易吾經術，慮易誘也。深宮燕閒，猶之乎聆炯誨、納顯諍，屬屬乎其弗敢弛也；夙夜寧寂，猶之乎奉駿奔、事對越，勉勉乎其弗敢間也。日取諸前言往行，以涵泳於吾心，叅酌於世務；而本其所為心，則又兢兢業業，舉經術、世務而一以貫之。毋勤始而怠終，毋炫名而遺實，是隨所聞見與所不聞見，皆若乾道之常運，純亦不已焉。斯
translation_en: …seek in the mental discipline (xinfa) of the Imperial Ancestors, how could there be any other standard? Therefore, though possessing an extraordinary and eminent nature, He does not presume upon it as His own, fearing that it easily leads to arrogance; though in the prime of youth, like the rising sun and swelling stream, He does not rely upon it, fearing that it easily leads to indolence; though surrounded by the magnificent spectacles of supreme wealth and honor, He does not indulge Himself in them, lest it easily lead to extravagance. Though His majesty suffices to awe all officials and His eloquence suffices to encompass and subdue all things, He dares not rely solely on His own judgment, lest it easily lead to the obstruction of counsel; though His spare energy suffices to enrich memorization and recitation and to adorn literary composition, He dares not give free rein to it, lest He stray into external trivialities; though graceful beauties and favored attendants wait upon Him daily in a circle seeking advancement, He does not exchange the sages and worthies for them, and as for the doctrines of immortals, alchemy, hunting excursions, and militaristic exploits, He does not exchange canonical scholarship for them, lest He be easily seduced. In the leisure of the deep palace, it is just as if He were listening to luminous instruction and accepting outspoken remonstrance, remaining reverently attentive without daring to relax; in the quietude of morning and night, it is just as if He were performing the swift service of sacrifice and standing in the presence of Heaven, remaining tirelessly diligent without daring to let His effort lapse. Daily He draws upon the words and deeds of the past to immerse His mind in them and to deliberate upon the affairs of the world; and rooting them in the workings of His mind, with cautious and trembling care He takes canonical scholarship and worldly affairs and threads them together on a single principle. Neither diligent at the beginning only to grow lax at the end, nor flaunting reputation while neglecting reality—thus, both in what is seen and heard and in what is unseen and unheard, all is like the constant revolution of the Way of Heaven (Qiandao), pure and unceasing. Then…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之美可承帝王之盛不難致也高成且將
讓德區區漢唐宋諸君又何足多談
第二問
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批我
皇上祗承天戒昭示臣民蓋尚實而非尚文也此作善敷厲揄揚末進忠
悃尤占偉識異日必不負所學者
同考試官教諭王批心本忠愛體得對揚是華
國器
===
天之實者
考試官教諭賈批援古證今揚厲備至篇末
讜言尤臣子因事納誨之忠也允宜高薦
考試官教諭汪批得敷對之體非徒以文取
也錄之
帝王之克謹天戒非緣戒而後求謹也其
感格有本而銷弭有實故天鑒其令德而
降之嘉福雖異而無損也夫帝王之精氣
上貫于天而下通於烝庶其夙夜閼閔欲
punctuated:
祖宗之美可承，帝王之盛不難致也。高、成且將讓德，區區漢、唐、宋諸君，又何足多談！

第二問
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批：我皇上祗承天戒，昭示臣民，蓋尚實而非尚文也。此作善敷厲揄揚，末進忠悃，尤占偉識，異日必不負所學者。
同考試官教諭王批：心本忠愛，體得對揚，是華國器。
天之實者。
考試官教諭賈批：援古證今，揚厲備至。篇末讜言，尤臣子因事納誨之忠也，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭汪批：得敷對之體，非徒以文取也，錄之。

帝王之克謹天戒，非緣戒而後求謹也；其感格有本，而銷弭有實，故天鑒其令德而降之嘉福，雖異而無損也。夫帝王之精氣，上貫于天，而下通於烝庶。其夙夜閼閔，欲
translation_en:
… the admirable achievements of the imperial ancestors can be carried forward, and the flourishing age of the ancient emperors and kings will not be difficult to attain. Even Gaozong of Yin and King Cheng of Zhou would yield in virtue; as for the mere rulers of Han, Tang, and Song, how could they be worth much discussion!

Second Question
Xu Changzhao
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: Our August Emperor reverently heeds the warnings of Heaven and clearly proclaims this to his officials and people, valuing substance rather than mere form. This essay skillfully sets forth and extols this, and at the end presents loyal sincerity, demonstrating particularly great insight. In the future he will surely not fail what he has learned.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang: His heart is rooted in loyalty and affection, and he grasps the proper form for responding to the sovereign [or: grasping the reality of responding to and extolling Heaven]. He is a vessel to adorn the state.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia: Citing the ancient to substantiate the present, his praise and elaboration are thoroughgoing. The forthright words at the end of the piece especially show the loyalty of a minister offering admonition on the occasion of events; he truly deserves a high recommendation.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: He has grasped the proper form of an expository response. He is not selected merely for his literary style; record it for printing.

That emperors and kings are able to be謹 (heedful) of the warnings of Heaven is not because they seek to be heedful only after a warning occurs; their moving and reaching Heaven has a fundamental root, and their dispelling of calamities has substance. Therefore Heaven beholds their virtuous character and sends down auspicious blessings, so that even if there are anomalies, no harm comes of them. Now the vital spirit of emperors and kings penetrates upward to Heaven and communicates downward to the multitude of the people. Day and night they are sorrowfully concerned [?], desiring…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以握天人之會而固其存何甞一日忘祗
畏哉及至天心示儆而深惟所以迎和卻
沴之實莫急於惠民故側身脩行旣先百
司庶府以請命于天而後舉元元之急而
振業之俾有寧宇故民心得而天意回曆
祚滋固此本實俱得之效而非以循常式
按舊儀示具而已彼循式按儀業祈天者
亦豈能盡罷不舉哉顧感格銷弭之無道
而顓顓以是爲亟圖則末矣故太上脩本
===
實其次脩儀式非是愚難言之玆愚生所
以閱覽往籍而竊窺我
太祖
皇上之能得
天也自昔至治之世豈能必氣運之常休嘉哉
則堯舜被之矣洪水猛獸日聞於區夏而
唐虞終不失爲郅隆之會堯舜不以是故
貶聖名者何哉欽明允恭其自結于天心
者已厚而警予其咨之語於二聖日諄復
punctuated:
以握天人之會而固其存，何甞一日忘祗畏哉？及至天心示儆，而深惟所以迎和卻沴之實，莫急於惠民。故側身脩行，旣先百司庶府以請命于天，而後舉元元之急而振業之，俾有寧宇。故民心得而天意回，曆祚滋固，此本實俱得之效，而非以循常式、按舊儀示具而已。彼循式按儀業祈天者，亦豈能盡罷不舉哉？顧感格銷弭之無道，而顓顓以是爲亟圖，則末矣。故太上脩本實，其次脩儀式，非是，愚難言之。玆愚生所以閱覽往籍，而竊窺我太祖、皇上之能得天也。
自昔至治之世，豈能必氣運之常休嘉哉？則堯、舜被之矣。洪水猛獸，日聞於區夏，而唐、虞終不失爲郅隆之會，堯、舜不以是故貶聖名者，何哉？「欽明」「允恭」，其自結于天心者已厚，而「警予」「其咨」之語，於二聖日諄復…
translation_en:
… thereby grasp the convergence of Heaven and humankind and secure their preservation—how could they ever for a single day forget reverent awe? And when the mind of Heaven manifests a warning, they deeply reflect that in the substantive reality of welcoming harmony and repelling noxious influences, nothing is more urgent than showing kindness to the people. Therefore, humbling themselves and cultivating their conduct, they first lead the hundred officials and various bureaus to plead for the mandate from Heaven, and afterward take up the urgent needs of the common people and succor their livelihoods, ensuring they have peaceful dwellings. Thus, the hearts of the people are won and the will of Heaven is turned back, and the dynastic fortune grows ever more secure. This is the efficacy of attaining both the root and the substance, and not merely following routine formulas and adhering to old ceremonies as an outward formality. As for those who follow formulas and adhere to ceremonies in praying to Heaven, how could such practices be entirely abolished and not performed? Yet if one lacks the proper way to move Heaven and dispel calamities, and instead focuses exclusively on these formalities as the most urgent priority, that is to attend only to the branches. Therefore, the highest course is to cultivate the root and substance, and the next is to cultivate ceremonies and formulas; beyond this, I find it difficult to speak of. This is why I, a foolish student, in perusing past records, have ventured to glimpse how our Grand Progenitor and Your Majesty have been able to win the favor of Heaven.

From of old, in eras of supreme governance, how could one guarantee that the cosmic cycles and auspices were always felicitous? Indeed, Yao and Shun experienced such trials. Great floods and fierce beasts were heard of daily throughout the Chinese realm, yet the Tang and Yu eras ultimately did not fail to be an age of supreme flourishing, and Yao and Shun did not on that account suffer any diminution of their reputations as sages. Why was this? Through "reverent brightness" and "sincere courtesy," the bond they had formed with the mind of Heaven was already deep, and expressions such as "warning me" and "sighing over it" were repeated earnestly day after day by the two sages…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉及考其所以祗事而弭災者非有殊郵
絕迹可具述也羲和分宅璣衡齊政用以
欽若于泱漭無垠之表第不越于民時之
敬授民食之惟時止爾故帝王履常撫順
固無一念不敬天無一念不勤民及遇譴
告則又以帝天視聽主於民心而惠民急
焉是謂本實而堯舜其盛也後世若漢之
文帝以日食求直言數蠲田租宋藝祖因
苦雨焚香禱天曹州饑運粟賑之斯亦足
===
稱勤恤民隱哉試方之堯舜則莫有敢與
者以感格無本而僅能省躬施惠於一時
所謂亡羊補牢第脩儀式爾故曰次也我
太祖高皇帝滌新諸夏統一天人諸所
規畫皆足以繫輿情鞏
明命至詳也居嘗
諭學士宋濂朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民兢
兢業業不敢自逸此其心雖古堯舜何以加
焉乃洪武三年庚戌夏乆不雨欲
punctuated: 焉。及考其所以祗事而弭災者，非有殊郵絕迹可具述也。羲和分宅，璣衡齊政，用以欽若于泱漭無垠之表，第不越于民時之敬授、民食之惟時止爾。故帝王履常撫順，固無一念不敬天，無一念不勤民；及遇譴告，則又以帝天視聽主於民心，而惠民急焉。是謂本實，而堯、舜其盛也。後世若漢之文帝，以日食求直言，數蠲田租；宋藝祖因苦雨，焚香禱天，曹州饑，運粟賑之。斯亦足稱勤恤民隱哉！試方之堯、舜，則莫有敢與者，以感格無本，而僅能省躬施惠於一時，所謂亡羊補牢，第脩儀式爾，故曰次也。我太祖高皇帝滌新諸夏，統一天人，諸所規畫，皆足以繫輿情、鞏明命，至詳也。居嘗諭學士宋濂：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」此其心雖古堯、舜，何以加焉？乃洪武三年庚戌夏，乆不雨，欲
translation_en:
… thereon. Yet when we examine the means by which they reverently served Heaven and averted calamities, there were no extraordinary marvels or unmatched feats that could be recounted in detail. Commissioning the Xi and He brothers to reside in their respective quarters and using the armillary sphere and sighting tube to order the seven governance-regulators—whereby they reverently conformed to Heaven across the vast and boundless expanse—amounted to nothing more than respectfully granting the seasons to the people and attending timely to the people's food. Therefore, when emperors and kings tread the normal path and rule in times of harmony, they inherently have not a single thought that does not revere Heaven, nor a single thought that is not diligent toward the people; and when they encounter portents and warnings from Heaven, taking the view that the seeing and hearing of the Sovereign in Heaven rests upon the hearts of the people, they make showing kindness to the people their urgent priority. This is what is called the fundamental substance, and Yao and Shun were its pinnacle.

In later ages, rulers such as Emperor Wen of the Han sought frank remonstrance because of a solar eclipse and repeatedly remitted the land tax; the Founding Ancestor (Taizu) of the Song burned incense and prayed to Heaven on account of excessive rains, and when there was famine in Caozhou, transported grain to relieve it. Were these not also worthy of being praised as diligent compassion for the sufferings of the people? Yet if we compare them with Yao and Shun, none would dare place them on the same level. That is because their moving of Heaven lacked the fundamental root, and they were merely able to examine themselves and bestow favors temporarily—what is called mending the fold after the sheep are lost, merely cultivating the outward ceremony; hence they are called secondary.

Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), cleansed and renewed the Chinese lands and unified the realms of Heaven and humanity; all that he planned and instituted was fully sufficient to bind popular sentiment and consolidate the Bright Mandate, down to the finest detail. In ordinary times he once instructed the Academician Song Lian 宋濂: "In acting as sovereign, above We stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, and below We stand in awe of the millions of the common people, cautious and industrious, not daring to indulge in ease." Even with the ancient Yao and Shun, how could such a mind be surpassed? Then, in the summer of the geng戌 year, the third year of the Hongwu reign (1370), when there had been no rain for a long time, he wished to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
躬禱於山川壇先命
皇后與諸妃執爨為農家食
皇太子諸王供饋于齋所至期素服草履徒
步詣于壇席藁露坐晝曝日中夜臥于地
衣不解帶
皇太子捧榼進蔬食雜麻麥菽粟已而大雨
至九年秋以七曜紊度求直言十八年春
以五星竝見求直言二十六年夏以太白
經天
===
京師大旱求直言諸以軍興水旱𧖟蝗雷震
免租者十有六賑者三贖鬻子者一夫天
厭元亂民幸得脫湯火已戴
聖祖之德厚矣而灑惠弛征用以厚集瘡痍祗
承天戒若此故雖有災沴不敵禎符茂啓
無疆之曆迄于今是賴非
聖祖之得天有是哉頃者象緯失次
皇上既惕心引慝
帥先羣臣復
punctuated: 躬禱於山川壇，先命皇后與諸妃執爨為農家食，皇太子、諸王供饋于齋所。至期，素服草履，徒步詣于壇，席藁露坐，晝曝日中，夜臥于地，衣不解帶。皇太子捧榼進蔬食，雜麻麥菽粟。已而大雨至。九年秋，以七曜紊度求直言；十八年春，以五星竝見求直言；二十六年夏，以太白經天、京師大旱求直言；諸以軍興、水旱、𧖟蝗、雷震免租者十有六，賑者三，贖鬻子者一。夫天厭元亂，民幸得脫湯火，已戴聖祖之德厚矣；而灑惠弛征，用以厚集瘡痍、祗承天戒若此，故雖有災沴，不敵禎符，茂啓無疆之曆，迄于今是賴。非聖祖之得天，有是哉？頃者象緯失次，皇上既惕心引慝，帥先羣臣，復
translation_en: …pray in person at the Altar of Mountains and Rivers, he first ordered the Empress and the imperial consorts to tend the stoves and prepare peasant fare, while the Heir Apparent and the princes served the food at the place of fasting. When the appointed day arrived, dressed in plain garments and straw sandals, he walked on foot to the altar, where he sat in the open on a straw mat, exposed to the sun by day and sleeping on the ground by night without unfastening his sash. The Heir Apparent held the food containers and presented vegetable fare mixed with hemp seeds, wheat, beans, and millet. Soon afterward, a great rain fell. In the autumn of the ninth year (1376), because the seven luminaries were out of their regular courses, he sought直言 (forthright counsel); in the spring of the eighteenth year (1385), because the five planets appeared simultaneously, he sought forthright counsel; in the summer of the twenty-sixth year (1393), because Venus crossed the meridian in daylight and there was a great drought in the capital, he sought forthright counsel. Moreover, on account of military mobilizations, floods and droughts, plagues of caterpillars and locusts, and lightning strikes, he remitted taxes sixteen times, provided famine relief three times, and redeemed children who had been sold once. Now, Heaven had grown weary of the disorders of the Yuan, and the people, fortunate to escape boiling water and fire, already cherished the profound virtue of our Sacred Ancestor. Yet he showered benevolence and relaxed exactions in order to generously comfort the wounded and afflicted and reverently heed the warnings of Heaven in this manner. Therefore, although there were calamities and noxious influences, they were no match for the auspicious omens, flourishingly opening up a boundless dynastic destiny upon which we rely down to the present day. Had our Sacred Ancestor not won the favor of Heaven, could this have been so? Recently, the celestial bodies have strayed from their stations. His Majesty has already been fearful at heart and taken the blame upon himself, leading the officials, and furthermore…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
前志不載若幽求子今亦罕傳之矣乃荀
悅申鑒當時號為小荀子與徐幹中論頗
近正理皆可附儒家之後何通事之弗錄
也至其首論諸子為入道見志之書其說
未敢深信而孟軻之淵懿博達固所謂絕
塵而奔者亦與諸子槩列此其見與班氏
何異若班氏之言曰使其人遭明王聖主
得其所折中皆股肱之材也嗟嗟此豈蘇
張公孫龍輩能當之乎又何罪夫劉通事
===
也自是則文中鹿門可綴於儒齊丘無能
天隱玄真可歸於道餘蓋更僕未易數矣
大都諸子皆出於漢後多倣象為之或不
甚雅馴姑不遠論即以鬻子捕獸逐麋之
對文王不以為耄夫而師事之因自詮次
其言為百家之始而文義簡短不類周初
且班志僅六篇至逢行珪表上乃有十四
篇得非後世依託而增益之者乎故舉鬻
子而諸子可例也乃執事下詢欲舉諸子
punctuated: 前志不載，若《幽求子》，今亦罕傳之矣。乃荀悅《申鑒》，當時號為「小荀子」，與徐幹《中論》頗近正理，皆可附儒家之後，何通事之弗錄也？至其首論諸子為入道見志之書，其說未敢深信；而孟軻之淵懿博達，固所謂絕塵而奔者，亦與諸子槩列，此其見與班氏何異？若班氏之言曰：「使其人遭明王聖主，得其所折中，皆股肱之材也。」嗟嗟！此豈蘇、張、公孫龍輩能當之乎？又何罪夫劉通事也！自是，則《文中》、《鹿門》可綴於儒，《齊丘》、《無能》、《天隱》、《玄真》可歸於道，餘蓋更僕未易數矣。大都諸子皆出於漢後，多倣象為之，或不甚雅馴。姑不遠論，即以《鬻子》捕獸逐麋之對，文王不以為耄夫而師事之，因自詮次其言，為百家之始；而文義簡短，不類周初。且《班志》僅六篇，至逢行珪表上，乃有十四篇，得非後世依託而增益之者乎？故舉《鬻子》而諸子可例也。乃執事下詢，欲舉諸子
translation_en:
… were not recorded in previous bibliographic treatises, while a work like the Master Youqiu (Youqiu zi 幽求子) is also rarely transmitted today. Yet Xun Yue's 荀悅 Extended Reflections (Shenjian 申鑒)—known in its own time as the "Lesser Xunzi"—along with Xu Gan's 徐幹 Balanced Discourses (Zhonglun 中論), are both quite close to orthodox principle and could well be appended after the Confucian school; why then did the Receptionist [Liu Xie 劉勰] fail to record them? As for his opening argument that the Various Masters are books for entering the Way and manifesting one's aspirations, I dare not fully credit that view; moreover, someone as profound, admirable, broad, and penetrating as Meng Ke 孟軻 [Mencius]—truly one who, as the saying goes, "gallops ahead leaving the dust behind"—is likewise lumped together indiscriminately with the other Masters. How does this view differ from that of Ban Gu 班固? For in Ban's words: "Had those men encountered an enlightened king or a sage ruler and found proper balance through him, they would all have been talents fit to serve as his right-hand ministers." Alas! How could the likes of Su Qin 蘇秦, Zhang Yi 張儀, or Gongsun Long 公孫龍 possibly be worthy of such praise? And given that, how can one blame Receptionist Liu?

From that point onward, the Master Explaining the Center (Wenzhong zi 文中子) and the Master of Lumen (Lumen zi 鹿門子) may be appended to the Confucians, while Qi Qiu 齊丘 [Hua shu 化書], the Master of Inaction (Wuneng zi 無能子), the Master of Heavenly Concealment (Tianyin zi 天隱子), and the Master of Mysterious Truth (Xuanzhen zi 玄真子) may be assigned to the Daoists; as for the rest, they could not easily be counted even if one changed attendants while reciting them. For the most part, the Masters that appeared after the Han were largely produced by imitation, and at times their style is not particularly refined or orthodox. Setting aside more distant examples, take the Master Yu (Yuzi 鬻子) and his reply concerning catching beasts and chasing elk: King Wen 文王 did not dismiss him as a senile old man, but served him as a teacher and consequently compiled and arranged his words himself, making them the beginning of the Hundred Schools. Yet the style and meaning are brief and curtailed, not resembling works of the early Zhou. Furthermore, Ban Gu's treatise records only six chapters, whereas by the time Feng Xinggui 逢行珪 presented it with a memorial, there were fourteen chapters—could this be anything other than later generations falsely attributing writings to him and expanding the text? Thus, by citing the Master Yu, the other Masters may be judged by analogy. Now Your Excellency inquiries of us below, wishing to take all the Various Masters…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而別以九流舉九流而歸之六家而務求
不詭於六籍之義爲意甚盛愚則以班志
區囿已定無容復述而雜家多本於道縱
橫持論頗涉於名農事有羲和授時之義
於陰陽家頗近卽函九爲六亦無不可者
第求以不詭於六籍之義則難言之矣夫
六籍爲敎舉帝王賢聖之蘊奧具載其中
其分經辨義則若春夏秋冬各有令序無
相越也其會經合義則若眞精元氣自爲
===
脉絡無相離也彼諸子者曾庶幾有一於
是乎故覽華而食實棄邪而採正雖在其
人之所决擇而終不可以烏附之僅效媿
吾稻粱者此經子之辨也顧農雜縱橫諸
家其術在今頗衰止不足深較今所病者
惟道與儒而儒道二家最後出者又惟釋
氏當周末釋起西竺其敎略類道流而加
以超脫寂滅爲宗意青牛老氏旣適流沙
而其敎始出亦道家之別支而獨詣者也
punctuated:
而別以九流，舉九流而歸之六家，而務求不詭於六籍之義，爲意甚盛。愚則以班志區囿已定，無容復述。而雜家多本於道，縱橫持論頗涉於名，農事有羲和授時之義，於陰陽家頗近，卽函九爲六，亦無不可者。第求以不詭於六籍之義，則難言之矣。夫六籍爲敎，舉帝王賢聖之蘊奧具載其中。其分經辨義，則若春夏秋冬各有令序，無相越也；其會經合義，則若眞精元氣自爲脉絡，無相離也。彼諸子者，曾庶幾有一於是乎？故覽華而食實，棄邪而採正，雖在其人之所决擇，而終不可以烏附之僅效，媿吾稻粱者，此經子之辨也。
顧農、雜、縱橫諸家，其術在今頗衰止，不足深較。今所病者惟道與儒，而儒、道二家最後出者又惟釋氏。當周末，釋起西竺，其敎略類道流，而加以超脫寂滅爲宗。意青牛老氏旣適流沙而其敎始出，亦道家之別支而獨詣者也。
translation_en:
… and classify them into the Nine Streams, then take the Nine Streams and reduce them to the Six Schools, while striving to seek out those meanings that do not deviate from the Six Classics—this intention is most noble. Yet in my humble view, the classifications in Ban Gu's "Treatise on Literature" (Ban zhi) are already fixed and need not be recounted again. Moreover, the Eclectic School (Zajia) is mostly rooted in the Daoist School (Daojia), the arguments maintained by the School of Diplomacy (Zongheng) touch considerably upon the School of Names (Mingjia), and the Agriculturalists' (Nong) affairs possess the meaning of Xi and He granting the seasons, bringing them quite close to the Yin-Yang School; thus, even if one were to subsume the Nine into the Six, there would be nothing improper in it. However, if one seeks in them meanings that do not deviate from the Six Classics, that is difficult to speak of indeed. Now, as for the teaching of the Six Classics, all the profound mysteries of emperors, kings, worthies, and sages are completely contained therein. When one divides the Classics to distinguish their meanings, they are like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, each having its seasonal order without overstepping one another; when one synthesizes the Classics to unite their meanings, they are like true essence and primordial vital energy (yuanqi), naturally forming an interconnected network of vessels without separating from one another. Have those Various Masters ever come close to possessing even a single aspect of this? Therefore, admiring the blossoms while eating the fruit, and discarding the heterodox while selecting the orthodox, although it lies in the individual's own discernment and choice, one ultimately cannot allow the mere occasional efficacy of乌附 (aconite/wolfsbane) to put our rice and millet to shame—this is the distinction between the Classics and the Masters.

However, as for the Agriculturalist, Eclectic, Diplomacy, and other schools, their arts have in the present day largely declined and ceased, so they are not worth examining deeply. What causes affliction today is solely Daoism in relation to Confucianism, and emerging after both the Confucian and Daoist schools is solely Buddhism (Shishi). Toward the end of the Zhou dynasty, Buddhism arose in Western India (Xizhu); its teachings slightly resembled the Daoist current, while further taking transcendence and nirvana (extinction) as its fundamental tenet. I suspect that after Laozi on his dark ox went off to the Flowing Sands, this teaching first emerged—it too is a separate branch of the Daoist school that reached its own unique extreme.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
自漢明帝求得其書初尚不敢列於諸家
其後始漸起而與道爲二後又漸起而與
儒道鼎足爲三今則無論儒道卽神聖若
吾夫子者亦幾與分庭而爭席矣在
國初爲文引用老子莊列者有禁今則佛經
僧錄竄入其中輒矜炫以爲獨得其靡曼
不根殊甚此所以
功令數下而禁戒之諄切也今欲正經術其
要莫急於辨意見夫意見者固吾心之虛
===
靈所觸而通者也業豈能盡廢然其端有
正有私士之潛心經術積久而貫通以試
之用輒資深逢原出入不悖所聞此意見
之正也非是私矣其經術非能熟習而精
詣之也其佛老莊列亦非能熟習而精詣
之也第以其質之偶得於穎悟涉獵其藩
復胷度而臆决之嘵嘵然以語諸人曰儒
也以試之天下國家其用正佛老也以用
之身心性命其義精久而援引二氏附和
punctuated: 自漢明帝求得其書，初尚不敢列於諸家，其後始漸起而與道爲二，後又漸起而與儒、道鼎足爲三。今則無論儒、道，卽神聖若吾夫子者，亦幾與分庭而爭席矣。在國初，爲文引用《老子》、莊、列者有禁；今則佛經、僧錄竄入其中，輒矜炫以爲獨得，其靡曼不根殊甚。此所以功令數下，而禁戒之諄切也。今欲正經術，其要莫急於辨意見。夫意見者，固吾心之虛靈所觸而通者也，業豈能盡廢？然其端有正有私。士之潛心經術，積久而貫通，以試之用，輒資深逢原，出入不悖所聞，此意見之正也，非是私矣。其經術非能熟習而精詣之也，其佛、老、莊、列亦非能熟習而精詣之也，第以其質之偶得於穎悟，涉獵其藩，復胷度而臆决之，嘵嘵然以語諸人曰：「儒也，以試之天下國家，其用正；佛、老也，以用之身心性命，其義精。」久而援引二氏，附和
translation_en:
Since Emperor Ming of the Han (Han Mingdi 漢明帝) sought and obtained their texts, at first they still did not dare to rank themselves among the various schools of thought. Only later did Buddhism gradually rise to form a pair with Daoism, and later still it gradually rose to stand as a tripod of three alongside Confucianism and Daoism. Today, not to speak of Confucianism and Daoism as traditions, even towards a divine sage like our Master [Confucius], they nearly claim equal status as host and guest and vie with him for the seat of honor. In the early days of our Dynasty, citing the Laozi, Zhuangzi, or Liezi in compositions was prohibited. Today, however, Buddhist sutras and monastic records are slipped into them, and writers invariably boast and show off, considering this their unique insight; such florid and baseless writing is extreme indeed. This is why examination regulations have been handed down repeatedly to prohibit and warn against it so earnestly.

Today, if we wish to rectify classical learning, nothing is more urgent than distinguishing among personal opinions. Now, opinions are indeed what the empty and numinous faculty of our mind penetrates when stirred by contact; how could they be entirely abolished in one's studies? Yet in their beginnings, some are orthodox and some are selfishly biased. When a scholar immerses his mind in classical learning, accumulating it over a long time until he achieves thorough comprehension, and then tests it in practical application, he invariably draws deeply upon it to meet the source on every side, going in and out without contradicting what he has learned—this is orthodox opinion, and not something selfishly biased. [As for others,] it is not that they are able to thoroughly practice and attain refined mastery of classical learning, nor that they are able to thoroughly practice and attain refined mastery of the Buddha, Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Liezi. Merely because their natural disposition happens to hit upon some clever insight, they dabble at the outer hedges of those teachings, and then gauge them in their own breasts and decide by conjecture, clamoring as they tell people: "Confucianism is to be tested in the realm and the state, for its practical application is orthodox; Buddhism and Daoism are to be applied to body, mind, and human nature and destiny, for their meaning is subtle." Over time, they cite the two teachings, latching them onto…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以經術而舉世鶩之矣故聽其說若不異
於聖人而繹其旨又若蘇張之縱橫公孫
龍之堅白又徐而覈其實又若似於無非
無舉之鄉原是說之難持者也故旣辨意
見而每歲所取士必嚴核所誦法其浮誕
無當者卽負藻才輒擯不錄則士爲學必
知守六經其爲文必不悖六經正道明而
私說息矣
第四問
===
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批名賢二祠風化所關此對
尚論先哲軒輊較然足覘嚮往末欲推明禮意詳覈
奏
報尤得愼重之指可錄
考試官教諭賈批評品甚精而議處更有灼
見
考試官教諭汪批稽覈詳確
昔之君子其砥行植業非以爲名也人或
punctuated:
以經術，而舉世鶩之矣。故聽其說，若不異於聖人；而繹其旨，又若蘇、張之縱橫，公孫龍之堅白；又徐而覈其實，又若似於無非無舉之鄉原，是說之難持者也。故旣辨意見，而每歲所取士，必嚴核所誦法，其浮誕無當者，卽負藻才，輒擯不錄。則士爲學必知守六經，其爲文必不悖六經，正道明而私說息矣。

第四問
陶明禮
同考試官訓導丁批：〔名、賢二祠，風化所關。此對尚論先哲，軒輊較然，足覘嚮往。末欲推明禮意，詳覈奏報，尤得愼重之指。可錄。〕
考試官教諭賈批：〔評品甚精，而議處更有灼見。〕
考試官教諭汪批：〔稽覈詳確。〕

昔之君子，其砥行植業，非以爲名也。人或
translation_en:
…with classical learning, and the whole world runs after them. Thus, when one listens to their doctrines, they seem no different from those of the sages; yet when one unpacks their purport, they are like the vertical and horizontal alliances of Su Qin 蘇秦 and Zhang Yi 張儀, or the "hard and white" sophistries of Gongsun Long 公孫龍; and when one calmly examines their reality, they resemble the "village honest men" (xiangyuan 鄉原), who have nothing to be criticized and nothing to be praised—such doctrines are hard to guard against. Therefore, having distinguished between correct and private views, in selecting scholars each year we must strictly verify the models they recite and follow; those who are superficial, absurd, and wide of the mark, even if they possess ornate literary talent, should immediately be rejected and not recorded. Then in pursuing their studies, scholars will surely know to abide by the Six Classics, and in composing their essays they will surely not go against the Six Classics; the correct Way will be made clear and private doctrines will cease.

Question 4
Tao Mingli 陶明禮
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Ding 丁: [The Two Shrines of Eminent Officials and Local Worthies are vital to moral transformation. This response evaluates past worthies, clearly distinguishing their relative merits, which suffices to show the candidate's aspirations. At the end, his desire to elucidate the intent of the rites and carefully verify memorials and reports to the throne especially grasps the principle of prudence. Worthy of selection.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia 賈: [His evaluations are very precise, and his discussion of measures shows even greater insight.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang 汪: [His investigation and verification are detailed and accurate.]

When the gentlemen of antiquity whetted their conduct and established their achievements, they did not do so for the sake of reputation. If others happened to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
舉名而歸之則其舉之者必且惴惴然若
操九鼎捧璧玉惟恐一不當而至於毀也
故所舉之賢益彰而可以風厲于當世後
之君子其身已有意於爲名其子若孫又
欲以其名爲祖父光寵而議舉者與柄舉
者又且重違其欲名之心或徇于情怵于
勢而掩于利舉爼豆之大典雷同附和以
歸諸無異常人之身而卓犖瑰瑋者或遺
於聞見靡所章勸甚無謂也此豈崇祀指
===
哉按周制凡有功紀于王之太常祭于大
烝司勳詔之爲典凡六王功曰勳國功曰
功民功曰庸事功曰勞治功曰力戰功曰
多匪是者弗得濫及其道德爲後學準繩
則秩祀瞽宗次亦祀于社以示不忘玆先
王之崇德報功章往而勸來者禮意最深
遠矣
明興稽古經制爲名宦鄉賢二祠于學宮士之
丕懋勳猷行能信於鄉國足應祀典者各
punctuated: 舉名而歸之，則其舉之者必且惴惴然，若操九鼎、捧璧玉，惟恐一不當而至於毀也。故所舉之賢益彰，而可以風厲于當世。後之君子，其身已有意於爲名，其子若孫又欲以其名爲祖父光寵，而議舉者與柄舉者又且重違其欲名之心，或徇于情，怵于勢，而掩于利，舉爼豆之大典，雷同附和，以歸諸無異常人之身；而卓犖瑰瑋者，或遺於聞見，靡所章勸，甚無謂也。此豈崇祀指哉？按周制，凡有功紀于王之太常，祭于大烝，司勳詔之爲典凡六：王功曰勳，國功曰功，民功曰庸，事功曰勞，治功曰力，戰功曰多；匪是者，弗得濫及。其道德爲後學準繩，則秩祀瞽宗，次亦祀于社，以示不忘。玆先王之崇德報功，章往而勸來者，禮意最深遠矣。明興，稽古經制，爲名宦、鄉賢二祠于學宮，士之丕懋勳猷、行能信於鄉國、足應祀典者，各
translation_en:
… elevate his reputation and attribute it to him, then those who recommended him would surely be filled with trepidation, as if holding the Nine Tripods or cradling a jade disk, fearing only that a single misstep might lead to ruin. Therefore, the worthies who were recommended became all the more illustrious and could inspire and rouse the age. Among gentlemen of later times, they themselves already harbor the intention of seeking fame, and their sons and grandsons likewise wish to use that fame to bring glory and favor to their fathers and grandfathers. Meanwhile, those who deliberate on the recommendations and those who hold the authority to approve them are further reluctant to go against this desire for fame. Some yield to personal sentiment, some are cowed by power and influence, and some are blinded by profit. Taking the great institution of sacrificial vessels, they echo one another in blind conformity and bestow it upon persons no different from ordinary men; whereas those who are truly preeminent and extraordinary are sometimes overlooked in what is heard and seen, leaving nothing by which to display encouragement. This is utterly meaningless! How could this be the purpose of honoring them with sacrifices?

According to the institutions of the Zhou, all who had merit were recorded on the King's Grand Banner and sacrificed to at the Great Winter Sacrifice, as proclaimed by the Director of Merit (Sixun) under six categories: merit on behalf of the royal house was called supreme merit (xun); merit on behalf of the state was called state merit (gong); merit on behalf of the people was called civil merit (yong); merit in handling affairs was called diligent service (lao); merit in administration was called administrative force (li); and merit in warfare was called martial achievement (duo). Anyone who did not fall under these categories was not permitted to be improperly included. As for those whose morality and virtue served as a standard for later scholars, they received ranked sacrifices in the Blind Musicians' Academy (Guzong), and next below them were sacrificed to at the local altars of the soil, to show that they were not forgotten. In this way, the former kings revered virtue and rewarded merit, illuminating the past to encourage the future—the meaning of their rites was most profound and far-reaching indeed.

When the Ming arose, it examined ancient institutions and established the two shrines of Eminent Officials and Local Worthies within the Confucian schools. As for scholars who greatly exerted themselves in meritorious plans, or whose conduct and abilities were trusted in their local communities and states so as to be worthy of answering the sacrificial statutes, each…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以所由舉入祠而歲令握紀之臣謹察其
不如法者輒得裁罷每二丁釋奠禮畢有
司率博士謁祠唯謹誠重之也粵西故仕
國其士習樸茂頗有先民之遺風故其爲
賢亦略相等今考諸故牒宦績自史祿而
下凡百三十七人獻民自陳元而下亦百
二十七人不具述述其較著者則賈琮爲
刺史察民所爲盜之故因而撫荒蠲役戮
止渠魁百姓以安巷路間皆以來晚歌之
===
得便計矣而許仲宣不待奏報輒罷所部
兵俾不委命於炎瘴者殆萬餘人無何交
州送款上疏待罪見何定也而余靖之帥
二廣幾十年恩信被於異域其功尤足多
者若陳臨閔死囚之無嗣令其妻得侍獄
中舉子雖情涉姑息其事或難盡循而哀
矜之仁不可少也士燮守交趾中原人士
往依避難者以百數其保境功比於竇融
偉矣陳坦然單騎行賊壘爲書約矢射圍
punctuated: 以所由舉入祠，而歲令握紀之臣謹察其不如法者，輒得裁罷。每二丁釋奠禮畢，有司率博士謁祠唯謹，誠重之也。粵西故仕國，其士習樸茂，頗有先民之遺風，故其爲賢亦略相等。今考諸故牒，宦績自史祿而下凡百三十七人，獻民自陳元而下亦百二十七人，不具述。述其較著者：則賈琮爲刺史，察民所爲盜之故，因而撫荒蠲役，戮止渠魁，百姓以安，巷路間皆以來晚歌之，得便計矣；而許仲宣不待奏報，輒罷所部兵，俾不委命於炎瘴者殆萬餘人，無何交州送款，上疏待罪，見何定也；而余靖之帥二廣幾十年，恩信被於異域，其功尤足多者。若陳臨閔死囚之無嗣，令其妻得侍獄中舉子，雖情涉姑息，其事或難盡循，而哀矜之仁不可少也。士燮守交趾，中原人士往依避難者以百數，其保境功比於竇融，偉矣；陳坦然單騎行賊壘，爲書約矢射圍
translation_en: …are nominated and inducted into the shrines according to their respective merits, while each year the officials holding disciplinary authority are ordered to carefully inspect them, immediately removing any who do not conform to the regulations. Whenever the sacrifices of the two ding days are concluded, the local authorities lead the Erudites to pay reverence at the shrines with the utmost solemnity, for they truly attach great importance to them. Western Yue [Guangxi] has long been a land that produces officials; the customs of its literati are simple and substantial, retaining much of the lingering spirit of the ancients, and thus the worthies among them are roughly comparable in both categories. Examining the old records today, those noted for official achievements from Shi Lu 史祿 downward number one hundred and thirty-seven in all, while local worthies from Chen Yuan 陳元 downward likewise number one hundred and twenty-seven. Without recounting them all, let us mention the more prominent among them. When Jia Cong 賈琮 served as Regional Inspector, he investigated the reasons why the people had turned to banditry, and accordingly pacified the荒-stricken areas, remitted labor services, and executed only the ringleaders. The common people were thereby settled, and in the lanes and roads all sang of how late he had come—he had hit upon an expedient plan indeed! Yet Xu Zhongxuan 許仲宣, without waiting for a reply to his memorial, on his own initiative disbanded the troops under his command, thus sparing over ten thousand men from abandoning their lives to the fiery miasmas; before long Jiaozhou submitted in allegiance, and he presented a memorial awaiting punishment—how resolute was his discernment! And Yu Jing 余靖 commanded the two Guang provinces for nearly ten years, his grace and good faith extending to foreign lands, so that his achievements are especially worthy of praise. As for Chen Lin 陳臨, who pitied a condemned prisoner for having no heir and allowed the man's wife to attend him in prison so that he might beget a son—although his feelings bordered on laxity and such a practice could hardly be followed in every case, his compassionate benevolence is not to be slighted. When Shi Xie 士燮 governed Jiaozhi, men of learning from the Central Plains who went to rely on him for refuge from chaos numbered in the hundreds; his merit in preserving the territory, comparable to that of Dou Rong 竇融, was magnificent indeed! Chen Tanran 陳坦然 rode alone to the rebel ramparts and wrote a letter tied to an arrow to shoot into the besieged…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中諭叛卒禍福無何卒降而賊自平事聞
賜錦袍銀帶悉謝不受義何高也而蔣允
濟守邕管恩信結於民心思之如一日庶
幾廩廩德讓君子之風焉若趙觀文再試
上第以言忤宰相意輒謝病歸雖所志未
盡効於時而嘉遯之節不可易也故其英
聲駿烈雖去今數百餘年而猶能使人仰
慕不輟藉令俎豆者而皆若前數公豈不
光我庠序油然觀感而興起者乎顧有或
===
謬不然於今者何也其内有所親厚則尺
寸之功而揚詡之以為蓋世也其外有所
憑藉則取節之行而藻飾之以為邁夷也
其下有所結納則里巷之譽而畀翼之以
為懿爍也故有奮臆妄議持方寸之楮鼓
其喙於握紀者之前不踰月已得報祀何
後世之多賢而祀易成也則前所謂情徇
勢怵而利之掩也頃者
聖天子深惟崇報之義
punctuated: 中，諭叛卒禍福，無何卒降而賊自平，事聞，賜錦袍銀帶，悉謝不受，義何高也！而蔣允濟守邕管，恩信結於民心，思之如一日，庶幾廩廩德讓君子之風焉。若趙觀文再試上第，以言忤宰相意，輒謝病歸，雖所志未盡効於時，而嘉遯之節不可易也。故其英聲駿烈，雖去今數百餘年，而猶能使人仰慕不輟。藉令俎豆者而皆若前數公，豈不光我庠序，油然觀感而興起者乎？顧有或謬不然於今者，何也？其内有所親厚，則尺寸之功而揚詡之以為蓋世也；其外有所憑藉，則取節之行而藻飾之以為邁夷也；其下有所結納，則里巷之譽而畀翼之以為懿爍也。故有奮臆妄議，持方寸之楮，鼓其喙於握紀者之前，不踰月已得報祀。何後世之多賢而祀易成也？則前所謂情徇勢怵而利之掩也。頃者，聖天子深惟崇報之義，
translation_en: … into the besieged encirclement, instructing the rebel soldiers on the consequences of good and bad fortune; before long, the soldiers surrendered and the rebels were naturally pacified. When the matter was reported to the throne, he was bestowed a brocade robe and a silver belt, all of which he declined to accept—how lofty was his righteousness! Furthermore, when Jiang Yunji 蔣允濟 guarded Yongguan 邕管, his grace and trustworthiness bound the hearts of the people, who remembered him continuously as if for a single day; he nearly attained the awe-inspiring demeanor of a gentleman of virtuous deference. As for Zhao Guanwen 趙觀文, he passed the re-examination in the highest grade, but because his words offended the Grand Councilor's wishes, he promptly pleaded illness and returned home. Although his ambitions were not fully realized in his time, his integrity in noble withdrawal cannot be lightly dismissed.
