Therefore, although their illustrious reputations and great achievements are separated from the present by several hundred years, they still cause people to look up to and admire them unceasingly. Supposing that those who receive sacrificial offerings in the temples were all like the several gentlemen mentioned above, would that not bring glory to our local schools and spontaneously inspire those who observe them to rise up in emulation? Yet at present there are cases that go absurdly contrary to this—why is that? Internally, where there is personal favoritism, a mere inch of merit is extolled and boasted of as surpassing the age; externally, where there is reliance on powerful backing, a single commendable act is embellished and dressed up as transcending the ordinary; below, where there is collusion and patronage, mere village praise is boosted and given wings as shining virtue. Thus there are those who, giving vent to subjective whims and reckless proposals, hold a square inch of paper and wag their tongues before the authorities who hold the reins of governance, and in less than a month have already obtained approval for shrine sacrifices. Why are there so many worthies in later ages, and why are sacrificial shrines so easily established? It is what was referred to earlier as yielding to personal feelings, being cowed by influence, and being blinded by profit. Recently, His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven, deeply reflecting on the principle of honoring and repaying merit, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
特採言官疏
令禮官下所司釐正而爲籍
奏之
德意甚厚今長吏方兢兢奉行日求所不應祀
者亟罷之以儆煩濫但其故老無徴載籍
希闊靡所考慿卽銖稱而櫛數之未必無
遺議者稽覈難也且其前已令得冒祠今
卽罷去於章勸之楮已損故不若及今而
愼爲之禁滌時之弊而原禮之意以檢律
===
之庶可止也何謂時弊曰今之議舉者習
於文矣不考論其行事而詳著之以待稽
覈惟以獎飾浮詞虛張之故稱宦蹟則曰
約已裕民頌思勿替矣誦獻民則曰好義
循禮無問顯晦矣欲不與則恐賢而見遺
欲與則屢詢而乖實甚則有貴顯異籍未
甞睹其平生徒以其祖籍之偶同則曰此
吾鄉之哲者相率而牽引之而不知其無
當也而白屋寒畯或有高義卓行庶幾於
punctuated:
特採言官疏，令禮官下所司釐正而爲籍奏之，德意甚厚。今長吏方兢兢奉行，日求所不應祀者亟罷之，以儆煩濫。但其故老無徴，載籍希闊，靡所考慿，卽銖稱而櫛數之，未必無遺議者，稽覈難也。且其前已令得冒祠，今卽罷去，於章勸之楮已損，故不若及今而愼爲之禁，滌時之弊而原禮之意以檢律之，庶可止也。

何謂時弊？曰：今之議舉者習於文矣，不考論其行事而詳著之以待稽覈，惟以獎飾浮詞虛張之。故稱宦蹟，則曰「約已裕民，頌思勿替」矣；誦獻民，則曰「好義循禮，無問顯晦」矣。欲不與，則恐賢而見遺；欲與，則屢詢而乖實。甚則有貴顯異籍，未甞睹其平生，徒以其祖籍之偶同，則曰「此吾鄉之哲者」，相率而牽引之，而不知其無當也；而白屋寒畯，或有高義卓行，庶幾於
translation_en:
…specially adopted the memorial of a Censor, ordering the ritual officials to instruct the relevant authorities to rectify the matter, compile a register, and report it to the throne—His virtuous intent is exceedingly generous. Right now, senior local officials are conscientiously carrying this out, daily seeking those who ought not to be enshrined and promptly removing them so as to warn against proliferation and abuse. Yet because the elders provide no corroboration and written records are sparse, there is nothing to rely on for verification; even if one weighs them ounce by ounce and counts them tooth by tooth like a comb, it is not certain there will be no lingering criticisms, for investigation and verification are difficult. Moreover, since in the past they were already allowed to falsely enter the shrines, even if they are removed now, the records meant to display encouragement have already been compromised. Therefore, it is better to carefully establish prohibitions starting from the present, cleansing away current abuses and tracing the original meaning of the rites to examine and regulate them; only then may the practice be halted.

What are the current abuses? Those who propose candidates for enshrinement today are accustomed to superficial rhetoric. They do not examine and discuss a person's actual deeds and record them in detail to await verification, but merely exaggerate them with flattering, empty words. Thus, when praising official achievements, they say: "He restrained himself and enriched the people, and praise and longing for him have never ceased." When extolling local worthies, they say: "He loved righteousness and abided by ritual propriety, whether prominent or obscure." If the authorities wish not to grant enshrinement, they fear a worthy person might be overlooked; if they wish to grant it, repeated inquiries reveal discrepancies with the facts. In extreme cases, there are noble and prominent figures registered elsewhere whose lives the locals have never witnessed; merely because their ancestral registration happens to be the same, people say, "This is a wise man of our locality," leading one another to drag him in without realizing how inappropriate it is. Meanwhile, humble scholars from thatched huts who may possess lofty righteousness and outstanding conduct, nearly approaching…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
太丘叔度之流者輒棄不復道則徇迹之
過也故議舉者務必詳述其事一切爲浮
漫語者罷之其異籍而不出其鄕亦不必
援引之以爲重果行義無玷卽隱約窮巷
亦與表見而又推明禮意以示之禮之祀
于大烝以功六也試桉其所表樹於六者
孰當如僅守尺寸持祿無顯過者不得槩
祠禮之祀于瞽宗以道德也今所稱賢于
鄕者試詰其行事于孔氏之道率履幾何
===
闡發幾何不如是則無非無譽者又慮其
愿也亦不得從先進之林而登之祀典故
實者不能遺而虛者不能飾而典禮可正
也今
令甲每
旌表孝節必以疏
聞候
報可良以重風化也俎豆於聖人之宮爲百世
規其隆渥豈下
punctuated: 太丘、叔度之流者，輒棄不復道，則徇迹之過也。故議舉者務必詳述其事，一切爲浮漫語者罷之；其異籍而不出其鄕，亦不必援引之以爲重；果行義無玷，卽隱約窮巷，亦與表見。而又推明禮意以示之。禮之祀于大烝，以功六也，試桉其所表樹，於六者孰當？如僅守尺寸、持祿無顯過者，不得槩祠。禮之祀于瞽宗，以道德也，今所稱賢于鄕者，試詰其行事，于孔氏之道率履幾何？闡發幾何？不如是，則無非無譽者，又慮其愿也，亦不得從先進之林而登之祀典。故實者不能遺，而虛者不能飾，而典禮可正也。今令甲：每旌表孝節，必以疏聞，候報可，良以重風化也。俎豆於聖人之宮，爲百世規，其隆渥豈下
translation_en: …men of the caliber of Chen Shi 陳寔 (Taiqiu 太丘) and Huang Xian 黃憲 (Shudu 叔度)—are summarily cast aside and never spoken of again. This is the fault of judging merely by outward status. Therefore, those who deliberate on nominations must give a detailed account of the candidate's actual deeds, and all recommendations consisting of vague and extravagant rhetoric should be rejected. As for those registered elsewhere who were not actually raised in the locality, there is no need to drag them in to lend prestige to the place. Conversely, if a man's conduct and righteousness are truly without blemish, even if he lived in obscurity in a impoverished alley, he should be granted recognition. Furthermore, the underlying meaning of the rites should be elucidated and made manifest to all. According to ritual principle, sacrifices at the Great Winter Sacrifice (Dazheng) are offered on the basis of six types of meritorious service; let us examine a candidate's achievements and see which of the six he truly fulfills. Those who merely abided by minor rules and held onto their emoluments without committing glaring faults must not be indiscriminately enshrined. According to ritual principle, sacrifices at the Blind Musicians' Academy (Guzong) are offered on the basis of morality and virtue; for those nowadays acclaimed as local worthies, let us scrutinize their deeds and ask: to what extent did they follow and practice the Way of Confucius, and to what extent did they elucidate and promote it? If they have not done so, then even if they are free of blame and devoid of praise, one must still guard against their being mere "village honest men" (yuan), and they too must not be placed among the ranks of the worthy predecessors or entered into the sacrificial canon. Thus, those of genuine merit cannot be overlooked, while those of empty reputation cannot be dressed up with false praise, and the canonical rites can be rectified. Under current statutory regulations, whenever filial piety or chastity is to be honored with atestimonial arch, it must be reported to the throne in a memorial to await imperial approval—truly because great weight is attached to moral transformation. Yet to receive sacrificial offerings in the temple of the Sage as a model for a hundred generations—how could such exalted favor be any less significant than…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旌表哉似宜倣奏
聞之例歲舉行之俟覈實
報可乃祠則柄有所握而名不得以徇人卽求
名者雖日奔走焉而終不得以虛濫應祀
此敦禮之大原雖煩瀆而必不可巳者愚
生之所竊望也
第五問
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳批丈地均糧
國家重務而弊孔不塞貽害匪輕子能究極根源而區畫周詳具覘成
筭是可悉見諸行矣
考試官教諭賈批條答清丈利弊明如指掌
考試官教諭汪批遠猷卓識經濟才也
夫國之所急在足賦民之所急在樂業顧
天下未有不樂業之民而能出其身以供
國賦者此酌時經制之略所以急於民也
民之生資地力以贍公私之求其贍私恒
急而贍公恒緩故賦額之不可詘夫人而
punctuated:
旌表哉？似宜倣奏聞之例，歲舉行之，俟覈實報可乃祠。則柄有所握，而名不得以徇人；卽求名者雖日奔走焉，而終不得以虛濫應祀。此敦禮之大原，雖煩瀆而必不可巳者，愚生之所竊望也。

第五問
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳批：丈地均糧，國家重務，而弊孔不塞，貽害匪輕。子能究極根源而區畫周詳，具覘成筭，是可悉見諸行矣。
考試官教諭賈批：條答清丈利弊，明如指掌。
考試官教諭汪批：遠猷卓識，經濟才也。

夫國之所急在足賦，民之所急在樂業。顧天下未有不樂業之民，而能出其身以供國賦者。此酌時經制之略，所以急於民也。民之生資地力以贍公私之求，其贍私恒急，而贍公恒緩。故賦額之不可詘，夫人而
translation_en:
… official commendation (jingbiao)? It seems appropriate to imitate the precedent of submitting memorials to the throne, carrying it out annually, and waiting until the facts have been verified and imperial approval returned before enshrining them. Then authority will be firmly held, and honors cannot be granted out of personal favor; even if those seeking fame bustle about daily, in the end they will not be able to gain sacrificial honors through empty and excessive claims. This is the great foundation for honoring the rites—though it may seem tedious and importunate, it is something that absolutely cannot be dispensed with, and is what this foolish student humbly hopes for.

Question Five
Peng Ziguang 彭子光
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Chen: Surveying land and equalizing grain taxes is a weighty affair of the state, yet if the loopholes for abuse are not stopped up, the harm bequeathed is no light matter. You are able to thoroughly trace the root causes and make comprehensive, detailed plans, fully demonstrating a well-formed strategy that can be entirely put into practice.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jia: Itemized responses on the advantages and abuses of the cadastral survey, as clear as pointing to one's palm.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wang: Far-reaching plans and outstanding insight—a talent for statecraft.

Now, what is urgent for the state lies in having sufficient tax revenue, and what is urgent for the people lies in enjoying their livelihoods. Yet in all the world there have never been people who do not enjoy their livelihoods and yet are able to come forth in person to supply the state's taxes. This is why the strategy of deliberating on the times and establishing regulations must urgently prioritize the people. The people's livelihood depends on the productivity of the land to meet both public and private demands; they are always urgent in meeting their private needs and always slow in meeting public ones. Therefore, that the tax quota cannot be allowed to fall short is something that everyone…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知之然使有其賦無其民弗能供也有其
民而不均其賦弗能久也故均賦則賦足
而民安不均賦則賦不足而民擾吾欲求
其安而去其擾則莫若舉今已足額之田
酌貧富而均其輸爲法制以經之故上無
加賦之害而下有安業之利是我之所急
嘗在於民而其利更及於賦也夫古今田
賦之屢變也雖使大撓持籌隸首布筭弗
能悉矣然大較有二三代以上其田常在
===
官三代以下其田常在民田在官則貢之
助之徹之其法惟在正經界經界旣正則
事權常握于上而民無他冀故什一行而
頌聲作然自春秋之後而法已陵夷雖好
古若孟軻亦僅能舉大略而已由是秦人
始變阡陌而田漸入於民卽武帝時去周
秦未遠也而董仲舒已謂富者田連阡陌
而貧者無立錐之地則其制之不均槩可
睹云于是限于漢均于魏永業于唐皆以
punctuated: 知之。然使有其賦無其民，弗能供也；有其民而不均其賦，弗能久也。故均賦則賦足而民安，不均賦則賦不足而民擾。吾欲求其安而去其擾，則莫若舉今已足額之田，酌貧富而均其輸，爲法制以經之。故上無加賦之害，而下有安業之利，是我之所急嘗在於民，而其利更及於賦也。夫古今田賦之屢變也，雖使大撓持籌，隸首布筭，弗能悉矣。然大較有二：三代以上，其田常在官；三代以下，其田常在民。田在官，則貢之、助之、徹之，其法惟在正經界。經界旣正，則事權常握于上，而民無他冀，故什一行而頌聲作。然自春秋之後，而法已陵夷，雖好古若孟軻，亦僅能舉大略而已。由是秦人始變阡陌，而田漸入於民。卽武帝時，去周、秦未遠也，而董仲舒已謂「富者田連阡陌，而貧者無立錐之地」，則其制之不均，槩可睹云。于是限于漢，均于魏，永業于唐，皆以
translation_en: …knows this. Yet if there is the tax quota without the people, it cannot be supplied; and if there are the people without equalizing their taxes, it cannot endure. Therefore, when taxes are equalized, revenues are sufficient and the people are at peace; when taxes are not equalized, revenues are insufficient and the people are disturbed. If we wish to seek their peace and remove their disturbance, nothing is better than taking the lands that today already meet the quota, weighing poverty and wealth to equalize their contributions, and establishing institutional regulations to govern them. Thus above there is no harm of increasing taxes, while below there is the benefit of secure livelihoods; in this way, what we treat as urgent is always the people, yet the benefit extends further to the tax revenues. Now as for the repeated changes in land taxation from antiquity to the present, even if Da Nao held the tally sticks and Li Shou laid out the counting rods, they could not exhaust them all. Yet in broad outline there are two phases: during the Three Dynasties and before, the land constantly belonged to the state; after the Three Dynasties, the land constantly belonged to the people. When the land belonged to the state—whether under the tribute (gong), aid (zhu), or assessment (che) systems—the method lay solely in rectifying the field boundaries. Once the boundaries were rectified, authority was constantly held above and the people had no other designs; thus the one-tenth tax was practiced and songs of praise arose. Yet after the Spring and Autumn period, the system had already declined; even someone as fond of antiquity as Meng Ke (Mencius) could only cite its general outline. From this point, the men of Qin first altered the field ridges and paths (qianmo), and land gradually passed into the hands of the people. Even in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, which was not far removed from Zhou and Qin, Dong Zhongshu already said that "the rich have fields connecting ridges and paths, while the poor lack even ground enough to plant an awl"—so the inequality of the system can generally be seen. Thereupon, land was restricted under the Han, equalized under the Wei, and made into perpetual holdings (yongye) under the Tang, all in order to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
抑雄擅之家而禁其圍奪使編戸齊氓稍
得事休息其法非不善也然限田議始仲
舒而述於師丹哀帝終不能用魏孝文用
李安世之說爲均田尚屬草創至唐武德
間復加損益而爲口分永業之制顧令民
得以徙遷鬻其田而制益紊矣厥後括田
行於開元致張虛數方田行於熙寧而旋
以焚擾報罷其利端弊孔大都與漢唐宋
相終始而卒無善制者豈非惠民之無術
===
哉
高皇帝起蹟民間習聞豪宗梗賦狀故元年戊
申首定賦法曁辛酉而黃冊成巳廉知富
民詭灑州縣度田多不實乃分遣國子生
武淳等周行天下度其稅糧多寡爲區毎
區有長四人領以耆民躬履田畝按區運
步因圖次其田形籍
奏之謂之魚鱗圖冊較前代獨詳且前代抑
豪右皆主於裁其田必不能奪富者之有
punctuated:
抑雄擅之家，而禁其圍奪，使編戸齊氓稍得事休息，其法非不善也。然限田議始仲舒，而述於師丹，哀帝終不能用；魏孝文用李安世之說爲均田，尚屬草創；至唐武德間，復加損益，而爲口分、永業之制，顧令民得以徙遷鬻其田，而制益紊矣。厥後括田行於開元，致張虛數；方田行於熙寧，而旋以焚擾報罷。其利端弊孔，大都與漢、唐、宋相終始，而卒無善制者，豈非惠民之無術哉！

高皇帝起蹟民間，習聞豪宗梗賦狀，故元年戊申，首定賦法。曁辛酉而黃冊成，巳廉知富民詭灑，州縣度田多不實，乃分遣國子生武淳等周行天下，度其稅糧多寡爲區。毎區有長四人，領以耆民，躬履田畝，按區運步，因圖次其田形，籍奏之，謂之魚鱗圖冊，較前代獨詳。且前代抑豪右，皆主於裁其田，必不能奪富者之有
translation_en:
…restrain powerful and monopolizing families and prohibit their encroachment and seizure, allowing registered commoners to gain a measure of rest and relief; these laws were not without merit. Yet the proposal to limit landholdings began with Dong Zhongshu and was carried forward by Shi Dan 師丹, though Emperor Ai 哀帝 ultimately could not put it into practice. Emperor Xiaowen of Wei 魏孝文帝 adopted the proposal of Li Anshi 李安世 to institute the equal-field system (juntian 均田), which was still in a rudimentary stage. By the Wude 武德 era (618–626) of the Tang, adjustments were again made to form the system of personal-share (koufen 口分) and hereditary (yongye 永業) lands, yet because the people were permitted to sell their land when relocating, the system grew increasingly disordered. Thereafter, land registration (kuotian 括田) was carried out during the Kaiyuan 開元 era (713–741), resulting in inflated and false figures; the square-field system (fangtian 方田) was carried out during the Xining 熙寧 era (1068–1077), only to be quickly rescinded due to reports of disruption and turmoil. Their sources of benefit and loopholes of abuse largely persisted from beginning to end through the Han, Tang, and Song, and that they ultimately lacked a sound system—was this not for want of an effective method to benefit the people?

The August Emperor Gao 高皇帝 [the Hongwu Emperor] rose from among the common people and was thoroughly familiar with how powerful lineages obstructed taxation. Therefore, in his first year, the wushen 戊申 year (1368), he first established the taxation laws. By the xinyou 辛酉 year (1381), the Yellow Registers (Huangce 黃冊) were completed. Having already discovered through investigation that wealthy commoners were fraudulently parcelling out their holdings to evade taxes and that the land measurements of subprefectures and counties were largely inaccurate, he dispatched National University Students (guozisheng 國子生) such as Wu Chun 武淳 to travel throughout the empire, dividing the land into districts (qu 區) according to the amount of tax grain. Each district had four district heads (zhang 長), led by local elders, who personally walked the fields, paced off measurements district by district, and mapped and ordered the shapes of the fields; they registered and memorialized these to the throne, calling them the Fish-Scale Illustrated Registers (Yulin tuce 魚鱗圖冊), which were uniquely detailed compared to those of former dynasties. Moreover, when former dynasties restrained the powerful and wealthy, they always focused on curtailing their landholdings; yet they certainly could not seize what the rich possessed…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以為貧者之食故法易格今不責其治田
多寡而惟即多寡定賦故富者不能巧避
而賦易均前代履畝主括地則筭及林麓
山川主檢覆則筭及室廬里落主畫方則
先定品式後履田畝今惟就田定區法簡
而易覈古者八尺為步步百為畝周時建
司馬法止用六尺其步益縮迨于唐始用
二百四十步為畝視周制倍寬今用之則
計畝廣而民稅輕故漢元始時田賦號稱
===
極盛而考諸洪武間天下額田凡八百四
十九萬六千有奇尚溢於元始八百二十
七萬五百有奇之數茲善制之明驗哉承
平久而奸巧叢矣富者得田而賦不及貧
者得賦而田不及憂樂倒置
國計滋損蓋自弘治以後而額田堇堇四百
餘萬視洪武初殺半矣
天子閔然念之
令司農下郡國按額履畝別其勤惰而殿最
punctuated: 以為貧者之食，故法易格；今不責其治田多寡，而惟即多寡定賦，故富者不能巧避，而賦易均。前代履畝，主括地則筭及林麓山川，主檢覆則筭及室廬里落，主畫方則先定品式、後履田畝；今惟就田定區，法簡而易覈。古者八尺為步，步百為畝；周時建司馬法，止用六尺，其步益縮；迨于唐，始用二百四十步為畝，視周制倍寬；今用之，則計畝廣而民稅輕。故漢元始時田賦號稱極盛，而考諸洪武間，天下額田凡八百四十九萬六千有奇，尚溢於元始八百二十七萬五百有奇之數，茲善制之明驗哉！承平久而奸巧叢矣，富者得田而賦不及，貧者得賦而田不及，憂樂倒置，國計滋損。蓋自弘治以後，而額田堇堇四百餘萬，視洪武初殺半矣。天子閔然念之，令司農下郡國，按額履畝，別其勤惰而殿最
translation_en: …to serve as food for the poor, and thus the laws were easily obstructed. Today, we do not restrict how much or how little land they cultivate, but simply assess taxes according to the amount held; therefore, the rich cannot cleverly evade them, and taxes are easily equalized. When previous dynasties surveyed the fields, if they focused on sweeping up all land, their calculations extended even to forests, foothills, mountains, and streams; if they focused on inspection and verification, their calculations extended even to houses, cottages, and village settlements; if they focused on the square-field method, they first established the grades and formulas and only afterward surveyed the acreage. Today, we simply demarcate districts based on the actual fields, so the method is simple and easy to verify. In antiquity, eight chi made a pace (bu), and one hundred paces made a mu. In the Zhou era, when the Sima method was established, they used only six chi, so the pace shrank further. By the Tang dynasty, they first used two hundred and forty paces to make a mu, which was more than twice as generous as the Zhou system. Today we use this standard, so the measured mu is wide and the people's tax burden is light. Thus, during the Yuanshi reign of the Han dynasty (1–5 CE), land and tax revenues were acclaimed as having reached their greatest height; yet if we examine the Hongwu reign (1368–1398), the registered land of the empire totaled over 8,496,000 qing, still exceeding the Yuanshi figure of over 8,270,500 qing. Is this not clear proof of a good system? When peace has lasted long, deceit and cunning proliferate: the rich acquire the land while the taxes do not reach them, and the poor acquire the taxes while the land does not reach them. Sorrow and joy are inverted, and the state finances suffer increasing loss. Indeed, from the Hongzhi reign (1488–1505) onward, the registered land has barely exceeded four million qing—reduced by half compared to the beginning of the Hongwu reign! The Son of Heaven, reflecting on this with compassion, ordered the Minister of Revenue to instruct the prefectures and principalities to survey the acreage according to the quotas, distinguishing the diligent from the negligent and ranking their merits and demerits…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之即有强宗巨室亦皆俯首聽命而不敢
以骫
天子之明法諸願延須臾以承
休澤者喁喁如也乃粤西則豪右踰制或不
下他藩而谿峒土酋或蠶食齊民之業莫
敢誰何或田稍犬牙其中輒以此輩爲解
而避租賦此清理視他藩尤難之難也顧
德意所嚮諸長吏莫不奉行唯謹會峒蠻稍欲
恣睢以傲命吏我巳分布健兒入其巢不
===
旬月而渠黨面縛如犬左效諸酋聞之益
回心面内願奉約束初額田九萬六千三
百有奇後失額一萬八千有奇今竣事田
九萬六千五百有奇稅糧稱是蓋粤西之
履畝屢矣皆奪於羣議迄無成功至是始
復額有羨咸誦
聖天子威德萬里盛矣乃執事猶惓惓焉其爲
西人計慮至深遠也愚則以爲莫若勤民
而均其賦且吾所謂均非謂賦可勿急也
punctuated: 之。即有强宗巨室，亦皆俯首聽命，而不敢以骫天子之明法；諸願延須臾以承休澤者，喁喁如也。乃粤西則豪右踰制，或不下他藩；而谿峒土酋，或蠶食齊民之業，莫敢誰何；或田稍犬牙其中，輒以此輩爲解而避租賦：此清理視他藩尤難之難也。顧德意所嚮，諸長吏莫不奉行唯謹。會峒蠻稍欲恣睢以傲命吏，我巳分布健兒入其巢，不旬月而渠黨面縛如犬左效。諸酋聞之，益回心面内，願奉約束。初，額田九萬六千三百有奇，後失額一萬八千有奇；今竣事，田九萬六千五百有奇，稅糧稱是。蓋粤西之履畝屢矣，皆奪於羣議，迄無成功；至是始復額有羨，咸誦聖天子威德萬里，盛矣！乃執事猶惓惓焉，其爲西人計慮至深遠也。愚則以爲莫若勤民而均其賦。且吾所謂均，非謂賦可勿急也，
translation_en: … them. Even powerful lineages and great households all bow their heads and obey orders, not daring to bend the clear laws of the Son of Heaven; all those who wish to prolong their lives a little while to receive His beneficent grace look up in eager expectation. Yet in Guangxi (Yuexi), powerful families overstep the regulations, perhaps no less than in other provinces; meanwhile, native chieftains in the stream valleys and mountain fastnesses sometimes encroach upon the property of commoner subjects like silkworms, and no one dares question them; or where registered fields slightly interlock with their lands, people readily use these chieftains as an excuse to evade land taxes. Thus, clearing up land registration here is the most difficult of difficulties compared to other provinces. Yet wherever the imperial benevolent intent is directed, the senior officials without exception carry it out with utmost diligence. It happened that the valley barbarians were somewhat inclined to act outrageously and defy the commissioned officials, so our forces deployed stalwart troops to enter their lairs, and in less than a month the ringleaders and their partisans were bound with their hands behind their backs like dogs, offering submission [?]. Hearing of this, the various chieftains increasingly turned their hearts inward in allegiance and wished to abide by the regulations. Initially, the quota of land was over 96,300 qing, and later over 18,000 qing of the quota was lost; now that the survey is completed, the land totals over 96,500 qing, and the tax grain corresponds to this. Indeed, field surveys have been attempted repeatedly in Guangxi, yet all were thwarted by mass objections and hitherto achieved no success; only now has the quota been restored with a surplus, and everyone praises the awe-inspiring virtue of the Sacred Son of Heaven reaching ten thousand li—how magnificent! Yet you, sir, are still earnestly concerned; your planning and consideration for the people of Guangxi are most profound and far-reaching. In my humble view, nothing is better than being diligent on behalf of the people and equalizing their taxes. Moreover, what I call equalizing does not mean that taxes need not be treated as urgent; …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
非盡如前代欲限制其田以遺貧民業也
非舉貧富而較量之欲平衡而稱適也物
之不齊物理固然惟計今見額多田則多
賦少田則少賦田膏腴則從重田瘠鹵則
從輕俾貧弱者不致偏累而稍紓其目前
之急富而强有力者不得隱匿詭灑以公
賦積私家是謂均平固
皇上之所為履畝意也昔杜君卿有言簿書旣
廣必籍衆功籍衆功則政由羣吏欲以紀
===
人事之衆寡明地利之多少雖申商督刑
不可得而詳矣此疾諸胥之緣絕為奸也
執事謂冊籍得無為異日者憂誠慮之矣
今惟督縣官務精稽覈倣魚鱗之式為之
一不當毋但罪吏卽縣官亦得議廢置有
不人人自効者乎及籍成以上諸郡郡以
上諸司亦復精覈如前則參伍旣備弊安
得而乘也豪家張虛愒而食僮田且役其
人為之佃僕恐致厲階固矣今田已籍于
punctuated: 非盡如前代欲限制其田以遺貧民業也，非舉貧富而較量之、欲平衡而稱適也。物之不齊，物理固然。惟計今見額，多田則多賦，少田則少賦，田膏腴則從重，田瘠鹵則從輕，俾貧弱者不致偏累，而稍紓其目前之急；富而强有力者不得隱匿詭灑，以公賦積私家。是謂均平，固皇上之所為履畝意也。昔杜君卿有言：「簿書旣廣，必籍衆功；籍衆功，則政由羣吏。欲以紀人事之衆寡，明地利之多少，雖申、商督刑，不可得而詳矣。」此疾諸胥之緣絕為奸也。執事謂冊籍得無為異日者憂，誠慮之矣。今惟督縣官務精稽覈，倣魚鱗之式為之；一不當，毋但罪吏，卽縣官亦得議廢置，有不人人自効者乎？及籍成以上諸郡，郡以上諸司，亦復精覈如前，則參伍旣備，弊安得而乘也？豪家張虛愒而食僮田，且役其人為之佃僕，恐致厲階，固矣。今田已籍于
translation_en:
…Nor does it mean strictly following previous dynasties in attempting to limit landholdings in order to leave livelihoods for the poor, nor weighing the rich and the poor against one another to force an equal balance and uniform standard. That things are unequal is inherently the nature of things. We should simply reckon by the current actual quotas: those with more land pay more tax, and those with less land pay less tax; fertile land is assessed heavily, and barren or saline land is assessed lightly. This ensures that the poor and weak are not disproportionately burdened and may somewhat relieve their immediate distress, while the wealthy and powerful cannot conceal their holdings or fraudulently scatter their registrations to hoard public revenue in private households. This is what is meant by equitable equalization, and it is indeed His Majesty's intention in conducting the land survey.

In the past, Du Junqing (Du You 杜佑) said: "Once the registers and documents become vast, one must rely on the efforts of the many; relying on the efforts of the many means administration falls into the hands of the lesser clerks. If one wishes to record the size of the population and clarify the yield of the land, even if Shen Buhai 申不害 and Shang Yang 商鞅 were to supervise the punishments, it would be impossible to ascertain the details." This expressed his hatred for petty clerks colluding and tampering with records to commit fraud. When Your Excellency asks whether the registers might not become a source of worry in the future, you have truly given this deep thought. Now we need only charge the county magistrates to be thorough and precise in their verification, modeling the registers on the "fish-scale" format. If there is a single discrepancy, we should not merely punish the clerks, but also deliberate on dismissing or demoting the county magistrate—who then would not exert himself to the utmost? Once the registers are completed and submitted to the prefectures, and the prefectures submit them to the provincial offices, if each level again verifies them as thoroughly as before, then with cross-checking fully in place, how could any abuses find an opening?

That powerful families use empty threats [?] to swallow up the lands of the Zhuang 獞 [written 僮] people and even press the people themselves into service as tenant-serfs will, it is feared, give rise to calamity—this is certainly true. Now that the lands have already been registered with…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官諸獞亦頗知其不足恃第桉畝而酌其
賦責之必輸及登稼時禁豪毋虐取之使
獞亦得爲食否則還之獞人以供吾賦或
稍與輕科以懷之其無主者入爲官田以
待別授且令以後豪家毋得窺小利而納
獞人故佃僕可馭也其猺獞故有生熟二
種今熟者已願就田賦而齒編氓亦宜與
之輕科而重禁里魁毋得苛求使之安堵
其生猺獞每不利於熟者之來歸而爲我
===
用或行煽誘或肆讎殺或指其田爲彼田
而羣起與爭則申固兵防禁其出沒重則
兵之如是足矣不必求諸化之外也土酋
在上世止責以扞掫藉其兵力故田無頃
畝而聽其自輸糧爲額今原額不失姑聽
其便第在左江者頗輸租而在右江者率
漸積逋負故督責宜加焉其有怙强而奪
民田或受民詭託以滋隱避第桉籍而清
之重則罪及酋必不能捍吾法矣贍兵之
punctuated: 官，諸獞亦頗知其不足恃，第桉畝而酌其賦，責之必輸。及登稼時，禁豪毋虐取之，使獞亦得爲食；否則還之獞人以供吾賦，或稍與輕科以懷之。其無主者，入爲官田以待別授，且令以後豪家毋得窺小利而納獞人，故佃僕可馭也。其猺、獞故有生、熟二種，今熟者已願就田賦而齒編氓，亦宜與之輕科，而重禁里魁毋得苛求，使之安堵。其生猺、獞每不利於熟者之來歸而爲我用，或行煽誘，或肆讎殺，或指其田爲彼田而羣起與爭，則申固兵防，禁其出沒，重則兵之，如是足矣，不必求諸化之外也。土酋在上世止責以扞掫，藉其兵力，故田無頃畝，而聽其自輸糧爲額。今原額不失，姑聽其便；第在左江者頗輸租，而在右江者率漸積逋負，故督責宜加焉。其有怙强而奪民田，或受民詭託以滋隱避，第桉籍而清之，重則罪及酋，必不能捍吾法矣。贍兵之
translation_en:
… the government, the various Zhuang (Tong 獞) peoples also realize quite well that those powerful families cannot be relied upon. We need only assess the tax according to the acreage and require them to pay it without fail. When the crops are harvested, we should prohibit the powerful families from tyrannically seizing them, so that the Zhuang may also have food to eat. Otherwise, the land should be returned to the Zhuang people so that they may pay our taxes, or we may grant them a slightly lighter tax rate in order to win them over. As for land without an owner, it should be confiscated as government land to await reallocation. Moreover, we should order that henceforth powerful families must not eye petty profits and take in Zhuang people; thus, these tenant-servants can be kept under control.

Among the Yao (猺) and Zhuang, there have traditionally been two kinds, the "raw" (unassimilated) and the "cooked" (assimilated). Now that the assimilated ones are already willing to accept land taxes and beenrolled among the registered commoners, we should likewise grant them a light tax rate, and strictly forbid the village headmen from making harsh exactions, allowing them to live in peace. The unassimilated Yao and Zhuang often find it against their interests when the assimilated ones submit and serve our purposes; at times they engage in incitement and enticement, at times they indulge in vengeful killings, or else they claim those lands as their own and rise up in bands to contend for them. In such cases, we should strengthen our military defenses to prevent their raids, and in serious cases use military force against them. Doing this is sufficient; there is no need to seek results beyond the pale of civilization.

In past generations, the native chieftains (tuqiu 土酋) were charged only with guarding the frontiers while we relied upon their military strength; therefore, their lands were not measured in qing and mu, and they were allowed to deliver grain voluntarily as a fixed quota. Now, so long as the original quota is not lost, we may for the time being allow them to do as suits their convenience. Yet while those along the Zuo River (Zuojiang 左江) generally pay their grain tribute, those along the You River (Youjiang 右江) have for the most part gradually accumulated arrears, so supervision and enforcement should be stepped up. Where there are those who rely on force to seize commoners' lands, or accept fraudulent commendations of land from commoners to increase tax evasion, we need only clear up the matter according to the registers. In serious cases, punishment should extend to the chieftain himself, and they will certainly not be able to defy our laws.

As for the [lands] that support the troops …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
田業不可罷卽以供餉而不責其賦且吾
餉亦可以罷給而備軍與諸荒蕪而始籍
者則徐待三年後始征其租或仍以輕科
取之朝耕尺寸之田暮入差徭之籍玆陳
靖之慷慨於宋代者其言可繹也而又廣
招徠勤督率毋使草萊彌目有土而不可
食是吾不務加賦而惟務足民久之民足
而賦均足焉玆非兩利而俱便者乎故不
限而畫一不均而稱平不永業口分而公
===
私無困可以廣
德意而惠無窮雖不貢不徹而其意未嘗不同
於三代竊以爲粵西便計或不出此猶慮
其狂瞽而無當也惟進教之
punctuated: 田業不可罷，卽以供餉而不責其賦，且吾餉亦可以罷給而備軍與。諸荒蕪而始籍者，則徐待三年後始征其租，或仍以輕科取之。「朝耕尺寸之田，暮入差徭之籍」，玆陳靖之慷慨於宋代者，其言可繹也。而又廣招徠、勤督率，毋使草萊彌目，有土而不可食。是吾不務加賦而惟務足民，久之民足而賦均足焉，玆非兩利而俱便者乎？故不限而畫一，不均而稱平，不永業口分而公私無困，可以廣德意而惠無窮。雖不貢不徹，而其意未嘗不同於三代。竊以爲粵西便計或不出此，猶慮其狂瞽而無當也，惟進教之。
translation_en: …fields and estates cannot be abolished, then let them directly supply military rations without demanding regular land taxes from them; moreover, our own ration disbursements can then be discontinued and set aside for military campaigns. As for all those barren lands that are newly registered, wait patiently until after three years before beginning to levy their rent, or else continue to collect from them at a light tax rate. "In the morning they plow a few inches of land; by evening they are entered into the registers for corvée labor"—this was what Chen Jing 陳靖 lamented with deep emotion during the Song dynasty, and his words are well worth pondering. Furthermore, we should broadly attract settlers and diligently supervise and lead them, so as not to let weeds and brush fill the eyes, having land that cannot produce food. In this way, we do not strive to increase taxes, but strive only to make the people self-sufficient; after a long time, when the people have enough, the tax revenues will equally suffice. Is this not mutually beneficial and convenient for both sides? Therefore, without imposing land-holding limits, there is uniformity; without forced equalization, there is fairness; without permanent-tenure (yongye) and personal-share (koufen) allotments, neither public nor private interests suffer distress, whereby we can broaden the imperial benevolent intent and bestow boundless favor. Although we institute neither the tribute (gong) nor the tithe (che) systems, the underlying spirit is no different from that of the Three Dynasties. I venture to think that convenient measures for Guangxi (Yuexi 粵西) perhaps do not go beyond this; yet I still fear that my views are rash, blind, and wide of the mark, and I pray only to be admitted and instructed.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
秋八月廣西鄉試竣事宗正
幸以薄技共盛典當有言申
告諸士曰茲非成周時所稱
賢能書哉彼鄉大夫提衡而
品裁者皆平居所灼見不謬
其實故能光天府而重祖廟
===
之藏與天球琬琰交珍而世
守然所用稍有不適輒以罰
舉者無赦故往往稱得人今
宗正於諸士卽稱同業然居
產殊壤未甞通邂逅接殷勤
也僅以方寸之管盈尺之楮
權衡於三日間所揮霍卽揮
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

秋八月，廣西鄉試竣事。宗正幸以薄技共盛典，當有言申告諸士曰：「茲非成周時所稱『賢能書』哉？彼鄉大夫提衡而品裁者，皆平居所灼見，不謬其實，故能光天府而重祖廟之藏，與天球、琬琰交珍而世守。然所用稍有不適，輒以罰舉者無赦，故往往稱得人。今宗正於諸士，卽稱同業，然居產殊壤，未甞通邂逅、接殷勤也。僅以方寸之管、盈尺之楮，權衡於三日間所揮霍，卽揮
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn, the Guangxi Provincial Examination was brought to completion. I, Zongzheng, having had the good fortune to participate in this grand ceremony with my meager skills, ought to have some words to declare to the scholars, saying: "Is this not what in the era of the flourishing Zhou was called a 'register of the worthy and able'? Those whom the District Grandees weighed and evaluated were all men whose qualities they had clearly observed in everyday life, without mistaking their true reality. Thus, those registers could bring glory to the Keeper of the Treasures and add weight to the holdings of the ancestral temple, being treasured alongside the Heavenly Scepter and the wanyan jades, and guarded from generation to generation. Yet if those who were employed proved even slightly unsuitable, the recommenders were immediately punished without pardon; therefore, the system was consistently praised for obtaining the right men. Now, although I, Zongzheng, may be called a fellow scholar in the same pursuits as you gentlemen, we dwell in and hail from different lands, and have never had occasion to meet by chance or exchange cordialities. Merely by means of a tiny writing brush and a foot-long sheet of paper, I have weighed and judged what was dashed off in the space of three days; and even in what was dashed…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
霍僅取一藝能稱別質文不
諄其意指即赫然賢儶選矣
是能必其德行果醇固而適
用者乎漢初取士御史下郡
守勸駕而署其行義及年其
後定四科以學通行脩經中
博士者爲次高等猶庶幾三
===
物之指最後定口率郡口二
十萬幷邇蠻徼者歲舉不過
一人何其儉也粤西故雜蠻
落入
昭代始駸駸媲盛中土即一二窟
穴近亦解辮受約束蔚然爲
文明隩區士授經率多專門
punctuated: 霍，僅取一藝能稱，別質文，不諄其意指，即赫然賢儶選矣。是能必其德行果醇固而適用者乎？漢初取士，御史下郡守勸駕，而署其行義及年；其後定四科，以學通行脩、經中博士者爲次高等，猶庶幾三物之指；最後定口率，郡口二十萬幷邇蠻徼者，歲舉不過一人，何其儉也！粤西故雜蠻落，入昭代始駸駸媲盛中土；即一二窟穴，近亦解辮受約束，蔚然爲文明隩區。士授經率多專門
translation_en: …what they dash off—and even in what they dash off, merely selecting a single literary skill that meets the standard, distinguishing substance and style without straying from the intended purport—and suddenly they are illustriously chosen as worthy and outstanding men! Can this guarantee that their moral conduct is truly pure and steadfast, and suited for practical use? In the early Han dynasty, in selecting scholars, the Censors instructed the Commandery Governors to urge them to set out for the capital, while recording their righteous conduct and age. Later, four categories were established, placing those of comprehensive learning, cultivated conduct, and mastery of the Classics worthy of Erudites into the second highest grade, which still approximated the purport of the "three things" of antiquity. Finally, a population ratio was fixed: a commandery with a population of two hundred thousand, or one bordering the barbarian frontiers, recommended no more than one man per year—how frugal that was! Western Yue [Guangxi] was formerly interspersed with barbarian settlements, and only upon entering our Illustrious Dynasty did it gradually come to rival the flourishing of the Central Lands; even the one or two rebel lairs have recently unbound their braided hair and submitted to regulation, luxuriantly becoming a culturally refined heartland. The scholars who transmit the Classics are mostly specialized…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
名家乃今積三載輒得五十
有五人計所遇殆倍蓰漢氏
而其夙夜黽勉袚心注目而
求之者第以其經中博士業
止爾有如察署行義其出入
或悖所聞以試諸用輒弗當
而因按舉不適者罪安所離
===
遏玆宗正之所爲葸葸懼也
顧聞之士在校若金在陶惟
主德所鎔鑄必有顯効頃者世風
日競於文士潄藝尤靡曼不
根有傷雅道
天子閔之
下功令數加釐正西士雖疎逖
punctuated: 名家。乃今積三載輒得五十有五人，計所遇殆倍蓰漢氏。而其夙夜黽勉，袚心注目而求之者，第以其經中博士業止爾。有如察署行義，其出入或悖所聞，以試諸用輒弗當，而因按舉不適者罪，安所離遏？玆宗正之所爲葸葸懼也。顧聞之，士在校若金在陶，惟主德所鎔鑄，必有顯効。頃者世風日競於文，士潄藝尤靡曼不根，有傷雅道。天子閔之，下功令數加釐正。西士雖疎逖，
translation_en:
…renowned masters. Yet nowadays, every three years fifty-five men are selected; reckoning the favor they enjoy, it is nearly double or fivefold that of the Han dynasty. However, what is sought day and night with diligent exertion, cleansing the mind and fixing the gaze, goes no further than their proficiency in the Erudite curriculum of the Classics. Suppose one were to inspect and record their moral conduct and righteousness, and their comings and goings proved contrary to what was heard of them, or when tested in practical application they continually proved unsuitable—then if they were investigated and impeached for the offense of making unfitting recommendations, how could one escape or avert blame? This is why I, Zongzheng, am so timorously fearful.

Yet I have heard that scholars in schools are like metal in the foundry: according to how the sovereign's virtue melts and casts them, there will surely be manifest results. Recently, the customs of the age have increasingly competed in literary ornament, and the scholars' immersion in the arts has become especially florid and rootless, harming the refined Way. The Son of Heaven pitied this and handed down examination regulations to repeatedly rectify and correct it. Although the scholars of Guangxi are distant and remote,…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
猶訢訢知嚮方焉乃御史教
選之
請代也
上念粤西當賓興有日矣故事御
史當按部必引
奏始
遣也恐致後期乃
===
詔閣臣趣御史大夫特疏御史名
以
請不踰時
命下趣御史行夫粤西遠在萬里
蕞爾諸士何足廛
聖衷而眷眷若此是其中得無有
倜儻瑰瑋之士足以副
punctuated: 猶訢訢知嚮方焉。乃御史教選之請代也，上念粤西當賓興有日矣。故事，御史當按部，必引奏始遣也，恐致後期，乃詔閣臣趣御史大夫特疏御史名以請。不踰時，命下，趣御史行。夫粤西遠在萬里，蕞爾諸士，何足廛聖衷而眷眷若此？是其中得無有倜儻瑰瑋之士，足以副
translation_en: … still joyfully know the direction toward which they should turn. When Censor Jiao Xuan requested to be replaced, the Emperor bore in mind that the time for the triennial賓興 (guest-recommending) examination in Guangxi was approaching. According to precedent, when a Censor is to tour a region as Regional Inspector, he must first be presented in a memorial and granted an audience before being dispatched. Fearing that this would result in a delay past the scheduled date, the Emperor issued an edict to the Grand Secretaries to urge the Censor-in-Chief to submit a special memorial requesting the appointment of the Censor by name. Within no time, the command came down urging me, the Censor, to set out. Now, Guangxi lies ten thousand li away; how could its humble scholars in such a tiny region be worthy of occupying the Sacred Mind and receiving such solicitous concern as this? Could it not be that among them there are extraordinary and brilliant scholars sufficient to live up to …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德意應
昌會陋漢氏而庶幾成周濟濟
之盛者乎比御史至百執事
皆驚顧以爲迅速旣而得其
所繇皆感激頌
聖德不遠裔土況諸士又所賓興
而求者也有不益感奮願效
===
其材諝以佐
任使而終始所砥礪必本德行
兢兢然罔敢玷闕用少報萬
分之一庶幾足稱賢能書哉
宗正請執簡俟其後
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學敎
諭賈宗正謹序
punctuated:
德意、應昌會，陋漢氏而庶幾成周濟濟之盛者乎？比御史至，百執事皆驚顧以爲迅速。旣而得其所繇，皆感激，頌聖德不遠裔土。況諸士又所賓興而求者也，有不益感奮，願效其材諝以佐任使，而終始所砥礪必本德行，兢兢然罔敢玷闕，用少報萬分之一，庶幾足稱賢能書哉！宗正請執簡俟其後。
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學敎諭賈宗正謹序。
translation_en:
… His Majesty's gracious intent and respond to this flourishing juncture, looking down upon the Han dynasty and coming close to the abundant splendor of the accomplished Zhou? When the Censor arrived, all the officiating functionaries looked at one another in astonishment at how swift his journey had been. Once they learned the reason behind it, they were all deeply moved and praised His Majesty's sacred virtue for not treating this distant borderland as too remote. How much more so for the scholars themselves, who are the very ones being recommended as honored guests and sought out by the court! Could any among them fail to be even more moved and inspired, wishing to offer their talents and wisdom to assist in the tasks entrusted to them, while ensuring from beginning to end that their self-cultivation is rooted in virtuous conduct—cautious and reverent, never daring to incur the slightest blemish or deficiency—so as to repay even a ten-thousandth part of this grace, and thus perhaps prove worthy of the register of the worthy and capable? I, Zongzheng, beg leave to hold the writing tablets and await what follows.

Respectfully prefaced by Jia Zongzheng 賈宗正, Instructor of the Confucian School of Le'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄕試錄序
萬曆壬午秋八月廣西當復
大比士前御史李東敖選相
繼疏
請代
上命御史馬呈圖馳往監臨之至
則謹布禮官科條令西士力
===
正文體以歸大雅諸不急務
姑未遑專意掄文旣戒旣毖
乃提調以左參政彭富右參
政胡維新監試以按察使陳
應春右參政兼僉事葉朝陽
其執經品藻則以敬修暨敎
諭賈宗正爲考試官敎諭梁
punctuated:
廣西鄕試錄序

萬曆壬午秋八月，廣西當復大比士。前御史李東、敖選相繼疏請代，上命御史馬呈圖馳往監臨之。至則謹布禮官科條，令西士力正文體以歸大雅，諸不急務姑未遑，專意掄文，旣戒旣毖。乃提調以左參政彭富、右參政胡維新，監試以按察使陳應春、右參政兼僉事葉朝陽，其執經品藻則以敬修暨敎諭賈宗正爲考試官，敎諭梁
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), Guangxi was once again scheduled to hold the great triennial examination of scholars. After the former Investigating Censors Li Dong 李東 and Ao Xuan 敖選 successively submitted memorials requesting to be replaced, His Majesty ordered Investigating Censor Ma Chengtu 馬呈圖 to ride posthaste to serve as Supervising Official. Upon his arrival, he carefully promulgated the regulations of the Ministry of Rites, instructing the scholars of Guangxi to strive to rectify their literary style so as to return to classical elegance. Setting aside for the moment all non-urgent affairs, he devoted his full attention to selecting literary talent, exercising the utmost caution and care. Thereupon, Administration Vice Commissioners of the Left Peng Fu 彭富 and of the Right Hu Weixin 胡維新 were appointed as Proctors; Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yingchun 陳應春 and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Ye Chaoyang 葉朝陽 were appointed as Examination Overseers. As for holding the Classics to evaluate and grade the essays, I, Jingxiu 敬修, together with County Director of Studies Jia Zongzheng 賈宗正, were appointed as Examiners, while County Directors of Studies Liang…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
懋勳王希堯訓導郭藎臣丁
繼宗張沛陳茂薦爲同考試
官餘百執事亦各愼遴部署
以待乃合饗誓衆就棘闈以
提學僉事袁昌祚所選士一
千五百有奇嚴扃鑰而試之
三擇其儁五十有五人籍
===
奏之敬修嘗聞三代之盛南不
過衡山而粤西當衡嶽西南
數百餘里未列禹貢職方氏
然南交分宅紀在帝典而八
桂扶疎由秦漢迄今世以名
郡孰謂山海經盡繆悠語也
第其時山川尚蘊祕神奇卽
punctuated:
懋勳、王希堯，訓導郭藎臣、丁繼宗、張沛、陳茂薦爲同考試官。餘百執事，亦各愼遴部署以待。乃合饗誓衆，就棘闈，以提學僉事袁昌祚所選士一千五百有奇，嚴扃鑰而試之。三擇其儁五十有五人，籍奏之。
敬修嘗聞：三代之盛，南不過衡山；而粤西當衡嶽西南數百餘里，未列《禹貢》、《職方氏》。然南交分宅，紀在《帝典》；而八桂扶疎，由秦、漢迄今，世以名郡，孰謂《山海經》盡繆悠語也？第其時山川尚蘊祕神奇，卽
translation_en:
… Maoxun 梁懋勳 and Wang Xiyao 王希堯, and Assistant Instructors Guo Jinchen 郭藎臣, Ding Jizong 丁繼宗, Zhang Pei 張沛, and Chen Maojian 陳茂薦 served as Associate Examiners. The remaining hundred or so functionaries were also each carefully selected and deployed at the ready. Then, having held a joint banquet and administered the oath to the assembled staff, they entered the thorny examination compound. Taking the more than one thousand five hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Changzuo 袁昌祚, they strictly locked the gates and examined them. Through three sessions they selected fifty-five outstanding men among them, registered their names, and memorialized the results to the throne.

I, Jingxiu 敬修, have heard that at the height of the Three Dynasties, their southern reach did not extend beyond Mount Heng; and since Guangxi lies several hundred li southwest of the Southern Marchmount Heng, it was not listed in the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) or the Director of Domain (Zhifang shi). Yet the allotment of a residence in Nanjiao is recorded in the Canon of the Emperor (Di dian), and the luxuriant "Eight Cassia" region has, from the Qin and Han down to the present, been renowned through the ages for its famed commanderies—who then could say that the Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhai jing) consists entirely of absurd and groundless words? It is only that in those early times its mountains and rivers still harbored their mysterious and wondrous qualities, and even if…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有雄特右武尠文學故後世
靡得稱云玆敬修幸以校役
遡洮源出靈渠其堯山漓水
環車憺後先奇秀刺目彼靈
氣在天地蜿蜒南下若大軍
鼓行將趨溟海始飲馬蓐食
而三江若帶諸山皆屹然壁
===
立若重關束扼之此其積久
磅礴以待
文明
鴻化厚發於賢儁有顯融也頃歲
十寨平捷告
郊
廟岑溪大峒亦相率蛾伏願繕城
punctuated: 有雄特，右武尠文學，故後世靡得稱云。玆敬修幸以校役，遡洮源，出靈渠，其堯山、漓水環車憺後先，奇秀刺目。彼靈氣在天地，蜿蜒南下，若大軍鼓行，將趨溟海，始飲馬蓐食；而三江若帶，諸山皆屹然壁立，若重關束扼之。此其積久磅礴，以待文明鴻化，厚發於賢儁，有顯融也。頃歲十寨平，捷告郊廟；岑溪、大峒亦相率蛾伏，願繕城
translation_en: … there were outstanding figures, they esteemed martial valor and were sparing in literary learning, so later generations had nothing to praise of them. Now I, Jingxiu, have had the good fortune, on this mission of examining, to travel upstream to the source of the Tao River and emerge from the Ling Canal, where Mount Yao and the Li River surrounded my carriage curtains before and behind, their marvellous beauty striking the eye. That numinous vitality in heaven and earth winds its way southward, like a great army advancing to the beat of drums, about to hasten toward the southern sea, having just watered its horses and eaten on its bedding-mats; meanwhile the Three Rivers are like a sash, and the mountains all stand sheer as walls, as though double passes bound and held them in check. This has accumulated and spread vast over a long time, awaiting our civilized and glorious era and its great transforming influence to burst forth richly in worthy talents who achieve illustrious distinction. In recent years the Ten Stockades (Shizhai) have been pacified, and the victory was announced at the suburban altar and imperial ancestral temple; Cenxi and Dadong have likewise one after another submitted like ants, asking to repair their walls …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
授田如昭江俱齒編氓守亭
障者歲鮮橫草之警川無駭
艫陸無剽橐皆喁喁仰
聖德苞覆萬里諸士益得以從事
鉛槧而希大雅之矩日彬彬
焉卽銓第其所爲文類能明
習世務而不詭於道義其咀
===
華斂鍔視
制式罔失尺矱而英思勁氣坌發
滃溢直與此中奇秀爭雄長
於穎素間莫可禁圉非夫
聖化之型範靈氣之鼓籥也有是
哉顧惟士起三代所敷對率
簡質無長語而考論其所表
punctuated: 授田如昭江，俱齒編氓。守亭障者歲鮮橫草之警，川無駭艫，陸無剽橐，皆喁喁仰聖德苞覆萬里。諸士益得以從事鉛槧，而希大雅之矩，日彬彬焉。卽銓第其所爲文，類能明習世務而不詭於道義；其咀華斂鍔，視制式罔失尺矱，而英思勁氣坌發滃溢，直與此中奇秀爭雄長於穎素間，莫可禁圉。非夫聖化之型範、靈氣之鼓籥也，有是哉？顧惟士起三代，所敷對率簡質無長語，而考論其所表
translation_en: …and receive allotments of land, just as at Zhaojiang, all being enrolled among the registered commoners. Those guarding the outposts and frontier barriers rarely face the alarm of insurgency throughout the year; on the rivers there are no startled vessels, and on land no plundered satchels. All look up in eager admiration as the sagely virtue encompasses and shelters ten thousand li. The scholars have thus been ever more able to devote themselves to writing and scholarship, aspiring to the standards of high elegance and growing daily more refined. Now, in evaluating and ranking the essays they have composed, they generally prove able to understand and be versed in worldly affairs without departing from moral principle. In savoring literary flowers and tempering their sharp edges, they observe the prescribed examination forms without losing a single foot or inch of the standard; yet their heroic thoughts and vigorous spirit burst forth and overflow, directly vying for supremacy with the wondrous beauty of this region upon brush-tip and white silk, impossible to hold back or confine. Were it not for the molding influence of sagely transformation and the bellows-breath of the numinous ether, how could such things be? Yet when we reflect on the scholars who arose in the Three Dynasties, the responses they set forth were generally simple and unadorned, without superfluous words, and when one examines and evaluates what they manifested and…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
樹輒與言相畫一以其心榮
利不入而一意於亮天工明
主德故稱為不二心之臣盛
莫加焉今諸士言則旣纚纚
侈矣假令以厝諸用能一一
必成信者乎夫論疆土則化
軼三代而謂無一庶幾於三
===
代之士者耻也言詞視三代
益閎以肆而行實不相副者
虛也語曰玉產於山工得琢
焉而眞璞不完士脩於家主
得用焉而純白不存信若言
也毋寧
國家熈化靡所恃賴將五嶠三
punctuated: 樹，輒與言相畫一。以其心榮利不入，而一意於亮天工、明主德，故稱為不二心之臣，盛莫加焉。今諸士言則旣纚纚侈矣，假令以厝諸用，能一一必成信者乎？夫論疆土，則化軼三代，而謂無一庶幾於三代之士者，耻也；言詞視三代益閎以肆，而行實不相副者，虛也。語曰：「玉產於山，工得琢焉，而眞璞不完；士脩於家，主得用焉，而純白不存。」信若言也，毋寧國家熈化靡所恃賴，將五嶠三
translation_en: …achieved, their deeds invariably matched their words as one. Because desire for glory and profit did not enter their minds, and they were single-mindedly devoted to assisting in Heaven's work and manifesting their ruler's virtue, they were acclaimed as ministers of undivided loyalty—nothing could surpass such excellence! Now, the words of you scholars are already flowing and extravagant; yet suppose they were put into practice—could each and every one of them certainly prove trustworthy in accomplishment? Indeed, if we speak of territory, our civilizing transformation surpasses that of the Three Dynasties, so to say that there is not a single scholar who approaches those of the Three Dynasties is a disgrace; and for one's rhetoric to be ever more grand and unrestrained compared to that of the Three Dynasties while one's actual conduct fails to match it is emptiness. As the saying goes: "Jade is produced in the mountains, and when the artisan gets to carve it, its true uncarved simplicity is no longer intact; the scholar cultivates himself at home, and when the ruler gets to employ him, his pure, unadorned integrity no longer remains." If this saying were truly so, then not only would the radiant transformation of the state have nothing upon which to rely, but would not the Five Ridges and Three…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
江得無謂其生也實徼靈于
彼今不惠之光寵而重泄越
之慚負若何今有指嘉畝以
語人曰是歲萬鍾其藨蔉不
力登囷不如數則世必以譙
語者爲謾諸士今萬鍾價矣
行奉
===
大對服中外事以自試於藨蔉
一切聲利棼華方日朋起而
戰其中扃稍不制而甘之必
且言行相背馳若兩人然業
何辭而謝斯世之不譙吾謾
也尚務守一於其心如農夫
之有畔歲服勤以爲常罔以
punctuated: 江得無謂其生也，實徼靈于彼，今不惠之光寵，而重泄越之慚，負若何？今有指嘉畝以語人曰：「是歲萬鍾。」其藨蔉不力，登囷不如數，則世必以譙語者爲謾。諸士今萬鍾價矣，行奉大對，服中外事，以自試於藨蔉。一切聲利棼華，方日朋起而戰其中扃，稍不制而甘之，必且言行相背馳，若兩人然。業何辭而謝斯世之不譙吾謾也？尚務守一於其心，如農夫之有畔，歲服勤以爲常，罔以
translation_en: …and Three Rivers not also say that since their very birth in fact drew spiritual efficacy from those lands, if today they do not bestow glory and honor upon them, but instead heap upon them the shame of dissipation and transgression, how great is that betrayal? Suppose someone today points to a fine field and tells people, "This yields ten thousand zhong a year." If the weeding and hilling are not done with effort, and what is brought into the granary falls short of that amount, then the world will surely reproach the speaker as a deceiver. The scholars today are valued at ten thousand zhong! Soon they will present their Great Responses at the Palace Examination and take up service at court and in the provinces, testing themselves in the work of weeding and hilling. Every sort of fame, profit, and纷华 [tangled splendor] will daily rise up together and wage war within their inmost minds. If they fail even slightly to master these and instead indulge in them, their words and deeds will inevitably run counter to each other, as though they were two different people. By what words could we then excuse ourselves and ask the world not to reproach us as deceivers? May they strive to guard single-mindedness in their hearts, like a farmer keeping to his field boundaries, making diligent labor year after year their constant rule, never allowing…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
靡麗渝貞繁膴改素諸所展
錯各求自効其長而要諸衷
皆務斷斷明
主德勿後斯樹駿垂鴻榮鏡史籍
敬修且竦意以拜諸士之貺
是舉也前總督兩廣兵部右
侍郎兼右僉都御史今晉南
京都察院右都御史劉堯誨
威略茂宣弘裨文敎今總督
兩廣兵部尚書兼左副都御
史陳瑞規恢謨烈賁及章縫
巡撫廣西兵部右侍郎兼右
僉都御史郭應聘德威乂孚
文武丕式若前總兵署都督
punctuated:
靡麗渝貞、繁膴改素。諸所展錯，各求自効其長，而要諸衷，皆務斷斷明主德勿後。斯樹駿垂鴻，榮鏡史籍，敬修且竦意以拜諸士之貺。
是舉也，前總督兩廣、兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，今晉南京都察院右都御史劉堯誨，威略茂宣，弘裨文敎；今總督兩廣、兵部尚書兼左副都御史陳瑞，規恢謨烈，賁及章縫；巡撫廣西、兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史郭應聘，德威乂孚，文武丕式。若前總兵、署都督
translation_en:
…extravagance alter their integrity, nor rich emoluments change their plain simplicity. In all that they put into practice and administer, let each seek to exert his strengths in service, while in the depths of their hearts, let all strive single-mindedly to make manifest the Sovereign's virtue without lagging behind. Thus shall they establish great achievements and hand down grand legacies, shining gloriously in the historical records; and I, Jingxiu, shall with respectful attention bow to receive the gift of these scholars' accomplishments.

In this undertaking, the former Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief of the Nanjing Censorate, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, grandly displayed his awe-inspiring strategy and greatly aided civil education; the current Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Minister of War and concurrently Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Chen Rui 陳瑞, expanded his splendid plans and illustrious achievements, bestowing grace upon the Confucian scholars; and the Grand Coordinator of Guangxi, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, Guo Yingping 郭應聘, inspired lasting trust through his virtue and majesty, serving as a great model in both civil and military affairs. As for the former Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同知王尚文崇儒奮武參議
彭應時李淶副使徐儒皆以
綜理宣猷副總兵李應祥參
將白玉金丹周勳署都指揮
僉事戴應麟鍾維岳蔡春及
皆以扞掫祗事其入
賀則右布政使今轉左胡定副
===
使秦寵其遷秩及檄調則右
布政吳善參政項思教參議
陳尚伊副使劉世賞吳哲而
刑部員外郎孫從龍行人司
行人孫愈賢則皆以使
命弭節玆土光重人文者也法得
竝書
punctuated: 同知王尚文，崇儒奮武；參議彭應時、李淶，副使徐儒，皆以綜理宣猷；副總兵李應祥，參將白玉、金丹、周勳，署都指揮僉事戴應麟、鍾維岳、蔡春及，皆以扞掫祗事。其入賀，則右布政使今轉左胡定，副使秦寵；其遷秩及檄調，則右布政吳善，參政項思教，參議陳尚伊，副使劉世賞、吳哲；而刑部員外郎孫從龍，行人司行人孫愈賢，則皆以使命弭節玆土，光重人文者也。法得竝書。
translation_en: … [Acting Commissioner-in-Chief] Vice Commissioner Wang Shangwen 王尚文, who revered Confucian scholars and roused martial vigor; Assistant Administration Commissioners Peng Yingshi 彭應時 and Li Lai 李淶, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Ru 徐儒, who all promulgated administrative plans through comprehensive management; Vice Regional Commander Li Yingxiang 李應祥, Assistant Regional Commanders Bai Yu 白玉, Jin Dan 金丹, and Zhou Xun 周勳, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Dai Yinglin 戴應麟, Zhong Weiyue 鍾維岳, and Cai Chunji 蔡春及, who all respectfully discharged their duties in defense and patrol. Among those who went to the court to offer congratulations were Right Administration Commissioner Hu Ding 胡定, now transferred to Left Administration Commissioner, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qin Chong 秦寵; among those promoted or transferred by dispatch were Right Administration Commissioner Wu Shan 吳善, Administration Vice Commissioner Xiang Sijiao 項思教, Assistant Administration Commissioner Chen Shangyi 陳尚伊, and Surveillance Vice Commissioners Liu Shishang 劉世賞 and Wu Zhe 吳哲; while Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice Sun Conglong 孫從龍 and Messenger in the Messenger Office Sun Yuxian 孫愈賢 both halted their envoys' carriages in this land on imperial missions, bringing luster and weight to literary culture. By standard rule, all are entitled to be recorded together.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
江西贛州府興國縣儒學教
諭汪敬修謹序
punctuated: 江西贛州府興國縣儒學教諭汪敬修謹序。
translation_en: Respectfully prefaced by Wang Jingxiu 汪敬修, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xingguo County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史馬呈圖〔道甫四川內江縣人辛酉貢士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政彭富〔中禮雲南大理衛籍合肥縣人壬戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政胡維新〔文化浙江餘姚縣人己未進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使陳應春〔汝和福建長樂縣人壬戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政兼按察司僉事葉朝陽〔見心浙江秀水縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
江西贛州府興國縣儒學教諭汪敬修〔道卿直隸婺源縣人庚午貢士〕
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教諭賈宗正〔誠甫浙江東陽縣人庚午貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府蘭陽縣儒學教諭梁懋勳〔孺建廣東番禺縣人甲子貢士〕
湖廣鄖陽府竹山縣儒學教諭王希堯〔惟中雲南中衛籍直隸當塗縣人己卯貢士〕
應天府溧陽縣儒學訓導郭藎臣〔孝仲四川成都縣人丙子貢士〕
湖廣長沙府湘鄉縣儒學訓導丁繼宗〔惟孝湖廣沅州人丁卯貢士〕
直隸蘇州府長洲縣儒學訓導張沛〔德夫福建甌寧縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆十年廣西鄉試

監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史馬呈圖〔道甫，四川內江縣人，辛酉貢士。〕

提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參政彭富〔中禮，雲南大理衛籍，合肥縣人，壬戌進士。〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政胡維新〔文化，浙江餘姚縣人，己未進士。〕

監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使陳應春〔汝和，福建長樂縣人，壬戌進士。〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司右參政兼按察司僉事葉朝陽〔見心，浙江秀水縣人，乙丑進士。〕

考試官
江西贛州府興國縣儒學教諭汪敬修〔道卿，直隸婺源縣人，庚午貢士。〕
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教諭賈宗正〔誠甫，浙江東陽縣人，庚午貢士。〕

同考試官
河南開封府蘭陽縣儒學教諭梁懋勳〔孺建，廣東番禺縣人，甲子貢士。〕

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰辭達而已矣
脩道之謂教道也者不可須臾離也
舜何人也予何人也有爲者亦若是
易
聖人養賢以及萬民
九二之孚有喜也
言行君子之所以動天地也可不慎乎
===
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
有能奮庸煕帝之載使宅百揆亮采惠疇
非天私我有商惟天佑于一德
下民惟民歸于一德德惟一動罔不吉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
子曰：「辭達而已矣。」
「脩道之謂教。道也者，不可須臾離也。」
「舜，何人也？予，何人也？有爲者亦若是。」

易：
「聖人養賢以及萬民。」
「九二之孚，有喜也。」
「言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎？」
「昔者聖人之作《易》也，將以順性命之理。是以立天之道，曰陰與陽；立地之道，曰柔與剛；立人之道，曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故《易》六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故《易》六位而成章。」

書：
「有能奮庸煕帝之載，使宅百揆，亮采惠疇？」
「非天私我有商，惟天佑于一德；下民惟民歸于一德。德惟一，動罔不吉。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books (Sishu):
"The Master said, 'In language it is simply required that it convey the meaning.'" (Analects 15.41)
"'Cultivating the Way is called instruction. As for the Way, it may not be left for an instant.'" (Doctrine of the Mean 1)
"'What kind of man was Shun? What kind of man am I? Anyone who makes the effort can also become like that.'" (Mencius 3A.1)

Classic of Changes (Yi):
"'The sage nourishes the worthy, and thereby reaches the myriad people.'" (Hexagram 27, Yi, Commentary on the Decision)
"'The sincerity of Nine in the Second Place brings joy.'" (Hexagram 58, Dui, Commentary on the Images)
"'Words and deeds are that whereby the noble man moves Heaven and Earth. Must one not be cautious with them?'" (Great Commentary, Part I, 8)
"'In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes, they intended it to accord with the principles of inherent nature and destiny. Therefore they established the Way of Heaven and called it Yin and Yang; they established the Way of Earth and called it the Soft and the Hard; they established the Way of Man and called it Benevolence and Righteousness. Combining the Three Powers and doubling them, therefore in the Changes six lines form a hexagram; dividing the Yin and dividing the Yang, and alternately using the Soft and the Hard, therefore in the Changes six positions form a pattern.'" (Discussion of the Trigrams, 2)

Classic of Documents (Shu):
"'Is there anyone who can vigorously display his merits and make bright the Emperor's undertakings, whom I may place in charge of all the ministers, to assist in affairs and accord with his peers?'" ("Canon of Shun")
"'It was not that Heaven was partial to our House of Shang; it was only that Heaven aided pure and single virtue. [It was not that our Shang sought] the lower people; it was only that the people turned to pure and single virtue. Where virtue is pure and single, every movement is without fail auspicious.'" ("Both Possessed Pure Virtue")

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歲月日時無易百穀用成
惟公克成厥終
詩
我稼旣同上入執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索
綯亟其乘屋其始播百穀二之日鑿氷
冲冲三之日納于凌陰四之日其蚤獻
羔祭韭
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天
受祿于天保右命之自天申之干祿百福
===
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
成王不敢康夙夜基命宥密
春秋
夏單伯會伐宋莊公十有四年
次于陘 楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵俱
僖公四年
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒成公九年秋楚公
子壬夫帥師侵宋襄公元年
五月公及諸侯盟于皐鼬定公四年
punctuated:
「歲月日時無易，百穀用成。」
「惟公克成厥終。」

《詩》
「我稼旣同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿氷冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。」
「鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。」
「受祿于天，保右命之，自天申之。干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。」
「成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。」

《春秋》
「夏，單伯會伐宋。」（莊公十有四年）
「次于陘。」「楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。」（俱僖公四年）
「楚公子嬰齊帥師伐莒。」（成公九年）「秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋。」（襄公元年）
「五月，公及諸侯盟于皐鼬。」（定公四年）
translation_en:
"When the years, months, days, and hours have no irregularity, all the grains are brought to maturity."
"Only you, the Duke, can bring it to its completion."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"When our harvest is gathered in, we go up and enter to undertake the work on the houses. By day go gather the thatch-grass, by night twist it into ropes. Hasten to get up on the roofs; soon we shall begin to sow the hundred grains. In the days of the second month, they hew out the ice with ringing blows; in the days of the third month, they convey it to the ice-house; in the days of the fourth month, very early, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with scallions."
"The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the heavens."
"He receives blessings from Heaven; it protects, helps, and appoints him, and from Heaven repeats its favors to him. In seeking office he obtains a hundred blessings, and his descendants are a thousand, a hundred million. Solemn and august, fit to be lord, fit to be king!"
"Cheng Wang did not dare to take his ease; morning and night he laid the foundations of the appointment in deep and quiet wisdom."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In summer, the Earl of Shan joined in invading Song." (Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang)
"The armies halted at Xing." "Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the armies; a covenant was made at Shaoling." (Both in the fourth year of Duke Xi)
"Prince Yingqi of Chu led a force and invaded Ju." (Ninth year of Duke Cheng) "In autumn, Prince Renfu of Chu led a force and made an incursion into Song." (First year of Duke Xiang)
"In the fifth month, the Duke and the feudal lords made a covenant at Gaoyou." (Fourth year of Duke Ding)

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禮記
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
天子使其大夫爲三監監於方伯之國
大章章之也
儒有內稱不辟親外舉不辟怨程功積事
推賢而進達之不望其報君得其志苟
利國家不求富貴其舉賢援能有如此
者
第貳場
===
論
平天下之要道
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬宋以文彦博富弼同平章事誥〔至和二〕
〔年〕
擬吏部尚書兼翰林院學士李賢等
進
大明一統志表〔天順五年〕
punctuated:
《禮記》：
「凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。」
「天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國。」
「大章，章之也。」
「儒有內稱不辟親，外舉不辟怨；程功積事，推賢而進達之，不望其報。君得其志，苟利國家，不求富貴。其舉賢援能有如此者。」

第貳場
論：
「平天下之要道。」

詔誥表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢賜天下田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬宋以文彦博、富弼同平章事誥〔至和二年〕。
擬吏部尚書兼翰林院學士李賢等進《大明一統志》表〔天順五年〕。
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"Whenever one serves as an envoy for the ruler, once he has received the command, the ruler's words do not remain overnight at his home."
"The Son of Heaven appoints his Grand Masters as the Three Overseers, to oversee the states of the Regional Earls."
"The 'Great Brilliance' (Dazhang) music means to make illustrious."
"The Confucian scholar, in recommending from within, does not avoid kinsmen, and in nominating from without, does not avoid enemies. He measures merits and accumulates achievements, recommending the worthy and advancing them without expecting any recompense. When his ruler attains his ambition, so long as it benefits the state, the scholar seeks neither wealth nor eminence. Such is his way of nominating the worthy and bringing forward the capable."

Second Session
Discourse:
"The Essential Way of Pacifying the Realm."

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial (answer one of the following):
An imitation of the Han edict granting the realm a remission of half the land tax (second year of Emperor Wen [178 BCE]).
An imitation of the Song mandate appointing Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi jointly as Joint Managers of Affairs (second year of the Zhihe era [1055]).
An imitation of the memorial by Minister of Personnel concurrently Hanlin Academician Li Xian and others presenting the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi) (fifth year of the Tianshun era [1461]).

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
判語五條
講讀律令
市司評物價
私越冒度關津
聞有恩赦而故犯
有司官吏不住公廨
第叁場
策五道
問書陳典學詩咏緝煕即紀傳所稱唐虞
===
三代之隆亦各有師授故君人者未有
不懋學而能以明聖自表見者也後世
學術廢闕主德鮮茂間有喜近儒紳游
神縹素則前史以為艷談若召講石渠
稱制臨決講論經理夜分不寐精選文
學之士更日直宿引入與論前言往行
自巳至申然後釋卷寫尚書無逸篇于
屏玆其章章較著也其於古帝王所謂
學者同乎抑或華實異也
punctuated:
判語五條：
講讀律令；
市司評物價；
私越冒度關津；
聞有恩赦而故犯；
有司官吏不住公廨。

第叁場
策五道

問：《書》陳典學，《詩》咏緝煕；即紀傳所稱唐、虞、三代之隆，亦各有師授。故君人者，未有不懋學而能以明聖自表見者也。後世學術廢闕，主德鮮茂。間有喜近儒紳、游神縹素，則前史以為艷談。若召講石渠，稱制臨決；講論經理，夜分不寐；精選文學之士，更日直宿；引入與論前言往行，自巳至申然後釋卷；寫《尚書·無逸篇》于屏：玆其章章較著也。其於古帝王所謂學者同乎？抑或華實異也？

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上神聖天縱
銳意進脩
卽位以來非隆冬盛夏不輟
講筵卽
端居
禁中亦日
親典籍無它嗜好雖高成不足侔矣顧帝王之
學非專事博雅爲名必有本始嘗觀我
太祖
===
成祖與儒臣論經術治理每推原於心體
世宗殖學甚盛而
敬一之箴學士大夫至今誦之玆非卓然與
唐虞三代同源合契者哉玆欲繩
祖武而纂
聖傳惟
聖天子已有定術顧揚厲
休美而因獻其矻矻之思以少佐
聖學之萬一則諸士烏得以不敏謝也其著于
punctuated: 皇上神聖天縱，銳意進脩。卽位以來，非隆冬盛夏不輟講筵；卽端居禁中，亦日親典籍，無它嗜好，雖高、成不足侔矣。顧帝王之學，非專事博雅爲名，必有本始。嘗觀我太祖、成祖與儒臣論經術治理，每推原於心體；世宗殖學甚盛，而《敬一》之箴，學士大夫至今誦之。玆非卓然與唐、虞、三代同源合契者哉？玆欲繩祖武而纂聖傳，惟聖天子已有定術；顧揚厲休美，而因獻其矻矻之思，以少佐聖學之萬一，則諸士烏得以不敏謝也？其著于…
translation_en: His Majesty the Emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, is keenly committed to advancing in learning and self-cultivation. Since ascending the throne, save during the depth of winter and the height of summer, he has never suspended the Classics Mat lectures; even when dwelling in solemn retirement within the Forbidden Palace, he daily familiarizes himself with the canonical texts and has no other indulgences—so that even Gaozong of Yin and King Cheng of Zhou are not enough to match him. Yet the learning of emperors and kings does not consist merely in pursuing broad erudition for the sake of reputation; it must have a fundamental source. I have observed that when Our Taizu and Chengzu discussed classical scholarship and principles of governance with their Confucian ministers, they invariably traced them back to the substance of the mind; and Shizong cultivated learning in great abundance, while his Admonition on Reverent Singleness (Jingyi zhi zhen) is recited by scholars and grandees to this day. Does this not stand out as sharing the same origin and tallying perfectly with Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties? Now, in wishing to follow in the footsteps of the imperial ancestors and carry on the transmission of the sages, the Sage Son of Heaven already possesses an established method; yet to extol his splendid virtues and thereby offer up your diligent reflections so as to give some slight aid—even a ten-thousandth part—to his sage learning: how could you gentlemen decline on the plea of dullness? Set this forth in…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
篇
問帝王保命凝圖於天人之際兢兢焉稽
古孰踰堯舜二典所載可鏡已三代而
後時亦有詔災異求直言與蠲租賑粟
者以文以實可指乎我
太祖順天應人再造寰宇考其求言之
詔或以五星竝見或以七曜紊度而蠲賑之
令無歲不下何
敕天閔人之切也亦可揚厲之幷遡其本歟今
===
皇上
德茂中外
道洽華夷至盛也邇象緯失次至廑
下諭脩省都畿彌月不雨疫癘爲眚則又
躬自齋禱卽靈雨三應且不謂祥貺也更
命司農發帑賑卹惠藥以濟所疾苦覈民間積
逋盡蠲之春噓和洽咸用汔康此其
敬天勤民之心何如于
祖宗有相符否夫
punctuated:
篇。
問：帝王保命凝圖，於天人之際兢兢焉。稽古孰踰堯、舜？《二典》所載，可鏡已。三代而後，時亦有詔災異、求直言，與蠲租賑粟者，以文、以實，可指乎？我太祖順天應人，再造寰宇。考其求言之詔，或以五星竝見，或以七曜紊度；而蠲賑之令，無歲不下。何敕天閔人之切也！亦可揚厲之，幷遡其本歟？今皇上德茂中外，道洽華夷，至盛也。邇象緯失次，至廑下諭脩省。都畿彌月不雨，疫癘爲眚，則又躬自齋禱；卽靈雨三應，且不謂祥貺也。更命司農發帑賑卹，惠藥以濟所疾苦，覈民間積逋盡蠲之。春噓和洽，咸用汔康。此其敬天勤民之心何如？于祖宗有相符否？夫
translation_en:
… your essays.
Question: In preserving the Mandate and consolidating their rule, emperors and kings have been cautiously reverent regarding the relationship between Heaven and humankind. Examining antiquity, who surpassed Yao and Shun? What is recorded in the Two Canons (Er dian) can serve as a mirror. After the Three Dynasties, there were also times when edicts were issued on the occasion of natural disasters and anomalies to seek candid remonstrance, and when taxes were remitted and grain distributed in relief. Which of these were mere formality and which were substantive—can you point them out? Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), acting in accordance with Heaven and responding to the people, remade the realm. If we examine his edicts seeking counsel, some were prompted by the simultaneous appearance of the five planets, others by the seven luminaries falling out of their regular courses; meanwhile, orders for tax remission and famine relief were handed down without a single year's interruption. How earnest was his reverence for Heaven's warnings and his compassion for the people! Can you also extol these deeds and trace them back to their fundamental source? Today, His Majesty's virtue flourishes both within the court and throughout the provinces, and his Way permeates Chinese and non-Chinese alike; this is the height of prosperity. Recently, when the celestial bodies lost their regular order, it went so far as to trouble him to issue edicts calling for self-cultivation and introspection. When the capital region went a full month without rain and epidemic disease wrought affliction, he personally fasted and prayed; even when timely rains responded three times, he still did not regard them as auspicious blessings. Instead, he further commanded the Minister of Revenue (sinong) to disburse treasury funds for relief and aid, to bestow medicines to succor those suffering from illness, and to verify the accumulated tax arrears among the people and remit them in full. Like the warm breath of spring spreading harmony, all were thereby brought to peace and well-being. What is the nature of this heart that reveres Heaven and labors diligently for the people? Does it correspond with that of the Imperial Ancestors? Now, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天心仁愛因象致儆今旣消弭之顧
當宁尤切切不置卽非
堯舜之心與諸士生斯世幸親見之豈無所攄
究以寬
宸懷萬分一執事者將轉以
聞
問太史公有言學者載籍極博猶考信於
六藝則周孔代降士之立言者第取諸
六藝足矣而何其說之多岐也漢初止
===
敘六家其後稍別爲九流而諸子肇編
則自周文有感於捕獸逐麋之對而師
事鬻子始也嗣是老莊競鶩而鬼谷鶡
冠子華野老青史尉繚皆以子名紛紛
莫可究詰云漢成帝始令劉子政校讎
殺青所紀凡百八十餘家視前滋侈矣
迨梁通事舍人復加品隲之爲說似核
然首稱諸子爲入道見志之書而大賢
若子輿氏亦臚列其內何比方失倫也
punctuated:
天心仁愛，因象致儆。今旣消弭之，顧當宁尤切切不置，卽非堯、舜之心與？諸士生斯世，幸親見之，豈無所攄究，以寬宸懷萬分一？執事者將轉以聞。
問：太史公有言：「學者載籍極博，猶考信於六藝。」則周、孔代降，士之立言者第取諸六藝足矣，而何其說之多岐也？漢初止敘六家，其後稍別爲九流；而諸子肇編，則自周文有感於捕獸逐麋之對，而師事鬻子始也。嗣是老、莊競鶩，而鬼谷、鶡冠、子華、野老、青史、尉繚皆以「子」名，紛紛莫可究詰云。漢成帝始令劉子政校讎殺青，所紀凡百八十餘家，視前滋侈矣。迨梁通事舍人復加品隲之，爲說似核，然首稱「諸子爲入道見志之書」，而大賢若子輿氏亦臚列其內，何比方失倫也！
translation_en:
… Heaven’s heart is benevolent and loving, sending warnings through celestial phenomena. Now, even after these portents have been dispelled, the Emperor on the throne remains earnestly concerned and will not set the matter aside—is this not the very mind of Yao and Shun? Born into this age and fortunate enough to witness this in person, how could you scholars have nothing to set forth from your inquiries to ease the imperial solicitude by even one part in ten thousand? The officiating examiners will transmit your responses to the throne.

Question: The Grand Historian [Sima Qian 司馬遷] once said, “Though written records available to scholars are vastly extensive, one must still verify their credibility against the Six Arts.” Thus, in the ages following the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, it should have sufficed for scholars establishing their own teachings simply to draw upon the Six Arts—why, then, did their doctrines diverge in so many directions? In the early Han, only Six Schools were recounted, which were later further differentiated into the Nine Streams. Yet the compilation of the Various Masters (zhuzi 諸子) actually began when King Wen of Zhou, moved by the reply concerning catching beasts and chasing elk, served Master Yu (Yuzi 鬻子) as his teacher. Thereafter, Laozi and Zhuangzi vied in pursuing their own paths, while Guiguzi 鬼谷子, Heguanzi 鶡冠子, Zihuazi 子華子, Yelao 野老, Qingshizi 青史子, and Weiliaozi 尉繚子 all took the title of “Master” (zi 子), proliferating in such confusion that they could hardly be exhaustively investigated. Emperor Cheng of the Han first ordered Liu Zizheng [Liu Xiang 劉向] to collate and prepare the bamboo texts; what he recorded totaled more than one hundred and eighty schools, far more expansive than before. Coming down to the Liang dynasty, the Palace Receptionist [Liu Xie 劉勰] further evaluated and ranked them. His account seems incisive, yet he begins by declaring that “the Various Masters are books for entering the Way and manifesting one’s intent,” and even lists a great worthy such as Mister Ziyu [Mencius 孟子] among them—how improperly matched and out of order is such a comparison! …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
顧其說其人可詳述歟厥後齊丘文中
鹿門玄眞代有著述較前數子其說孰
爲得也頃者士習浮誕爲文或祖述老
莊靡曼不根之談數
下功令禁止至其覽華而食實棄邪而採正
不爲彼說所誘奪則在其人自决擇何
如爾玆欲舉諸子而別以九流舉九流
而本諸六家要其歸務不詭於六藝其
究安在幸詳言之非第以徵博雅也
===
問古者司勳詔功祭于大烝爲典凡六其
有道與德者使敎焉沒則以爲樂祖而
祭于瞽宗次亦祠于社示不忘云玆名
宦鄕賢之所爲祀也
明興立二祠于學宮歲二丁釋奠畢有司帥博
士弟子謁祠意義甚盛姑無暇遠引卽
以粵西舊牒所紀載者而尚論其世則
宦蹟自史祿而下百數十人其中則有
歌賈父來晚者有稱府君恩廣大者有
punctuated:
顧其說其人，可詳述歟？厥後齊丘、文中、鹿門、玄眞，代有著述，較前數子，其說孰爲得也？頃者士習浮誕，爲文或祖述老、莊靡曼不根之談，數下功令禁止。至其覽華而食實，棄邪而採正，不爲彼說所誘奪，則在其人自决擇何如爾。玆欲舉諸子而別以九流，舉九流而本諸六家，要其歸務不詭於六藝，其究安在？幸詳言之，非第以徵博雅也。

問：古者司勳詔功，祭于大烝，爲典凡六。其有道與德者使敎焉，沒則以爲樂祖而祭于瞽宗，次亦祠于社，示不忘云，玆名宦、鄕賢之所爲祀也。明興，立二祠于學宮，歲二丁釋奠畢，有司帥博士弟子謁祠，意義甚盛。姑無暇遠引，卽以粵西舊牒所紀載者，而尚論其世。則宦蹟自史祿而下百數十人，其中則有歌賈父來晚者，有稱府君恩廣大者，有
translation_en:
Yet can that discourse and that man be recounted in detail? Thereafter, Qiqiu 齊丘 (Tan Qiao 譚峭, Qiqiuzi 齊丘子), Wenzhong 文中 (Wang Tong 王通, Wenzhongzi 文中子), Lumen 鹿門 (Pi Rixiu 皮日休, Lumenzi 鹿門子), and Xuanzhen 玄眞 (Zhang Zhihe 張志和, Xuanzhenzi 玄眞子) wrote works across succeeding ages; compared with the several masters mentioned before, whose teachings were closer to the mark? Recently, literati customs have grown frivolous and extravagant, and in composing essays some model themselves on the ornate, baseless talk of Laozi 老子 and Zhuangzi 莊子, so that official regulations have repeatedly been handed down to prohibit it. As for surveying the blossoms while feeding on the fruit, casting aside the heterodox while selecting the orthodox, and not being seduced or robbed of one's judgment by their doctrines—that depends simply on how a person makes his own choice. Now, if we wish to take up the Various Masters and classify them into the Nine Streams, and take up the Nine Streams and trace them back to the Six Schools, while ensuring that their ultimate aim does not deviate from the Six Arts, where does the final resolution lie? Please set this forth in detail; this is not merely to test your breadth of learning and refinement.

Question: In antiquity, the Director of Merit Awards (sixun 司勳) proclaimed meritorious deeds for sacrifice at the Great Winter Sacrifice (dazheng 大烝), for which there were six categories of canons in all. Those who possessed the Way and virtue were employed to teach; when they died, they were honored as Patriarchs of Music (yuezu 樂祖) and sacrificed to in the Hall of the Blind Musicians (guzong 瞽宗), or next in rank were enshrined at the local altar of the soil (she 社), so as to show that they were not forgotten. This is the origin of the sacrifices to Eminent Officials (minghuan 名宦) and Local Worthies (xiangxian 鄉賢). With the rise of the Ming, two shrines were established within the Confucian school compounds. Twice each year, on the ding days after the śākyamuni-like libation sacrifice to Confucius (shidian 釋奠) is completed, the local authorities lead the erudites and students to pay homage at the shrines—an institution of most magnificent import. Setting aside distant examples for the moment, let us examine past ages simply on the basis of what is recorded in the old registers of western Yue (Guangxi). In official achievements, from Shi Lu 史祿 downward there have been well over a hundred men. Among them were one of whom people sang, "Father Jia (Jia Cong 賈琮) came late!"; one of whom people praised the Prefect's boundless grace; one who…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
便宜活萬夫者有恩信被異域者此其
彪然較著也獻民自陳元而下亦百數
人則有士依避難者有再試及第而高
遜者有抵營諭賊使順歸者有去邕州
而人思之如一日者亦其彪然較著也
可具述歟頃者積漸滋濫
天子
令禮臣覆言官疏
下郡國釐正之至斤斤矣顧典籍廢缺靡所
考鏡故有列祀者未必皆名賢而名且
賢者曾不得以希俎豆之餘芬與烝庶
無異甚非所以重盛典章往而勸來也
玆欲精覈而愼擇之務令祀必當其實
毋徇世俗爲低昂其道何繇願悉心言
之以觀嚮往
問聖人養天下在田賦爲貢爲助爲徹其
法在正經界心至均也三代下田不皆
在官故有限有均有永業爲塞兼幷計
punctuated:
便宜活萬夫者，有恩信被異域者，此其彪然較著也。獻民自陳元而下亦百數人，則有士依避難者，有再試及第而高遜者，有抵營諭賊使順歸者，有去邕州而人思之如一日者，亦其彪然較著也。可具述歟？頃者積漸滋濫，天子令禮臣覆言官疏，下郡國釐正之，至斤斤矣。顧典籍廢缺，靡所考鏡，故有列祀者未必皆名賢，而名且賢者曾不得以希俎豆之餘芬，與烝庶無異，甚非所以重盛典、章往而勸來也。玆欲精覈而愼擇之，務令祀必當其實，毋徇世俗爲低昂，其道何繇？願悉心言之，以觀嚮往。

問：聖人養天下在田賦，爲貢、爲助、爲徹，其法在正經界，心至均也。三代下田不皆在官，故有限、有均、有永業，爲塞兼幷計…
translation_en:
… those who acted on their own authority as circumstances demanded to save the lives of ten thousand men, and those whose grace and good faith extended to foreign lands—these are the most brilliantly conspicuous among them. As for local worthies, from Chen Yuan 陳元 on down there have also been a hundred or more: there were those upon whom scholars relied for refuge in times of turmoil, those who passed the examinations with high honors a second time yet loftily withdrew into retirement, those who went straight into rebel camps to admonish the bandits and bring them to peaceful submission, and those who after leaving Yongzhou 邕州 were longed for by the people as if not a day had passed—these too are the most brilliantly conspicuous among them. Can you recount them in detail? Recently, over time, the selections have become increasingly indiscriminate. The Son of Heaven ordered the officials of the Ministry of Rites to review the memorials of the speaking officials, and sent orders down to the prefectures and principalities to rectify the rosters—most discerning and meticulous indeed! Yet because records and registers have fallen into ruin and are incomplete, there is nothing to examine as a mirror of the past. Thus, those who are enrolled for sacrifice are not necessarily all eminent or worthy, while those who were truly eminent and worthy cannot even hope for the lingering fragrance of the sacrificial vessels, being treated no differently from the common multitude. This is gravely contrary to the purpose of honoring a grand institution, illustrating the past, and encouraging the future. Now, if we wish to verify with precision and select with care, ensuring that the sacrifices unfailingly match true merit without bowing to vulgar worldly opinion in raising or lowering anyone, by what way may this be achieved? I hope you will speak of this with your whole mind, so that we may observe where your aspirations lie.

Question: The sages nourished the Empire through land and taxes. Whether by the Tribute (gong 貢), Aid (zhu 助), or Tithing (che 徹) system, their method lay in rectifying the field boundaries, and their intention was the utmost equity. After the Three Dynasties, land did not all belong to the state; thus there were systems of land limitation (xiantian 限田), land equalization (juntian 均田), and perpetual holdings (yongye 永業), designed to block land aggrandizement…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
耳其于古法得失何如承平日久詭灑
吞噬賦且混淆矣百姓苦之幸
天子神聖
下所司清丈天下莫不願觀化成緩須臾視
息也寧獨粤以西姑即粤以西清丈言
之古今墾業若干盈虧無定數能試屈
指否
憲式示所部則官履畝胥里執度罔不詳覈
敝源則平額復夙夜祗竣玆役矣第魚
===
鱗叢造舞弄抽移究詰爲難郡若縣長
吏少不慎偵之不無貽憂異日者否况
俠豪大家佃僕異種相藉避征稅久之
恐成厲階破壞良法以累蔀屋氓不淺
計坊之當何以重之人有遺力故地有
遺利將何以督成之地有可耕人無可
耕將何以招徠之猺獞非吾族類將何
以馴伏使回心疾耕以同齊民世酋負
固隱蓄將何以處置俾盡獻圖版以增
punctuated: 耳。其于古法得失何如？承平日久，詭灑吞噬，賦且混淆矣，百姓苦之。幸天子神聖，下所司清丈，天下莫不願觀化成，緩須臾視息也，寧獨粤以西！姑即粤以西清丈言之：古今墾業若干，盈虧無定數，能試屈指否？憲式示所部，則官履畝，胥里執度，罔不詳覈敝源，則平、額復，夙夜祗竣玆役矣。第魚鱗叢造，舞弄抽移，究詰爲難，郡若縣長吏少不慎偵之，不無貽憂異日者否？况俠豪大家，佃僕異種，相藉避征稅，久之恐成厲階，破壞良法，以累蔀屋氓不淺。計坊之當何以重之？人有遺力，故地有遺利，將何以督成之？地有可耕，人無可耕，將何以招徠之？猺、獞非吾族類，將何以馴伏，使回心疾耕，以同齊民？世酋負固隱蓄，將何以處置，俾盡獻圖版，以增
translation_en:
… only. How do their merits and defects compare to the ancient methods? After a long period of peace, through fraudulent registration, parceling out of holdings, and predatory annexation, the tax assessments have fallen into confusion, and the common people suffer from it. Fortunately, the Son of Heaven in his divine sagacity has ordered the competent authorities to conduct a cadastral survey. No one in the realm does not wish to linger a moment longer in life to witness the completion of this transformation—and how could this be true only of the region west of Guangdong [Guangxi]? Let us speak provisionally of the cadastral survey in Guangxi: how much land has been reclaimed from antiquity to the present, and as its gains and losses have no fixed numbers, can you try to reckon them on your fingers?

Model regulations have been promulgated to the subordinate jurisdictions: officials inspect the fields in person, while clerks and village heads hold the measuring rods; none fail to thoroughly investigate the sources of abuse, so that tax grades are equalized and quotas restored, working reverently day and night to complete this task. Yet when the fish-scale registers are compiled in great masses, clerks manipulate them by extracting and shifting entries, making investigation and verification difficult. If prefectural and county magistrates are the least bit careless in inspecting them, will this not inevitably leave trouble for a future day? Moreover, powerful magnates and great families, whose tenants and bondservants are of non-Han stock, rely on one another to evade tax levies. Over time, there is reason to fear this will become a source of calamity, ruining good laws and gravely burdening the common folk in their thatched huts. In devising means to guard against [坊, read 防?] this, how should we give it due weight? Because people have untapped strength, the land has untapped benefits—how shall we supervise and bring this to fruition? Where there is land fit for tillage but no people to till it, how shall we attract settlers? The Yao and Zhuang are not of our kind—how shall we tame and pacify them so that they turn their hearts to diligent farming and become like the registered commoners? Hereditary chieftains rely on their strongholds to conceal resources and populations—how shall we deal with them so that they present all their maps and registers to increase…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國額夫必使土無曠民無游卽寸尺盡入貢
賦斯毋負於
聖人均天下之心也諸生首四民受廛或有慨
于中如漢文學論鹽鐵者其籌之
punctuated: 國額？夫必使土無曠、民無游，卽寸尺盡入貢賦，斯毋負於聖人均天下之心也。諸生首四民受廛，或有慨于中，如漢文學論鹽鐵者，其籌之。
translation_en: …the state's tax quota? Truly, only when we ensure that no land lies fallow and no people wander idle, so that every inch and foot is brought into tribute and taxation, will we not fail the Sage's intention of equalizing the realm. You students stand at the head of the four classes of people who hold homesteads; perhaps you harbor deep reflections within, like the Han literati who debated salt and iron. Lay out your plans for this!
