title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天下而會之心本也以吾心而通乎天下機也
不求其本則將率吾之意而强人必從不持其
機則雖有意於人之從而其勢亦從窒也然則
天下之不治未必皆斯人之過或者吾亦有過
焉爾君子之道則不然卽吾之所欲而推之而
不病其爲私因人之所欲而應之而不嫌其爲
徇吾固不待施之政敎而其心將日下焉者必
不吾違天下亦不待吾政敎之加而其心將日
上焉者必不吾拂始也能通天下之志而終也
===
聯屬天下以成其身此致治之所以爲盛也而
其要豈外于絜矩哉曷觀之天地乎天地之于
萬物未嘗有心而能使萬物各得其所靈者爲
人蠢者爲鳥獸跂息蠕動者爲昆虫皆以類聚
足于天地之化而無不均焉故曰天地無心而
成化至于栽培傾覆之際若其有必然者而亦
非有所厚薄其間是故春榮而秋瘁晝動而夜
息雖物亦不自知其所以然而於天地又奚憾
焉使其道有所偏則物不得其平而天地之化
punctuated: 天下而會之心，本也；以吾心而通乎天下，機也。不求其本，則將率吾之意而强人必從；不持其機，則雖有意於人之從，而其勢亦從窒也。然則天下之不治，未必皆斯人之過，或者吾亦有過焉爾。君子之道則不然，卽吾之所欲而推之，而不病其爲私；因人之所欲而應之，而不嫌其爲徇。吾固不待施之政敎，而其心將日：「下焉者必不吾違。」天下亦不待吾政敎之加，而其心將日：「上焉者必不吾拂。」始也能通天下之志，而終也聯屬天下以成其身，此致治之所以爲盛也，而其要豈外于絜矩哉？曷觀之天地乎？天地之于萬物，未嘗有心，而能使萬物各得其所。靈者爲人，蠢者爲鳥獸，跂息蠕動者爲昆虫，皆以類聚，足于天地之化，而無不均焉。故曰：「天地無心而成化。」至于栽培傾覆之際，若其有必然者，而亦非有所厚薄其間。是故春榮而秋瘁，晝動而夜息，雖物亦不自知其所以然，而於天地又奚憾焉？使其道有所偏，則物不得其平，而天地之化
translation_en: … the entire world and unifying it in one's mind is the foundation; using my mind to communicate with the entire world is the pivotal mechanism. If one does not seek the foundation, one will follow one's own willful intentions and force others to obey; if one does not grasp the mechanism, then even if one wishes for others to follow, the situation will inevitably become obstructed. Thus, when the world is not well governed, it is not necessarily all the fault of the people; perhaps I, too, have faults in the matter. The Way of the noble man is not so. He extends what he himself desires without worrying that it is selfish; he responds according to what others desire without suspecting that it is pandering. Before I even apply government and instruction, my mind will say: "Those below will surely not defy me." And before the world even experiences the application of my government and instruction, its mind will say: "He who is above will surely not oppose us." In the beginning, he is able to comprehend the aspirations of the world, and in the end, he binds the world together as one body with his own person. This is how the attainment of order becomes flourishing—and how could its essence lie outside the principle of the measuring square (xieju)? Why not observe Heaven and Earth? Toward the myriad things, Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind, yet they enable the myriad things each to find its proper place. The intelligent become humans, the dull-witted become birds and beasts, and those that crawl, breathe, and wriggle become insects and reptiles; all gather according to their kind, finding sufficiency in the transformations of Heaven and Earth without any inequality. Therefore it is said: "Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind and yet accomplish transformation." When it comes to planting and nurturing or overthrowing and destroying, although there seems to be an inevitability to it, there is no partiality of favor or disfavor therein. For this reason, things flourish in spring and wither in autumn, move by day and rest by night; even the things themselves do not know why they are so, so what resentment could they harbor toward Heaven and Earth? If their Way were biased in any respect, things would not obtain their equilibrium, and the transformations of Heaven and Earth…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
或幾乎塞矣故曰以直養萬物夫聖人之道猶
天地也聖人之于萬民猶其于萬物也然天地
無心以成之而聖人有心以應之宜若異于天
地焉者而不知聖人之心上與天地一下與天
下一雖聖人不得以私心與之而天下囿于聖
人之道亦若天之覆地之載而取足于聖人之
仁是其有心之化未必非無心者以致之也君
子知治天下之道其本在我而其機又不必求
諸天下故反而觀之吾心焉思吾所喜天下必
===
有欣然以同樂者思吾所憎天下必有拂然以
同惡者思吾所憂天下必有惻然以同戚者思
吾所懼天下必有凜然以同畏者夫吾凡以求
治者為天下也非為我也故其視吾之心惟天
下而其視天下皆吾之心其忍恝然而已哉蓋
天下之所欲不能自遂必賴吾以濟之而其所
惡亦不能自去又必賴吾以袪之然則天下之
望我也甚殷而我之慰天下也亦甚切蓋嘗盡
吾之孝矣而不忍民之頑囂未變也蓋嘗致吾
punctuated: 或幾乎塞矣。故曰：「以直養萬物。」夫聖人之道，猶天地也；聖人之于萬民，猶其于萬物也。然天地無心以成之，而聖人有心以應之，宜若異于天地焉者；而不知聖人之心，上與天地一，下與天下一，雖聖人不得以私心與之，而天下囿于聖人之道，亦若天之覆、地之載，而取足于聖人之仁，是其有心之化，未必非無心者以致之也。君子知治天下之道，其本在我，而其機又不必求諸天下，故反而觀之吾心焉。思吾所喜，天下必有欣然以同樂者；思吾所憎，天下必有拂然以同惡者；思吾所憂，天下必有惻然以同戚者；思吾所懼，天下必有凜然以同畏者。夫吾凡以求治者，為天下也，非為我也。故其視吾之心惟天下，而其視天下皆吾之心，其忍恝然而已哉？蓋天下之所欲，不能自遂，必賴吾以濟之；而其所惡，亦不能自去，又必賴吾以袪之。然則天下之望我也甚殷，而我之慰天下也亦甚切。蓋嘗盡吾之孝矣，而不忍民之頑囂未變也；蓋嘗致吾
translation_en:
…would almost be obstructed. Therefore it is said: "Nourish the myriad things with uprightness." Now, the Way of the sage is like heaven and earth; the sage's relation to the myriad people is like that of heaven and earth to the myriad things. Yet heaven and earth bring them to completion without deliberate mind, whereas the sage responds to them with deliberate mind, which would seem to differ from heaven and earth. Yet one fails to realize that the mind of the sage is one with heaven and earth above, and one with the world below. Even the sage cannot participate in this with a selfish mind, and the world, encompassed within the Way of the sage, is likewise as if sheltered by heaven and supported by earth, drawing sufficiency from the sage's benevolence. Thus, the transformation wrought by his deliberate mind is not necessarily not brought about by having no deliberate mind.

The gentleman knows that in the Way of governing the world, the root lies within oneself, and its vital mechanism need not be sought out in the world; therefore, he turns back and examines his own mind. Reflecting on what I rejoice in, there must be those in the world who gladly share the same joy; reflecting on what I loathe, there must be those in the world who indignantly share the same aversion; reflecting on what I worry about, there must be those in the world who sorrowfully share the same grief; reflecting on what I fear, there must be those in the world who tremblingly share the same dread. Now, in all my seeking to bring about order, it is for the sake of the world, not for myself. Therefore, when he looks into his own mind, there is only the world, and when he looks at the world, it is all his own mind—how could he bear to remain indifferent and nothing more? For what the world desires, it cannot fulfill by itself, and must rely on me to accomplish it; and what it hates, it likewise cannot remove by itself, and again must rely on me to dispel it. This being so, the world's expectation of me is most earnest, and my comforting of the world is likewise most urgent. I may have exhausted my filial piety, yet I cannot bear that the obstinacy and insincerity of the people have not yet been transformed; I may have carried to the utmost my…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之弟矣而不忍民之交相為瘉也蓋嘗廣吾之
慈矣而不忍民之顛連無告也不惟是也為天
下進賢則與天下同舉之為天下退不肖則與
天下同棄之為天下生財則不敢斂天下之怨
為天下用財則不敢後天下之費凡利在天下
者興之必力而不敢私一身之圖凡害在天下
者除之必速而不敢貽一身之患茲絜矩之道
所由立也今夫工師之為矩也寸寸度之至于
尋丈不繆然後合眾材成大用均齊方正而無
===
偏枉之失也此法廢即公輸無所用其巧離婁
無所用其明夫治器亦有然者何獨至于治天
下疑之君子之為矩也其亦有由矣始之以致
格其準繩之稽乎繼之以誠正其程度之立乎
約之以脩身其範圍之定乎吾之心不出是理
之外而天下之心不出吾心之外同人于野吾
得此道于易焉遵道遵路吾得此道于書焉徧
為爾德吾得此道于詩焉順事恕施吾得此道
于春秋焉以天下為一家以中國為一人吾得
punctuated: 之弟矣，而不忍民之交相為瘉也；蓋嘗廣吾之慈矣，而不忍民之顛連無告也。不惟是也，為天下進賢，則與天下同舉之；為天下退不肖，則與天下同棄之；為天下生財，則不敢斂天下之怨；為天下用財，則不敢後天下之費。凡利在天下者，興之必力，而不敢私一身之圖；凡害在天下者，除之必速，而不敢貽一身之患。茲絜矩之道所由立也。今夫工師之為矩也，寸寸度之，至于尋丈不繆，然後合眾材成大用，均齊方正而無偏枉之失也。此法廢，即公輸無所用其巧，離婁無所用其明。夫治器亦有然者，何獨至于治天下疑之？君子之為矩也，其亦有由矣。始之以致格，其準繩之稽乎？繼之以誠正，其程度之立乎？約之以脩身，其範圍之定乎？吾之心不出是理之外，而天下之心不出吾心之外。「同人于野」，吾得此道于《易》焉；「遵道遵路」，吾得此道于《書》焉；「徧為爾德」，吾得此道于《詩》焉；「順事恕施」，吾得此道于《春秋》焉；「以天下為一家，以中國為一人」，吾得…
translation_en: …brotherly respect, yet cannot bear that the people still mutually harm one another; and I have broadened my parental kindness, yet cannot bear that the people are in distress with no one to turn to. Not only this: in advancing the worthy for the empire, one promotes them together with the empire; in dismissing the unworthy for the empire, one casts them aside together with the empire; in generating wealth for the empire, one dares not accumulate the resentment of the empire; in expending wealth for the empire, one dares not put the empire's expenditures last. Whatever brings benefit to the empire, one must exert every effort to promote it, never daring to pursue selfish schemes for oneself; whatever brings harm to the empire, one must swiftly eradicate it, never daring to leave behind troubles from selfish regard for oneself. This is whereby the Way of the measuring square (xieju zhi dao) is established. Now, when a master artisan makes use of the carpenter's square, he measures inch by inch until at lengths of eight or ten feet there is no error; only then does he join the various timbers to complete a great structure, uniform, regular, square, and upright, without the flaw of being skewed or crooked. If this method is abandoned, then even Gongshu Ban 公輸班 would have nowhere to apply his skill, and Li Lou 離婁 would have nowhere to apply his keen sight. Since this is true even in fashioning vessels, why should anyone doubt it when it comes to governing the empire? When the noble man applies the measuring square, it too has its origin. Beginning with the extension of knowledge and the investigation of things, is this not the verification of the plumb line and level? Continuing with making the thoughts sincere and rectifying the mind, is this not the establishment of the standard and measure? Summing it up with the cultivation of the person, is this not the fixing of the mold and bounds? My mind does not go beyond this principle, and the minds of the empire do not go beyond my mind. "Fellowship with men in the open country"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Changes (Yi); "follow the Way and follow the road"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Documents (Shu); "universally practice your virtue"—I have obtained this Way from the Book of Odes (Shi); "act in accordance with circumstances and apply reciprocity"—I have obtained this Way from the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); "regard the empire as one family and the Central States as one person"—I have obtained…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
此道于禮焉必如夫子之所謂已所不欲勿施
于人必如孟子之所謂行有不得反求諸已視
家知國視國知天下若是而曰天下不平未之
有也不然四海遠矣或以壅滯而不能平兆民
廣矣或以怨懣而弗可平萬機煩矣或以叢脞
而弗暇平天下之治果何由而成之嘗考益之
戒舜曰罔違道以干百姓之譽罔咈百姓以從
已之欲然後知絜矩之道盡是矣已之所欲咈
百姓以從之固不可至于順斯民之情以求其
===
譽則亦以欲從人耳而聖王固不屑爲之也何
也天下之民至愚而神者也惟其神也必有機
以鼓舞之惟其愚也必有本以禁道之若一徇
其情而違道有所不計則吾之所施已不得其
平而何以平天下爲哉故雖政教以督率之而
不爲多事刑罰以董治之而不爲寡恩征伐以
勦刈之而不爲過暴要皆去其所以不平者就
其所以平者故絜矩之道操之若約而施之寔
博爲之似易而推之寔難行之若近而垂之愈
punctuated: 此道于《禮》焉。必如夫子之所謂「已所不欲，勿施于人」，必如孟子之所謂「行有不得，反求諸已」，視家知國，視國知天下，若是而曰天下不平，未之有也。不然，四海遠矣，或以壅滯而不能平；兆民廣矣，或以怨懣而弗可平；萬機煩矣，或以叢脞而弗暇平；天下之治，果何由而成之？嘗考益之戒舜曰：「罔違道以干百姓之譽，罔咈百姓以從已之欲。」然後知絜矩之道盡是矣。已之所欲，咈百姓以從之，固不可；至于順斯民之情以求其譽，則亦以欲從人耳，而聖王固不屑爲之也。何也？天下之民，至愚而神者也。惟其神也，必有機以鼓舞之；惟其愚也，必有本以禁道之。若一徇其情而違道有所不計，則吾之所施已不得其平，而何以平天下爲哉？故雖政教以督率之，而不爲多事；刑罰以董治之，而不爲寡恩；征伐以勦刈之，而不爲過暴。要皆去其所以不平者，就其所以平者。故絜矩之道，操之若約，而施之寔博；爲之似易，而推之寔難；行之若近，而垂之愈…
translation_en:
…this Way from the Rites (Li). Only when one truly follows what the Master called "Do not do to others what you do not wish for yourself," and what Mencius called "When in your conduct you do not succeed, turn inward and examine yourself," looking at the family to know the state, and looking at the state to know the world—if one acts thus and yet someone says the world is not brought to peace and order, such a thing has never been. Otherwise, the Four Seas are distant, and perhaps because of blockage and stagnation they cannot be brought to order; the millions of people are vast, and perhaps because of resentment and frustration they cannot be pacified; the myriad affairs of state are繁complex, and perhaps because of petty fussiness there is no leisure to bring them to order—how then could the governance of the world ultimately be achieved?

I have examined the admonition of Yi 益 to Shun 舜, which says: "Do not go against the Way to seek the praise of the hundred surnames; do not oppose the hundred surnames to follow your own desires." Only then did I realize that the Way of the measuring square (xieju) is fully exhausted in this. To oppose the hundred surnames in order to follow what one desires for oneself is certainly impermissible; yet as for indulging the feelings of these people in order to seek their praise, that too is merely following others out of desire, and the sage kings certainly disdained to do it. Why is this? The people of the world are utterly ignorant and yet espiritually perceptive. Because they are perceptive, there must be a spring of action to rouse and inspire them; because they are ignorant, there must be a fundamental standard to restrain and guide them. If one wholly indulges their feelings without regard for violating the Way, then what one dispenses has already lost its fairness and balance—and how then could one bring peace and balance to the world? Therefore, even if one uses governance and instruction to supervise and lead them, it is not considered meddlesome; even if one uses punishments and penalties to correct and govern them, it is not considered lacking in grace; even if one uses punitive expeditions to cut down and eradicate them, it is not considered excessively violent. In essence, all of these remove what causes imbalance and achieve what brings balance. Thus, as for the Way of the measuring square, grasping it seems simple, yet applying it is truly broad; practicing it seems easy, yet extending it is truly difficult; carrying it out seems near at hand, yet handing it down ever more…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乂協和于堯風動于舜平成于夏允殖于殷咸
和于周凡古帝王治道之美至歷千載如一日
者彼皆得是要也嗣乃窮以知術驅以法令壞
以侈靡愛養變爲窮黷則矩敝矣制度弛爲優
游則矩失矣紀綱淪爲姑息則矩移矣忠厚改
爲紛更則矩違矣其僅足以望古之治者則驩
虞焉耳其于平天下之要槩乎未有聞也善圖
治者觀古今得失之故可以鑒哉
表
擬吏部尚書兼翰林院學士李賢等
進
大明一統志表天順五年
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批鋪張我
朝輿圖一統之盛規模弘遠體裁莊重而文采蔚然奪目是表中之
獨步者宜錄以式
考試官教諭賈批敘事詳核措詞駢麗而末
更寓規諷之忠非徒工於四六而已
punctuated:
乂。協和于堯，風動于舜，平成于夏，允殖于殷，咸和于周，凡古帝王治道之美，至歷千載如一日者，彼皆得是要也。嗣乃窮以知術，驅以法令，壞以侈靡：愛養變爲窮黷，則矩敝矣；制度弛爲優游，則矩失矣；紀綱淪爲姑息，則矩移矣；忠厚改爲紛更，則矩違矣。其僅足以望古之治者，則驩虞焉耳，其于平天下之要，槩乎未有聞也。善圖治者，觀古今得失之故，可以鑒哉！

表

擬吏部尚書兼翰林院學士李賢等進《大明一統志》表〔天順五年〕

譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批：鋪張我朝輿圖一統之盛，規模弘遠，體裁莊重，而文采蔚然奪目，是表中之獨步者，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭賈批：敘事詳核，措詞駢麗，而末更寓規諷之忠，非徒工於四六而已。
translation_en:
… enduringly ordered [?]. Whether it was harmonizing under Yao, moving like the wind under Shun, bringing peace and order under the Xia, fostering abundant growth under the Yin, or achieving universal harmony under the Zhou—in all the excellence of the ancient sovereigns' way of governance, which endured through a thousand years as though a single day, they all grasped this essential principle. Later ages, however, exhausted the people with clever schemes, drove them with laws and ordinances, and corrupted them with extravagance: when loving nurture turned into exhaustive militarism, the carpenter's square of the measuring-square way was ruined; when institutions slackened into idle complacency, the square was lost; when discipline and order sank into lax indulgence, the square was displaced; and when loyal magnanimity changed into chaotic meddling, the square was violated. Those who barely managed to approximate the governance of antiquity achieved only superficial, short-lived pleasure [huanyu], and of the essentials for bringing peace to the world, they had heard nothing at all. Those who are skilled at planning for good governance, by observing the causes of success and failure past and present, can indeed take this as a mirror!

Memorial

An Imitation Memorial by Minister of Personnel Concurrent Hanlin Academician Li Xian 李賢 and Others Presenting the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi 大明一統志) [fifth year of the Tianshun reign (1461)]

By Tan Rushi 譚汝試
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Guo comments: It sets forth the grandeur of our dynasty's unified territory on a vast and far-reaching scale, with a solemn and dignified form and dazzling literary brilliance. It is peerless among the memorials and ought to be recorded as a model.
Examiner Instructor Jia comments: The narrative is detailed and accurate, the phrasing is ornate in parallel prose, and the conclusion further embodies the loyalty of remonstrance and admonition—it is not merely skillful in four-six parallel prose alone.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭汪批豐贍典則是足以華
國矣錄之
天順五年某月某日具官臣賢等奉
命編緝
大明一統志成謹用繕寫裝潢呈
進者伏以受
天明命萬年仰
日月之照臨纘
祖鴻圖一統昭
===
乾坤之覆載
創貽有自
紹述彌光臣賢等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首粤惟古
昔帝王肇建無窮之緒必資紀録永垂可
乆之規畫野制昉軒轅步極筭精豎亥爰
稽謨典參攷職方封山濬川咨十二官而
命牧揆敎奮衞別五百里而建侯郊鄘之
鼎始新卜年卜世洛師之墨初食宜民宜
人辨區域於司徒執度相參乎居邑藏簡
punctuated:
考試官教諭汪批：豐贍典則，是足以華國矣，錄之。

天順五年某月某日，具官臣賢等奉命編緝《大明一統志》成，謹用繕寫裝潢呈進者。伏以受天明命，萬年仰日月之照臨；纘祖鴻圖，一統昭乾坤之覆載。創貽有自，紹述彌光。臣賢等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。粤惟古昔帝王，肇建無窮之緒；必資紀録，永垂可乆之規。畫野制昉軒轅，步極筭精豎亥。爰稽謨典，參攷職方。封山濬川，咨十二官而命牧；揆敎奮衞，別五百里而建侯。郊鄘之鼎始新，卜年卜世；洛師之墨初食，宜民宜人。辨區域於司徒，執度相參乎居邑；藏簡…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Wang commented: "Rich, abundant, and adhering to classical standards, this is truly sufficient to bring glory to the state. Record it."

On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of the Tianshun reign (1461), Your Servant [Li] Xian 李賢 and others, holding their respective offices, having received the imperial command to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi), have completed the work and respectfully had it copied out in a fair hand and mounted for presentation to the throne.

We humbly consider: Receiving the bright mandate of Heaven, for ten thousand years all look up to the shining presence of the sun and moon; continuing the grand enterprise of the Ancestors, the great unification manifests the overarching and sustaining embrace of Heaven and Earth. Founding and bequeathing have their origins; inheriting and transmitting shine ever brighter. Your Servant Xian and others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground.

Examining the emperors and kings of antiquity, when they first established an endless patrimony, they invariably relied upon written records to hand down enduring standards forever. The system of dividing the fields originated with Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor], and pacing out the poles was calculated with precision by Shuhai. Looking into the "Counsels" and "Canons" [of the Book of Documents] and cross-referencing the Director of Domains (Zhifang) [in the Rites of Zhou]: raising mounds on mountains and dredging rivers, [Shun] consulted the Twelve Pastors and appointed regional governors; measuring instruction and rousing defense, [Yu] differentiated the five-hundred-li zones and established feudal lords. When the tripods at Jia鄘 [Jiaorul] were newly settled, the years and generations were divined; when the ink on the tortoise shell at the Luo capital was first consumed by fire, it was fitting for the common people and fitting for the worthies. Distinguishing regions under the Minister of Education (Situ), holding the measure to compare the settlements and towns; storing the bamboo slips…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
編於外史保障兼重乎塞垣山海不經宇
寰徒記迨金玉靡昭王度而埏垓空侈帝
紘鹿逐龍興府籍先收於勝筭狐鳴虎踞
霸功誰紀乎偏安混一無由函三奚望欽
惟
聖祖肇造
洪基
握彖契元首三才而開物除凶刷恥渾六合
以爲家率土共惟
===
帝臣蒸民會歸
皇極尚
廑貽燕爰集儒髦言輯輶軒將欲載艱難之
業志餘弓鼎竟未成渾灝之書事豈偶然
時如有待恭惟
皇帝陛下
德隆協帝
福斂惟皇
正位
punctuated: 編於外史，保障兼重乎塞垣；山海不經，宇寰徒記。迨金玉靡昭王度，而埏垓空侈帝紘。鹿逐龍興，府籍先收於勝筭；狐鳴虎踞，霸功誰紀乎偏安？混一無由，函三奚望？欽惟聖祖肇造洪基，握彖契元，首三才而開物；除凶刷恥，渾六合以爲家。率土共惟帝臣，蒸民會歸皇極。尚廑貽燕，爰集儒髦。言輯輶軒，將欲載艱難之業；志餘弓鼎，竟未成渾灝之書。事豈偶然？時如有待。恭惟皇帝陛下：德隆協帝，福斂惟皇。正位
translation_en:
… tablets with the Scribes of the Exterior, while protective bulwarks gave equal weight to the frontier walls; yet the accounts of mountains and seas were uncanonical, and the records of the realm were registered in vain. When the standard of jade and gold no longer manifested the kingly measure, the eight extremities merely boasted in vain of the imperial cord. As the deer was pursued and the dragon rose, the registers of the storehouses were first gathered into the winning strategy; where foxes cried and tigers crouched, who would record hegemonic achievements amid partial regimes? With no way to achieve unification, how could one hope to encompass the Three Powers?

We reverently reflect that the Sacred Ancestor first established the Great Foundation. Grasping the hexagram judgments and tallying with the Primal, he stood at the head of the Three Powers and inaugurated all things; eliminating the wicked and wiping away disgrace, he blended the Six Directions into a single household. All within the borders of the land together became subjects of the Emperor, and the multitudes of the people converged upon and returned to the August Ultimate. Still solicitous of bequeathing peace to posterity, he thereupon assembled eminent Confucians. Words were gathered from light carriages, intending to record the enterprise of hardship and difficulty; yet the ambition remained with the bow and cauldron left behind, and in the end the vast and boundless book was not completed. How could this matter be accidental? The time seemed to await what was to come.

We respectfully reflect upon Your Majesty the Emperor: your virtue is exalted in harmony with the Lord on High, and your blessings are gathered as the August Sovereign. Taking your rightful place …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
紫樞受球而綴下國
穆容
黼宁輯瑞而覲羣工
中天化日重暉
慶合堯封而再覩異域青雲簇彩
聖占周曆以彌昌蓋觀乎天文人文已見
化成之治而思夫丕承丕顯可忘
啓佑之功爰率
祖之攸行乃自
===
天而申
命取材藝苑分館蓬山競效編摩期奏全功于
菲劣誰能筆削仰承
獨斷於淵深類以羣分例因義起經史之網羅
盡矣流略之證引昭然系首
大明尊歸一統昭回
玉版鑠懿金鋪翼翼
京師儷
天樞而表則巍巍方岳絡地軸而作屏由二十
punctuated: 紫樞，受球而綴下國；穆容黼宁，輯瑞而覲羣工。中天化日重暉，慶合堯封而再覩；異域青雲簇彩，聖占周曆以彌昌。蓋觀乎天文、人文，已見化成之治；而思夫丕承、丕顯，可忘啓佑之功？爰率祖之攸行，乃自天而申命。取材藝苑，分館蓬山。競效編摩，期奏全功于菲劣；誰能筆削，仰承獨斷於淵深。類以羣分，例因義起。經史之網羅盡矣，流略之證引昭然。系首大明，尊歸一統；昭回玉版，鑠懿金鋪。翼翼京師，儷天樞而表則；巍巍方岳，絡地軸而作屏。由二十
translation_en:
… the Purple Pivot, receiving the jade regalia and binding together the subordinate states; maintaining a solemn countenance before the embroidered screen, gathering the jade tallies and granting audience to the assembled officials. At mid-heaven the transforming sun shines anew, a felicitous convergence seen once more across the realm of Yao; in foreign lands auspicious clouds cluster in splendor, a sacred omen that the calendar of Zhou shall flourish ever more. Indeed, by observing the patterns of heaven and the patterns of humanity, one already beholds a governance of perfected transformation; yet in reflecting upon the great inheritance and the great manifestation of glory, how could one forget the meritorious work of opening and aiding the dynasty?

Thus following the path trodden by the Ancestors, a renewed mandate was issued from Heaven. Materials were gathered from the garden of letters, and bureaus were apportioned on the sacred mount of Penglai. All vied to contribute to the compilation and polishing, hoping to achieve the complete work despite our meager abilities; yet who among us could wield the brush to revise and excise, looking upward to receive His Majesty's sole decision from the depths of his wisdom? Categories were divided according to kind, and editorial principles arose from moral meaning. The net cast over the Classics and Histories was exhaustive, and the citations from the various schools and epitomes were made brilliantly clear. At the head of the lineage is placed the Great Ming, so that supreme reverence returns to the Grand Unity; the text shines brightly upon jade tablets and gleams with beauty beneath gilded door-knockers. The reverent Capital matches the Celestial Pivot to stand as the model for the world; the lofty regional mountains and provinces lace together the terrestrial axis to serve as a protective screen. From the twenty-…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
八宿之分垣察氛祲于經緯從千八百國
之列土稽沿革于封疆采謠問俗而媺惡
互陳胙土藉茅而親賢並建志學校志書
院志戎衞具文武之弛張紀公署紀壇廟
紀關梁儼幽明之森列山川詳流峙之勝
用示壯觀方産存華實之毛豈珍異品徵
文獻於鄉賢名宦而流寓幷收卓矣風猷
如在摭遺跡於寺觀墓陵而僊釋附紀逖
哉玄覽何窮褒列女以嗣徽音王化首二
===
南之意别裔夷不亂華夏聖人嚴四塞之
防文省而意則該實符而名不爽使寸天
尺地一舉目而可知即往古來今如指掌
而易見傳疑傳信此豈一家之言有要有
倫可為萬世之典尤詳禹貢無論周官臣
等才謝三長慙左狐之上乘業窮五技拜
班馬於下風窺測海天僅同蠡管閱歷寒
暑甫竣槧鉛緬懷二酉之藏竊比九州之
戒傳誤敢辭譌豕反約或免汗牛幸萃全
punctuated: 八宿之分垣，察氛祲于經緯；從千八百國之列土，稽沿革于封疆。采謠問俗，而媺惡互陳；胙土藉茅，而親賢並建。志學校、志書院、志戎衞，具文武之弛張；紀公署、紀壇廟、紀關梁，儼幽明之森列。山川詳流峙之勝，用示壯觀；方産存華實之毛，豈珍異品？徵文獻於鄉賢、名宦，而流寓幷收，卓矣風猷如在；摭遺跡於寺觀、墓陵，而僊釋附紀，逖哉玄覽何窮！褒列女以嗣徽音，王化首二南之意；别裔夷不亂華夏，聖人嚴四塞之防。文省而意則該，實符而名不爽。使寸天尺地，一舉目而可知；即往古來今，如指掌而易見。傳疑傳信，此豈一家之言？有要有倫，可為萬世之典。尤詳《禹貢》，無論《周官》。臣等才謝三長，慙左、狐之上乘；業窮五技，拜班、馬於下風。窺測海天，僅同蠡管；閱歷寒暑，甫竣槧鉛。緬懷二酉之藏，竊比九州之戒。傳誤敢辭譌豕？反約或免汗牛。幸萃全
translation_en: …the enclosures of the twenty-eight lunar mansions, it observes auspicious and ominous vapors across the warp and woof of the heavens; following the arrayed territories of the eighteen hundred states, it investigates historical changes across the frontiers. Gathering folk songs and inquiring into local customs, both virtues and vices are mutually set forth; bestowing soil wrapped in white cogon grass, both imperial kinsmen and worthy ministers are jointly enfeoffed. Recording state schools, recording academies, and recording military guards, it sets out in full the relaxation and tension of civil and military administration; chronicling government offices, chronicling altars and temples, and chronicling passes and bridges, it displays in solemn array the realms of the unseen and the manifest. For mountains and rivers, it details the scenic beauty of their flowing waters and towering peaks, thereby displaying a magnificent spectacle; for local products, it preserves what grows with blossom and fruit, how could it prize exotic curiosities? Verifying documents and worthies among local sages and eminent officials, while also including sojourners—lofty indeed, their moral influence seems present still; gathering vestiges of the past from monasteries, Daoist temples, tombs, and mausoleums, while appending records of immortals and Buddhists—far-reaching indeed, how inexhaustible is this profound survey! Praising exemplary women so that they may carry on the virtuous reputation of the royal consorts embodies the meaning of placing the two Nan odes at the head of kingly transformation; distinguishing border tribes so that they do not confound the Chinese states reflects the sages' strict maintenance of defenses along the four frontiers. Its phrasing is economical, yet its meaning is comprehensive; the reality matches, and the names do not err. It enables every inch of heaven and foot of earth to be known at a single glance, and allows the past and present to be easily seen as if pointing to one's own palm. Transmitting both what is doubtful and what is certain, how could this be the words of a single school? Possessing both essentials and order, it can serve as a canon for ten thousand generations. It is even more detailed than the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong), to say nothing of the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan). Your servants lack the three excellences of a historian and are ashamed before the supreme mastery of Zuo Qiuming and Dong Hu; exhausted in our five meager skills, we bow downwind to Ban Gu and Sima Qian. Peering into and measuring the sea and sky, we are merely like those using a calabash dipper or a hollow tube; passing through winters and summers, we have only just completed our work with writing tablets and lead powder. Fondly recalling the archives of the Two You Mountains, we privately compare this work to the admonitions of the Nine Provinces. In transmitting errors, how dare we disavow mistakes like taking "hog" for "hai"? Yet by returning to conciseness, perhaps we may avoid books so numerous as to make oxen sweat. Fortunately having compiled the complete…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
編上塵
乙覽伏願
體元居正
纂大合華
安富尊榮勿恃輿圖之廣
威嚴順治當知創守之難
凜馭馬以持盈
訓旅獒而慎德則豐亨豫大和調玉燭於
瑤圖而鼎盛泰來化溢金甌於
===
寶曆臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表隨
進以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
punctuated:
編，上塵乙覽。伏願體元居正，纂大合華；安富尊榮，勿恃輿圖之廣；威嚴順治，當知創守之難。凜馭馬以持盈，訓《旅獒》而慎德。則豐亨豫大，和調玉燭於瑤圖；而鼎盛泰來，化溢金甌於寶曆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至。謹奉表隨進以聞。

第叁場
策五道
第一問
translation_en:
… compilation, and present it to the attention of Your Majesty's nocturnal perusal. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will embody the primal origin and abide in rectitude, succeed to the great enterprise and unite the flourishing realm; enjoying peace, wealth, honor, and glory, do not presume upon the vastness of the empire's territory; governing with majesty, dignity, and compliant order, remain ever mindful of the difficulties of founding and preserving the state. Maintain reverence as if driving horses with worn reins to preserve fullness, and take warning from the "Hounds of Lü" (Lü ao) to be prudent in virtue. Then, in abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness, harmony will attune the jade candle of the seasons across the precious realm; and as supreme flourishing and peace arrive, transformative influence will overflow the golden vessel of the state throughout the imperial calendar. Your servants are overcome with the utmost awe and trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty. We reverently present this memorial accompanying the submitted work for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays
First Question

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批我
祖宗心法同符帝王而
皇上心法同符
祖宗
聖學淵源度越千古矣是作能窺測其精微揚厲其盛美而要歸於純
亦不已尤見忠懇宜錄以式
考試官敎諭賈批揄揚我
皇上緝熙
===
聖學旣極詳悉而末所敷陳尤知靖獻之義是涵濡
聖化而有得者
考試官敎諭汪批規頌得體具見學識
論聖學者豈以萬乘之尊躬博士之業足
稱述哉其研精省驗欲以資化理故日求
諸聞且見者以廣其聰明其操存檢約欲
以敦化原故日求諸不聞且見者以養其
純一二者交致于心亹亹而不息故德業
長裕而名號休美也非
punctuated:
譚汝試
同考試官訓導郭批：我祖宗心法，同符帝王；而皇上心法，同符祖宗。聖學淵源，度越千古矣！是作能窺測其精微，揚厲其盛美，而要歸於純亦不已，尤見忠懇。宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭賈批：揄揚我皇上緝熙聖學，旣極詳悉；而末所敷陳，尤知靖獻之義。是涵濡聖化而有得者。
考試官敎諭汪批：規頌得體，具見學識。
論聖學者，豈以萬乘之尊、躬博士之業足稱述哉？其研精省驗，欲以資化理，故日求諸聞且見者，以廣其聰明；其操存檢約，欲以敦化原，故日求諸不聞且見者，以養其純一。二者交致于心，亹亹而不息，故德業長裕而名號休美也。非
translation_en:
Tan Rushi

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo comments: The method of the mind-and-heart (xinfa) of our Imperial Ancestors matched that of the ancient sovereigns and kings, and the method of the mind-and-heart of His Majesty matches that of our Imperial Ancestors. The fountainhead of His sage learning surpasses all antiquity! This composition is able to fathom its subtleties and extol its splendid beauty, while its essential conclusion returns to unceasing purity, which especially reveals loyalty and earnestness. It should be recorded as a model.

Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: In praising and extolling how His Majesty brings luminous continuity to His sage learning, it is already extremely detailed and thorough; and what is set forth at the end especially shows an understanding of the principle of quiet devotion and presentation to the throne. This is someone who has been steeped in the sage's transformative influence and has gained from it.

Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Both admonition and eulogy hit the proper balance, fully demonstrating learning and insight.

When discussing sage learning, how could it be that merely taking up the pursuits of an Erudite in person while holding the exalted position of Lord of Ten Thousand Chariots suffices to merit praise and recounting? His refined investigation and reflective examination are intended to aid transformative governance; therefore He daily seeks within what is heard and seen in order to broaden His intelligence and discernment. His preservation of the mind and self-restraint are intended to thicken the source of transformation; therefore He daily seeks within what is neither heard nor seen in order to nourish His pure oneness. Both are jointly brought to the mind, tirelessly and without cease; therefore His virtuous achievements are ever abundant and His reputation and title are splendid and fine. Unless one is…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
大聖人其孰能與此者乎請對揚之今夫烝庶
之家稍能操奇贏必聚詩書延師儒不惜
伏臘費課其子力學上則望其邁迹夏倫
顯融於當世次亦望其辨物數計資糈謹
守先世之籍毋墜況人主之尊纂有鴻業
爲宗社天人之所繫命非第奇贏任也故
典學緝熈之說自高成二君而始見於詩
書顧所從來久遠矣考諸韓詩外傳謂黃
帝學于大墳顓頊學于祿圖堯學于務成
===
子附舜學于尹壽禹學于西王國湯學于
貸乎相文王學于錫疇子斯武王學于太
公雖於六籍靡所考見而帝王之務學玆
亦足以徵焉晚近世而斯道闕矣其稍能
近儒紳親縹素考䲥於今古之林則前史
往往豔談之故石渠臨決肇於宣帝夜分
講論見於光武文學直宿引與論議著於
貞觀自巳至申然後釋卷稱於興國屏書
無逸紀於明道非不誠好學也而終不能
punctuated: 大聖人，其孰能與此者乎？請對揚之。今夫烝庶之家，稍能操奇贏，必聚《詩》、《書》，延師儒，不惜伏臘費，課其子力學。上則望其邁迹夏倫，顯融於當世；次亦望其辨物數、計資糈，謹守先世之籍毋墜。況人主之尊，纂有鴻業，爲宗社天人之所繫命，非第奇贏任也。故「典學」、「緝熈」之說，自高、成二君而始見於《詩》、《書》，顧所從來久遠矣。考諸《韓詩外傳》，謂黃帝學于大墳，顓頊學于祿圖，堯學于務成子附，舜學于尹壽，禹學于西王國，湯學于貸乎相，文王學于錫疇子斯，武王學于太公。雖於六籍靡所考見，而帝王之務學，玆亦足以徵焉。晚近世而斯道闕矣，其稍能近儒紳、親縹素、考䲥於今古之林，則前史往往豔談之。故石渠臨決，肇於宣帝；夜分講論，見於光武；文學直宿，引與論議，著於貞觀；自巳至申然後釋卷，稱於興國；屏書《無逸》，紀於明道。非不誠好學也，而終不能
translation_en:
… a great sage, who could attain to this? Allow me to respond and extol it.

Now, among the families of the common people, those slightly able to manage a surplus of wealth will invariably gather the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), invite teachers and Confucian scholars, and spare no expense at the summer and winter festivals to task their sons with diligent study. At best, they hope their sons will surpass the footsteps of their peers [?] and achieve prominence and glory in the present age; failing that, they still hope they will learn to distinguish goods and numbers, calculate wealth and provisions, and carefully guard the patrimony of their ancestors without letting it fall into ruin. How much more so for the exalted ruler of men, who inherits the great enterprise upon which the destiny of the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, Heaven, and man all depend—a responsibility far beyond merely managing a surplus of wealth!

Therefore, the doctrines of "constant study" (dianxue) and "continuing the bright perfection" (jixi) first appeared in the Odes and Documents with the two sovereigns Gaozong and King Cheng, yet their origins stretch back far into antiquity. Examining the Outer Commentary to the Book of Odes by Master Han (Hanshi waizhuan), it states that the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) studied under Dafen, Zhuanxu studied under Lutu, Yao studied under Wucheng Zifu, Shun studied under Yin Shou, Yu studied under Xiwang Guo, Tang studied under Dai Zixiang [?], King Wen studied under Xichou Zisi, and King Wu studied under Taigong. Although these accounts cannot be verified in the Six Classics, they nonetheless suffice to attest to the devotion to learning of the emperors and kings of old.

In more recent ages, this Way fell into neglect. Whenever a ruler was even slightly able to draw close to Confucian gentlemen, be intimate with books and scrolls, and roam in inquiry [?] through the forest of past and present, the former histories would invariably speak of it with admiring praise. Thus, personally presiding over decisions at the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge) began with Emperor Xuan of Han; lecturing and discussing until midnight was seen in Emperor Guangwu of Han; having Fellows of the Institute of Literary Worthies (Wenxue) keep night duty and summoning them for discussions became renowned in the Zhenguan era (under Emperor Taizong of Tang); putting down the scroll only after reading from the si hour to the shen hour (9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) was praised in the Taiping Xingguo era (under Emperor Taizong of Song); and inscribing "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) upon a folding screen was recorded in the Mingdao era (under Emperor Renzong of Song). It is not that they were not genuinely fond of learning, yet in the end they were unable…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與聖人聯鑣而共軌者其所繇異術也彼
唐虞三代經綸探討原非二途其學巳實
而不華而危微祗敬之念其握之爲本始
者尤足以綱百爲而統羣籍故能神聖獨
詣卓然稱邁迹蕘倫之主彪炳往牒若漢
唐宋數君其能然乎而亦不失爲堇堇守
先籍者則學之功也洪惟
皇上
睿德天授
===
聖功日新
卽位以來非隆冬盛夏不輟
講筵
端居
禁中亦日
親典籍無他嗜好嘗于
文華殿
御書學二帝三王治天下大經大法又甞
御書謹天戒任賢能親賢臣遠嬖佞明賞罰謹
punctuated: 與聖人聯鑣而共軌者，其所繇異術也。彼唐、虞、三代，經綸探討，原非二途，其學巳實而不華；而危微祗敬之念，其握之爲本始者，尤足以綱百爲而統羣籍。故能神聖獨詣，卓然稱邁迹蕘倫之主，彪炳往牒。若漢、唐、宋數君，其能然乎？而亦不失爲堇堇守先籍者，則學之功也。洪惟皇上，睿德天授，聖功日新。卽位以來，非隆冬盛夏不輟講筵；端居禁中，亦日親典籍，無他嗜好。嘗于文華殿御書「學二帝三王治天下大經大法」，又甞御書「謹天戒、任賢能、親賢臣、遠嬖佞、明賞罰、謹
translation_en:
…drive abreast and share the same track with the sages is because the methods they followed were different. In the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, statecraft and scholarly inquiry were originally not two separate paths, so their learning was already substantial and not merely ornate; moreover, their mindfulness of the precariousness of the human mind, the subtlety of the moral mind, and reverent vigilance—which they grasped as the fundamental beginning—was especially sufficient to serve as the guiding cord for all actions and to unify all books. Therefore, they were able to uniquely attain divine sageliness, standing out eminently as rulers who surpassed the traces of others and transcended their peers [?], shining brilliantly in past records. Could those several rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties be like this? Yet that they still did not fail to be rulers who at least preserved the former canons [?] was the achievement of learning.

Humbly reflecting upon His Majesty the Emperor: his perspicacious virtue is bestowed by Heaven, and his sagely achievements are daily renewed. Since ascending the throne, except in the depth of winter and the height of summer, he has not suspended the Classics Mat lectures; dwelling in rectitude within the Forbidden Palace, he also daily familiarizes himself with the canons and records, having no other pastimes. Once, in the Wenhua Hall (Hall of Literary Brilliance), he wrote in his imperial hand: "Learn the great standards and great laws by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings governed All under Heaven." He also once wrote in his imperial hand: "Heed the warnings of Heaven, employ the worthy and capable, stay close to worthy ministers, keep aloof from favorites and flatterers, make rewards and punishments clear, be cautious in…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
出入愼起居節飲食收放心存敬畏納忠言
撙節用凡十二事蓋瞽御之所未箴工師之
所未誦而我
皇上方且兢兢然常凝常運於淵閎沕穆之原
而研精省驗於鑒觀獻納之所翕受殆舉
二帝三王而羨墻見也故邇來邊堠息燧
海波鮮揚河淮安流遼左屢捷大小臣工
皆恇法守職中外樂業兹非
懋學之符鏡哉乃執事復求所以佐萬分一
===
者愚以爲今所急第法
祖宗巳爾夫人主之銳意有爲語以帝王則怡
然滿志語以先世家法必且謂其習見而
易爲然馳神遠慕未易以驟至而見成功
則內惑而趨不固此武帝神宗之所以鮮
完美也故不若學
祖宗效何者以
祖宗所得雖二帝三王不能加也甞觀我
太祖之
punctuated:
出入、愼起居、節飲食、收放心、存敬畏、納忠言、撙節用」，凡十二事。蓋瞽御之所未箴，工師之所未誦，而我皇上方且兢兢然常凝常運於淵閎沕穆之原，而研精省驗於鑒觀獻納之所翕受，殆舉二帝三王而羨墻見也。故邇來邊堠息燧，海波鮮揚，河淮安流，遼左屢捷，大小臣工皆恇法守職，中外樂業，兹非懋學之符鏡哉？

乃執事復求所以佐萬分一者，愚以爲今所急，第法祖宗巳爾。夫人主之銳意有爲，語以帝王則怡然滿志，語以先世家法，必且謂其習見而易爲。然馳神遠慕，未易以驟至而見成功，則內惑而趨不固，此武帝、神宗之所以鮮完美也。故不若學祖宗效。何者？以祖宗所得，雖二帝三王不能加也。甞觀我太祖之
translation_en:
… be circumspect in goings and comings, be careful in daily routine, moderate food and drink, recover the strayed mind, maintain reverence and awe, accept loyal counsel, and economize in expenditure”—twelve matters in all. Indeed, these are things about which the blind musicians and attendants had not yet admonished, and which the master artisans had not yet recited; yet our August Sovereign is even now cautiously and constantly concentrating and exercising his mind at the deep, vast, and profoundly solemn source, while refining his spirit and examining through experience that which is gathered and received from historical reflection and proffered counsel—almost bringing forth the Two Emperors and Three Kings and seeing them, like Shun, in his soup and on his walls! Therefore, in recent times the border watchtowers have extinguished their beacon fires, the sea waves are seldom whipped up, the Yellow and Huai rivers flow peacefully in their courses, Liaodong has won repeated victories, officials great and small all stand in awe of the law and abide by their duties, and both the court and the provinces rejoice in their livelihoods. Is this not the tally and mirror of his strenuous devotion to learning?

Yet Your Excellency still seeks a way to assist by even one ten-thousandth part. In my humble opinion, what is urgent today is simply to model oneself upon the Imperial Ancestors, and nothing more. Now, when a ruler is keenly intent on accomplishing great things, if one speaks to him of the ancient Emperors and Kings, he is delighted and filled with ambition; if one speaks to him of the family laws of his own forebears, he will surely consider them familiar sights and easy to practice. However, when one lets the spirit gallop in distant admiration, it is not easy to arrive suddenly and see successful results; then inwardly one becomes perplexed and one's direction is not firm. This is why Emperor Wu of Han and Shenzong of Song seldom achieved perfection. Therefore, nothing is as effective as emulating the Imperial Ancestors. Why is this? Because what our Imperial Ancestors attained, even the Two Emperors and Three Kings could not surpass. I have observed that our Taizu's…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖學淵源未易殫述而舉其大略則若
諭李善長以心爲身之主帥若一事不合理則
百事皆廢所以常自點檢
諭宋濂以人心虛靈乗氣機出入操而存之爲
難玆非危微之後再揭奧眇者乎
成祖之
諭楊士奇也曰帝王之學貴切己實用一切浮
泛無益之語勿進至其
諭解縉則謂每退朝默坐未嘗不思管束此心
===
爲切要思爲人君但于宮室車馬服食玩好
無所增加則天下自然無事皇皇乎
聖學之大律也迨于
世宗殖學甚盛每
清問策士
裁决章疏皆啓口成章公卿大夫曾不能賛
一詞而其所爲
敬一箴者有曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗純又舉
聖學之要領而標禁之至矣盡矣則今所當仰
punctuated: 聖學淵源，未易殫述。而舉其大略，則若諭李善長：「以心爲身之主帥，若一事不合理，則百事皆廢，所以常自點檢。」諭宋濂：「以人心虛靈，乗氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」玆非「危微」之後再揭奧眇者乎？成祖之諭楊士奇也，曰：「帝王之學，貴切己實用，一切浮泛無益之語勿進。」至其諭解縉，則謂：「每退朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要。思爲人君，但于宮室、車馬、服食、玩好無所增加，則天下自然無事。」皇皇乎！聖學之大律也。迨于世宗，殖學甚盛，每清問策士、裁决章疏，皆啓口成章，公卿大夫曾不能賛一詞。而其所爲《敬一箴》者，有曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。」又舉聖學之要領而標禁之，至矣，盡矣！則今所當仰…
translation_en: …the fountainhead of His sagely learning is not easy to recount in full. Yet to cite its main outlines: there was His instruction to Li Shanchang 李善長 that "the mind is the commander of the body; if a single matter fails to accord with principle, then a hundred matters will all be ruined, and therefore I constantly examine myself." And His instruction to Song Lian 宋濂 that "the human mind is numinous and subtle, going out and coming in as it rides the springs of vital energy; to grasp and preserve it is difficult." Is this not a renewed disclosure of profound subtleties following upon the teaching of the "precarious and subtle" (wei wei 危微)? When Chengzu 成祖 instructed Yang Shiqi 楊士奇, He said: "The learning of emperors and kings values what is pertinent to oneself and of practical use; do not present any superficial, vague, and unprofitable words." As for His instruction to Xie Jin 解縉, He stated: "Every time I retire from court and sit in silence, I never fail to reflect that restraining this mind is what is most urgent. I reflect that in being a ruler of men, so long as one adds nothing further to palaces, carriages and horses, clothing and food, or curiosities and pastimes, the empire will naturally be free of trouble." How august! This is the great standard of sagely learning. Coming down to Shizong 世宗, the cultivation of His learning was flourishing indeed. Whenever He posed gracious inquiries in examining scholars by policy questions or decided upon memorials, the words fell from His lips as finished compositions, to which the dukes, ministers, and grandees could not add a single word. Moreover, in the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi zhen 敬一箴) that He composed, it is said: "Without reverence there is no gathering together; without oneness there is no purity." Thus He once again raised up the essential import of sagely learning and set it forth as a standard and prohibition—reaching the utmost and exhausting all! Then what ought today to be reverently…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
求
祖宗心法者夫寧有他矩哉故特達卓偉之質
不以自有恐易驕也日升川至之年不以
自恃恐易惰也窮富極貴鉅麗之觀不以
自御慮易侈也其威足以震懾庶官而辨
足以籠挫萬物不敢自用慮易壅也其餘
力足富記誦而麗詞章不敢自逞慮騖於
外也綽約靡曼便嬖使令日嬛給而伺進
不以易吾聖賢神僊黃白與遊畋喜功之
===
說不以易吾經術慮易誘也
深宮燕閒猶之乎聆炯誨納顯諍屬屬乎其
弗敢弛也夙夜寧寂猶之乎奉駿奔事對
越勉勉乎其弗敢間也日取諸前言往行
以涵泳於吾心叅酌於世務而本其所爲
心則又兢兢業業舉經術世務而一以貫
之毋勤始而怠終毋炫名而遺實是隨所
聞見與所不聞見皆若乾道之常運純亦
不已焉斯
punctuated: 求祖宗心法者，夫寧有他矩哉？故特達卓偉之質，不以自有，恐易驕也；日升川至之年，不以自恃，恐易惰也；窮富極貴鉅麗之觀，不以自御，慮易侈也；其威足以震懾庶官，而辨足以籠挫萬物，不敢自用，慮易壅也；其餘力足富記誦而麗詞章，不敢自逞，慮騖於外也；綽約靡曼、便嬖使令，日嬛給而伺進，不以易吾聖賢，神僊黃白與遊畋喜功之說，不以易吾經術，慮易誘也。深宮燕閒，猶之乎聆炯誨、納顯諍，屬屬乎其弗敢弛也；夙夜寧寂，猶之乎奉駿奔、事對越，勉勉乎其弗敢間也。日取諸前言往行，以涵泳於吾心，叅酌於世務，而本其所爲心，則又兢兢業業，舉經術世務而一以貫之。毋勤始而怠終，毋炫名而遺實，是隨所聞見與所不聞見，皆若乾道之常運，純亦不已焉，斯
translation_en:
… seek the mental discipline of the imperial ancestors—could there be any other standard? Therefore, endowed with extraordinary and preeminent qualities, he does not presume upon them as his own, fearing lest he easily grow arrogant; in the prime of youth, like the rising sun and swelling streams, he does not rely upon it, fearing lest he easily grow indolent; amid the magnificent spectacles of supreme wealth and rank, he does not indulge himself with them, concerned lest he easily grow extravagant. Though his majesty suffices to overawe all officials and his eloquence suffices to encompass and subdue all things, he dares not rely solely on his own judgment, concerned lest he easily become cut off from counsel. Though his spare energy suffices to enrich his memorization and recitation and to beautify his literary compositions, he dares not indulge his talents, concerned lest he chase after externals. Though delicate beauties and flattering favorites wait upon his commands, displaying nimble wit day by day as they watch for a chance to advance, he does not exchange our sages and worthies for them; and as for the doctrines of immortals, alchemy, hunting excursions, and the love of martial exploits, he does not exchange our classical statecraft for them, concerned lest he easily be led astray.

In the leisure of the deep palace, it is just as if he were listening to luminous instruction and accepting outspoken remonstrance—so attentive is he that he dares not relax. In the quiet solitude of morning and night, it is just as if he were performing the swift services of the ancestral temple and standing in reverent communion before Heaven—so diligent is he that he dares not allow a lapse. Daily he draws upon the words and deeds of the past to steep his mind in them and to deliberate upon worldly affairs; and taking the cultivation of his mind as the foundation, with cautious reverence he unites classical learning and practical statecraft with a single thread. Neither diligent at the start only to grow lax at the end, nor making a display of reputation while neglecting reality—thus, whether in what is seen and heard or in what is unseen and unheard, all is like the constant revolution of the Way of Heaven, pure and unceasing. Then…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之美可承帝王之盛不難致也高成且將
讓德區區漢唐宋諸君又何足多談
第二問
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批我
皇上祗承天戒昭示臣民蓋尚實而非尚文也此作善敷厲揄揚末進忠
悃尤占偉識異日必不負所學者
同考試官教諭王批心本忠愛體得對揚是善
發事
===
天之實者
考試官教諭賈批援古證今楊厲備至篇末
讜言尤臣子因事納誨之忠也允宜高薦
考試官教諭汪批得敷對之體非徒以文取
也錄之
帝王之克謹天戒非緣戒而後求謹也其
感格有本而銷弭有實故天鑒其令德而
降之嘉福雖異而無損也夫帝王之精氣
上貫于天而下通於烝庶其夙夜閔閔欲
punctuated:
祖宗之美可承，帝王之盛不難致也。高、成且將讓德，區區漢、唐、宋諸君，又何足多談！

第二問
徐昌兆
同考試官訓導張批：我皇上祗承天戒，昭示臣民，蓋尚實而非尚文也。此作善敷厲揄揚，末進忠悃，尤占偉識，異日必不負所學者。
同考試官教諭王批：心本忠愛，體得對揚，是善發事天之實者。
考試官教諭賈批：援古證今，楊厲備至，篇末讜言，尤臣子因事納誨之忠也，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭汪批：得敷對之體，非徒以文取也，錄之。

帝王之克謹天戒，非緣戒而後求謹也。其感格有本，而銷弭有實，故天鑒其令德，而降之嘉福，雖異而無損也。夫帝王之精氣，上貫于天，而下通於烝庶。其夙夜閔閔，欲
translation_en:
… the admirable traditions of the Imperial Ancestors may be carried on, and the flourishing rule of the ancient emperors and kings will not be difficult to attain. Even Gaozong of Yin and King Cheng of Zhou would yield to him in virtue; as for the mere rulers of Han, Tang, and Song, how could they be worth much discussion?

Second Policy Question
By Xu Changzhao (徐昌兆).
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: Our August Sovereign reverently receives Heaven's admonitions and clearly proclaims them to his officials and people, valuing substance rather than mere outward form. This essay excels at expounding and extolling his virtue; at the end it offers loyal sincerity, showing particularly grand insight. In the future he will surely not betray what he has learned.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang: Rooted in a heart of loyalty and affection, it grasps the proper form of responding to the sovereign and is skilled at bringing out the reality of serving Heaven.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia: Citing antiquity to verify the present, its praise and exhortation are thoroughgoing. The forthright counsel at the end of the piece especially shows the loyalty of a minister offering admonition on the occasion of events; he truly deserves a high recommendation.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: It attains the proper form of an expository reply and is not selected merely for its literary style. Record it.

That emperors and kings are able to heed Heaven's admonitions with reverence is not because they seek to be reverent only after an admonition occurs. Their moving of Heaven has a fundamental root, and their dispelling of calamities has substantive reality; therefore Heaven examines their fine virtue and sends down auspicious blessings upon them, so that even if anomalies appear, they cause no harm. Now, the vital spirit of emperors and kings penetrates upward to Heaven and communicates downward to the multitude of the people. Morning and night they are anxiously concerned, wishing…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以握天人之會而固其存何嘗一日忘祗
畏哉及至天心示儆而深惟所以迎和卻
沴之實莫急於惠民故側身脩行旣先百
司庶府以請命于天而後舉元元之急而
振業之俾有寧宇故民心得而天意回曆
祚滋固此本實俱得之效而非以循常式
按舊儀示具而已彼循式按儀業祈天者
亦豈能盡罷不舉哉顧感格銷弭之無道
而顓顓以是爲亟圖則末矣故太上脩本
===
實其次脩儀式非是愚難言之玆愚生所
以閱覽往籍而竊窺我
太祖
皇上之能得
天也自昔至治之世豈能必氣運之常休嘉哉
則堯舜被之矣洪水猛獸日聞於區夏而
唐虞終不失爲郅隆之會堯舜不以是故
貶聖名者何哉欽明允恭其自結于天心
者已厚而警予其咨之語於二聖日諄復
punctuated:
以握天人之會而固其存，何嘗一日忘祗畏哉？及至天心示儆，而深惟所以迎和卻沴之實，莫急於惠民。故側身脩行，旣先百司庶府以請命于天，而後舉元元之急而振業之，俾有寧宇。故民心得而天意回，曆祚滋固。此本實俱得之效，而非以循常式、按舊儀示具而已。彼循式按儀，業祈天者，亦豈能盡罷不舉哉？顧感格銷弭之無道，而顓顓以是爲亟圖，則末矣。故太上脩本實，其次脩儀式，非是，愚難言之。玆愚生所以閱覽往籍，而竊窺我太祖、皇上之能得天也。
自昔至治之世，豈能必氣運之常休嘉哉？則堯、舜被之矣。洪水猛獸，日聞於區夏，而唐、虞終不失爲郅隆之會；堯、舜不以是故貶聖名者，何哉？欽明允恭，其自結于天心者已厚，而「警予」、「其咨」之語，於二聖日諄復
translation_en:
… to grasp the nexus between Heaven and humanity and secure its preservation, when have they ever for a single day forgotten reverent awe? And when the mind of Heaven sends down warnings, they deeply reflect that in the substantive measures for welcoming harmony and repelling baleful influences, nothing is more urgent than showing kindness to the people. Therefore, humbling themselves and cultivating their conduct, they first lead the hundred offices and myriad bureaus to plead for the mandate from Heaven, and then address the urgent needs of the common people, relieving them and restoring their livelihoods so that they have peaceful dwellings. Thus, the hearts of the people are won, the will of Heaven is turned back, and the dynastic fortune grows ever more secure. This is the efficacy of attaining both the root and the substance, and not merely following routine formulas and adhering to old rituals to make a show of compliance. As for following formulas and adhering to rituals, how could those engaged in praying to Heaven completely abolish and fail to perform them? Yet if one lacks the true way to move Heaven and dispel calamities, and instead focuses exclusively on such formalities as the most urgent priority, that is merely attending to the branches. Therefore, the highest course is to cultivate the root and substance; the next is to cultivate ritual and formula. Beyond this, I find it difficult to speak of. This is how I, a humble student, by perusing ancient records, have ventured to glimpse how our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) and Your Majesty have been able to win the favor of Heaven.

From of old, in ages of supreme governance, how could one be certain that the cosmic cycles andetherial forces would always be auspicious and favorable? Indeed, Yao and Shun experienced the contrary. Great floods and fierce beasts were heard of daily throughout the Chinese realm, yet the eras of Tang and Yu never ceased to be a time of supreme flourishing, and Yao and Shun did not on that account suffer any diminution of their sage renown. Why was this? Reverent, enlightened, and sincerely courteous, the bond they had formed with the mind of Heaven was already deep, and expressions like "warning me" and "sighing in lament" were repeated daily and earnestly by the two sages…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉及考其所以祗事而弭災者非有殊郵
絶迹可具述也羲和分宅璣衡齊政用以
欽若于沴𠃔無垠之表第不越于民時之
敬授民食之惟時止爾故帝王履常撫順
固無一念不敬天無一念不勤民及遇譴
告則又以帝天視聽主於民心而惠民急
焉是謂本實而堯舜其盛也後世若漢之
文帝以日食求直言數蠲田租宋藝祖因
苦雨焚香禱天曹州饑運粟賑之斯亦足
===
稱勤恤民隱哉試方之堯舜則莫有敢與
者以感格無本而僅能省躬施惠於一時
所謂亡羊補牢第脩儀式爾故曰次也我
太祖高皇帝滌新諸夏統一天人諸所
規畫皆足以繫輿情鞏
明命至詳也居甞
諭學士宋濂朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民兢
兢業業不敢自逸此其心雖古堯舜何以加
焉乃洪武三年庚戌夏久不雨欲
punctuated: 焉。及考其所以祗事而弭災者，非有殊郵絶迹可具述也。羲和分宅，璣衡齊政，用以欽若于沴𠃔無垠之表，第不越于民時之敬授、民食之惟時止爾。故帝王履常撫順，固無一念不敬天，無一念不勤民；及遇譴告，則又以帝天視聽主於民心，而惠民急焉。是謂本實，而堯、舜其盛也。後世若漢之文帝，以日食求直言，數蠲田租；宋藝祖因苦雨焚香禱天，曹州饑，運粟賑之。斯亦足稱勤恤民隱哉！試方之堯、舜，則莫有敢與者，以感格無本，而僅能省躬施惠於一時，所謂「亡羊補牢」，第脩儀式爾，故曰次也。我太祖高皇帝滌新諸夏，統一天人，諸所規畫，皆足以繫輿情、鞏明命，至詳也。居甞諭學士宋濂：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」此其心，雖古堯、舜何以加焉！乃洪武三年庚戌夏，久不雨，欲
translation_en: … there. Yet when we examine the means by which they reverently attended to affairs and averted calamities, there were no extraordinary marvels or unprecedented feats that could be recounted in detail. Xi and He were assigned their respective stations, and the jade-pearled armillary sphere and sighting tube regulated theSeven Governments, whereby they reverently accorded with Heaven beyond the boundless realm of noxious vapors [?]; yet all this went no further than respectfully granting the seasons to the people and ensuring that the people's food was attended to in due time. Therefore, when sovereigns tread the normal course and preside over auspicious times, they naturally have not a single thought that does not revere Heaven, nor a single thought that is not diligent toward the people. And when they encounter celestial warnings and admonitions, recognizing that the Lord of Heaven sees and hears through the hearts of the people, they make showing kindness to the people their urgent priority. This is what is called the fundamental substance, and Yao and Shun represent its pinnacle. In later ages, rulers such as Emperor Wen of the Han sought frank remonstrance on account of solar eclipses and repeatedly remitted the land tax; the Founding Ancestor (Taizu) of the Song burned incense and prayed to Heaven because of relentless rains, and when there was famine in Caozhou, he transported grain to relieve the people. Could these not also be called diligent in showing compassion for the hidden sufferings of the people? Yet if one tries to compare them with Yao and Shun, no one would dare rank them as equals. This is because their efforts to move and reach Heaven lacked the fundamental root, and they were merely able to examine themselves and bestow favors at a particular moment—what is called "mending the fold after the sheep are lost"—simply performing the outward ceremonies. Hence they are called secondary. Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), cleansed and renewed all the Chinese lands and unified the realms of Heaven and Man; all that he planned and established was sufficient to bind the popular sentiment and consolidate the Bright Mandate in the utmost detail. In ordinary times he once instructed the Academician Song Lian (宋濂): "In ruling as sovereign, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, and below I stand in awe of the millions of people; cautious and conscientious, I dare not indulge in ease." Such a heart—even with the ancient Yao and Shun, how could one surpass it! Then, in the summer of the gengxu year, the third year of the Hongwu reign (1370), when it had not rained for a long time, he wished to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
躬禱於山川壇先命
皇后與諸妃執爨爲農家食
皇太子諸王供饋于齋所至期素服草履徒
步詣于壇席藁露坐晝曝日中夜臥于地
衣不解帶
皇太子捧榼進蔬食雜麻麥菽粟已而大雨
至九年秋以七曜紊度求直言十八年春
以五星竝見求直言二十六年夏以太白
經天
===
京師大旱求直言諸以軍興水旱𧖟蝗雷震
免租者十有六賑者三贖鬻子者一夫天
厭元亂民幸得脫湯火已戴
聖祖之德厚矣而灑惠弛征用以厚集瘡痍祗
承天戒若此故雖有災沴不敵禎符茂啓
無疆之曆迄于今是賴非
聖祖之得天有是哉頃者象緯失次
皇上旣惕心引慝
帥先羣臣復
punctuated:
躬禱於山川壇，先命皇后與諸妃執爨，爲農家食，皇太子、諸王供饋于齋所。至期，素服草履，徒步詣于壇，席藁露坐，晝曝日中，夜臥于地，衣不解帶。皇太子捧榼進蔬食，雜麻、麥、菽、粟，已而大雨。至九年秋，以七曜紊度，求直言；十八年春，以五星竝見，求直言；二十六年夏，以太白經天、京師大旱，求直言。諸以軍興、水、旱、𧖟蝗、雷震，免租者十有六，賑者三，贖鬻子者一。夫天厭元亂，民幸得脫湯火，已戴聖祖之德厚矣；而灑惠弛征，用以厚集瘡痍，祗承天戒若此，故雖有災沴，不敵禎符，茂啓無疆之曆，迄于今是賴。非聖祖之得天，有是哉？

頃者象緯失次，皇上旣惕心引慝，帥先羣臣，復
translation_en:
… personally pray at the Altar of Mountains and Rivers. He first ordered the Empress and the imperial consorts to tend the stoves and prepare farm-style meals, while the Heir Apparent and the princes served the food at the place of fasting. When the appointed time came, dressed in plain garments and straw sandals, he walked on foot to the altar, where he sat in the open air on a straw mat, exposing himself to the sun by day and sleeping on the ground by night without unfastening his belt. The Heir Apparent carried food containers to present coarse fare mixed with hemp seeds, wheat, beans, and millet; before long, a great rain fell. By the autumn of the ninth year (1376), because the seven luminaries were out of their regular courses, he sought forthright counsel; in the spring of the eighteenth year (1385), because the five planets appeared simultaneously, he sought forthright counsel; in the summer of the twenty-sixth year (1393), because Venus crossed the meridian in daylight and there was a severe drought in the capital, he sought forthright counsel. In all, on account of military campaigns, floods, droughts, plagues of caterpillars and locusts, and lightning strikes, taxes were remitted sixteen times, relief was distributed three times, and children who had been sold were redeemed once. Now, Heaven had grown weary of the disorders of the Yuan, and the people, fortunate to escape from boiling water and fire, already bore deep gratitude for the profound virtue of our Sacred Ancestor. Yet he showered benevolence and relaxed exactions in order to generously comfort the wounded and afflicted, reverently heeding the warnings of Heaven in such a manner. Therefore, even though there were calamities and anomalies, they were no match for the auspicious omens, flourishingly inaugurating a boundless dynastic calendar upon which we rely to this day. Had our Sacred Ancestor not won the favor of Heaven, could things have been thus?

Recently, when the celestial bodies lost their regular order, His Majesty, already filled with trepidation and taking the blame upon himself, led all the officials and furthermore…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
採言官疏
下禮臣飭中外脩省務實保民重以春夏間
不雨環郊圻數百里疫癘交蒸良可閔惻
皇上勅躬齋禱旋
令禮官趣京兆尹謁祠如儀無何靈雨三應
玄貺響答
皇上方且愀然不為快心動色以侈昭格更
命司農發帑賑粟施藥餌省行戶邮商人而補
其直減契券之稅以濟所疾苦已復蠲諸
===
藩積逋海內喁喁交口而頌
盛德此豈脩儀節為文具第令無遜漢宋二君
已哉嘗觀
文華殿
御書首謹天戒時星象順序雨暘未愆期也而
聖心已惓切焉則其
精意所感格不燔柴而饗不祝史而歆尤昭
然與天合符此非本實俱得紹堯舜而繩
太祖之懿矩者乎昔桓公問管仲以王者何貴
punctuated: 採言官疏，下禮臣飭中外脩省，務實保民。重以春夏間不雨，環郊圻數百里疫癘交蒸，良可閔惻。皇上勅躬齋禱，旋令禮官趣京兆尹謁祠如儀。無何，靈雨三應，玄貺響答。皇上方且愀然，不為快心動色，以侈昭格；更命司農發帑賑粟，施藥餌，省行戶，邮商人而補其直，減契券之稅，以濟所疾苦。已復蠲諸藩積逋，海內喁喁，交口而頌盛德。此豈脩儀節為文具，第令無遜漢、宋二君已哉！嘗觀文華殿御書，首謹天戒，時星象順序，雨暘未愆期也，而聖心已惓切焉；則其精意所感格，不燔柴而饗，不祝史而歆，尤昭然與天合符。此非本實俱得，紹堯、舜而繩太祖之懿矩者乎？昔桓公問管仲以王者何貴，
translation_en: … adopted the memorials of the speaking officials and sent instructions down to the officials of the Ministry of Rites to admonish the inner court and the provinces to cultivate themselves and examine their conduct, striving for practical measures to protect the people. Added to this, between spring and summer there was no rain, and for several hundred li around the suburban territory adjacent to the capital, pestilence and epidemics steamed forth together—truly something to evoke pity and grief. His Majesty disciplined His own person in fasting and prayer, and forthwith ordered the ritual officials to urge the Governor of the Capital Prefecture to visit the shrines and pray according to the prescribed rites. Before long, numinous rain responded thrice, and the mysterious blessings of Heaven answered like an echo. Yet His Majesty remained solemn and did not show delight or change expression so as to boast of having visibly moved Heaven. Instead, He further commanded the Minister of Revenue to disburse treasury funds and distribute grain in relief, dispense medicines, reduce the burdens on the guild merchants, show compassion to traders by making up the fair price of their goods, and reduce taxes on contracts and deeds in order to relieve the people's hardships and sufferings. Thereafter, He again remitted the accumulated tax arrears of the various provinces, so that all within the seas looked up eagerly and with one voice praised His abundant virtue. How could this merely be cultivating ceremonial details as empty formalities, simply so as not to fall short of those two rulers of the Han and Song! I have observed the imperial calligraphy in the Hall of Literary Splendor (Wenhua dian), which places at the very head "Heeding the Warnings of Heaven." At that time, the stars and celestial phenomena were in harmonious order, and rain and sunshine had not missed their proper seasons, yet the Imperial Mind was already earnestly concerned. Thus, what His sincere intent has moved and reached is accepted without burning the sacrificial firewood, and delighted in without the prayers of the invocators—all the more clearly matching the tally of Heaven. Is this not a case of attaining both the root and the reality, continuing the line of Yao and Shun and following the admirable standard of the Grand Progenitor (Taizu)? In antiquity, Duke Huan asked Guan Zhong what a true king values most, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
因語以貴天桓公仰而視天無得也仲曰
所謂天者非謂蒼蒼莽莽之天也君人者
以百姓爲天故敬天勤民用若兩驂而機
則環貫明君欲謹天戒未有不自勤民始
也今虜騎款關太倉之積足支數年
京師間稍多蓋藏而四方烝庶日就瘠薄可
爲寒心故毋以
京師槩視天下而自謂豐亨豫大爲足恃稍
寬督責之令俾民之上歲賦不能如期與
===
或麗于罰不能卽輸贖粟者毋致以肌膚
爲縓絏箠楚之叢而徐責其輸斯長吏得
以安意奉職而民困漸起矣諸腹裏客兵
業未可亟亟裁罷第徐爲解散之或還屬
籍或就屯伍終其身闕者不補積數年後
可使漸耗而吾民亦漸免於供餉之煩亦
一便也士額業不可增其多材郡邑第當
如禮臣議按歲而補其額數毋令民間俊
秀以留滯抱扼腕吏自郡守以上頃適道
punctuated: 因語以貴天。桓公仰而視天，無得也。仲曰：「所謂天者，非謂蒼蒼莽莽之天也。君人者，以百姓爲天。」故敬天勤民，用若兩驂，而機則環貫。明君欲謹天戒，未有不自勤民始也。今虜騎款關，太倉之積足支數年，京師間稍多蓋藏，而四方烝庶日就瘠薄，可爲寒心。故毋以京師槩視天下，而自謂豐亨豫大爲足恃。稍寬督責之令，俾民之上歲賦不能如期、與或麗于罰不能卽輸贖粟者，毋致以肌膚爲縓絏箠楚之叢，而徐責其輸，斯長吏得以安意奉職，而民困漸起矣。諸腹裏客兵，業未可亟亟裁罷，第徐爲解散之，或還屬籍，或就屯伍，終其身闕者不補，積數年後可使漸耗，而吾民亦漸免於供餉之煩，亦一便也。士額業不可增，其多材郡邑，第當如禮臣議，按歲而補其額數，毋令民間俊秀以留滯抱扼腕。吏自郡守以上，頃適道
translation_en:
… and he answered that he values Heaven. Duke Huan looked up and gazed at the sky, getting nothing from it. Guan Zhong said: "What is meant by Heaven does not refer to the vast azure sky. One who rules over men takes the common people as Heaven." Therefore, revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people function like two outside horses of a team, yet their mechanism is linked in an unbroken ring. When an enlightened ruler wishes to heed the warnings of Heaven, he never fails to begin by being diligent toward the people.

Today, northern nomadic horsemen come peacefully to the border passes, the reserves of the Great Granary are sufficient to last for several years, and around the capital there are somewhat plentiful stores. Yet the multitude of commoners across the four quarters grow more gaunt and impoverished by the day, which is enough to chill the heart. Therefore, do not judge the entire empire by the standard of the capital, nor tell yourself that abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness are enough to rely upon. Slightly relax the orders for strict exaction and reproof, so that those among the people who cannot deliver their annual taxes on schedule, or who have incurred penalties and cannot immediately pay grain in redemption, do not have their flesh and skin made a thicket for bindings and whippings; instead, require their payments gradually. Thus senior local officials will be able to perform their duties with a tranquil mind, and the distress of the people will gradually be relieved.

As for the various non-local garrison troops in the interior, since they cannot yet be precipitously reduced or disbanded, simply disperse them gradually: let some return to their original regimental registers and others take up stations in military farming colonies, and when they die, leave their vacancies unfilled. Over the course of several years, their numbers can be made to dwindle gradually, and our people will also gradually be spared the burden of supplying their provisions—this, too, is an expedient measure.

Since the quota of government students cannot be increased, in prefectures and counties rich in talent one should simply follow the deliberations of the officials of the Ministry of Rites and fill the quota numbers on an annual basis, so as not to let talented men among the populace wring their hands in frustration over being held back. As for officials from Grand Protectors [Prefects] on up, recently when traveling on the roads…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
路皆自貶損以明
聖德至與齊民無異而郵傳積困尚未盡蘇謂
宜杜耗蠹之源嚴苛索之禁庶民力不疲
於奔命得轉而緣南畝而所最急者似宜
優養言官之氣使幸畢其誠且屢求直言
前事可質驗也凡此皆不務變法而稍變
通之以勸吾民而又加恩勿濫賞賚勿輕
燕私勿昵諸不急之工一切省罷則實政
實惠可與堯舜同符
===
太祖合契用以祇若
天心而
眷命益篤矣漢儒謂災異為天之仁愛誠然哉
詩曰畏天之威于時保之竊謂可以仰舒
宸慮者或不出此非敢如京房劉向拘拘徵驗
之說也惟恕其狂
第三問
楊允京
同考試官教諭梁批諸子百家書浩瀚充棟學
punctuated:
路皆自貶損，以明聖德，至與齊民無異；而郵傳積困尚未盡蘇，謂宜杜耗蠹之源，嚴苛索之禁，庶民力不疲於奔命，得轉而緣南畝。而所最急者，似宜優養言官之氣，使幸畢其誠，且屢求直言，前事可質驗也。凡此皆不務變法，而稍變通之以勸吾民。而又加恩勿濫、賞賚勿輕、燕私勿昵，諸不急之工一切省罷，則實政實惠，可與堯、舜同符，太祖合契，用以祇若天心，而眷命益篤矣。漢儒謂「災異為天之仁愛」，誠然哉！《詩》曰：「畏天之威，于時保之。」竊謂可以仰舒宸慮者，或不出此，非敢如京房、劉向拘拘徵驗之說也。惟恕其狂。
第三問
楊允京
同考試官教諭梁批：諸子百家書浩瀚充棟，學
translation_en:
… the roads have all curtailed their own entitlements in order to manifest the Emperor's sagely virtue, to the point where they are no different from commoners; yet the accumulated distress of the postal relay system has still not been completely relieved. I would say we ought to stop up the sources of waste and embezzlement and strictly enforce prohibitions against extortionate demands, so that the people's strength will not be exhausted by rushing about on official service and they may instead turn back to tending their southern acres. And what is most urgent of all is that it seems proper to generously nurture the spirit of the speaking officials, allowing them the good fortune to express their sincerity to the fullest, while repeatedly seeking out forthright words—past events can be verified as proof of this. In all these matters, we need not strive to alter the laws, but merely adapt them slightly in order to encourage our people. Furthermore, if in bestowing favor there is no excess, in granting rewards there is no frivolity, in private leisure there is no undue familiarity, and all non-urgent construction projects are altogether curtailed and halted, then through substantive governance and substantive beneficence we may match the tallies of Yao and Shun and accord with the standard of Taizu. Thereby we shall reverently conform to the mind of Heaven, and its favored mandate will grow ever more steadfast. When the Han Confucians said that "calamities and anomalies are Heaven's benevolent love," how true that is! The Book of Odes says: "Revere the majesty of Heaven, and thus preserve its mandate." I venture to think that what may serve to relieve the imperial anxiety perhaps does not go beyond this; it is not that I dare to cling narrowly to theories of portents and verifications like Jing Fang and Liu Xiang. I ask only that you pardon my rashness.

Question Three
Yang Yunjing
