title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者鮮克遡核是篇考覽周詳品隲妥當而結以辨意
見一段尤切玄竅是有關於世教者錄之
考試官教諭賈批考據詳核而斷案瞭然足
占素養
考試官教諭汪批學識俱到
夫夏商以前正道明私說息迨于周末文
勝能言之士欲以謏聞譁世各騁其所長
爭為名高夫子慮道之不明文之煩惑也
乃返而端居洙泗之上取帝王列國之簡
冊品裁而刪定之為經凡六雖文學若游
夏至不能贊一辭何其雅醇而要眇與天
地相終始弗可易也兩漢以來人各是其
所見若别子析統自為名家久而分鑣竝
驅幾舉吾道而裂之迄于今益流宕靡曼
不可底止其上者自謂獨得旨趣而炫以
為奇次亦剽竊其餘稍緣飾之而矜以為
博此世道升降之大較而士習之通患也
嘗考司馬遷敘傳陰陽儒墨名法不過六
punctuated:
者鮮克遡核。是篇考覽周詳，品隲妥當，而結以辨意見一段，尤切玄竅，是有關於世教者，錄之。
考試官教諭賈批：考據詳核，而斷案瞭然，足占素養。
考試官教諭汪批：學識俱到。
夫夏、商以前，正道明，私說息。迨于周末，文勝，能言之士欲以謏聞譁世，各騁其所長，爭為名高。夫子慮道之不明、文之煩惑也，乃返而端居洙泗之上，取帝王列國之簡冊，品裁而刪定之，為經凡六。雖文學若游、夏，至不能贊一辭，何其雅醇而要眇，與天地相終始，弗可易也！兩漢以來，人各是其所見，若别子析統，自為名家。久而分鑣竝驅，幾舉吾道而裂之。迄于今，益流宕靡曼，不可底止。其上者自謂獨得旨趣，而炫以為奇；次亦剽竊其餘，稍緣飾之，而矜以為博。此世道升降之大較，而士習之通患也。嘗考司馬遷《敘傳》，陰陽、儒、墨、名、法，不過六
translation_en:
… [schol]ars are rarely able to trace and verify them. This essay is thorough in its examination and perusal, and sound in its critical assessments; its concluding section on distinguishing personal opinions hits the profound crux of the matter especially well. Because it has bearing on the moral instruction of the age, we select it for inclusion.

Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: The evidential research is detailed and accurate, and the conclusions are crystal clear—sufficient to show his long-cultivated learning.

Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Both scholarship and insight have reached the mark.

Prior to the Xia and Shang dynasties, the orthodox Way was bright and private doctrines were dormant. By the end of the Zhou, however, literary artifice prevailed. Eloquent scholars sought to clamor for the world's attention with petty learning, each giving free rein to his own strengths and competing for lofty reputations. The Master [Confucius], anxious lest the Way become obscured and writings become overly elaborate and confusing, returned to dwell in dignity beside the Zhu and Si rivers. Taking up the bamboo tablets and records of the sovereigns and the various states, he evaluated, pared down, and settled them, making six Classics in all. Even disciples distinguished in literature like Ziyou and Zixia could not add a single word. How refined, pure, essential, and subtle they are—coeval with Heaven and Earth from beginning to end, never to be altered!

Since the Western and Eastern Han, men have each affirmed their own views, like secondary sons splitting off from the main lineage to establish their own noted schools. Over time they galloped abreast along separate tracks, nearly tearing our Way asunder. Down to the present day, writing has grown ever more unrestrained and florid, with no end in sight. Those of the higher sort claim to have uniquely grasped the essential purport and flaunt it as novelty; the next tier merely plagiarize the leftovers, dress them up slightly, and boast of their erudition. This is the broad outline of the rise and decline of moral order in the world, and the common malady of literati customs.

I have examined Sima Qian's "Autobiographical Postface" (Xuzhuan), in which the Yin-Yang, Confucian, Mohist, Nominalist, and Legalist schools amount to no more than six…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
家迨劉子政當孝成之世受詔卒父業始
總加校定為七略奏之而以諸子為一略
次於六藝凡百八十九家中分為十種班
固用其說作藝文志而黜小說家不列第
以儒道陰陽名法縱橫墨與農雜定為九
種皆原其所本始而諸子始有區囿矣顧
其書亦多散佚不存姑以今所睹記者論
之則儒家首晏嬰而孫卿子陸賈典語賈
誼新書仲舒繁露劉向說苑桓寬鹽鐵楊
===
雄法言諸書僅得儒者之流裔而子思曾
孟舉世所誦服以羽翼六經乃槩列其中
舛矣若孔叢子亦志述仲尼稍附益之與
陸賈輩無異而班志弗及何也道家首伊
尹太公其書鮮存今所知則鬻子老子文
子管子莊列關尹鶡冠諸家而辛鈃子華
其說皆祖尚老氏或其書後出故不錄爾
陰陽則司星子韋與黃帝泰素不盡顓為
陰陽家言法家則有慎子韓非名家則有
punctuated: 家。迨劉子政當孝成之世，受詔卒父業，始總加校定，為《七略》奏之，而以諸子為一略，次於六藝，凡百八十九家，中分為十種。班固用其說作《藝文志》，而黜小說家不列，第以儒、道、陰陽、名、法、縱橫、墨與農、雜，定為九種，皆原其所本始，而諸子始有區囿矣。顧其書亦多散佚不存，姑以今所睹記者論之，則儒家首晏嬰，而《孫卿子》、陸賈《典語》、賈誼《新書》、仲舒《繁露》、劉向《說苑》、桓寬《鹽鐵》、楊雄《法言》諸書，僅得儒者之流裔；而子思、曾、孟，舉世所誦服以羽翼六經，乃槩列其中，舛矣。若《孔叢子》，亦志述仲尼，稍附益之，與陸賈輩無異，而班志弗及，何也？道家首伊尹、太公，其書鮮存，今所知則《鬻子》、《老子》、《文子》、《管子》、莊、列、關尹、鶡冠諸家；而辛鈃、子華，其說皆祖尚老氏，或其書後出，故不錄爾。陰陽則司星子韋與《黃帝泰素》，不盡顓為陰陽家言；法家則有《慎子》、韓非；名家則有
translation_en:
… schools. By the time of Liu Zizheng [Liu Xiang 劉向], during the reign of Emperor Xiaocheng, he received an imperial command to complete his father's work [actually completed by his son Liu Xin 劉歆], and for the first time comprehensively collated and edited the texts, compiling the Seven Summaries (Qilüe) and presenting it to the throne. In it, he made the Various Masters (Zhuzi) into one summary, placed right after the Six Arts, totaling one hundred and eighty-nine masters subdivided into ten categories. Ban Gu 班固 adopted his classification in composing the "Treatise on Literature" (Yiwen zhi), though he excluded the School of Minor Talks from the main count, establishing nine categories out of the Confucian, Daoist, Yin-Yang, Nominalist, Legalist, Diplomatist, Mohist, Agriculturist, and Syncretist schools, tracing the origins of each—whereupon the Various Masters first had distinct boundaries.

Yet many of those books have been scattered and lost and no longer survive. To speak tentatively on the basis of what is seen and recorded today: the Confucian school is headed by Yan Ying 晏嬰, while works such as the Master Sun Qing [Xunzi 荀子], Lu Jia's 陸賈 Classic Discourses (Dianyu) [New Discourses, Xinyu], Jia Yi's 賈誼 New Writings (Xinshu), Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 Luxuriant Gems of the Spring and Autumn (Chunqiu fanlu), Liu Xiang's Garden of Persuasions (Shuoyuan), Huan Kuan's 桓寬 Discourses on Salt and Iron (Yantie lun), and Yang Xiong's 楊雄 Model Sayings (Fayan) capture only the collateral offshoots of the Confucians. Meanwhile, Zisi 子思, Zengzi 曾子, and Mencius (Mengzi 孟子), whom the whole world recites and reveres as wings to the Six Classics, were indiscriminately grouped among them—which is an error! As for the Kongcongzi 孔叢子, it too records and transmits the words of Zhongni [Confucius], slightly augmenting them, no different from men like Lu Jia; why then did Ban Gu's treatise fail to mention it?

The Daoist school is headed by Yi Yin 伊尹 and Taigong 太公, whose books rarely survive. Those known today include the Master Yu (Yuzi 鬻子), the Laozi 老子, the Master Wen (Wenzi 文子), the Guanzi 管子, Zhuangzi 莊子, Liezi 列子, Guanyinzi 關尹子, and the Pheasant Cap Master (Heguanzi 鶡冠子); whereas Xin Jian 辛鈃 [Jiyan 計然 / Wenzi] and Master Zihua (Zihuazi 子華子), whose doctrines both take Laozi as their ancestor and model, were perhaps not recorded because their books appeared later. In the Yin-Yang school, Star Steward Ziwei (Sixing Ziwei 司星子韋) and the Yellow Emperor's Grand Basis (Huangdi Taisu 黃帝泰素) do not exclusively expound Yin-Yang doctrines. In the Legalist school, there are the Master Shen (Shenzi 慎子) and Han Fei 韓非; in the Nominalist school, there are…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鄧析尹文公孫龍墨家止有墨子七十二
篇縱横若蘇張詳具史記而爲書無考若
鬼谷之飛箝捭闔固蘇張所北面而師事
之者今其書尚在何偶遺之耶雜家則有
尉繚子吕氏春秋淮南内外諸篇農家書
皆鮮傳即汜勝之十八篇其單言稍散見
於載籍非完書也至梁通事舎人劉勰復
爲著論而諸子益燦然可睹矣其中所稱
述自孟軻荀卿而下共二十三家内管晏
===
莊列墨翟尹文鬼谷尸佼尉繚鶡冠文子
愼到韓非吕氏淮南凡一十五家已考論
于前可略也惟青史子在小説家乃班氏
所黜居九種之外野老在農家隨巢在墨
家志有其目而二書皆闕騶子在陰陽申
商在法家其言行史記具之而爲書亦世
所鮮覿云勰又於陸賈劉楊之外益以王
符潜夫崔寔正論仲長昌言杜夷幽求以
廣班志所未備然四子皆出班氏之後故
punctuated: 鄧析、尹文、公孫龍。墨家止有《墨子》七十二篇。縱横若蘇、張，詳具《史記》，而爲書無考；若鬼谷之《飛箝》、《捭闔》，固蘇、張所北面而師事之者，今其書尚在，何偶遺之耶？雜家則有《尉繚子》、《吕氏春秋》、《淮南》内外諸篇。農家書皆鮮傳，即《汜勝之》十八篇，其單言稍散見於載籍，非完書也。至梁通事舎人劉勰復爲著論，而諸子益燦然可睹矣。其中所稱述，自孟軻、荀卿而下，共二十三家。内管、晏、莊、列、墨翟、尹文、鬼谷、尸佼、尉繚、鶡冠、文子、愼到、韓非、吕氏、淮南，凡一十五家，已考論于前，可略也。惟《青史子》在小説家，乃班氏所黜，居九種之外；《野老》在農家，《隨巢》在墨家，志有其目，而二書皆闕；《騶子》在陰陽，申、商在法家，其言行《史記》具之，而爲書亦世所鮮覿云。勰又於陸賈、劉、楊之外，益以王符《潜夫》、崔寔《正論》、仲長《昌言》、杜夷《幽求》，以廣班志所未備。然四子皆出班氏之後，故
translation_en:
… Deng Xi 鄧析, Yin Wen 尹文, and Gongsun Long 公孫龍. Among the Mohists, there are only the seventy-two chapters of the Mozi 墨子. As for the School of Diplomacy (Zongheng), figures like Su Qin 蘇秦 and Zhang Yi 張儀 are recorded in detail in the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji 史記), yet their writings cannot be verified; whereas the "Flying Pincers" (Feiqian 飛箝) and "Opening and Closing" (Baihe 捭闔) of the Master of Ghost Valley (Guiguzi 鬼谷子)—whom Su and Zhang indeed faced north to serve as their teacher—still survive today, so why were they accidentally omitted? Among the Syncretists (Zajia), there are the Weiliaozi 尉繚子, the Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lü (Lüshi chunqiu 吕氏春秋), and the Inner and Outer chapters of the Huainanzi 淮南子. The writings of the Agriculturists (Nongjia) have rarely been transmitted; even the eighteen chapters of Fan Shengzhi 汜勝之 have only isolated sayings slightly scattered across various texts and are no longer a complete work.

When it came to the Liang dynasty, the Palace Receptionist (tongshi sheren) Liu Xie 劉勰 again wrote a critical discourse on them, whereby the Various Masters became even more brilliantly clear to behold. Those whom he cited and discussed, from Meng Ke 孟軻 (Mencius) and Xun Qing 荀卿 (Xunzi) downward, totaled twenty-three masters in all. Among them, Guan Zhong 管仲, Yan Ying 晏嬰, Zhuangzi 莊子, Liezi 列子, Mo Di 墨翟, Yin Wen, Guiguzi, Shi Jiao 尸佼, Wei Liao 尉繚, the Heguanzi 鶡冠子, the Wenzi 文子, Shen Dao 愼到, Han Fei 韓非, Master Lü, and the Huainanzi—fifteen masters in total—have already been examined and discussed above, so they may be passed over here. Only the Qingshizi 青史子 belongs to the School of Minor Talks (Xiaoshuojia), which Ban Gu 班固 dismissed and placed outside the Nine Schools; the Yelao 野老 among the Agriculturists and Suichaozi 隨巢子 among the Mohists have their titles listed in the treatise, yet both books are lost; the Zouzi 騶子 of the Yin-Yang school and Shen Buhai 申不害 and Shang Yang 商鞅 of the Legalists have their words and deeds fully recounted in the Records of the Grand Historian, yet their books are likewise rarely seen in the world. Beyond Lu Jia 陸賈, Liu Xiang 劉向, and Yang Xiong 楊雄, Liu Xie further added Wang Fu's 王符 Comments of a Recluse (Qianfu lun 潜夫論), Cui Shi's 崔寔 Discourse on Government (Zhenglun 正論), Zhongchang Tong's 仲長統 Forthright Discourses (Changyan 昌言), and Du Yi's 杜夷 Seeking in Seclusion (Youqiuzi 幽求子), in order to expand upon what Ban Gu's treatise had not yet covered. However, all four of these masters appeared after Ban Gu, and therefore…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
前志不載若幽求子今亦罕傳之矣乃荀
悅申鑒當時號為小荀子與徐幹中論頗
近正理皆可附儒家之後何通事之弗錄
也至其首論諸子為入道見志之書其說
未敢深信而孟軻之淵懿博達固所謂絶
塵而奔者亦與諸子槩列此其見與班氏
何異若班氏之言曰使其人遭明王聖主
得其所折中皆股肱之材也嗟嗟此豈蘇
張公孫龍輩能當之乎又何罪夫劉通事
===
也自是則文中鹿門可綴於儒齊丘無能
天隱玄眞可歸於道餘蓋更僕未易數矣
大都諸子皆出於漢後多倣象為之或不
甚雅馴姑不遠論即以鬻子捕獸逐麋之
對文王不以為耄夫而師事之因自詮次
其言為百家之始而文義簡短不類周初
且班志僅六篇至逢行珪表上乃有十四
篇得非後世依託而增益之者乎故舉鬻
子而諸子可例也乃執事下詢欲舉諸子
punctuated: 前志不載。若《幽求子》，今亦罕傳之矣。乃荀悅《申鑒》，當時號為「小荀子」，與徐幹《中論》頗近正理，皆可附儒家之後，何通事之弗錄也？至其首論諸子為入道見志之書，其說未敢深信；而孟軻之淵懿博達，固所謂絕塵而奔者，亦與諸子槩列，此其見與班氏何異？若班氏之言曰：「使其人遭明王聖主，得其所折中，皆股肱之材也。」嗟嗟！此豈蘇、張、公孫龍輩能當之乎？又何罪夫劉通事也？自是，則《文中》、《鹿門》可綴於儒，《齊丘》、《無能》、《天隱》、《玄眞》可歸於道，餘蓋更僕未易數矣。大都諸子皆出於漢後，多倣象為之，或不甚雅馴。姑不遠論，即以《鬻子》捕獸逐麋之對，文王不以為耄夫而師事之，因自詮次其言為百家之始，而文義簡短，不類周初；且班志僅六篇，至逢行珪表上，乃有十四篇，得非後世依託而增益之者乎？故舉《鬻子》而諸子可例也。乃執事下詢，欲舉諸子
translation_en:
… the earlier bibliography does not record them. As for the Master Youqiu (Youqiu zi), today it is also rarely transmitted. Yet Xun Yue's Extended Reflections (Shenjian)—which at the time was styled the "Lesser Master Xun" (Xiao Xunzi)—and Xu Gan's Balanced Discourses (Zhonglun) both come quite close to orthodox principle and could well be appended after the Confucian school; why did the Receptionist [Liu Xie] fail to record them? As for his opening argument that the Various Masters are books for entering the Way and manifesting one's aspirations, I dare not fully credit that view; moreover, Meng Ke [Mencius], in his profound virtue and broad mastery—truly one who, as the saying goes, gallops off leaving the dust behind—is also lumped together on the same level with the Various Masters. How does his view differ from that of Ban Gu? Take Ban's words: "Had those men encountered an enlightened king or a sage ruler and found proper balance through him, they would all have been talents fit to serve as his right-hand men." Alas! How could the likes of Su Qin, Zhang Yi, or Gongsun Long ever be worthy of that? What fault, then, can we find with Receptionist Liu?

After this period, the Master Shown Within the Word (Wenzhongzi) and Master Lumen (Lumenzi) may be attached to the Confucians, while Master Qiqiu (Qiqiu zi), Master Wuneng (Wunengzi), Master Tianyin (Tianyinzi), and Master Xuanzhen (Xuanzhenzi) may be assigned to the Daoists; as for the rest, one could change attendants and still not easily count them all. For the most part, those Various Masters that appeared after the Han were largely composed in imitation, and at times are not very refined or orthodox. Setting aside distant examples for the moment, take simply Master Yu (Yuzi): because of his reply about catching beasts and chasing elk, King Wen did not regard him as a senile old man, but served him as a teacher, and subsequently compiled and ordered his words himself as the beginning of the Hundred Schools. Yet its wording and meaning are brief and clipped, unlike works of the early Zhou; furthermore, Ban's bibliography lists only six chapters, whereas by the time Feng Xinggui presented it with a memorial, there were fourteen chapters—could this not be a case of later generations falsely attributing their own additions to it? Thus, by citing Master Yu, the other Masters may be judged by analogy.

Now Your Excellency inquires of us below, wishing to take all the Various Masters…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而別以九流舉九流而歸之六家而務求
不詭於六籍之義爲意甚盛愚則以班志
區囿已定無容復述而雜家多本於道縱
橫持論頗涉於名農事有羲和授時之義
於陰陽家頗近卽函九爲六亦無不可者
第求以不詭於六籍之義則難言之矣夫
六籍爲敎舉帝王賢聖之蘊奧具載其中
其分經辨義則若春夏秋冬各有令序無
相越也其會經合義則若眞精元氣自爲
===
脉絡無相離也彼諸子者曾庶幾有一於
是乎故覽華而食實棄邪而採正雖在其
人之所決擇而終不可以烏附之僅效媲
吾稻粱者此經子之辨也顧農雜縱橫諸
家其術在今頗衰止不足深較今所病者
惟道與儒而儒道二家最後出者又惟釋
氏當周末釋起西竺其敎略類道流而加
以超脫寂滅爲宗意青牛老氏旣適流沙
而其敎始出亦道家之別支而獨詣者也
punctuated: 而別以九流，舉九流而歸之六家，而務求不詭於六籍之義，爲意甚盛。愚則以《班志》區囿已定，無容復述；而雜家多本於道，縱橫持論頗涉於名，農事有羲和授時之義，於陰陽家頗近，卽函九爲六，亦無不可者。第求以不詭於六籍之義，則難言之矣。夫六籍爲敎，舉帝王賢聖之蘊奧具載其中。其分經辨義，則若春夏秋冬各有令序，無相越也；其會經合義，則若眞精元氣自爲脉絡，無相離也。彼諸子者，曾庶幾有一於是乎？故覽華而食實，棄邪而採正，雖在其人之所決擇，而終不可以烏附之僅效，媲吾稻粱者，此經、子之辨也。顧農、雜、縱橫諸家，其術在今頗衰止，不足深較。今所病者惟道與儒，而儒、道二家最後出者，又惟釋氏。當周末，釋起西竺，其敎略類道流，而加以超脫寂滅爲宗。意青牛老氏旣適流沙，而其敎始出，亦道家之別支而獨詣者也。
translation_en: … and distinguish them into the Nine Streams (jiuliu), and then take the Nine Streams and reduce them to the Six Schools (liujia), striving to seek meanings that do not deviate from the Six Classics (liuji)—this intention is most noble. Yet in my humble view, the categorization in Ban Gu's "Treatise on Literature" (Banzhi) is already settled and needs no repetition. Moreover, the Syncretists (zajia) mostly derive from the Daoists (dao); the arguments maintained by the Diplomats (zongheng) touch considerably upon the Logicians (ming); and agricultural affairs (nongshi) embody the principle of Xi and He granting the seasons, which is quite close to the Yin-Yang school (yinyangjia). Thus, even to subsume the Nine into the Six is by no means impermissible. However, to require that their meanings do not deviate from the Six Classics is something difficult to speak of. Now, the teachings of the Six Classics contain in full all the profound mysteries of the emperors, kings, worthies, and sages. When we divide the Classics and distinguish their meanings, they are like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, each having its seasonal order without overstepping one another; when we synthesize the Classics and unite their meanings, they are like true essence and primordial qi naturally forming an interconnected network of vessels without separating from one another. Have those various Masters (zhuzi) ever come close to possessing even one aspect of this? Therefore, admiring the blossoms while eating the fruit, and discarding the heterodox while adopting the orthodox, though a matter of an individual's own choice, in the end one cannot take the mere occasional efficacy of aconite (wufu) and compare it to our rice and millet—this is the distinction between the Classics and the Masters. Yet as for the Agriculturalists, Syncretists, Diplomats, and other schools, their arts have in present times largely declined and ceased, and are not worth scrutinizing deeply. What causes harm today lies solely between Daoism and Confucianism (ru), and emerging after the two schools of Confucianism and Daoism, there is also Buddhism (Shishi). At the end of the Zhou dynasty, Buddhism arose in Western India (Xizhu). Its teachings slightly resembled the Daoist current, while adding transcendence and nirvana (jiemie) as its fundamental tenets. One suspects that after Laozi on his dark ox went to the Flowing Sands (Liusha), this teaching first emerged—being also a separate branch of the Daoist school that reached its own unique attainment. …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
自漢明帝求得其書初尚不敢列於諸家
其後始漸起而與道爲二後又漸起而與
儒道鼎足爲三今則無論儒道卽神聖若
吾夫子者亦幾與分庭而爭席矣在
國初爲文引用老子莊列者有禁今則佛經
僧錄竄入其中輒矜炫以爲獨得其靡曼
不根殊甚此所以
功令數下而禁戒之諄切也今欲正經術其
要莫急於辨意見夫意見者固吾心之虛
===
靈所觸而通者也業豈能盡廢然其端有
正有私士之潛心經術積久而貫通以試
之用輒資深逢原出入不悖所聞此意見
之正也非是私矣其經術非能熟習而精
詣之也其佛老莊列亦非能熟習而精詣
之也第以其質之偶得於穎悟涉獵其藩
復胷度而臆決之嘵嘵然以語諸人曰儒
也以試之天下國家其用正佛老也以用
之身心性命其義精久而援引二氏附和
punctuated: 自漢明帝求得其書，初尚不敢列於諸家，其後始漸起而與道爲二，後又漸起而與儒、道鼎足爲三。今則無論儒、道，卽神聖若吾夫子者，亦幾與分庭而爭席矣。在國初，爲文引用《老子》、莊、列者有禁，今則佛經、僧錄竄入其中，輒矜炫以爲獨得，其靡曼不根殊甚。此所以功令數下，而禁戒之諄切也。今欲正經術，其要莫急於辨意見。夫意見者，固吾心之虛靈所觸而通者也，業豈能盡廢？然其端有正有私。士之潛心經術，積久而貫通，以試之用，輒資深逢原，出入不悖所聞，此意見之正也。非是，私矣。其經術非能熟習而精詣之也，其佛、老、莊、列亦非能熟習而精詣之也，第以其質之偶得於穎悟，涉獵其藩，復胷度而臆決之，嘵嘵然以語諸人曰：「儒也，以試之天下國家，其用正；佛、老也，以用之身心性命，其義精。」久而援引二氏，附和
translation_en:
Since Emperor Ming of Han (漢明帝) sought out and obtained their texts, at first they still did not dare to rank themselves among the various schools of thought. Only later did Buddhism gradually rise to form a pair with Daoism, and later still it gradually rose to stand as one of three legs of a tripod alongside Confucianism and Daoism. Today, to say nothing of Confucianism and Daoism, even toward a divine sage like our Master Confucius, they nearly claim equal standing as host and guest and vie for the seat of honor. At the beginning of our dynasty, there were prohibitions against quoting the Laozi (老子), Zhuangzi (莊子), and Liezi (列子) in essay writing. Today, however, Buddhist sutras and monastic records are slipped into essays, and writers boastfully show them off as their own unique insights; their ornate and groundless nature is extreme. This is why official regulations concerning the examinations have been issued repeatedly, prohibiting and warning against this with earnest urgency.

If we now wish to rectify classical scholarship, nothing is more urgent than distinguishing among personal opinions. Now, personal opinions are assuredly what the clear and numinous faculty of our mind contacts and comprehends—how could they be entirely discarded in one's studies? Yet in their beginnings, some are orthodox and some are selfishly biased. When a scholar immerses his mind in classical scholarship, accumulating learning over a long time until he achieves thorough comprehension, and then tests it in practical application, he draws deeply upon it and meets its source everywhere, going in and out without contradicting what he has learned—this is orthodox opinion. Anything other than this is selfish bias. Such men have neither thoroughly practiced nor attained profound mastery of classical scholarship, nor have they thoroughly practiced or attained profound mastery of Buddhism, Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Liezi. Merely relying on what their natural资质 happens to grasp through clever intuition, they skim the outer fence of these teachings, conjecture in their breasts, and decide by arbitrary guesswork, clamoring as they tell others: "Confucianism, when tested in the realm and the state, is orthodox in its public function; Buddhism and Daoism, when applied to body, mind, and human nature and destiny, are subtle in their inner meaning." Over time, they cite the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism to chime in with…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以經術而舉世騖之矣故聽其說若不異
於聖人而繹其旨又若蘇張之縱橫公孫
龍之堅白又徐而覈其實又若似於無非
無舉之鄉原是說之難持者也故旣辨意
見而每歲所取士必嚴核所誦法其浮誕
無當者卽負藻才輒擯不錄則士為學必
知守六經其為文必不悖六經正道明而
私說息矣
第四問
===
同考試官訓導丁批名賢二祠風化所關此對
尚論先哲軒輊較然足覘嚮往末欲推明禮意詳覈
奏
策尤得慎重之指可錄
考試官教諭賈批評品甚精而議處更有灼
見
考試官教諭汪批稽覈詳確
昔之君子其砥行植業非以為名也人或
banxin: 鄉試錄 七十二 陶明禮
punctuated:
以經術，而舉世騖之矣。故聽其說，若不異於聖人；而繹其旨，又若蘇、張之縱橫，公孫龍之堅白；又徐而覈其實，又若似於無非無舉之鄉原，是說之難持者也。故旣辨意見，而每歲所取士，必嚴核所誦法，其浮誕無當者，卽負藻才，輒擯不錄。則士為學必知守六經，其為文必不悖六經，正道明而私說息矣。
第四問
同考試官訓導丁批：名、賢二祠，風化所關。此對尚論先哲，軒輊較然，足覘嚮往。末欲推明禮意，詳覈奏策，尤得慎重之指，可錄。
考試官教諭賈批：評品甚精，而議處更有灼見。
考試官教諭汪批：稽覈詳確。
昔之君子，其砥行植業，非以為名也。人或
translation_en:
…with classical learning, and the whole world chases after it. Thus, when one listens to their words, they seem no different from those of the sages; yet when one unravels their underlying purport, they resemble the alliance strategies of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, or the "hard and white" sophistry of Gongsun Long; and when one calmly examines their actual substance, they resemble the "village honest men" (xiangyuan) who attract neither blame nor praise—these are doctrines that cannot be sustained. Therefore, once we have distinguished between proper and partisan views, in selecting scholars each year we must strictly verify what they recite and model themselves upon. Those whose writings are superficial, extravagant, and unfounded, even if they possess华美 literary talent, should immediately be rejected and not selected. Then scholars in pursuing their learning will surely know to hold fast to the Six Classics, and in composing their essays will surely not contravene the Six Classics; the orthodox Way will be illuminated, and private doctrines will cease.

Question Four

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Ding: The two shrines to Eminent Officials and Local Worthies are of vital concern to moral transformation. In critically discussing the former worthies, this response makes clear distinctions in their relative merits, which suffices to show the candidate's own aspirations. At the end, the desire to elucidate the intent of the rites and carefully verify memorialized recommendations especially grasps the principle of prudence. Worthy of selection.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jia: The evaluations are very precise, and the proposed measures show even more penetrating insight.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: The investigation and verification are detailed and accurate.

When the gentlemen of antiquity honed their conduct and established their achievements, they did not do so for the sake of fame. When others happened to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
舉名而歸之則其舉之者必且惴惴然若
操九鼎捧璧玉惟恐一不當而至於毀也
故所舉之賢益彰而可以風厲于當世後
之君子其身已有意於為名其子若孫又
欲以其名為祖父光寵而議舉者與柄舉
者又且重違其欲名之心或徇于情怵于
勢而掩于利舉爼豆之大典雷同附和以
歸諸無異常人之身而卓犖瑰瑋者或遺
於聞見靡所章勸甚無謂也此豈崇祀指
===
哉按周制凡有功紀于王之太常祭于大
烝司勳詔之為典凡六王功曰勳國功曰
功民功曰庸事功曰勞治功曰力戰功曰
多匪是者弗得濫及其道德為後學準繩
則秩祀瞽宗次亦祀于社以示不忘玆先
王之崇德報功章往而勸來者禮意最深
遠矣
明興稽古經制為名宦鄕賢二祠于學宮士之
丕懋勳猷行能信於鄕國足應祀典者各
punctuated:
舉名而歸之，則其舉之者必且惴惴然，若操九鼎、捧璧玉，惟恐一不當而至於毀也。故所舉之賢益彰，而可以風厲于當世。後之君子，其身已有意於為名，其子若孫又欲以其名為祖父光寵，而議舉者與柄舉者又且重違其欲名之心，或徇于情，怵于勢，而掩于利，舉爼豆之大典，雷同附和，以歸諸無異常人之身；而卓犖瑰瑋者，或遺於聞見，靡所章勸，甚無謂也。此豈崇祀指哉？
按周制，凡有功，紀于王之太常，祭于大烝，司勳詔之。為典凡六：王功曰勳，國功曰功，民功曰庸，事功曰勞，治功曰力，戰功曰多。匪是者弗得濫及。其道德為後學準繩，則秩祀瞽宗，次亦祀于社，以示不忘。玆先王之崇德報功、章往而勸來者，禮意最深遠矣。
明興，稽古經制，為名宦、鄕賢二祠于學宮。士之丕懋勳猷、行能信於鄕國，足應祀典者，各
translation_en:
… nominate them and accord them such renown, those making the nomination would surely be filled with trepidation, as though holding the Nine Tripods or cradling a jade disk, fearing only that a single misstep might lead to ruin. Consequently, the worthies who were nominated became all the more illustrious and could inspire and rouse the men of their age. As for the gentlemen of later times, they themselves already harbored the intention of seeking fame, and their sons and grandsons likewise wished to use that fame to bring glory and favor upon their fathers and grandfathers. Meanwhile, those who deliberated on nominations and those who held the authority to make them were reluctant to thwart this desire for fame; some yielded to personal feelings, were intimidated by power, or were blinded by profit, taking the great rite of sacrificial vessels and echoing one another in blind conformity to bestow it upon men no different from ordinary folk. Meanwhile, those of extraordinary and outstanding character were sometimes overlooked in what was heard and seen, leaving nothing by which to honor and encourage virtue—this is utterly senseless. How could this be the purpose of reverent sacrifice?

According to the institutions of the Zhou, all who achieved merit had it recorded upon the King's Great Banner and were sacrificed to at the Great Winter Sacrifice, as proclaimed by the Director of Merit. There were six categories in this canon: merit in serving the royal house was called "distinction" (xun); merit in serving the state was called "achievement" (gong); merit in serving the people was called "service" (yong); merit in handling affairs was called "toil" (lao); merit in governance was called "effort" (li); and merit in battle was called "valor" (duo). Those who did not meet these criteria were not permitted to be indiscriminately included. As for those whose morality served as a standard for later scholars, they received regular sacrifices in the Blind Musicians' Hall (Guzong), and next to that were also sacrificed to at the community altar, so as to show they were not forgotten. In this way, the former kings revered virtue and rewarded merit, honoring the past to encourage the future—the meaning of their rites was most profound and far-reaching.

With the rise of the Ming, antiquity was examined to establish regular institutions, and the two shrines of Eminent Officials and Local Worthies were erected within the school precincts. For scholars who greatly exerted themselves in meritorious plans, or whose conduct and abilities were trusted in their local communities and states so as to be worthy of the sacrificial canon, each…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以所由舉入祠而歲令握紀之臣謹察其
不如法者輒得裁罷每二丁釋奠禮畢有
司率博士謁祠唯謹誠重之也粵西故仕
國其士習樸茂頗有先民之遺風故其爲
賢亦略相等今考諸故諜宦績自史祿而
下凡百三十七人獻民自陳元而下亦百
二十七人不具述述其較著者則賈琮爲
刺史察民所爲盜之故因而撫荒蠲役戮
止渠魁百姓以安巷路間皆以來晚歌之
===
得便計矣而許仲宣不待奏報輒罷所部
兵俾不委命於炎瘴者殆萬餘人無何交
州送款上疏待罪見何定也而余靖之帥
二廣幾十年恩信被於異域其功尤足多
者若陳臨閔死囚之無嗣令其妻得侍獄
中舉子雖情涉姑息其事或難盡循而哀
矜之仁不可少也士燮守交趾中原人士
往依避難者以百數其保境功比於竇融
偉矣陳坦然單騎行賊壘爲書約矢射圍
punctuated: 以所由舉入祠，而歲令握紀之臣謹察其不如法者，輒得裁罷。每二丁釋奠禮畢，有司率博士謁祠唯謹，誠重之也。粵西故仕國，其士習樸茂，頗有先民之遺風，故其爲賢亦略相等。今考諸故諜，宦績自史祿而下凡百三十七人，獻民自陳元而下亦百二十七人，不具述。述其較著者，則賈琮爲刺史，察民所爲盜之故，因而撫荒蠲役，戮止渠魁，百姓以安，巷路間皆以「來晚」歌之，得便計矣；而許仲宣不待奏報，輒罷所部兵，俾不委命於炎瘴者殆萬餘人，無何交州送款，上疏待罪，見何定也；而余靖之帥二廣幾十年，恩信被於異域，其功尤足多者；若陳臨閔死囚之無嗣，令其妻得侍獄中舉子，雖情涉姑息，其事或難盡循，而哀矜之仁不可少也。士燮守交趾，中原人士往依避難者以百數，其保境功比於竇融，偉矣；陳坦然單騎行賊壘，爲書約矢射圍
translation_en: … are recommended for induction into the shrines according to their respective merits, and each year the officials holding disciplinary authority are ordered to carefully inspect them, immediately removing any who do not conform to the regulations. Whenever the śākyamuni-like libation ceremony [釋奠] on the two ding days is concluded, the authorities lead the Erudites in paying homage at the shrines with the utmost reverence, truly attaching great importance to it. Guangxi is an old land of official service; the customs of its scholars are simple and substantial, retaining much of the lingering ethos of the ancients, and thus the worthies they have produced are roughly comparable to one another. Now, examining the old records, those of official merit from Shi Lu 史祿 downward number one hundred and thirty-seven men in all, and the local worthies from Chen Yuan 陳元 downward also number one hundred and twenty-seven men; we shall not recount them in full. To recount the more prominent among them: when Jia Cong 賈琮 served as Regional Inspector, he investigated the reasons why the people turned to banditry, and accordingly pacified the荒-stricken, remitted labor services, and executed only the ringleaders, whereby the common people were brought to peace and in the lanes and roads all sang of him as having “come too late”—he had hit upon an expedient course! And yet Xu Zhongxuan 許仲宣, without waiting for a response to his memorial, forthwith disbanded the troops under his command, sparing nearly ten thousand men from abandoning their lives to the fiery miasmas; before long Jiaozhou 交州 tendered its submission, and he submitted a memorial awaiting punishment—how resolute was his foresight! And Yu Jing 余靖 commanded the two Guang provinces for nearly ten years, his grace and good faith extending to foreign lands, so that his achievements are especially worthy of praise. As for Chen Lin 陳臨, who pitied a condemned prisoner for having no heir and allowed the man’s wife to attend him in prison so as to bear a son—although his sentiment bordered on lax indulgence and his action could hardly be followed in every case, such compassionate benevolence cannot be belittled. When Shi Xie 士燮 guarded Jiaozhi 交趾, gentlemen from the Central Plains who went to rely on him for refuge from the troubles numbered in the hundreds; his achievement in preserving the territory may be compared to that of Dou Rong 竇融—grand indeed! Chen Tanran 陳坦然 rode alone to the rebel ramparts and wrote a letter tied to an arrow to shoot into the besieged…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
中諭叛卒禍福無何卒降而賊自平事聞
賜錦袍銀帶悉謝不受義何高也而蔣允
濟守邕管恩信結於民心思之如一日庶
幾廩廩德讓君子之風焉若趙觀文再試
上第以言忤宰相意輒謝病歸雖所志未
盡効於時而嘉遯之節不可易也故其英
聲駿烈雖去今數百餘年而猶能使人仰
慕不輟藉令俎豆者而皆若前數公豈不
光我庠序油然觀感而興起者乎顧有或
===
謬不然於今者何也其內有所親厚則尺
寸之功而楊詡之以為蓋世也其外有所
憑藉則取節之行而藻飾之以為邁夷也
其下有所結納則里巷之譽而畀翼之以
為懿爍也故有奮臆妄議持方寸之楮皷
其喙於握紀者之前不踰月已得報祀何
後世之多賢而祀易成也則前所謂情徇
勢怵而利之掩也頃者
聖天子深惟崇報之義
punctuated: 中，諭叛卒禍福，無何卒降而賊自平，事聞，賜錦袍銀帶，悉謝不受，義何高也！而蔣允濟守邕管，恩信結於民心，思之如一日，庶幾廩廩德讓君子之風焉。若趙觀文再試上第，以言忤宰相意，輒謝病歸；雖所志未盡効於時，而嘉遯之節不可易也。故其英聲駿烈，雖去今數百餘年，而猶能使人仰慕不輟。藉令俎豆者而皆若前數公，豈不光我庠序，油然觀感而興起者乎？顧有或謬不然於今者，何也？其內有所親厚，則尺寸之功，而楊詡之以為蓋世也；其外有所憑藉，則取節之行，而藻飾之以為邁夷也；其下有所結納，則里巷之譽，而畀翼之以為懿爍也。故有奮臆妄議，持方寸之楮，皷其喙於握紀者之前，不踰月已得報祀。何後世之多賢而祀易成也？則前所謂情徇勢怵而利之掩也。頃者，聖天子深惟崇報之義，
translation_en: … into the encircled camp, instructing the rebel soldiers on the consequences of good and ill fortune. Before long, the soldiers surrendered and the rebels were pacified of their own accord. When the matter was reported to the court, he was bestowed a brocade robe and a silver belt, all of which he declined to accept—how lofty was his righteousness! And when Jiang Yunji 蔣允濟 guarded the Yongzhou Command (Yongguan 邕管), his grace and trustworthiness bound the hearts of the people, who longed for him as if a single day had passed; he nearly attained the awe-inspiring air of a gentleman of virtuous deference. As for Zhao Guanwen 趙觀文, he twice placed in the highest grade of the examinations, yet because his words offended the Chief Councilor's wishes, he promptly pleaded illness and returned home. Although his ambitions were not fully realized in his time, his integrity in noble withdrawal cannot be taken lightly. Therefore, although their heroic renown and illustrious achievements are removed from the present by several hundred years, they can still make people look up to them in unceasing admiration. Supposing that all those who receive sacrificial offerings in the shrines were like the several gentlemen mentioned above, would that not bring glory to our schools and cause people to be spontaneously moved by their example and roused to action? Yet why is it that today some cases are absurdly contrary to this? When inside there are close personal ties, then a tiny bit of merit is boasted of and extolled as surpassing the age; when outside there is powerful backing, then a single commendable act is embellished and dressed up as transcending the ordinary; when below there is collusion and patronage, then a reputation in the village lanes is lent wings and promoted as splendid perfection. Thus, there are those who assert their private whims and make reckless proposals, holding a square inch of paper and wagging their tongues before those who hold the reins of authority, and in less than a month they have already obtained approval for shrine sacrifices. Why are there so many worthies in later ages, and why are sacrifices so easily established? It is what was earlier called yielding to personal feelings, being intimidated by influence, and being blinded by profit. Recently, the Sacred Son of Heaven, deeply reflecting upon the meaning of honoring and repaying merit, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
特採言官疏
令禮官下所司釐正而爲籍
奏之
德意甚厚今長吏方兢兢奉行日求所不應祀
者亟罷之以儆煩濫但其故老無徵載籍
希闊靡所考騐卽銖稱而櫛數之未必無
遺議者稽覈難也且其前已令得冒祠今
卽罷去於章勸之褚已損故不若及今而
愼爲之禁滌時之弊而原禮之意以檢律
===
===
之庶可止也何謂時弊曰今之議舉者習
於文矣不考論其行事而詳著之以待稽
覈惟以奬飾浮詞虛張之故稱宦蹟則曰
約已裕民頌思勿替矣誦獻民則曰好義
循禮無問顯晦矣欲不與則恐賢而見遺
欲與則屢詢而乖實甚則有貴顯異籍未
甞睹其平生徒以其祖籍之偶同則曰此
吾鄉之哲者相率而牽引之而不知其無
當也而白屋寒畯或有高義卓行庶幾於
punctuated: 特採言官疏，令禮官下所司釐正，而爲籍奏之，德意甚厚。今長吏方兢兢奉行，日求所不應祀者亟罷之，以儆煩濫。但其故老無徵，載籍希闊，靡所考騐，卽銖稱而櫛數之，未必無遺議者，稽覈難也。且其前已令得冒祠，今卽罷去，於章勸之褚已損。故不若及今而愼爲之禁，滌時之弊，而原禮之意以檢律之，庶可止也。何謂時弊？曰：今之議舉者習於文矣，不考論其行事而詳著之以待稽覈，惟以奬飾浮詞虛張之。故稱宦蹟，則曰「約已裕民，頌思勿替」矣；誦獻民，則曰「好義循禮，無問顯晦」矣。欲不與，則恐賢而見遺；欲與，則屢詢而乖實。甚則有貴顯異籍，未甞睹其平生，徒以其祖籍之偶同，則曰「此吾鄉之哲者」，相率而牽引之，而不知其無當也。而白屋寒畯，或有高義卓行，庶幾於
translation_en: … has specially adopted the memorials of the speaking officials, ordering the ritual officials to direct the relevant authorities to rectify the matter and compile a register to be presented to the throne; His gracious intent is most profound. Now the senior local officials are conscientiously carrying this out, daily seeking out those who ought not to be enshrined and swiftly removing them so as to warn against proliferation and abuse. However, the elders can offer no corroboration and written records are sparse, leaving nothing by which to verify the facts; even if one were to weigh them grain by grain and count them tooth by tooth like a comb, it would not necessarily be free of lingering criticism, for verification is difficult. Moreover, since they were previously permitted to falsely occupy a place in the shrines, even if they are removed now, the tokens [?] of public commendation and encouragement have already been impaired. Therefore, it is better to establish cautious prohibitions from this moment on, cleanse away the abuses of the age, and trace back the true meaning of the rites so as to regulate and discipline the practice; in this way, perhaps it can be halted. What is meant by the abuses of the age? I say: those who propose candidates for enshrinement today have grown accustomed to mere literary embellishment. Rather than examining and discussing a person's actual deeds and recording them in detail to await verification, they merely exaggerate them with flattering, empty phrases. Thus, when praising someone's official career, they say, "He restrained himself and enriched the people; praise and longing for him have never ceased"; when eulogizing a local worthy, they say, "He loved righteousness and abided by the rites, whether in prominence or obscurity." If the authorities wish to withhold approval, they fear that a genuinely worthy man might be overlooked; if they wish to grant it, repeated inquiries reveal discrepancies with the facts. In extreme cases, there are men of high rank and prominence registered in other prefectures whose life and conduct the locals have never even witnessed; merely because their ancestral registration happens to be the same, people say, "This is a wise man of our locality," and follow one another in dragging his name in, unaware how inappropriate it is. Meanwhile, among humble scholars from thatched cottages, there may be those of lofty righteousness and outstanding conduct, coming close to …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
太丘叔度之流者輒棄不復道則徇迹之
過也故議舉者務必詳述其事一切爲浮
漫語者罷之其異籍而不出其鄕亦不必
援引之以爲重果行義無玷卽隱約窮巷
亦與表見而又推明禮意以示之禮之祀
于大烝以功六也試桉其所表樹於六者
孰當如僅守尺寸持祿無顯過者不得槩
祠禮之祀于瞽宗以道德也今所稱賢于
鄕者試詰其行事于孔氏之道率履幾何
===
闡發幾何不如是則無非無辜者又慮其
愿也亦不得從先進之林而登之祀典故
實者不能遺而虚者不能飾而典禮可正
也今
令甲每
旌表孝節必以疏
聞俟
報可良以重風化也俎豆於聖人之宮爲百世
規其隆渥豈下
punctuated: 太丘、叔度之流者，輒棄不復道，則徇迹之過也。故議舉者務必詳述其事，一切爲浮漫語者罷之；其異籍而不出其鄕，亦不必援引之以爲重；果行義無玷，卽隱約窮巷，亦與表見。而又推明禮意以示之。禮之祀于大烝，以功六也，試桉其所表樹，於六者孰當？如僅守尺寸、持祿無顯過者，不得槩祠。禮之祀于瞽宗，以道德也，今所稱賢于鄕者，試詰其行事，于孔氏之道率履幾何？闡發幾何？不如是，則無非無辜者，又慮其愿也，亦不得從先進之林而登之祀典。故實者不能遺，而虚者不能飾，而典禮可正也。今令甲，每旌表孝節，必以疏聞，俟報可，良以重風化也。俎豆於聖人之宮，爲百世規，其隆渥豈下
translation_en:
…the likes of Chen Shi (Taiqiu 太丘) and Huang Xian (Shudu 叔度), they are readily cast aside and never spoken of again—this is the fault of judging merely by outward status. Therefore, those who deliberate on nominations must recount the candidate's actual deeds in detail, and all nominations that consist of empty, vague rhetoric should be rejected. As for those registered elsewhere who were not raised in the local community, there is likewise no need to drag them in to lend prestige. Conversely, if a person's conduct and righteousness are truly without blemish, even if they lived in obscurity in a humble lane, they should be granted recognition.

Furthermore, the underlying meaning of the rites should be elucidated and made clear to all. In ritual, sacrifice at the Grand Winter Sacrifice (Dazheng 大烝) is based on six kinds of merit; let us examine a candidate's accomplishments and see which of the six they match. Those who merely abided by minor rules and held on to their salaries without glaring faults must not be indiscriminately enshrined. In ritual, sacrifice at the Music Master's Hall (Guzong 瞽宗) is based on moral virtue; for those nowadays acclaimed as local worthies, let us question their deeds: how much of the Way of Confucius did they personally practice? How much of it did they expound and illuminate? If they have not done so, then even if they are free of blame and transgression, one must still worry that they are merely sanctimonious village conformists (yuan 愿), and they too must not be placed among the ranks of the worthy predecessors or entered into the sacrificial canon. Thus, those of genuine substance cannot be overlooked, those of empty reputation cannot be glossed over, and the canonical rites can be rectified.

Under the current statutes, whenever filial piety or chastity is to be officially honored, it must be reported to the throne in a memorial to await approval—truly because great weight is attached to moral transformation. Yet to receive sacrificial offerings in the temple of the Sage, serving as a model for a hundred generations—how could such exalted favor be any less than…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旌表哉似宜倣奏
聞之例歲舉行之候覈實
報可乃祠則柄有所握而名不得以徇人卽求
名者雖日奔走焉而終不得以虚濫應祀
此敦禮之大原雖煩瀆而必不可巳者愚
生之所竊望也
第五問
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳批丈地均糧
===
國家重務而弊孔不塞貽害匪輕子能究極根源而區畫周詳具覘成
筭是可悉見諸行矣
考試官敎諭賈批條答清丈利弊明如指掌
考試官敎諭汪批遠猷卓識經濟才也
夫國之所急在足賦民之所急在樂業顧
天下未有不樂業之民而能出其身以供
國賦者此酌時經制之略所以急於民也
民之生資地力以贍公私之求其贍私恒
急而贍公恒緩故賦額之不可詘夫人而
punctuated:
旌表哉？似宜倣奏聞之例，歲舉行之，候覈實報可乃祠。則柄有所握，而名不得以徇人；卽求名者雖日奔走焉，而終不得以虚濫應祀。此敦禮之大原，雖煩瀆而必不可巳者，愚生之所竊望也。

第五問
彭子光
同考試官訓導陳批：丈地均糧，國家重務，而弊孔不塞，貽害匪輕。子能究極根源，而區畫周詳，具覘成筭，是可悉見諸行矣。
考試官敎諭賈批：條答清丈利弊，明如指掌。
考試官敎諭汪批：遠猷卓識，經濟才也。

夫國之所急在足賦，民之所急在樂業。顧天下未有不樂業之民，而能出其身以供國賦者，此酌時經制之略，所以急於民也。民之生，資地力以贍公私之求，其贍私恒急，而贍公恒緩。故賦額之不可詘，夫人而
translation_en:
…imperial testimonials of merit? It seems appropriate to follow the precedent of submitting memorials to the throne: conduct this annually, and wait until the facts are verified and imperial approval is returned before enshrining them. In this way, authority will be firmly held, and honors cannot be granted out of personal favor; even if those seeking fame bustle about daily, in the end they will not be able to receive sacrifices through false and excessive claims. This is the great foundation for honoring the rites—though it may seem troublesome and importunate, it absolutely must not be dispensed with, and it is what this humble student privately hopes for.

Fifth Question
Peng Ziguang
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen comments: Surveying the land and equalizing the grain tax is a weighty affair of the state, yet if the loopholes for corruption are not plugged, the resulting harm is no small matter. You are able to thoroughly trace the root causes and lay out comprehensive and detailed plans, fully demonstrating a well-formed strategy that can be entirely put into practice.
Examiner and Instructor Jia comments: Itemized responses on the advantages and disadvantages of the land survey, as clear as pointing to the palm of one's hand.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: Far-reaching plans and outstanding insight—a talent for statecraft!

Now, what is urgent for the state is having sufficient tax revenue, and what is urgent for the people is taking joy in their livelihoods. Yet in all the world there have never been people who do not take joy in their livelihoods who are nonetheless able to exert themselves to supply the state's taxes. This is why a strategy for regulating institutions according to the times must treat the people as its urgent priority. In their livelihoods, the people rely on the productivity of the land to meet both public and private demands; they are always urgent in meeting their private needs and slow in meeting public obligations. Therefore, that the tax quota cannot be reduced is something that every person…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知之然使有其賦無其民弗能供也有其
民而不均其賦弗能久也故均賦則賦足
而民安不均賦則賦不足而民擾吾欲求
其安而去其擾則莫若舉今已足額之田
酌貧富而均其輸為法制以經之故上無
加賦之害而下有安業之利是我之所急
嘗在於民而其利更及於賦也夫古今田
賦之屢變也雖使大撓持籌隸首布筭弗
能悉矣然大較有二三代以上其田常在
===
官三代以下其田常在民田在官則貢之
助之徹之其法惟在正經界經界既正則
事權常握于上而民無他冀故什一行而
頌聲作然自春秋之後而法已陵夷雖好
古若孟軻亦僅能舉大略而已由是秦人
始變阡陌而田漸入於民即武帝時去周
秦未遠也而董仲舒已謂富者田連阡陌
而貧者無立錐之地則其制之不均槩可
睹云于是限于漢均于魏永業于唐皆以
punctuated: 知之。然使有其賦，無其民，弗能供也；有其民，而不均其賦，弗能久也。故均賦則賦足而民安，不均賦則賦不足而民擾。吾欲求其安而去其擾，則莫若舉今已足額之田，酌貧富而均其輸，為法制以經之。故上無加賦之害，而下有安業之利，是我之所急嘗在於民，而其利更及於賦也。夫古今田賦之屢變也，雖使大撓持籌，隸首布筭，弗能悉矣。然大較有二：三代以上，其田常在官；三代以下，其田常在民。田在官，則貢之、助之、徹之，其法惟在正經界。經界既正，則事權常握于上，而民無他冀，故什一行而頌聲作。然自春秋之後而法已陵夷，雖好古若孟軻，亦僅能舉大略而已。由是秦人始變阡陌，而田漸入於民。即武帝時，去周、秦未遠也，而董仲舒已謂「富者田連阡陌，而貧者無立錐之地」，則其制之不均，槩可睹云。于是限于漢，均于魏，永業于唐，皆以
translation_en:
…knows this. Yet if there is the tax quota without the people, it cannot be supplied; if there are the people without equalizing their taxes, it cannot endure. Therefore, when taxes are equalized, revenues are sufficient and the people are at peace; when taxes are not equalized, revenues are insufficient and the people are disturbed. If we wish to seek their peace and remove their disturbance, nothing is better than taking the lands that today already meet the quota, weighing poverty and wealth to equalize their contributions, and establishing institutional laws to regulate them. Thus, above there is no harm of increasing taxes, while below there is the benefit of secure livelihoods. In this way, what we treat as urgent is always the people, yet the benefit extends further to the tax revenues.

As for the repeated changes in land taxation from antiquity to the present, even if Da Nao held the tally sticks and Li Shou laid out the counting rods, they could not exhaust them all. Yet in broad outline there are two phases: during the Three Dynasties and earlier, the land regularly belonged to the state; after the Three Dynasties, the land regularly belonged to the people. When the land belonged to the state—whether under the tribute (gong), aid (zhu), or shared (che) system—the method lay solely in rectifying the field boundaries. Once the boundaries were rectified, authority over affairs was constantly held above, and the people had no other ambitions; thus the one-tenth tax was practiced and songs of praise arose. Yet after the Spring and Autumn period, the system had already fallen into decay, and even someone as fond of antiquity as Meng Ke [Mencius] could only cite its general outline. From this point, the people of Qin first altered the field paths (qianmo), and land gradually passed into the hands of the people. Even in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, which was not far removed from the Zhou and Qin, Dong Zhongshu already said that "the rich have lands linked along the field paths, while the poor have not enough land to stand an awl," so the inequality of the system can generally be seen. Thereupon, the limitation of land holdings under the Han, the equalization of land under the Wei, and the perpetual-holding system under the Tang were all intended to…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
抑雄擅之家而禁其園奪使編戸齊氓稍
得事休息其法非不善也然限田議始仲
舒而述於師丹哀帝終不能用魏孝文用
李安世之說爲均田尚屬草創至唐武德
間復加損益而爲口分永業之制顧令民
得以徙遷鬻其田而制益紊矣厥後括田
行於開元致張虛數方田行於熙寧而旋
以棼擾報罷其利端弊孔大都與漢唐宋
相終始而卒無善制者豈非惠民之無術
哉
===
高皇帝起蹟民間習聞豪宗梗賦狀故元年戊
申首定賦法曁辛酉而黃冊成巳廉知富
民詭灑州縣度田多不實乃分遣國子生
武淳等周行天下度其稅糧多寡爲區每
區有長四人領以耆民躬履田畒按區運
步因圖次其田形籍
奏之謂之魚鱗圖冊較前代獨詳且前代抑
豪右皆主於裁其田必不能奪富者之有
punctuated:
抑雄擅之家，而禁其園奪，使編戸齊氓稍得事休息，其法非不善也。然限田議始仲舒，而述於師丹，哀帝終不能用；魏孝文用李安世之說爲均田，尚屬草創；至唐武德間，復加損益而爲口分、永業之制，顧令民得以徙遷鬻其田，而制益紊矣。厥後括田行於開元，致張虛數；方田行於熙寧，而旋以棼擾報罷。其利端弊孔，大都與漢、唐、宋相終始，而卒無善制者，豈非惠民之無術哉！

高皇帝起蹟民間，習聞豪宗梗賦狀，故元年戊申首定賦法。曁辛酉而黃冊成，巳廉知富民詭灑，州縣度田多不實，乃分遣國子生武淳等周行天下，度其稅糧多寡爲區。每區有長四人，領以耆民，躬履田畒，按區運步，因圖次其田形，籍奏之，謂之《魚鱗圖冊》，較前代獨詳。且前代抑豪右，皆主於裁其田，必不能奪富者之有
translation_en:
…curb powerful and monopolizing families and prohibit their seizures and enclosures [?], allowing registered commoners to gain some measure of rest and relief; these methods were not without merit. Yet the proposal to limit landholdings (xiantian) began with Dong Zhongshu and was reiterated by Shi Dan 師丹, though Emperor Ai 哀帝 ultimately could not put it into practice. Emperor Xiaowen of Wei 魏孝文 adopted the advice of Li Anshi 李安世 to institute the equal-field system (juntian), which was still in a rudimentary state. By the Wude 武德 era (618–626) of the Tang, adjustments were again made to create the system of personal share (koufen) and land in perpetuity (yongye); however, because the people were permitted to sell their land when relocating, the system grew increasingly disordered. Thereafter, the registration of unregistered lands (kuotian) was carried out in the Kaiyuan 開元 era (713–741), leading to inflated and false figures; the square-fields system (fangtian) was carried out in the Xining 熙寧 era (1068–1077), only to be quickly abolished due to the confusion and disruption it caused. The sources of benefit and loopholes for abuse largely lasted throughout the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, yet in the end no sound system was achieved—was this not for lack of an effective method to benefit the people?

The August Emperor Gao 高皇帝 [the Hongwu Emperor] rose from among the common people and was thoroughly familiar with how powerful lineages obstructed taxation. Therefore, in his first year, wushen (1368), he first established the taxation laws. By the xinyou year (1381), when the Yellow Registers (Huangce) were completed, he had already discovered through investigation that wealthy commoners were fraudulently parceling out their holdings to evade taxes and that the land measurements of subprefectures and counties were mostly inaccurate. He thereupon dispatched National University students (guozisheng) such as Wu Chun 武淳 to travel throughout the realm, dividing the land into districts (qu) according to the amount of tax grain. Each district had four headmen (zhang), led by local elders (qimin), who personally walked the fields, paced off measurements district by district, drew maps ordering the shapes of the plots, and entered them into registers to be memorialized to the throne. These were called the Fish-Scale Illustrated Registers (Yulin tuce), and they were uniquely detailed compared to those of former dynasties. Moreover, when former dynasties curbed powerful families, they always focused on curtailing their landholdings; yet one certainly cannot strip the wealthy of what they possess…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以爲貧者之食故法易格今不責其治田
多寡而惟卽多寡定賦故富者不能巧避
而賦易均前代履畝主括地則筭及林麓
山川主檢覆則筭及室廬里落主畫方則
先定品式後履田畝今惟就田定區法簡
而易覈古者八尺爲步步百爲畝周時建
司馬法止用六尺其步益縮迨于唐始用
二百四十步爲畝視周制倍寬今用之則
計畝廣而民稅輕故漢元始時田賦號稱
===
極盛而考諸洪武間天下額田凡八百四
十九萬六千有奇尚溢於元始八百二十
七萬五百有奇之數茲善制之明驗哉承
平久而奸巧叢矣富者得田而賦不及貧
者得賦而田不及憂樂倒置
國計滋損蓋自弘治以後而額田堇堇四百
餘萬視洪武初殺半矣
天子閔然念之
令司農下郡國按額履畝別其勤惰而殿最
punctuated: 以為貧者之食，故法易格；今不責其治田多寡，而惟即多寡定賦，故富者不能巧避，而賦易均。前代履畝，主括地則筭及林麓山川，主檢覆則筭及室廬里落，主畫方則先定品式、後履田畝；今惟就田定區，法簡而易覈。古者八尺為步，步百為畝；周時建《司馬法》，止用六尺，其步益縮；迨于唐始用二百四十步為畝，視周制倍寬；今用之，則計畝廣而民稅輕。故漢元始時，田賦號稱極盛，而考諸洪武間，天下額田凡八百四十九萬六千有奇，尚溢於元始八百二十七萬五百有奇之數，茲善制之明驗哉！承平久而奸巧叢矣，富者得田而賦不及，貧者得賦而田不及，憂樂倒置，國計滋損。蓋自弘治以後，而額田堇堇四百餘萬，視洪武初殺半矣。天子閔然念之，令司農下郡國，按額履畝，別其勤惰而殿最…
translation_en: …to make it food for the poor, and thus the laws were easily obstructed. Now, we do not take them to task over how much or how little land they cultivate, but simply fix their tax quota according to that amount; thus the wealthy cannot artfully evade it, and taxes are easily equalized. When previous dynasties conducted field-by-field surveys, if they aimed at comprehensive land sweeps, their calculations extended even to forests, foothills, mountains, and streams; if they aimed at inspection and verification, their calculations extended even to houses, cottages, and village settlements; if they aimed at square-grid mapping, they first established the grade formulas and only afterward paced out the fields. Now, we simply delineate districts based on the fields themselves, so the method is simple and easy to verify. In antiquity, eight chi made a pace (bu), and one hundred paces made a mu. In the Zhou period, when the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) was established, only six chi were used, so the pace shrank further. By the Tang dynasty, two hundred and forty paces first came to be used for a mu, which was more than twice as generous as the Zhou system. Since we use this today, the measured mu is broad and the people's tax burden is light. Therefore, while the registered land and taxes of the Yuanshi era (1–5 CE) of the Han dynasty were acclaimed as having reached the utmost peak, if we examine the figures from the Hongwu era (1368–1398), the quota of registered land in the empire totaled more than 8,496,000 [qing], still exceeding the Yuanshi figure of more than 8,270,500 [qing]. Is this not clear proof of an excellent institution! Yet as peace has endured for a long time, deceit and cunning have proliferated. The rich acquire land while the taxes do not reach them; the poor acquire taxes while the land does not reach them. Sorrow and joy are inverted, and the state finances suffer increasing loss. Indeed, since the Hongzhi era (1488–1505), the quota of registered land has been a mere four million and some odd [qing]—reduced by half compared to the beginning of the Hongwu era. The Son of Heaven, reflecting on this with compassion, ordered the Minister of Revenue to instruct the prefectures and principalities to survey the fields in person according to the quotas, distinguishing the diligent from the negligent and ranking their performance from lowest to highest…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之即有强宗巨室亦皆俯首聽命而不敢
以觖
天子之明法諸願延須臾以承
休澤者喁喁如也乃粤西則豪右踰制或不
下他藩而谿峒土酋或蠶食齊民之業莫
敢誰何或田稍犬牙其中輙以此輩為解
而避租賦此清理視他藩尤難之難也顧
德意所嚮諸長吏莫不奉行唯謹會峒蠻稍欲
恣睢以傲命吏我巳分布健兒入其巢不
===
旬月而渠黨面縛如犬左效諸酋聞之益
回心面内願奉約束初額田九萬六千三
百有奇後失額一萬八千有奇今竣事田
九萬六千五百有奇稅糧稱是蓋粤西之
履畆屢矣皆奪於羣議迄無成功至是始
復額有羡咸誦
聖天子威德萬里盛矣乃執事猶惓惓焉其為
西人計慮至深遠也愚則以為莫若勤民
而均其賦且吾所謂均非謂賦可勿急也
punctuated: 之。即有强宗巨室，亦皆俯首聽命，而不敢以觖天子之明法；諸願延須臾以承休澤者，喁喁如也。乃粤西則豪右踰制，或不下他藩；而谿峒土酋，或蠶食齊民之業，莫敢誰何；或田稍犬牙其中，輙以此輩為解，而避租賦。此清理視他藩尤難之難也。顧德意所嚮，諸長吏莫不奉行唯謹。會峒蠻稍欲恣睢以傲命吏，我巳分布健兒入其巢，不旬月而渠黨面縛如犬左效。諸酋聞之，益回心面内，願奉約束。初，額田九萬六千三百有奇，後失額一萬八千有奇；今竣事，田九萬六千五百有奇，稅糧稱是。蓋粤西之履畆屢矣，皆奪於羣議，迄無成功；至是始復額有羡，咸誦聖天子威德萬里，盛矣！乃執事猶惓惓焉，其為西人計慮至深遠也。愚則以為莫若勤民而均其賦。且吾所謂均，非謂賦可勿急也，
translation_en: … them. Even where there are powerful clans and great houses, they have all bowed their heads and obeyed orders, not daring to defy the clear laws of the Son of Heaven; and all those who wish to prolong their lives for a moment to receive His beneficent grace look up in eager anticipation. Yet in Guangxi (Yuexi), the transgressions of the powerful and wealthy are perhaps no less than in other provinces; meanwhile, native chieftains of the mountain streams and valleys sometimes encroach like silkworms upon the property of registered commoners without anyone daring to challenge them, or where fields interlock like dog's teeth with theirs, people readily use those chieftains as an excuse to evade land taxes. Thus, clearing up the land registers here is the hardest of the hard compared to other provinces. Nevertheless, wherever His virtuous intent directed, all the senior officials carried it out with utmost diligence. It happened that some valley barbarians grew somewhat unruly and acted arrogantly toward the appointed officials; we had already deployed sturdy soldiers to enter their lairs, and in less than a month their ringleaders and confederates were bound with hands tied behind their backs, offering submission like dogs [?]. When the various chieftains heard of this, they turned their hearts all the more toward the interior and willingly accepted our regulations. Originally, the quota of land was over 96,300 qing, and later over 18,000 of the quota was lost; now that the work is completed, the land amounts to over 96,500 qing, with tax grain proportionate to this. Indeed, land surveys have been attempted repeatedly in Guangxi, yet all were thwarted by the multitude of conflicting opinions and achieved no success until now, when the original quota has finally been restored with a surplus. All praise the Sacred Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue reaching ten thousand li—how magnificent! Yet Your Excellency is still earnestly concerned; your plans and deliberations for the people of Guangxi are deep and far-reaching indeed. In my humble opinion, nothing is better than being diligent toward the people and equalizing their taxes. Moreover, what I mean by equalization is not to say that taxes need not be treated as urgent, …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
非盡如前代欲限制其田以遺貧民業也
非舉貧富而較量之欲平衡而稱適也物
之不齊物理固然惟計今見額多田則多
賦少田則少賦田膏腴則從重田瘠鹵則
從輕俾貧弱者不致偏累而稍紓其目前
之急富而強有力者不得隱匿詭灑以公
賦積私家是謂均平固
皇上之所為履畝意也昔杜君卿有言簿書旣
廣必籍衆功籍衆功則政由羣吏欲以紀
===
人事之衆寡明地利之多少雖申商督刑
不可得而詳矣此疾諸胥之緣絕為奸也
執事謂冊籍得無為異日者憂誠慮之矣
今惟督縣官務精稽覈倣魚鱗之式為之
一不當毋但罪吏即縣官亦得議廢置有
不人人自効者乎及籍成以上諸郡郡以
上諸司亦復精覈如前則參伍旣備弊安
得而乘也豪家張虛愒而食僮田且役其
人為之佃僕恐致厲階固矣今田已籍于
punctuated: 非盡如前代欲限制其田以遺貧民業也，非舉貧富而較量之、欲平衡而稱適也。物之不齊，物理固然。惟計今見額，多田則多賦，少田則少賦，田膏腴則從重，田瘠鹵則從輕，俾貧弱者不致偏累而稍紓其目前之急，富而強有力者不得隱匿詭灑、以公賦積私家，是謂均平，固皇上之所為履畝意也。昔杜君卿有言：「簿書旣廣，必籍衆功；籍衆功則政由羣吏。欲以紀人事之衆寡、明地利之多少，雖申、商督刑，不可得而詳矣。」此疾諸胥之緣絕為奸也。執事謂「冊籍得無為異日者憂」，誠慮之矣。今惟督縣官務精稽覈，倣魚鱗之式為之，一不當，毋但罪吏，即縣官亦得議廢置，有不人人自効者乎？及籍成以上諸郡，郡以上諸司，亦復精覈如前，則參伍旣備，弊安得而乘也？豪家張虛愒而食僮田，且役其人為之佃僕，恐致厲階，固矣。今田已籍于
translation_en:
…nor does it entirely mean, as in former dynasties, seeking to limit landholdings in order to leave a livelihood for the poor; nor does it mean weighing the rich and the poor against each other in an attempt to equalize and level them. That things are unequal is naturally the principle of things. It is only a matter of calculating the current registered quota: where there is much land, levy much tax; where there is little land, levy little tax; where the land is fertile, assess it heavily; where the land is barren and saline, assess it lightly. Thus the poor and weak will not suffer disproportionate burdens and may somewhat relieve their immediate distress, while the rich and powerful will not be able to conceal land or falsely parcel it out across other households, enriching their private families at the expense of the public revenue. This is what is meant by equitable equalization, and it is indeed His Majesty's intention in conducting the cadastral survey.

In the past, Du Junqing 杜君卿 (Du You 杜佑) said: "Once the registers and account books become vast, one must rely on the efforts of the multitude; when one relies on the efforts of the multitude, administration falls into the hands of the lesser clerks. If one wishes thereby to record the multitude or scarcity of human affairs and clarify the abundance or meagerness of the land's yield, even if Shen Buhai 申不害 and Shang Yang 商鞅 were to supervise the punishments, it would be impossible to ascertain the details." This expressed his hatred of the petty clerks exploiting gaps to commit fraud. When Your Excellency asks whether "the registers might not become a source of worry in the future," you have truly given this deep thought. Now we need only supervise the District Magistrates to ensure that they conduct thorough and precise verifications, compiling the registers in imitation of the "fish-scale" (yulin 魚鱗) format. If there is a single discrepancy, not only should the clerks be punished, but the District Magistrate himself should also be subject to deliberation for dismissal or demotion—would not everyone then exert himself to the utmost? When the registers are completed and submitted to the prefectures, and from the prefectures submitted to the provincial agencies, if they too verify them just as thoroughly as before, then once cross-checking is complete, how could any abuses find an opening to creep in?

As for powerful families using empty threats [?] to swallow up the lands of the Zhuang 獞 [written 僮] people and furthermore pressing the people themselves into service as their tenant-serfs, the fear that this will give rise to calamity is certainly well-founded. Now that the lands have already been registered with the…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
官諸獞亦頗知其不足恃第桉畝而酌其
賦責之必輸及登稼時禁豪毋虐取之使
獞亦得爲食否則還之獞人以供吾賦或
稍與輕科以懷之其無主者入爲官田以
待別授且令以後豪家毋得窺小利而納
獞人故佃僕可馭也其猺獞故有生熟二
種今熟者已願就田賦而齒編氓亦宜與
之輕科而重禁里魁毋得苛求使之安堵
其生猺獞每不利於熟者之來歸而爲我
===
用或行煽誘或肆讎殺或指其田爲彼田
而羣起與爭則申固兵防禁其出沒重則
兵之如是足矣不必求諸化之外也土酋
在上世止責以扜掫藉其兵力故田無頃
畝而聽其自輸糧爲額今原額不失姑聽
其便第在左江者頗輸租而在右江者率
漸積逋負故督責宜加焉其有怙强而奪
民田或受民詭託以滋隱避第桉籍而清
之重則罪及酋必不能桿吾法矣贍兵之
punctuated: 官，諸獞亦頗知其不足恃。第桉畝而酌其賦，責之必輸；及登稼時，禁豪毋虐取之，使獞亦得爲食。否則還之獞人以供吾賦，或稍與輕科以懷之；其無主者入爲官田，以待別授。且令以後豪家毋得窺小利而納獞人，故佃僕可馭也。其猺、獞故有生熟二種，今熟者已願就田賦而齒編氓，亦宜與之輕科，而重禁里魁毋得苛求，使之安堵。其生猺、獞每不利於熟者之來歸而爲我用，或行煽誘，或肆讎殺，或指其田爲彼田而羣起與爭，則申固兵防，禁其出沒，重則兵之，如是足矣，不必求諸化之外也。土酋在上世止責以扜掫，藉其兵力，故田無頃畝，而聽其自輸糧爲額。今原額不失，姑聽其便；第在左江者頗輸租，而在右江者率漸積逋負，故督責宜加焉。其有怙强而奪民田，或受民詭託以滋隱避，第桉籍而清之，重則罪及酋，必不能桿吾法矣。贍兵之
translation_en: … the government, and the various Zhuang (獞) peoples also rather understand that these powerful families cannot be relied upon. We need only assess their taxes according to the acreage and require that they be paid in full; and when the harvest is brought in, forbid the powerful families from tyrannically seizing it, so that the Zhuang may also have enough to eat. Otherwise, the land should be returned to the Zhuang so that they may supply our tax quota, perhaps granting them a slightly lighter tax rate in order to win them over; as for land without an owner, it should be confiscated as government land to await reassignment to others. Moreover, let it be ordered that henceforth powerful families may not eye petty profits and take in Zhuang people; thus, these tenant-servants can be kept under control. As for the Yao (猺) and Zhuang, there have traditionally been two kinds, the "raw" [unassimilated] and the "cooked" [assimilated]. Now that the assimilated ones are already willing to submit to the land tax and be enrolled among the registered commoners, we should likewise grant them a light tax rate, while strictly forbidding the village heads (likui 里魁) from making harsh exactions, thereby allowing them to live in peace. As for the unassimilated Yao and Zhuang, they always find it against their interests when the assimilated ones submit and allow themselves to be used by us. Sometimes they engage in incitement and enticement, sometimes they indulge in vendettas and killings, and sometimes they claim that those fields are their own fields and rise up in bands to contend for them. In such cases, we should reinforce our military defenses and prohibit their raids and incursions, using military force against them if the offense is grave. Doing this is sufficient; there is no need to pursue them beyond the pale of civilization. In earlier generations, native chieftains (tuqiu 土酋) were charged only with standing guard and patrolling, as the state relied on their military strength; therefore, their fields were not measured in qing and mu, and they were allowed to deliver grain voluntarily as a fixed quota. Today, so long as the original quota is not lost, we may for the time being allow them to do as they find convenient. However, while those in Zuojiang (左江) are fairly dutiful in paying their tax grain, those in Youjiang (右江) generally have gradually accumulated arrears, so supervision and reprimands should be stepped up. Should there be any who rely on their strength to seize commoners' fields, or who accept fraudulent commendations of land from commoners to increase tax evasion, we need only clear up the matter according to the registers; in grave cases, the punishment should extend to the chieftain himself, and they will certainly not be able to defy our laws. As for the [fields] that support the troops …

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
田業不可罷卽以供餉而不責其賦且吾
餉亦可以罷給而備軍與諸荒蕪而始籍
者則徐待三年後始征其租或仍以輕科
取之朝耕尺寸之田暮入差徭之籍玆陳
靖之慷慨於宋代者其言可繹也而又廣
招徠勤督率毋使草萊彌目有土而不可
食是吾不務加賦而惟務足民乆之民足
而賦均足焉玆非兩利而俱便者乎故不
限而畫一不均而稱平不永業口分而公
===
私無困可以廣
德意而惠無窮雖不貢不徹而其意未甞不同
於三代竊以爲粤西便計或不出此猶慮
其狂瞽而無當也惟進教之
punctuated: 田業不可罷，卽以供餉而不責其賦；且吾餉亦可以罷給而備軍與。諸荒蕪而始籍者，則徐待三年後始征其租，或仍以輕科取之。朝耕尺寸之田，暮入差徭之籍，玆陳靖之慷慨於宋代者，其言可繹也。而又廣招徠，勤督率，毋使草萊彌目，有土而不可食。是吾不務加賦而惟務足民，乆之民足而賦均足焉，玆非兩利而俱便者乎？故不限而畫一，不均而稱平，不永業、口分而公私無困，可以廣德意而惠無窮。雖不貢、不徹，而其意未甞不同於三代。竊以爲粤西便計，或不出此。猶慮其狂瞽而無當也，惟進教之。
translation_en: …fields and estates for the sustenance of soldiers cannot be abolished, so let them directly supply military rations without demanding regular land tax from them; moreover, our own ration disbursements can then be discontinued and saved to provide for military campaigns [reading 軍興 for 軍與]. As for those wasteland fields that are newly registered, wait unhurriedly until after three years before beginning to levy rent on them, or else continue to collect from them at a light tax rate. "In the morning they plow a tiny patch of land, and by evening they are entered into the registers for corvée labor"—this was what Chen Jing 陳靖 lamented with indignation during the Song dynasty, and his words are worth pondering. Furthermore, we should broadly attract settlers and diligently supervise and lead them, so that weeds and brambles do not fill the eye, leaving land that cannot be cultivated for food. In this way, we do not strive to increase taxes, but strive only to make the people sufficient; after a long time, when the people have sufficiency, the tax revenues too will be equally sufficient. Is this not beneficial to both sides and convenient for all? Therefore, without imposing land-holding limits (xian 限), there is uniformity; without enforcing land equalization (jun 均), there is fairness; without instituting perpetual holdings (yongye 永業) and personal shares (koufen 口分), neither public nor private interests suffer distress. Thus we can broaden His Majesty's benevolent intentions and extend boundless grace. Even without the tribute (gong 貢) or tithe (che 徹) systems, the underlying spirit is no different from that of the Three Dynasties. I venture to think that an advantageous plan for Guangxi (Yuexi 粤西) perhaps goes no further than this. Yet I still fear that my words are rash, blind, and wide of the mark; I pray only that you will advance me and instruct me.

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
秋八月廣西鄉試竣事宗正
幸以薄技共盛典當有言申
告諸士曰玆非成周時所稱
賢能書哉彼鄉大夫提衡而
品裁者皆平居所灼見不謬
其實故能光天府而重祖廟
===
之藏與天球琬琰交珎而世
守然所用稍有不適輒以罰
舉者無赦故往往稱得人今
宗正於諸士卽稱同業然居
産殊壤未甞通邂逅接殷勤
也僅以方寸之管盈尺之楮
權衡於三日間所揮霍卽揮
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

秋八月，廣西鄉試竣事。宗正幸以薄技共盛典，當有言申告諸士曰：玆非成周時所稱「賢能書」哉？彼鄉大夫提衡而品裁者，皆平居所灼見，不謬其實，故能光天府而重祖廟之藏，與天球、琬琰交珎而世守。然所用稍有不適，輒以罰舉者無赦，故往往稱得人。今宗正於諸士，卽稱同業，然居産殊壤，未甞通邂逅、接殷勤也。僅以方寸之管、盈尺之楮，權衡於三日間所揮霍；卽揮
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn, the Guangxi Provincial Examination was brought to completion. I, Zongzheng, having been fortunate enough to participate in this grand ceremony with my modest skills, ought to offer some words of instruction and admonition to the scholars, saying: Is this record not what in the era of the flourishing Zhou was called a "Register of the Worthy and Capable"? In those days, those whom the District Grandees weighed and evaluated were all men whose qualities they had clearly observed in ordinary life, without mistaking the reality. Therefore, those registers could bring luster to the Sacred Repository and add weight to the treasures of the Ancestral Temple, being prized alongside the Heavenly Jade-Sphere and the Wanyan Scepters and guarded for generations. Yet if those who were employed proved even slightly unsuitable, the recommenders were immediately punished without pardon; hence, the system was often praised for obtaining the right men. Now, although I, Zongzheng, may be called a fellow scholar in the same pursuits as you gentlemen, we dwell in and hail from different regions, and have never had occasion to meet by chance or exchange cordialities. It is merely through a brush an inch thick and a sheet of paper a foot long that I have weighed what you dashed off during the space of three days; and even in what was dashed…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
霍僅取一藝能稱別質文不
諄其意指即赫然賢儔選矣
是能必其德行果醇固而適
用者乎漢初取士御史下郡
守勸駕而署其行義及年其
後定四科以學通行脩經中
博士者爲次高等猶庶幾三
===
物之指最後定口率郡口二
十萬幷邇蠻徼者歲舉不過
一人何其儉也粤西故雜蠻
落入
昭代始駸駸媲盛中土即一二窟
穴近亦解辮受約束蔚然爲
文明隩區士授經率多專門
punctuated: 霍，僅取一藝能，稱別質文，不諄其意指，即赫然賢儔選矣。是能必其德行果醇固而適用者乎？漢初取士，御史下郡守勸駕，而署其行義及年；其後定四科，以學通行脩、經中博士者爲次高等，猶庶幾三物之指；最後定口率，郡口二十萬幷邇蠻徼者，歲舉不過一人，何其儉也！粤西故雜蠻落，入昭代始駸駸媲盛中土；即一二窟穴，近亦解辮受約束，蔚然爲文明隩區，士授經率多專門
translation_en:
…dash off, and even in what they dash off, he selects them for a single literary skill, weighing and distinguishing substance and refinement. So long as they do not go counter [?] to the intended meaning, they are resplendently chosen as the peers of worthies. Can this guarantee that their moral conduct is truly pure and steadfast, and that they are suited for practical service?

In the early Han, when selecting men of talent, the Censors sent orders down to the Commandery Governors to urge candidates to take to the road, while recording their righteous conduct and their age. Later, the Four Categories were established, and those whose learning was comprehensive and whose conduct was cultivated—sufficient in the Classics to qualify as Erudites—were placed in the second-highest grade; this still came close to the purport of the "Three Things" of antiquity. Finally, ratios by population were fixed: a commandery with a population of two hundred thousand, as well as those bordering the southern tribal frontiers, recommended no more than one man a year—how sparing that was!

Western Yue [Guangxi] was formerly interspersed with tribal settlements. Only upon entering our illustrious dynasty did it gradually come to rival the flourishing Central Lands. Even the one or two remaining lairs have recently unbound their braided hair and submitted to governance, burgeoning into a heartland of civilization. The scholars who transmit the Classics are for the most part specialized…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
名家乃今積三載輒得五十
有五人計所遇殆倍蓰漢氏
而其夙夜黽勉袚心注目而
求之者第以其經中博士業
止爾有如察署行義其出入
或諄所聞以試諸用輒弗當
而因按舉不適者罪安所離
===
遏玆宗正之所爲葸葸懼也
顧聞之士在校若金在陶惟
主德所鎔鑄必有顯効頃者世風
日競於文士漱藝尤靡曼不
根有傷雅道
天子閔之
下功令數加釐正西士雖疎逖
punctuated: 名家。乃今積三載輒得五十有五人，計所遇殆倍蓰漢氏。而其夙夜黽勉，袚心注目而求之者，第以其經中博士業止爾。有如察署行義，其出入或諄所聞，以試諸用輒弗當；而因按舉不適者，罪安所離遏？玆宗正之所爲葸葸懼也。顧聞之，士在校若金在陶，惟主德所鎔鑄，必有顯効。頃者世風日競於文，士漱藝尤靡曼不根，有傷雅道。天子閔之，下功令，數加釐正。西士雖疎逖，
translation_en: …renowned specialists. Yet today, every three years fifty-five men are regularly selected; reckoning the opportunities they enjoy, this is nearly several times that of the Han dynasty. And yet what we strive for day and night, cleansing our minds and fixing our eyes to seek out, goes no further than their mastery of the Erudite curriculum in the Classics. Suppose we were to examine and record their moral conduct, and their comportment proved at variance with [?] what had been heard of them, or when tested in practical application they proved unsuitable; then if those who recommend them are held to account for selecting the unfit, how could we escape or stave off blame? This is why I, Zongzheng, am filled with anxious trepidation. Yet I have heard that scholars in the schools are like metal in the mold: however the ruler's virtue smelts and casts them, there will surely be manifest results. Recently, the customs of the age have increasingly competed in literary ornament, and the scholars' pursuit of the arts has become especially florid and rootless, to the detriment of the proper Way. The Son of Heaven, grieving over this, handed down Academic Regulations and repeatedly instituted rectifications. Although the scholars of the West [Guangxi] are distant and remote,…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
猶訢訢知嚮方焉乃御史敖
選之
請代也
上念粤西當賓興有日矣故事御
史當按部必引
奏始
遣也恐致後期乃
===
詔閣臣趣御史大夫特疏御史名
以
請不踰時
命下趣御史行夫粤西遠在萬里
蕞爾諸士何足廛
聖衷而眷眷若此是其中得無有
倜儻瑰瑋之士足以副
punctuated: 猶訢訢知嚮方焉。乃御史敖選之請代也，上念粤西當賓興有日矣。故事，御史當按部，必引奏始遣也。恐致後期，乃詔閣臣趣御史大夫，特疏御史名以請。不踰時，命下，趣御史行。夫粤西遠在萬里，蕞爾諸士，何足廛聖衷而眷眷若此？是其中得無有倜儻瑰瑋之士，足以副
translation_en: …still happily know the direction toward which they should turn. Now, when Investigating Censor Ao Xuan 敖選 requested to be replaced, His Majesty bore in mind that the time for the triennial賓興 (guest-forwarding examination) in Guangxi was drawing near. According to precedent, when a censor was due to tour a circuit as Regional Inspector, he had to be presented in audience and memorialized before being dispatched. Fearing that this would cause him to miss the scheduled date, His Majesty issued an edict to the Grand Secretaries to urge the Censor-in-Chief to submit a special memorial requesting the appointment with the censor's name. Before an hour had passed, the command came down urging the censor to set out. Now, Guangxi lies ten thousand li away; how could its humble scholars be worthy of troubling the Sacred Heart with such solicitous concern as this? Could it be that among them there are extraordinary and magnificent scholars capable of fulfilling…

title: 萬曆十年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德意應
昌會陋漢氏而庶幾成周濟濟
之盛者乎比御史至百執事
皆驚顧以為迅速旣而得其
所繇皆感激頌
聖德不遠裔土况諸士又所賓興
而求者也有不益感奮願效
===
其材諝以佐
任使而終始所砥礪必本德行
兢兢然罔敢玷闕用少報萬
分之一庶幾足稱賢能書哉
宗正請執簡俟其後
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教
諭賈宗正謹序
punctuated:
德意，應昌會，陋漢氏而庶幾成周濟濟之盛者乎？比御史至，百執事皆驚顧，以為迅速；旣而得其所繇，皆感激，頌聖德不遠裔土。况諸士又所賓興而求者也，有不益感奮，願效其材諝以佐任使，而終始所砥礪，必本德行，兢兢然罔敢玷闕，用少報萬分之一，庶幾足稱賢能書哉？宗正請執簡俟其後。
江西撫州府樂安縣儒學教諭賈宗正謹序。
translation_en:
…His Majesty's gracious intent, respond to this flourishing era, look down upon the Han dynasty, and nearly rival the abundant talent of the Western Zhou? When the Censor arrived, all the officiating functionaries looked at one another in astonishment, marveling at his speed; and once they learned the reason behind it, all were deeply moved with gratitude, praising His Majesty's sacred virtue for not treating these distant frontier lands as remote. How much more so for the scholars themselves, who are the very ones being recommended as honored guests and sought out by the court! Could there be any among them who are not all the more moved and roused, eager to offer their talents and wisdom to assist in the tasks entrusted to them, and who, in cultivating and tempering themselves from beginning to end, will not ground themselves in moral conduct, remaining ever cautious so as never to incur blemish or fault, thereby repaying even one ten-thousandth of His Majesty's grace, and nearly proving worthy of the Register of the Worthy and Capable? I, Zongzheng, beg to hold my writing tablets in hand and await what follows.

Respectfully prefaced by Jia Zongzheng 賈宗正, Instructor of the Confucian School of Le'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
